Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claim-Id: cfb62886f9854b6ab1a2f7e824417cdb Branch: dev1/fix/wake-notice-cancelled-outcome Base: 89cd2d30c93e At: 2026-11-04T18:15:54Z ### Checklist - [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help. - [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version. - [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed. ### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem **What the user sees.** When a background execution ends because it was cancelled, the runtime notice card in the transcript summarises it as **"1 unconfirmed"**, while the record printed one line below in the same card carries the badge **"cancelled"**. The card contradicts itself about the same execution, and the summary tells the researcher the outcome is unknown when they cancelled it themselves. - current: 1 cancelled execution → summary `Synced 1 background execution result(s)` + `1 unconfirmed`, record badge `cancelled`. - expected: 1 cancelled execution → summary `Synced 1 background execution result(s)` + `1 cancelled`, record badge `cancelled`. **Where.** `apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx:53-58` is the summary bucketing. It has three entries — `completed` (`:54`), `failed` (`:55`) and a catch-all (`:56`, `record.state !== "completed" && record.state !== "failed"`). `cancelled` is not a bucket of its own, so it falls into `chat.wakeNoticeUnconfirmed` (`:56`), even though the same file already maps it to its own badge label at `:26` (`cancelled: "chat.wakeNoticeState.cancelled"`). The catalog reflects that split: the summary keys are enumerated at `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:2631-2633` and the badge at `:2641` (zh: summary `:5591-5593`, badge `:5601`), and no `chat.wakeNoticeCancelled` summary key exists. The cancelled record is reachable, not hypothetical. `services/api/src/shell-executions.ts:850-851` queues the completion notice for every terminal state, and the cancelled branch of `settle` finishes the execution with `state: "cancelled"` at `:810-815` (`finish(execution, { state: observed.state, … })`). `services/api/src/notification-dispatch.ts:23` copies that catalog state into `RuntimeNoticeRecord.state`, and `packages/schema/src/execution.ts:45` lists `cancelled` among the `ManagedExecution` states. A notice persisted before `records` existed still renders from its counts (`WakeNotice.tsx:69-71`), so that path is unaffected. **Minimal reproduction (red first, no browser).** Add this case to `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` (the file already renders the component with `renderToStaticMarkup`): ```tsx const notice: RuntimeNotice = { executions: 1, timers: 0, prompt: "[Execution notifications]", records: [ { agentId: "main", kind: "execution", runnerId: "local", sourceId: "exec-1", state: "cancelled" }, ], }; const html = renderToStaticMarkup(createElement(WakeNotice, { notice })); assert.match(html, /1 cancelled/); ``` Run on the base commit: ``` cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/zz-wake-notice-cancelled-probe.test.tsx ``` Observed (the probe file is temporary and prints the two competing readings): ``` # \# SUMMARY "1 unconfirmed" # \# BADGE cancelled not ok 1 - probe: a cancelled execution is summarised as cancelled, not unconfirmed error: |- The input did not match the regular expression /1 cancelled/. Input: '

Synced 1 background execution result(s)1 unconfirmed

  • cancelled…' # tests 1 # pass 0 # fail 1 ``` **Fix direction (smallest slice).** Add one bucket to `outcomes` (`WakeNotice.tsx:53-58`) for `record.state === "cancelled"` and one message pair, `chat.wakeNoticeCancelled` — `"{count} cancelled"` next to `messages.ts:2633`, `"{count} 项已取消"` next to `:5593`. Keep the catch-all at `:56` for `unknown`, `queued`, `running` and for records with no catalog entry (`state` undefined), which is what "unconfirmed" actually means today. The per-record badge and the persisted-without-records path (`WakeNotice.tsx:69-71`) stay unchanged. **Acceptance.** - a notice with 1 completed + 1 failed + 1 cancelled execution summarises as `1 completed · 1 failed · 1 cancelled` with no `unconfirmed` — this is the assertion that fails on the base commit; - a record whose catalog entry is gone (no `state`) still summarises as `1 unconfirmed`; - `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` keeps its existing cases green, and the new case fails on `89cd2d30` for the reported reason, not for a missing import. ### Detailed Environment Information Description - Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (2026-11-04). - `apps/web` (React + Vite). Node `v22.23.2`, pnpm `11.1.2`, Linux x86_64. - Command: `cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/zz-wake-notice-cancelled-probe.test.tsx` - No browser and no backend are needed: the component is rendered with `react-dom/server`, the notice is a plain `RuntimeNotice` fixture, and the state it receives is the shape `runtimeNotice()` produces. ### Additional Information Duplicate check (open and closed, via the GitHub issue search): - `"wake notice"` → 10 results; none is about the summary buckets (closest: #63/#252/#253, earlier notification-delivery and e2e work). - `"WakeNotice"` → 0 results. - `"unconfirmed"` → 25 results; #874 is the Activity panel counting `unknown` as active (different component and different record), #541/#542/#547 are the backend shell-observation fix, #185/#187 the earlier Runner-status retry. None covers this card's summary. - `"cancelled"` → 76 results; #871 / PR #878 is the queued-cancel toast's hardcoded English, a different surface. Open PR check: the file lists of all 63 open pull requests were read through the API on 2026-11-04; none changes `apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx` (or `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx`). ### Version Information - `main` @ `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (2026-11-04) - Affected package: `apps/web` (`@sciencediscovery/web`)

issue:891.body:
## Summary

Three review findings from #870, #878 and #888 are real but cannot ride those pull requests without invalidating approvals they already hold, so they are recorded here instead of being lost when the threads close. Each item names the file and line on `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`.

## 1. `#870` — the leftovers test matches the sentinel on the error message only

`services/api/src/store-replace-cleanup.test.ts:107`

`await assert.rejects(writeRun(store, sessionId), /sentinel-rename/)` matches only the thrown error's own `message`. Test A in the same file (`:88`) deliberately concatenates `error.cause?.message`, test B does not. Today `writeArray` still calls plain `rename` (`services/api/src/store.ts:2159`), so the mock's `EPERM` carries the sentinel in its own message and the assertion passes.

Once #857 replaces that call with `renameReplace`, the thrown error is a `FileReplaceError` whose message is `Could not replace <dest> after 20 attempts (EPERM)` and whose sentinel lives only in `cause`, so this test fails for the wrong reason. The fix is to assert `cause.message`, or `error.name === "FileReplaceError"` plus the sentinel, the same way test A does.

## 2. `#878` — the "unexpected status" toast test never reaches the fallback branch

`apps/web/tests/QueuedCancelToast.test.ts:50`

`interrupted` is terminal (`isTerminalRunStatus`, `apps/web/src/run-stream/model.ts:127`), so `queuedCancelToast("interrupted", t)` returns `app.queuedCancelOutcome.finished` and the assertion `assert.match(toast.title, /更新|结束/)` passes on the terminal branch. Of the seven statuses only `queued` reaches `app.queuedCancelOutcome.statusDetail`, and that branch has no `detail`, so `/undefined/` can never appear either. A regression that drops `{ status }` from `statusDetail` stays green.

Coverage only — no user-visible defect.

## 3. `#878` — the fallback detail interpolates a raw enum token

`apps/web/src/run-stream/model.ts:145`

`t("app.queuedCancelOutcome.statusDetail", { status })` prints the raw value, so an unexpected status renders `当前状态：queued` in the Chinese UI — the same mixed-language outcome #871 was filed about, one layer deeper. The catalog has one status label today (`app.queued` = "Queued" / "排队中", `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:2516` and `:5482`). The sentence also hard-codes the Stop button's name (`messages.ts:2520`, `:5486`) instead of interpolating `composer.stop` (`messages.ts:406`).

## 4. `#888` — the desktop tool card keeps the English headings

`apps/desktop/src/app/tool-io.ts:60-63`, `apps/desktop/src/views/ToolCard.tsx:128`, `apps/desktop/src/text.ts`

The web card localises `Result` / `Error` / `Created files` / `Produced artifacts` in #888, but the desktop shell renders the same card from its own parser markers and its own catalog, so a zh-CN user in the desktop app keeps the English headings next to `输入`-style ones. #885 as filed only names the web card; localising the desktop twin is a separate change with its own catalog.

## Expected behaviour

1. `store-replace-cleanup.test.ts` asserts the sentinel through `cause` (or on `error.name`), so it fails for the right reason after #857.
2. `QueuedCancelToast.test.ts` drives a status that actually reaches `app.queuedCancelOutcome.statusDetail` and asserts the rendered detail.
3. The fallback detail maps the status through the existing run-status labels and interpolates the Stop label from `composer.stop`.
4. The desktop tool card localises the four headings from its own catalog, with the same zh-CN strings the web card now uses.

## 5. `#868` and `#887` each carry a copy of the reserved-name predicate — fold them into one when the second lands

`#866` (PR `#868`) added `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` inside `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts`; `#887` (PR `#890`) added the same predicate in
`packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts`, exported through the package index, because on the base the sanitizer had no reserved-name branch at all.

Both PR bodies say "whichever merges second folds the copy into `sanitizeUploadFilename`". That sentence is not a work item, so it is recorded here:
after both land, `workspace-upload.ts` should call the exported helper and drop its inline copy, and the superscript-digit class
(`com[1-9¹²³]` / `lpt[1-9¹²³]`) must be the same in both spellings while the copy still exists.

Expected: one predicate in `packages/workspace`, one call site in the sanitizer, no second regex in `services/api`, and the reject lists in
`workspace-upload.test.ts` and the workspace package tests agreeing.

## 6. The setup wizard's GB tier is the top of the ladder, so a free disk at or above ~1024 GiB prints `1024.0GB`

`apps/desktop/src/views/SetupWizard.tsx:127-128`

`scaledSize(size, printed, 4)` stops at unit 3 and the terminal branch prints `value.toFixed(1) + "GB"` with no further level, so the rule the
#879 rewrite enforces ("the unit follows the number that is printed") has no answer at the top: `formatWizardFreeSpace(1024 ** 4)` → `"1024.0GB"`,
`formatWizardFreeSpace(2 * 1024 ** 4)` → `"2048.0GB"`, switching at `1_099_457_940_685` bytes (1023.95 GiB, the first value whose one-decimal GB
rounds to 1024.0).

This is **pre-existing**, not introduced by #879/#880 — the base printed the same above 1 GiB — so it does not block that fix; it is a product call:

- add a TB tier so the ladder ends at `1.0TB`, or
- accept `1024.0GB` above 1 TiB and say so in the doc comment.

Expected: one of the two, decided explicitly, with the reading at and just below `1_099_457_940_685` pinned in `apps/desktop/tests/size-boundary.test.ts`.

issue:893.body:
# [Bug] Idea Tree initial ideation can fail due to inconsistent exploration-type instructions and proposal validation

## Summary

The Idea Tree research workflow can fail during its initial ideation round, leaving only the ROOT node and no generated candidate hypotheses.

The initial IDEATE prompt encourages `exploit` proposals except when deliberately exploring novel directions. However, an initial research tree has no existing candidates or insights that an `exploit` proposal can reference.

The validator correctly enforces references for exploit proposals, but the prompt does not adequately address this initial-state constraint.

## Observed behavior

**Original baseline run**

- Research created successfully.
- ROOT node persisted.
- LLM ideation invoked.
- Validation failed after one correction.
- Error: `Proposal references an unknown candidate or insight`
- Final research state: `interrupted`
- Candidate count: 0

**Diagnostic run with a temporary prompt modification**

- The IDEATE prompt was modified to explicitly require `explore` during the initial round.
- A mock-based direct engine test generated two candidates and completed evaluation.
- A real Agent E2E run using SiliconFlow DeepSeek V4.1 Flash still failed during ideation.
- Error: `Exploit proposals must name their evidence and targeted insight`
- Final research state: `interrupted`
- Candidate count: 0

The diagnostic modification was not accepted as a product fix. The original source file has been restored on disk, while the running process baseline remains unverified.

## Relevant code

- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/prompts.py`, initial IDEATE instructions (lines 11-14)
- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py`, proposal reference validation (lines 448-458)
- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py`, exploit proposal requirements (lines 459-467)
- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py`, correction and retry handling (lines 260-263)

## Expected behavior

When a research tree contains no prior candidate or insight, initial ideation should produce valid new candidate proposals without referencing nonexistent objects.

Invalid references must continue to be rejected. Subsequent exploit proposals should reference existing candidates and insights.

## Actual behavior

The initial ideation workflow terminates after proposal validation fails and one correction attempt does not resolve the invalid proposal.

No candidate hypotheses are persisted, preventing subsequent evaluation and tree evolution in the observed runs.

## Diagnostic findings

The evidence supports an inconsistency between initial-state prompt instructions and proposal validation requirements.

A mock-based test succeeded after clarifying the prompt, but a real-model diagnostic run still failed. The exact raw model responses and full effective prompts were not captured, so model noncompliance and correction-specific causes remain unverified.

## Suggested investigation

1. Inspect the effective IDEATE prompt and initial research state.
2. Verify how `explorationType` is generated and parsed.
3. Check that first-round proposals cannot reference nonexistent candidates or insights.
4. Examine correction behavior when exploit proposals lack valid references.
5. Add real-model integration tests alongside deterministic schema tests.
6. Preserve strict referential integrity; do not silently convert invalid exploit proposals into explore proposals without an explicit, validated design decision.

## Impact

Blocks candidate generation and downstream evaluation in the reproduced Idea Tree research runs.

## Reproduction context

- **Test environment**: ScienceDiscovery container deployment
- **Model**: SiliconFlow DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
- **Template**: `scientific-hypothesis-general/v1`
- **Trigger**: Create idea research with empty initial tree, invoke ideation stage

## Evidence availability

Research state JSON, SSE event records, test reports, and code version audit are available upon request. Internal identifiers will be sanitized before sharing.

## Suggested fix approaches

1. **Validator relaxation**: Allow empty references for exploit proposals in round 1 (auto-convert to explore)
2. **Prompt enhancement**: Add JSON schema examples and explicit round-1 markers
3. **Code-level enforcement**: Force `explorationType=explore` in round 1 before validation
4. **Model evaluation**: Assess instruction-following capability across different LLM providers

issue:894.body:
## 背景

当前 ScienceDiscovery 的 Desktop 与 Web 客户端在工作区视图、对话交互、会话与产物管理、设置以及全局辅助能力方面存在一定差异。为便于评估桌面端功能补齐范围，现基于前端实现对差异进行集中梳理，并为后续需求拆分和验收提供参考。

**关联：#718**（`v0.4.0-rc1` 版本需求与发布计划）。其中“桌面端支持科学记忆、Evolve”和“评估旧 UI 功能迁移”等事项与本 Issue 直接相关。

> **说明**
> - 本文是基于当前代码和界面实现的**初步差异盘点**，并非全部条目的最终功能验收结论；具体表现仍需结合实际版本验证。
> - Desktop 并非 Web 的简单复制：它已有独立的 `SetupWizard` / `Guide` 初始化引导、`shell-bridge` 和面板组织方式。因此目标是评估并补齐关键能力，而非机械地复刻 Web UI。
> - 本 Issue 用于**集中跟踪差异与讨论优先级**；不表示所列功能均已纳入 `v0.4.0-rc1` 交付范围。建议在 #718 的评审中明确具体范围。

## 一、右侧工作区与探索视图

Web 右侧面板包含多种专项视图；Desktop 的 `WorkspacePanel` 当前主要开放 `artifacts` 和 `files` 两个 group。

| 功能 | Web 端现有能力 / 实现线索 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Evolve 进化搜索** | `evolve/*`：算法选择、搜索网格/图、候选详情、评分图表、运行卡片及轮询 | **缺失**对应专项视图 |
| **Memory Graph 记忆图** | `MemoryGraphView.tsx`、`MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx`、`MemoryGraphCanvas.tsx` 等 | 存在 API 类型声明，**缺少 UI** |
| **Idea Tree 思路树** | `IdeaTreeView.tsx`、`IdeaTreeCanvas.tsx`、`IdeaTreeExplorer.tsx` 等 | 存在 API 类型声明，**缺少 UI** |
| **CSV 可视化工作台** | `csv-artifact/*`：散点图、直方图、箱线图等 | **部分实现**：主要提供基础表格展示 |
| **执行视图** | 展示 Subagent 执行情况 | **缺少对应视图** |
| **审查专家视图** | 审查专家相关 UI | **缺少对应视图**，具体交互需进一步核对 |

## 二、对话交互与执行过程展示

| 功能 | Web 端现有能力 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **对话输入区** | 选择专家、数据连接器、权限审查模式及自动审查配置；Agent 执行期间可继续发送指令 | **部分实现**：缺少连接器与自动审查等入口，执行期间不能继续发送指令；Desktop 另外支持添加文件 |
| **思考 / 行动步骤展示** | 工具失败时可复制关键诊断信息并快捷跳转 GitHub Issue；最终答案尾部展示产物；Subagent 运行状态有更丰富的 UI | **部分缺失**，建议逐项核对并补齐交互 |
| **轨迹模式** | 提供区别于常规对话的 Agent 行动轨迹视图 | **缺失** |

## 三、会话、项目与产物管理

| 功能 | Web 端现有能力 / 实现线索 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **会话管理** | 重命名、删除、会话级设置、归档、筛选 | 缺少会话级设置、归档及筛选 |
| **项目管理** | 重命名、删除、项目级设置 | 缺少项目级设置 |
| **产物 / 文件下载** | 支持选择多个目标进行下载 | 主要支持单文件下载，批量选择能力不足 |
| **工作区文件来源** | `WorkspaceFileProvenanceModal.tsx` | 缺少文件来源查看 UI |
| **产物树 / 工作区文件树** | `artifactTree.ts` 支持产物树组织 | Desktop 有独立的 `file-tree.ts`，但主要覆盖文件列表，未提供对应的产物树结构 |

## 四、设置与能力管理

| 功能 | Web 端现有能力 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **全局默认配置** | 运行时默认值、可选扩展、连接器、Web 访问等 | 缺少对应的完整配置入口 |
| **Runner 管理** | 本地 Runner 状态、远程 Runner 添加 / 管理 | 有 `RemoteHosts` 配置，但缺少完整 Remote Jobs 面板及本地 Runner 状态展示 |
| **模型与扩展能力** | Model、MCP、Web、Memory、Idea Tree、Skill、Specialist 等 | **部分实现**：MCP 主要为内置能力，缺少自定义添加；Skill 有基础添加方式，但缺少 Web 端更完整的管理、探索及导入流程；Web、Memory、Idea Tree 等配置入口缺失 |
| **运行与资源** | 超时、配额、运行状态 | 缺少配额及运行状态等配置 / 查看入口 |
| **网络与访问** | 网络代理、沙箱网络、权限、前后端连接配置 | 主要提供沙箱网络配置，选项相对受限；部分连接设置属于 Web 架构特有能力，**不必直接迁移** |

## 五、其他全局能力

| 功能 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- |
| **全局搜索** | 缺少对应入口 / 能力 |
| **模型用量** | 缺少用量查看入口 / 能力 |

## 六、建议的处理方式与优先级

建议按业务价值、实现依赖及平台适配成本拆分，而非一次性迁移所有界面：

1. **优先评估版本明确提出的核心能力**：Memory Graph / 科学记忆、Evolve，以及与 #718 相关的旧 UI 迁移范围。论文复现虽在 #718 中列出，但不在本次差异表的核对范围，建议另行确认。
2. **评估影响核心使用流程的功能差异**：执行期间追加指令、执行 / 轨迹展示、工具失败诊断、产物管理及会话 / 项目设置。
3. **逐步补齐探索与管理能力**：Idea Tree、CSV 可视化、MCP / Skill 管理、用量及全局搜索等；优先级需结合需求评审确定。
4. **区分跨端通用能力与平台特有能力**：复用可共享的状态管理和组件逻辑；Desktop 已具备的初始化引导、Shell 桥接及平台特定设置应予保留。

## 七、后续待办 / 验收检查

- [ ] 逐项复核上述差异在目标分支和实际 Desktop 构建中的表现，标记“缺失 / 部分实现 / 已有替代实现 / 不适用”
- [ ] 对照 #718 确定 `v0.4.0-rc1` 的实际交付范围，避免将全部差异默认纳入 RC1
- [ ] 为确认需要补齐的功能明确负责人、依赖、实现方案及独立验收标准
- [ ] 优先验证 Memory Graph、Evolve 及核心对话 / 工作区流程
- [ ] 检查 Desktop 特有能力是否受到迁移影响，避免简单复制 Web 造成回归
- [ ] 对较大的独立功能拆分子 Issue / PR，并在此维护链接及进度

---

**预期结果**：形成可核验的 Desktop / Web 功能差异清单，并将确定需要补齐的能力转化为有优先级、有验收标准的实施任务。

issue:896.body:
Related to #852 (analogous Desktop MCP settings semantics) and #718 (v0.4.0-rc1 settings consistency and module scope tracking).

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed, as confirmed by the reporter.
- [x] Environment details, reproduction steps, and the boundary between reporter observations and source inspection are provided below.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Desktop **System settings → Skills** exposes individual switches and **Enable all / Disable all**. These controls are intended to manage **global Skill enablement across projects and ordinary conversations**. Instead, the implementation reads and writes the currently active project's Skill selection.

The reporter tested the behavior and confirmed that JiuwenSwarm does not honor the project-level Skill selection. This bug remains unfixed. Desktop writes the wrong configuration scope, and its switches do not provide the intended global control over the Skills used by ordinary conversations.

This is scoped as a **Desktop bug**. Correcting Web's overall Skill management design is not a prerequisite for this issue. However, Desktop must use a coherent backend authority that JiuwenSwarm actually obeys, rather than introduce another disconnected switch.

#### Minimal reproduction

1. Run Desktop with the JiuwenSwarm executor and at least one installed ScienceDiscovery Skill.
2. Select project A and open **System settings → Skills**.
3. Disable an individual Skill, or select **Disable all**.
4. Inspect the saved settings: Desktop updates project A's `skillSelectionMode: "selected"` and `enabledSkillIds`, rather than a global enablement setting.
5. Switch to project B and inspect its Skill state. A system-wide control should not depend on which project was active when it was changed.
6. Start a new ordinary conversation/task and request an operation that requires the disabled Skill. Inspect actual Skill discovery/loading (`skill_tool` / `read_skill`), rather than judging only from the model's answer. The reporter confirmed that JiuwenSwarm ignores the project-level selection. Capture Skill-loading evidence when validating the fix.

Actual: the Desktop controls save project selection instead of global enablement, and JiuwenSwarm does not honor that selection in the reporter's test. The UI does not explain that scope or distinguish the selected list from the executor's own enablement state.

Expected: Desktop's system-level Skill switches control global enablement. Disabling a Skill must prevent newly started ordinary tasks from loading that Skill, regardless of the active project; enabling it restores availability. Availability does not mean every message must automatically execute the Skill.

#### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Individual and bulk switches read/write one authoritative global Skill enablement state. They must not silently modify the active project's selection.
- [ ] The same states are shown after changing projects or reopening settings, and a project need not be active to operate a global control.
- [ ] JiuwenSwarm's effective Skill availability respects the global switches for newly started tasks. A later task must not silently restore a globally disabled Skill through project selection or import/reconciliation.
- [ ] Verify disable, re-enable, and bulk disable across two projects through supported Desktop entry points and actual executor Skill-loading evidence. Include an ordinary conversation without an explicitly attached specialist. Test relevant specialist/subagent paths so they cannot bypass a Skill's global prohibition.
- [ ] Clearly define whether JiuwenSwarm-native builtin Skills are included. If excluded, label the bulk action's scope explicitly; do not imply that disabling the ScienceDiscovery catalog disables every executor Skill.
- [ ] Explain the default enabled set, the treatment of newly installed Skills, and when changes take effect. Keep installed, enabled, loaded, and executed states distinct; do not promise live reconfiguration of an existing task.
- [ ] Avoid competing global/project/executor switches overwriting each other. If project/session selection remains supported, it must operate within global enablement rather than override a global disable.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Reporter scenario: Desktop with JiuwenSwarm handling Skills. Exact Desktop build/OS and runtime flags were not supplied in this conversation.
- Source-inspection environment: Linux/WSL2 x86_64; previously recorded Node.js `v22.19.0`, pnpm `11.1.2`.
- No matching local running API/stack process was found during investigation, so the reporter's executor mode and exact settings were not independently inspected.
- No fresh native Desktop/browser reproduction or automated test run was performed for this report. This is not claimed as a Windows/macOS-only failure.
- No exception/stack trace was supplied; the issue concerns setting scope and execution behavior.

### Additional Information

#### Source evidence and investigation boundaries

- [Desktop Skills settings](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d/apps/desktop/src/views/settings/SkillsSettings.tsx): loads `getProjectSettings(activeProjectId)` and routes individual/bulk actions through `setEnabledSkills(client, activeProjectId, ...)`.
- [Desktop settings API](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d/apps/desktop/src/api/settings.ts): `setEnabledSkills` writes project settings with `skillSelectionMode: "selected"`. Bulk enable pins the current installed list; it is not the dynamic `all` mode.
- [Store settings resolution](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d/services/api/src/store.ts): global Skill-selection fields are currently skipped. Merely moving Desktop's existing write to `/api/settings` would not complete the fix.
- [Desktop stack startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d/scripts/start-stack.mjs): defaults `SCIENCE_AGENT_SKILL_SELECTION` to `desktop`.
- [JiuwenSwarm Skill installation](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts) and [reconciliation](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-skills.ts): the Desktop-selection mode aligns shared executor switches at task startup, skips JiuwenSwarm `builtin` Skills, and logs reconciliation failures instead of failing the task. This is an investigation lead, not proof of the reporter's exact runtime cause.

Web's JiuwenSwarm controls and Desktop's project selection currently target different state. This explains why comparing the two interfaces alone cannot establish effective enablement. The primary requested correction remains Desktop global semantics and executor enforcement.

The project currently has no product users requiring settings migration; migration is outside the requested scope. This issue is separate from the MCP correction in #852 and does not add MCP tool-level controls to its scope.

### Version Information

- Source inspected: `f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d`.
- Exact reporter binary/build: not supplied.
- Status: confirmed by the reporter and still unfixed. Source findings and reporter runtime observations are identified separately above.

issue:897.body:
Follow-up work for #834 (`feat(sizeopt): slim the Windows installer 797.6 -> ~578.0 MiB, merge 6 envs into 2`). That PR's code is reviewed; this issue carries the parts deliberately left out of it, so they are not only recorded in a review thread.

## 1. Real-machine smoke (the minimum the maintainer asked for)

The full matrix (three install-root lengths timed, bilingual screenshots, 30–60 s recording) was reduced to one smoke pass:

- [ ] One clean Windows machine: install → first launch, with a first-launch timing next to the f26 baseline.
- [ ] Actually trigger the over-long install-root refusal (`win_desktop/build/installer.nsh:306-339`): what the dialog says, and whether choosing "No" really aborts the install instead of continuing into `InstFiles`.
- [ ] One pass through each side of the uninstall "also delete user data" branch (`installer.nsh:541`).

Screenshots or a short written record are enough.

## 2. First-run bytecode completeness

`treeHasPycache` (`win_desktop/src/bootstrap.ts:230-251`) skips the first-run `compileall` as soon as one `__pycache__` directory holds one `.pyc` (`:243`). At the default install root that compile is not runnable anyway — `63 + 1 + 192 + 14 > 259` — so a complete shipped `.pyc` set is load-bearing, and the only place that dependency is written down is the A5 advisory (`assemble-backend.mjs:990-996`), which exists only on the build machine.

- [ ] Write a manifest or count of the precompiled set at assemble time and check it at bootstrap, so an incomplete set (quarantined file, partial copy, interrupted unpack) fails the build or names itself at first launch instead of surfacing as an `ImportError` at first tool use.

## 3. Smaller items raised in review

- [ ] `win_desktop/scripts/after-pack-trim-locales.cjs` hardening (see the #834 review threads for the specific asks).
- [ ] Stale documentation references to the removed per-service `services/<member>/uv.lock` files.

## Not in scope here

- The `uv sync` SIGTERM defect in `scripts/start-stack.mjs` stays in #834: it is a reproducible bug on the current head, not follow-up work.
- The patch-0019 wording in #834's description has been corrected and is accurate on the current head.

issue:898.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

When the model connection is reset after the model has already streamed part of its answer, the agent run fails. No layer retries it.

That is what ended three research jobs in the manual Nightly run [41852669139](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41852669139) on 2026-11-04 (branch `ci/l5-biomnibench-da`, head `b8819fc8b`, JiuwenSwarm backend, model `deepseek-flash` behind an OpenAI-compatible relay gateway).

### What failed

`research-1` (DRB-58) and `research-5` (DRB-75) both ended with:

```
run_error=[181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

The `[model-sse-summary]` lines in each job's `stack.log` (artifact `real-e2e-evidence-<shard>`) identify the request:

| Job | Request sent (UTC) | 200 headers | Connection reset | Streamed before reset | Attempts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| research-1 | 15:00:19.235 | 15:00:23.403 | **15:01:46.872** | 83 s, 848,494 bytes, text and tool calls | 1 |
| research-5 | 16:00:31.110 | 16:00:36.449 | **16:03:30.928** | 175 s, 2,791,403 bytes, text and tool calls | 1 |

`research-10` failed in the same way. Its run error reads `interaction round execution failed`, and each of its three failed runs directly follows a mid-stream reset (16:26:31.901, 16:31:37.391 and 16:49:24.951).

### The fault is external; the failure is ours

- 16 of the run's 382 requests to the gateway ended with `error.classification: network`. They came from 5 independent runners, and all of them fall between 15:01 and 16:50 UTC.
- The same gateway served 1,386 requests in the two earlier runs on this branch (03:07–06:38 and 10:09–12:50 UTC) without a single network reset.
- Streams of 176 s / 2.9 MB and 214 s / 2.8 MB completed normally in the same run, so a fixed size or duration limit is not the cause.
- 9 of the 16 resets were retried and recovered. They all came before any answer text or tool-call delta: either before the response opened, or while only reasoning had streamed. The head under test (PR #853) retries the second case.
- The other 7 happened after answer text or tool-call deltas had started. Nothing retried them. Every run failure in research-1, research-5 and research-10 follows one of these 7.

### Retry behaviour on `main` (`48848578`)

On the JiuwenSwarm backend, a model call travels Swarm → ScienceDiscovery model gateway (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`) → `packages/model/src/client.ts` → provider.

| Layer | What it retries | After the stream has started |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/model` `requestWithRetry` | Connect errors, header timeout, 429 and 5xx. Budget: `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_RETRIES=2`. Backoff: 0.5 s doubling up to 4 s, or a numeric `Retry-After`. Header timeout: `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600` | Nothing. The code says so: "Once the stream starts flowing, errors surface to the caller". `bodyTimeout: 0` also means a stalled body is never treated as lost |
| JiuwenSwarm model gateway | Nothing of its own. It holds response headers until the first answer byte, so a failure before the stream opens reaches Swarm as a real HTTP error | Forwards the error |
| Swarm's OpenAI SDK | Its built-in retries before a response arrives | Nothing |
| openJiuwen `agent_teams` `StreamController` | — | Re-drives a team member's round that failed with `181001`: up to 10 times, with a "continue" query. The main session run is not covered: research-1 and research-5 logged `run of <session> failed: [181001]` straight after the reset |
| Run | Nothing. `classifyRunFailure` maps ECONNRESET to `transport-error`, which is only displayed and recorded | — |

PR #853 adds one more retry in `streamModelTurn`: `network` and `timeout` errors are retried while `answerStarted` is still false. It cannot cover the 7 resets that came after output had started.

One safety property already holds. The gateway withholds tool-call arguments until the upstream turn finishes; in the meantime it sends empty deltas as progress. A stream cut mid-turn therefore never executes a partial tool call, so re-driving the failed turn cannot repeat a side effect. Text and reasoning deltas, on the other hand, are forwarded as they arrive. That is why the transport layer cannot replay the request transparently once text has started.

### How other agents handle a mid-stream drop

All rows except the DeepSeek API docs were read from current sources.

| Agent | Mid-stream drop | Budget and backoff | Partial output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) | Retries stream disconnects, connection failures, timeouts, 5xx and 429. A stream idle for `stream_idle_timeout_ms` (default 300000) counts as lost | `stream_max_retries` 5 and `request_max_retries` 4. Exponential backoff with jitter; server retry advice wins. After the budget runs out it falls back from WebSocket to HTTPS | Only items completed with `output_item.done` enter history. The retry re-samples from history: the partial item is dropped, completed tool calls are kept |
| [Grok Build](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build) | `StreamError` and `EventStreamError` are retried; `IdleTimeout` is not | 15 retries (`GROK_MAX_RETRIES`). 2 s doubling to 30 s, ±20% jitter. The first retry rebuilds the HTTP client; rate limits are retried once | The same request is re-sampled and the failed attempt is discarded |
| [pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) | Restarts the whole turn at the agent level, matching the error text (`terminated`, `socket hang up`, `other side closed`, `stream ended…`) | 3 retries, 2/4/8 s, capped at 60 s. Shows `Retrying (n/3)` and can be cancelled | The failed assistant message stays in the raw log but is hidden from the model; the agent continues from the previous message |
| [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) | Retries mid-stream errors, including `ECONNRESET` and `ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE` | 3 retries, 1/2/4 s. Failures before the stream opens have a separate policy (5 s up to 30 s) | Emits a `RETRY` event and resends the request |
| [DeepSeek API docs](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/rate_limit) | No agent. 500 and 503: "retry your request after a brief wait". Waiting streams receive `: keep-alive` comments, and the connection is closed if inference has not started within 10 minutes | — | No guidance on mid-stream drops |
| [DeepSeek-TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI) (third-party) | Retries only a stream that failed to open. A drop while reading the body is reported and not replayed, to avoid duplicated output | — | — |

The common pattern: retry at the turn, not at the HTTP request. Output counts only once an item or turn completes. On failure, the partial attempt is discarded and the turn is re-sampled from the last committed state, with a bounded, jittered backoff and a visible status.

## Design Ideas

1. **Re-drive the main run's failed turn on a transient transport fault.** This covers a `181001` caused by a network or stream error, or `transport-error`. Drop the failed round from the model's context and continue from the last committed round. openJiuwen already does this for team members, and pi does it for every turn. Budget 3–5 attempts with jittered exponential backoff capped at 30–60 s, honour cancellation, and show a retry status in the run timeline. Still to decide: whether this lives in the JiuwenSwarm patch set or in `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`. The native loop needs the same behaviour.
2. **Treat a stalled stream as lost.** Add an idle timeout on the response body (Codex uses 5 minutes), so a hung stream enters the same recovery instead of waiting forever.
3. **Use a fresh connection on the first retry**, as Grok Build does, so a reset does not reuse a broken pooled connection.
4. **Keep non-transient errors out:** authentication, quota, context-overflow, invalid-request and content-policy errors stay non-retryable.

Alternative, for comparison only: buffer text in the gateway as it already buffers tool calls, so the transport layer can replay the whole upstream request transparently. This would remove live text streaming on the Swarm path.

## Involved Public APIs

This may add settings for the turn retry budget and backoff and for the stream idle timeout, next to `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_RETRIES`. It may also add a run-timeline event for "retrying after a dropped model stream". No change to existing request or session APIs is expected.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `packages/model/src/client.ts`: retry policy, idle timeout, and the `retryErrors` wire diagnostics.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`, `jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`, the JiuwenSwarm patches, and the native loop.
- Web run timeline: the retry status, and partial text that a retry replaces.
- CI accounting (related to #813): `test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs` does not count these failures as provider faults; the run's verdict shows `provider faults 0`. The error text carries no 5xx status, and `PRODUCT_REPORT` (`main run must complete`, `delivery_status`) vetoes it in any case.
- PR #853: the retry it adds for interruptions during the reasoning phase.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- UT for `packages/model` and the gateway: a fake upstream returns 200, streams text and tool-call deltas, then resets the socket. Assert that the turn is re-driven within the budget, that no tool call from the cut attempt executes, and that exhaustion still fails with the original error and wire diagnostics.
- UT: a fake upstream stops sending bytes mid-stream. Assert that the idle timeout classifies the stream as lost and retries it.
- UT: 401/403, quota, context-overflow and invalid-request errors are not retried.
- Mocked E2E: the stub model resets the stream after some answer text. The run completes, the timeline shows the retry, and the answer text is not duplicated.
- Real nightly: wherever `[model-sse-summary]` shows a mid-stream `network` reset, a completed turn follows instead of a failed run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A stream reset after answer text or tool-call deltas have started no longer ends the main run while retry budget remains; the run continues from the last committed turn.
- [ ] No tool call from the interrupted attempt executes, and no completed tool call runs twice.
- [ ] The retry is visible in the run timeline and can be cancelled. When the budget is exhausted, the run fails with the original provider error preserved.
- [ ] Authentication, quota, context-overflow and invalid-request errors are not retried.
- [ ] The JiuwenSwarm and native backends behave the same.
- [ ] A test covering the mid-stream reset fails on current `main` and passes with the change.
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1` and `pnpm test:shared`.

## Additional Information

The other failures in run 41852669139 are outside this issue; they come from the head under test, not from the provider:

- `research-6`: none of the 16 evolve expansions produced a runnable candidate. The most common reason logged was that the 16000-token per-call cap was spent on reasoning.
- The mocked `standard-journeys` and `standard-config` workers: the head buffers reasoning deltas until answer text or a tool call starts.

The main scheduled Nightly that day ([41919338127](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41919338127), `main` `48848578`, provider called directly) passed, with no network reset in 826 requests.

issue:899.body:
## Summary

When the agent calls `ask_user` (for example, the `science-research-team` skill's coarse intent parsing asks the user to pick an analysis goal), the gateway treats the resulting user-input wait as a stall. With no answer within 240 s, the run is failed with:

```
Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms
```

A legitimate "waiting for the user" state should not be subject to the idle-progress watchdog, or should enter a distinct recoverable `waiting`/`blocked` state instead of `failed`.

## Reproduction

1. Start the local stack: `scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local`.
2. Register a working model and make it the default task model.
3. Create a project/session (approvalMode `always_allow`) and upload a CSV to the workspace.
4. Send a deliberately under-specified data-analysis prompt (no analysis goal):
   > 用science-research-team skill去帮我执行一个数据分析任务，需要用的数据是subspace_score_table.csv。
5. The main agent parses intent and calls `ask_user` with a 4-option clarification card ("本次数据分析的目标是什么？…").
6. Leave the question unanswered. After ~240 s the run fails with the stall error.

## Observed behaviour

- `ask_user` tool call at 11:04:47 (local) with a 4-option clarification question.
- No further gateway progress for 240 s (nobody answers in a headless/automated run).
- Run reaches `failed` with `Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms` (errorCode `timeout`).

Run evidence (local reproduction):

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Session ID | `a8bd3422-0ef1-4e14-a327-0a8a4b18982a` |
| Run ID | `f8b1b2d7-8f97-4744-9680-7d7ca3bf6496` |
| Final status | `failed` |
| Terminal error | `Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms` |

## Expected behaviour

`ask_user` (and the mapped approval / `requestApproval` user-input waits) should suspend or greatly extend the idle watchdog, and ideally surface a `waiting_for_user` / `blocked`-style state that can be resumed when the user answers — not `failed`.

## Environment

- ScienceDiscovery local stack on WSL2 (Ubuntu), JiuwenSwarm backend.
- Model: glm-5.3-flash via an OpenAI-compatible gateway (yibuapi.com/v1).
- Reproduced headlessly by driving `/api/sessions/{id}/messages` and polling `/runs`.

## Relates to

- #819 — same 240 s idle watchdog, different trigger (a hanging `todo_create`). This issue is the complementary case where "no progress" is *expected* because the run is waiting on the user.

issue:900.body:
## Summary

Registering a GLM (or other OpenAI-compatible) model with `apiVariant: "deepseek"` makes the runtime inject thinking-control parameters (`enable_thinking`, `reasoning`, `thinking.type`) into model requests. Some OpenAI-compatible gateways reject these with 400:

```
BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'Unsupported gateway parameters: enable_thinking, reasoning', 'type': 'model_gateway_error'}}
```

and separately, for the image-modality warmup probe:

```
BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'images are not supported by this gateway', 'type': 'model_gateway_error'}}
```

Main text/chat completions still succeed, but the housekeeping image probe fails on every start, leaving `image_input=unknown`.

## Reproduction

1. Register a model via `POST /api/models` with `apiProtocol: "openai-chat-completions"`, `apiVariant: "deepseek"`, and a GLM OpenAI-compatible `baseUrl`.
2. Start the stack and watch the JiuwenSwarm llm log for the image warmup probe ("What color is this image? Reply with one word.").

## Observed behaviour

- `llm_call_error … BadRequestError: 400 - Unsupported gateway parameters: enable_thinking, reasoning`
- `llm_call_error … images are not supported by this gateway`
- Warmup records `image_input=unknown (not cached)`.

## Expected behaviour

- Thinking-control params should only be injected for dialects/gateways that accept them, or a gateway rejection of those extra params should be tolerated rather than erroring the warmup.
- An "images not supported" rejection should be recorded cleanly as "image input not supported", not surfaced as a repeated 400 error.

## Environment

- ScienceDiscovery local stack on WSL2 (Ubuntu), JiuwenSwarm backend.
- Model: glm-5.3-flash, baseUrl `https://yibuapi.com/v1`, apiVariant `deepseek`.
- Main chat completion works (greeting + idea-tree runs succeeded); only the image probe is affected.

issue:903.body:
**Update:** `D1` is fixed inside `#890` itself at `fdb835fb6664acb85e77c2f64c1b3ebfb7fdb7ff` (red first in `ddd14462`; the stem is now cut at the first colon as well as the first dot, so `nul:stream` resolves to `nul` and `con:$DATA` to `con`, with `conin$`/`conout$` and trailing dot/space stripping unchanged). This issue therefore tracks `D2` only — the POSIX-side segment split where `CON\notes.txt` stays one segment and is accepted.

## Summary

`#890` adds a Windows-reserved-device-name guard to the session file write path — `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` in `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` plus a per-segment check in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`. It refuses `CON/notes.txt`, `nul.dir/x.csv` and `notes/CON.txt`.

**Residual coverage gap.** After `#890` (with `D1` fixed there), the input below is still accepted:

| Input | Predicate result at `#890`'s head | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CON\notes.txt` (POSIX host) | `false` | creates a file literally named `CON\notes.txt`; the same request is refused on a Windows host |

Both were raised as `medium, suggestion` review threads on `#890` (`F1` at `workspace.ts:479`, `F2` at `http/index.ts:3815`) and are tracked here instead of being fixed there. Expected behaviour for all of them: **`400`, naming the offending segment**, exactly as `CON/notes.txt` is answered today.

## D1 — `nul:stream` / `con:$DATA`: the stem keeps the colon, so the predicate misses the device

- **Where:** `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts:478-481` (predicate added by `#890`).
- **Cause:** the stem is everything before the first dot, so `nul:stream` keeps its colon, `WINDOWS_RESERVED_DEVICE_NAME` does not match it, and the predicate returns `false`. Windows resolves `nul:stream` as the `NUL` device plus the named stream `stream`, so the write does not create a file there.
- **Measured at `#890`'s head:** `"CON" → true`, `"nul.txt" → true`, `"nul.dir" → true`, but `"nul:stream" → false` and `"con:$DATA" → false`.
- **Failing input:** `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` with `{"path":"nul:stream"}` or `{"path":"con:$DATA"}`.
- **Observed:** on POSIX the route answers `201` and creates a file Windows cannot open; on Windows the write targets the device.
- **Expected:** `400`, naming the offending segment.
- **Suggested fix:** split the stem on `:` as well as `.` — for example `name.split(/[.:]/)[0]?.replace(/[. ]+$/, "")` — and add `nul:stream` / `con:$DATA` cases next to the existing ones. `conin$` / `conout$` do not contain a colon and must keep matching.

## D2 — `CON\notes.txt`: the segment walk splits on the host separator only

- **Where:** `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3815`.
- **Cause:** `relative(workspaceRoot, target).split(sep)` splits on `/` on Linux, so `CON\notes.txt` stays one segment, the stem reads `CON\notes`, and the predicate allows it — while the predicate and the route comment both claim the rule is platform-independent.
- **Failing input:** `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` with `{"path":"CON\\notes.txt"}` against a Linux server.
- **Observed:** `201` and a workspace file literally named `CON\notes.txt`; the same request is refused on a Windows host, so the answer depends on which platform serves it.
- **Expected:** refused on every host, with a test case alongside the existing `CON/notes.txt` one.
- **Suggested fix:** split on both separators (`relative(...).split(/[\\/]+/)`) and/or refuse `\` inside a segment.

## D3 — the duplicate private predicate in the upload path

- **Where:** `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts` (the upload path keeps its own private copy of the reserved-device-name check, wider in two respects: it recognises the named-stream form `NUL:anything` and superscript ports `[1-9¹²³]`).
- **Cause:** the same rule now lives in two places, so a later change to one does not reach the other — exactly how `D1` slipped past the shared predicate.
- **Expected:** after `#890` lands, the upload path imports `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` from `@sciencediscovery/workspace` instead of keeping a private copy (`workspace-upload.ts:19` already imports that package, so this is a one-line change plus deleting the local copy), and its tests keep covering the stream form and superscript ports through the shared predicate.
- **Why it belongs here and not in a new issue:** same family as `D2` — device-name detection precision and de-duplication — and it is one line of code once `#890` is on `main`.

## Acceptance

- All four inputs (`nul:stream`, `con:$DATA`, `CON\notes.txt`, and `notes\CON.txt`) answer `400` with the offending segment named.
- The `WSP-005` cases added by `#890` stay green.
- The guard's claim of being platform-independent holds on Linux and Windows.
- Any documentation or reply describing the guard must say **partial coverage** until this lands: `nul:stream`, `con:$DATA` and POSIX-side `CON\notes.txt` remain accepted.

issue:909.body:
## Summary

`ST` fails on a clean `main` because the pinned Python runtime is fetched from `astral-sh/python-build-standalone` and that download either answers `504` or streams at 9–31 KB/s, far past the 5-minute `execFile` cap in the test. It fails before any code under test runs, so it is not attributable to the PR whose run turns red — but it does turn `merge-gate` red, which is the one required check in this repository, so it blocks merges.

Current instance: `#678` (tip `5ad9b21b6aeb5d7f30556de8ddafc07d1246d85e`) is approved and otherwise green except `ST`.

## Where

- Test: `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts::a user initializes the pinned release into an empty installation and completes a real Evolve task@linux/amd64`
- Downloader: `scripts/binary-release/fetch-runtime.mjs`
- Asset: `https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/releases/download/20260805/cpython-3.12.13+20260805-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-install_only_stripped.tar.gz` — `34,184,519` bytes

## CI evidence

Run [`41999191976`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41999191976), job `ST` `127150383484` (`2026-11-05T09:04:19Z` → `09:09:17Z`): `{"status":"FAIL","planned":51,"executed":51,"passed":50,"failed":1}`, the only red identity is the test above, first line:

```
Download failed (504): https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/releases/download/20260805/cpython-3.12.13+20260805-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-install_only_stripped.tar.gz
```

## Control: the same case on a clean `main`

`main` at `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673`, tracked tree clean, dependencies installed and built the same way, no branch of `#678` present:

- `node scripts/binary-release/fetch-runtime.mjs --runtime python --arch x86_64 --output … --cache …` → **exit 124** (killed at a 300 s cap; it had written 0 bytes to disk, because the script reads the whole archive into memory before writing).
- `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "pinned release" test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` → **exit 1** after **301 s** (`duration_ms: 300128`), i.e. it hit the same `execFile` 5-minute cap with the same command and the same URL.

So the same case fails on `main` without the change under review.

## Observed throughput for that asset

| Reading | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `curl -sI` (same URL) | `HTTP/2 302` |
| `curl -sL -r 0-1048575` (1 MiB range) | `206`, `1,048,576` bytes in `33.48 s` → `31,322 B/s` |
| `curl -L` (full, 45 s cap) | `200`, `818,498` of `34,184,519` bytes in `45 s` → `18,185 B/s` |
| bare `node fetch` | `status 200` in `1.1 s`, then 0 bytes for 60 s before abort |
| independent samples of the same URL, three machines | `9,445` / `25,735` / `18,312` B/s |

At `9–31 KB/s` the `34 MB` asset needs roughly **18 to 60 minutes**, while the test allows 5.

## It is not deterministic

Fifteen minutes before the red run, the same case passed in merge-group run [`41997396390`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41997396390) (`2026-11-05T08:52:58Z` → `08:53:41Z`, `42.6 s`). `main`'s own `ST` was green in run [`41997392457`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41997392457) (`08:52Z`). So the failure tracks the download path degrading, not a fixed defect in the test.

## Why this is worth a fix rather than a retry

`merge-gate` is the only required status check here, and `ST` is one of the jobs it aggregates, so any PR can be blocked for a reason that has nothing to do with its diff, and a re-run only helps if the CDN happens to recover. Retries also cost a full `ST` cycle (≈5 minutes each time) and cannot be triggered by contributors: `POST /actions/jobs/{id}/rerun` and `POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` both answer `403 Must have admin rights to Repository` for a non-member token.

## Options, in the order we would pick them

1. **Cache the pinned runtime between runs** (keyed by the asset version), so the network is used once per version instead of on every `ST` run.
2. **Verify against a mirror first** and fall back to the GitHub release, or honour `fetch-runtime.mjs`'s resume/cache path when a partial download exists instead of restarting from byte 0.
3. **Fail fast and name the cause**: if the download cannot reach a minimum rate within N seconds, fail with a message that says "external asset download too slow", so the red check is self-explanatory.
4. If none of the above is wanted now, an explicit **retry/exemption policy for `ST` on this identity** would at least stop it blocking unrelated PRs.

If the project prefers that this be reported differently, say so and we will follow that shape instead.

issue:910.body:
## Summary

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts` gives its fault injection a wall-clock budget of about `200 ms` (`200` iterations at `1 ms`). On a busy runner that budget is exhausted before the injected fault lands, the case fails with `Timed out waiting for local fault injection`, and because `UT` is one of the jobs `merge-gate` aggregates, an unrelated pull request turns red on the only required status check in this repository.

Two pull requests were hit by the same identity in two different time windows today, and the same file passes in a normal run.

## Failing identity

```text
packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts::parallel 429 callers share cooldown, drain their queue and do not retry inside one slot@linux/amd64
message: "Timed out waiting for local fault injection"
```

## Evidence

**Hit 1 — `#872`**, `UT` job `126735548839`, run [`41875320473`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41875320473), read from the job's uploaded `ut-results` artifact (`group-227/worker-1-events.jsonl`; the job log itself only carries `Run`/`Done` lines). Group summary `planned 16 / executed 16 / passed 15 / failed 1`; whole layer `planned 6279 / executed 6279 / passed 6278 / failed 1`.

**Hit 2 — `#878`**, `UT` job `126741018427`, same identity, another window.

**Control — the same file passing**, `UT` job `126822084143` (`2026-11-04T19:54:21Z`): `Run 229/555: packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts (16)` → `Done (6210ms)`, layer `{"status":"PASS","planned":6281,"passed":6281,"failed":0}`.

Neither pull request touches `packages/data-source`: `#872` changes four files under `apps/web`, `#878` changes `apps/web` only. So the failing identity is unreachable from either diff.

## Cause

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts:98-101` polls for the first of 12 concurrent callers to observe the injected fault:

```ts
// ~200 iterations × 1 ms ≈ 200 ms total
```

When the event loop is loaded (parallel `UT` workers, coverage instrumentation), `200 ms` is not enough for the fault to be observed, and the wait falls through to `assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection")`. The product behaviour is correct; the budget is what fails.

## Effect

Any pull request can be blocked by this, and a re-run only helps if the runner happens to be less loaded. Contributors cannot re-run: `POST /actions/jobs/{id}/rerun` and `POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` answer `403 Must have admin rights to Repository` to a non-member token. So the only currently available recovery is asking a maintainer.

## Options

1. **Replace the fixed budget with a deadline** (for example `waitFor` with a `10 s` timeout and a short poll interval), so a loaded runner still passes and a genuinely missing fault still fails quickly enough.
2. **Wait on the event rather than polling** — if the injection can expose a promise or an emitter, awaiting it removes the timing assumption entirely.
3. If the current budget is deliberate, document the expected runner load and treat the red as a known flake; then it should not be able to block `merge-gate` for unrelated changes.

We can prepare option 1 as a pull request if that is the preferred shape; tell us which option you want and we will follow that instead of choosing for you.

issue:911.body:
## Summary

When a research agent writes files to its workspace during a run (e.g. `analysis.py`, `cleaned-data.csv`, SVG figures, `results.json`, helper scripts), those files are **not registered as artifacts** in the project's artifact list (`GET /api/projects/:id/artifacts`). Only files that were explicitly uploaded by the user before the run (e.g. `clinical_trial.csv`) appear as artifacts.

This means the user cannot download, preview, or manage the agent's output files through the artifact panel — they are stranded in the session workspace.

## Observed

During RR-02 (clinical trial re-analysis) on master `9e9d83d5` + WSL2:

- The agent wrote **8 files** to its session workspace:
  - `analysis.py` (41 KB)
  - `cleaned-data.csv` (4.6 KB)
  - `figures/fig1_endpoint_by_group.svg` (14.6 KB)
  - `figures/fig2_baseline_vs_endpoint.svg` (12.8 KB)
  - `figures/fig3_forest_plot.svg` (5.9 KB)
  - `figures/fig4_qq_residuals.svg` (12.9 KB)
  - `results/results.json` (6.1 KB)
  - `scripts/clinical_stats.py` (10.8 KB)

- `GET /api/projects/:id/artifacts` returned only **1 artifact**: `clinical_trial.csv` (the user's pre-run upload).

- The agent's output files were verifiably present in the session workspace (confirmed by direct filesystem access and by re-running `analysis.py` to reproduce identical results).

## Run identifiers

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Run ID | `9e7a4a73-680` (cancelled after 30 min driver timeout, but workspace files were written) |

issue:914.body:
## What happens

`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py::ArchitectureBoundaryTests::test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` can fail with `FileNotFoundError` instead of an assertion, because it walks `services/api` while other tests are writing and deleting their temp workspaces under `services/api/.tmp`.

Observed once on a pull request whose diff does not touch this test, `services/gateway`, or anything that writes `agent-skill-creator-*`:

```
FAILED tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py::ArchitectureBoundaryTests::test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names
  FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
  '.../services/api/.tmp/agent-skill-creator-1793877061398-12103/projects/15036584-.../sessions/f6ab2480-.../skill-snapshots/.716ffbc5-....skill-snapshot/antibody-design/scripts/install_pipeline_deps.sh'
```

- run `42015883088`, `UT` job `127206585414`: `planned 6366 / executed 6366 / passed 6365 / failed 1 / skipped 0`
- the group holding it: `1 failed, 30 passed in 4.55s`; the other 30 are gateway Python tests that ran normally
- the same test set passed on the previous tip of the same branch (run `41890794011`)

## Why

```python
NODE_ROOTS = (REPOSITORY_ROOT / "services" / "api", REPOSITORY_ROOT / "packages", REPOSITORY_ROOT / "apps" / "web", REPOSITORY_ROOT / "test" / "api")
IGNORED_DIRECTORIES = {"__pycache__", "dist", "node_modules"}

def _files(root):
    for path in root.rglob("*"):
        if path.is_file() and not any(part in IGNORED_DIRECTORIES for part in path.parts):
            yield path
```

`services/api/.tmp` is a live runtime workspace root: `services/api/src/server.test.ts` and the skill-creator paths create and remove session trees under it while other workers run. `_files()` lists a path and the test then reads it; when the owning test deletes it in between, the read raises and the whole boundary assertion is lost.

## Impact

Any pull request whose `UT` layer overlaps that window fails a test that has nothing to do with its diff. The cost is a full CI cycle plus a rerun we cannot perform ourselves (`POST /actions/runs/<id>/rerun-failed-jobs` → `403 Must have admin rights to Repository`), so it turns into a maintainer round-trip per hit.

## Proposed fix

1. Add `.tmp` to `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES`: like `dist`, it is generated runtime data, not source.
2. Treat a file that disappears between the listing and the read as gone rather than as a boundary violation (`FileNotFoundError` → skip that path); a source file removed mid-run cannot be asserted anyway.
3. Deterministic regression test: create `services/api/.tmp/probe.ts` containing a forbidden vendor token, run the boundary walk, and assert the walk reports nothing for it (this fails on `main` today, because `.tmp` is not ignored).

Related but distinct: `#872`, `#878` (a different `packages/data-source` timing flake) and `#909` (ST runtime download) — this one is a shared-root walk race, not a timeout.

issue:916.body:
## 问题背景

Windows 直接执行模式提供托管 Bash，但既有的 starter 环境可能没有安装 Agent 调用 `run_shell` 时依赖的常用 Unix 工具（如 `head`、`tail`、`wc`、`sort`、`grep`、`sed`）。同一条命令在不同 Windows 设备或历史安装环境中表现不一致；缺少明确的能力探测和诊断时，Agent 可能反复重试不可用的命令。

此外，Windows 的 `.cmd` / `.bat` 启动入口不能完全按原生可执行文件的方式处理，带空格和特殊字符的参数也需要正确传递。

## 预期行为

- 托管 Windows Bash 明确提供并能解析约定的基础 Unix 工具，不依赖用户机器碰巧安装了 Git Bash。
- 首次创建及历史 starter 环境升级后，工具集合保持一致；升级保留审计记录，重复启动不会无意义地迁移。
- Runner readiness 能暴露实际平台与 Shell 能力，Agent 的工具说明不再假设主机有某个命令。
- 对 Bash 标准的 command-not-found 失败给出准确、有限长度、可操作的诊断；保留原始 stderr，不将所有 exit 127 错误误判为命令缺失。
- 正确启动 Windows `.cmd` / `.bat` shim，且参数中的空格和特殊字符不被意外解释或丢失。

## 建议修复范围

1. 在 Windows 托管 starter 环境中提供 MSYS2 Bash 与必要的 coreutils / grep / sed，配置正确的工具查找路径。
2. 增加托管 Shell 的能力探测及 setup 后的状态刷新。
3. 为持久化 starter 增加按缺失项增量升级和幂等处理。
4. 完善 `run_shell` / `check_runner` 工具说明及缺失命令诊断。
5. 针对 Windows 脚本 shim 的启动与参数传递提供兼容路径。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 新安装 Windows 环境可通过真实 `run_shell` 调用使用约定的基础工具
- [ ] 历史环境可升级且保留原修订，重复启动不产生多余修订
- [ ] Runner 能力探测和 Agent 工具说明反映实际可用能力
- [ ] 缺失命令有准确、可恢复的提示，不破坏 stderr 和其他错误语义
- [ ] `.cmd` / `.bat` 启动及含空格、元字符的参数传递通过测试
- [ ] 相关 Runner / workspace 测试及 Windows 端到端流程验证

## 实现 PR

- #716 — `fix(runner): provide a managed Windows shell toolchain`

关联版本计划：#718（Windows Shell 工具链与能力诊断）。

issue:917.body:
## 问题背景

Agent 工具调用结果直接进入模型上下文时，Shell 执行、环境、文件传输、Skill、MCP 等工具可能返回冗长原始数据、敏感字段或与当前推理无关的内容，导致上下文浪费并增加信息泄露风险。

仅对返回内容做简单截断也不够：MCP 的 `structuredData`、`crossReferences` 等结构化业务数据可能被意外遗漏；真正发生截断后，如果没有可读取的引用，Agent 就无法恢复所需证据，影响后续分析。

## 预期行为

- 模型看到的是有边界、与任务相关的结果摘要，而不是无约束的原始工具输出。
- 敏感凭据、下载源 URL 等不必要信息不进入模型视图或长期保存的审计元数据；合法的下载候选 ID、许可证、归属信息及文件大小等业务字段仍被保留。
- MCP 输出保留 `structuredData`、`crossReferences` 和分析摘要中的有效业务数据，并在限制大小时优先维持可解释性。
- 真实业务数据因截断丢失时，若持久化成功，应返回可通过 `read_tool_output` 获取完整证据的引用；若不可恢复，要明确告知，不能静默假装完整。
- 小结果无需不必要的持久化；深层嵌套、循环引用及存储失败等边界情况应可控。
- arXiv 工具结果提供可用的分页和论文获取路径。

## 建议修复范围

1. 针对 Shell、执行管理、环境、NPU、传输与 Skill 工具定义适用的模型可见结果字段。
2. 对审计元数据中的敏感数据与原始大载荷做防御性清理，并限制递归深度。
3. 为 MCP 结果构造大小受限的投影，覆盖 JSON 文本、结构化记录、交叉引用与分析摘要。
4. 对发生信息损失的结果建立可恢复的 `read_tool_output` 引用与明确的失败回退提示。
5. 在下载、文献检索及 PDF 读取等真实链路中核对关键字段和结果语义。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 工具输出遵守模型上下文大小约束，不包含不必要的敏感字段
- [ ] MCP 结构化结果及交叉引用不被静默丢弃
- [ ] 截断导致业务信息损失时有可读取引用，或明确标识恢复不可用
- [ ] 小结果不产生不必要的证据持久化
- [ ] 深层嵌套、循环引用、存储失败等场景可预测且不泄露原始载荷
- [ ] 下载候选、许可证/来源信息、arXiv 分页及论文获取链路不回归
- [ ] 覆盖相关单元测试与端到端执行 / MCP 场景

## 实现 PR

- #717 — `fix(tools): bound model-facing execution and MCP results`

关联版本计划：#718（工具输出与结果投影优化）。

issue:918.body:
## What

`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:156` (`GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, added by #915) pins only one direction of the walk: both new cases assert that something is **not** reported. Nothing asserts that a violation still **is** reported after the ignore list changed.

## Trigger

`IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` is widened again, or `_files()` is narrowed, so that a real source root (`services/api`, `packages`, `apps/web`, `test/api`) stops being walked. Every current case still passes:

- `test_a_generated_workspace_is_not_walked` and `test_a_workspace_file_removed_after_listing_is_skipped` assert absence only;
- `test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` asserts `failures == []`, which a walk that sees nothing also satisfies.

The boundary test then silently stops policing the Gateway boundary with no red test anywhere.

## Fix

Add the mirror case in `GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, reusing the `mock.patch.object(sys.modules[__name__], "_files", ...)` plumbing already present at `:162`:

- have the patched walk yield a path under `services/api/src` (for example `services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts`) whose content contains a vendor token;
- assert `_node_boundary_failures()` returns that path, as `path: <relative>` or `content: <relative>`.

Three lines in the test file. No production code changes.

## Why it is worth a line

Measured at `f99cc8a24495544988045699b9e5c2429553e332` (review comment on #915): a fabricated `services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts` does produce `['path: services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts']`, and with the pre-change ignore set a probe in `services/api/.tmp` produces `['content: services/api/.tmp/probe-manual-537457.ts']`. The guard works today; only its regression direction is untested.

Found while reviewing #915 and tracked here so the review thread can be closed without losing the gap.

issue:919.body:
**Gap left by PR #892.** PR #892 adds the `cancelled` summary bucket in `apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx:53-58` and one test for it (`apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx:73-86`). Nothing in the tree asserts the other side of that rule any more: that `queued`, `running`, `unknown`, and a record with **no `state`** still render as `unconfirmed`, and that a mixed set of records summarises per bucket.

### Where

- `apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx:53-58` — the summary bucketing (`completed`, `failed`, and the catch-all `record.state !== "completed" && record.state !== "failed"`).
- `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx:73-86` — the only case covering this rule, and it feeds a single `cancelled` record.

### Why this matters

The catch-all is what keeps every other state honest. Adding the `cancelled` branch shifted the boundary between "has its own bucket" and "falls through to unconfirmed", and no test pins the fall-through side:

- a future bucket (or a reordering of the `if` chain) can reclassify `queued`/`running`/`unknown` silently, with all tests still green;
- `RuntimeNoticeRecord.state` is optional (`packages/schema/src/session.ts`), so a record with no `state` at all must still land in `unconfirmed` — nothing asserts it;
- the mixed case is the one a researcher actually sees: `1 completed + 1 failed + 1 cancelled` must summarise as `1 completed · 1 failed · 1 cancelled`, not collapse into one bucket.

### Acceptance

One added test in `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx`, red before the fix it claims to pin and green after, no product-code change:

1. a notice whose `records` are `queued`, `running`, `unknown`, and one object with no `state` renders `4 unconfirmed` and no `cancelled` bucket;
2. a notice with `1 completed + 1 failed + 1 cancelled` renders `1 completed · 1 failed · 1 cancelled` (the `·` join inside `.wake-notice-outcome`) and three badges.

Red-first evidence required in the PR body: the command `node --import tsx --test tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` before (failing assertion, quoted) and after (pass counts).

### Context

Raised as F1 in review thread `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM6zwwXP` / `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM6z-Dd6` on PR #892; deliberately not fixed in that tip, because adding it there would replace the approved head and restart the review for a test-only gap. Bug #889 and PR #892 are unaffected: the `cancelled` behaviour itself is covered by `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx:73-86`.

Branch: dev2/fix/web-settings-client-error
Base: f4dd18137e93
At: 2026-11-05T13:26:12Z

## What happens

`PUT /api/web/settings` answers **500 `{"error":"Internal server error"}`** when a caller sends a value `normalizeWebSettings` rejects, instead of a 400 that names the field. Two of the three user-facing rejections in that function are not recognised as client-input errors, so they fall through to the catch-all.

Reproduced against live `main` `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673` with a route-level probe (deleted afterwards, tree clean):

```
# status 500
# body {"error":"Internal server error"}
not ok 1 - PUT /api/web/settings answers a client error for an unsupported fetch provider
  error: an unsupported provider is a client error, got 500
  500 !== 400
# tests 1 / # pass 0 / # fail 1
```

Command: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/zz-web-settings-probe.test.ts`, where the probe starts `createApiServer` (offline MCP transport) and sends

```ts
fetch(`${origin}/api/web/settings`, {
  body: JSON.stringify({ fetchProvider: "definitely-not-a-provider" }),
  headers: { authorization: "Bearer test-token", "content-type": "application/json" },
  method: "PUT",
});
```

The same request with a valid provider answers 200, so the route itself and its auth are fine; only the rejection is misclassified.

## Expected

A 400 whose body names the offending field, e.g. `Unsupported web fetch provider` (and `Unknown web setting: <key>` for an unrecognised field), the way `deepseekEnabled must be a boolean` already answers 400 today.

## Root cause

- `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:377-379` (throw at `:378`) throws a plain `Error("Unsupported web fetch provider")`, and `:372` throws `Error("Unknown web setting: <key>")`.
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1255-1259` calls `store.updateWebSettings(await readJson(...))` with no local mapping, so both reach the shared chain at `:3894-3940`.
- That chain classifies plain errors by prose only: `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:24-31` (`is required`, `must`, `contains an unknown value`, `cannot`, `does not match`, `invalid`, `unsafe … path`, `plain basename`). Measured at this commit by importing the predicate:

```
"Unsupported web fetch provider" false
"Unknown web setting: nope" false
"deepseekEnabled must be a boolean" true
```

so the first two land in `unclassified_request_error` (`http/index.ts:3934-3940`) and become a 500 that is logged as a server fault.

## Smallest fix (one function + one dispatch line)

Give the two rejections a stable code and map it where the other codes are mapped — the same shape `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`/`SKILL_LIBRARY_VALIDATION` already use:

1. `services/api/src/store/settings.ts`: throw `Object.assign(new Error("Unsupported web fetch provider"), { code: "INVALID_WEB_SETTINGS" })` at `:377-379`, and the same code for the unknown-key throw at `:372`.
2. `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3932`, next to `SKILL_LIBRARY_VALIDATION`: `else if (code === "INVALID_WEB_SETTINGS") sendError(response, 400, message);`.

Do **not** import `SessionStoreHttpError` into `store/settings.ts` to get the 400: `services/api/src/store.ts:277-283` already imports `normalizeWebSettings` from that module, so the reverse import creates a cycle (the same reason #884's review rejected `ApiStatusError` there). Do not add another prose pattern either — `error-classification.ts:15-19` says new code should use a stable code.

## Acceptance

- `PUT /api/web/settings` with `{"fetchProvider":"definitely-not-a-provider"}` answers **400**, body names the field, and no `unclassified_request_error` is logged.
- `PUT /api/web/settings` with an unrecognised key (e.g. `{"nope":1}`) answers **400** naming it.
- A valid update (e.g. `{"searchCacheTtlSeconds":17}`) still answers **200** and reads back through `GET /api/web/settings`.

## Environment

`main` `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673`, Node `v22.23.2`, Linux, `services/api` test harness (`node --import tsx --test`). Route declared public surface in `test/contract/routes.json`.

The provenance reads `待提交` / `已提交`. Under English the labels stay the words the rest of the UI already uses: `Queued`, `Running`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Cancelled`, `Unknown`, and `Pending` / `Committed`. ## Where it comes from - `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:97`, `:111`, `:122` — `{item.state}`; the class must keep `item.state`, only the child text needs a label. - `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:98` — `t("activity.executionMeta", { provenance: item.provenance, workspace: item.workspaceId })` passes the raw token into the sentence. - `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:96`, `:110`, `:121` — the `label` prop of `ProcessRecord` interpolates `item.state`. - `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` carries 25 `activity.*` keys in both catalogues (en `2738-2759`, zh `5757-5778`) but none for these values, which is why this is the one activity surface that still shows English. Value domains, for whoever writes the keys: `packages/schema/src/execution.ts:45` (`queued|running|completed|failed|cancelled|unknown`), `apps/web/src/api/runs.ts:40` (timers: `pending|fired|cancelled`), `packages/schema/src/execution.ts:101` (provenance: `pending|committed|unconfirmed`). The probe below is a temporary file — it is not part of the branch, it exists to prove the failure: ```tsx // apps/web/tests/zz-activity-badge-probe.test.tsx (temporary, not committed) const activity = { executions: [{ id: "job", agentId: "main", runnerId: "local", workspaceId: "ws_a", state: "running", provenance: "pending" }], transfers: [], timers: [], agents: [], }; const client = { getAgentActivity: async () => activity } as unknown as ApiClient; let view: ReactTestRenderer; await act(async () => { view = create(createElement(LocaleProvider, { initialLocale: "zh-CN" }, createElement(AgentActivityPanel, { client, sessionId: "session" }))); }); const tree = JSON.stringify(view!.toJSON()); assert.match(tree, /执行/); assert.doesNotMatch(tree, /running/); ``` Command and observed output: ``` $ cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/zz-activity-badge-probe.test.tsx not ok 1 - zh-CN badge names the state in Chinese error: |- The input was expected to not match the regular expression /running/. rendered fragment: {"type":"span","props":{"className":"activity-badge running"},"children":["running"]} # tests 1 # pass 0 # fail 1 ``` The same render shows the second half of this issue: `"工作区 ws_a · 溯源 pending"` — `provenance` is untranslated in the sentence produced by `activity.executionMeta`, and the process record's label is `local · main · running`. ## Environment - `main` @ `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673` - node `v22`;
