pr:680.body:
Fixes #679

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

## What the problem is

`CasStore.has()` answered the existence question by calling `read()` and mapped only `ENOENT` to `false`. `read()` re-hashes the bytes, so an object whose bytes no longer match its digest made `has()` throw `CAS integrity failure` — from a method whose contract is a boolean. Its sibling `verify()` already maps the same condition to `false`, so the two predicates over one store disagreed:

```
put -> b94d27b9934d 11
has before -> true
verify after corruption -> false
has after corruption -> THREW CAS integrity failure
```

The overwrite keeps the byte length (11 → 11), i.e. exactly the "same size, different bytes" corruption the store detects elsewhere. Callers use `has()` as a cache probe in front of `put` / `retain` / republish decisions: with a corrupt blob they crashed instead of taking the republish branch.

## What changes

`has()` now maps the integrity failure to `false` the way `verify()` does:

```ts
// A corrupt object is not usable, so has() answers as verify() does: absent.
if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT" || (error as Error).message === "CAS integrity failure") return false;
```

`has(hash)` is a total boolean predicate again: `true` only when the object is present and valid, `false` when it is missing **or corrupt**. `read()` still rejects a corrupt object with `CAS integrity failure` — the detection is unchanged, only the boolean answer is. A valid object and a missing object behave exactly as before. Two lines of production code; no new dependency.

## Commits

- `15247383034b21965143ab7e21d0aa681b77a6ad` — the red test only.
- `dfbc783d4a24913d113fcab6e7516271c292ee23` — the fix.

The red test is the first commit, the fix is appended on top; no amend, no force-push.

## Red → green

Red on base `ad34dd7847` (test commit only):

```
cd packages/cas
node --import tsx --test src/index.test.ts

not ok 3 - a corrupted object is absent for has() and verify(), and read() still rejects it
  error: 'CAS integrity failure'
  stack: |-
    CasStore.read (.../packages/cas/src/index.ts:98:43)
    async CasStore.has (.../packages/cas/src/index.ts:76:7)
# tests 4
# pass 3
# fail 1
```

The test pins all three answers in one place: `verify()` is `false`, `has()` is `false`, and `read()` still rejects with `CAS integrity failure` (so the fix cannot be "stop checking digests").

Green on this tip:

```
node --import tsx --test src/index.test.ts
# tests 4 / # pass 4 / # fail 0

node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"
# tests 37 / # pass 37 / # fail 0
```

pr:716.body:
Windows direct execution provides managed Bash, but persisted environments can lack the Unix utilities that the tool contract implies, causing commands such as `head` to fail without actionable capability or recovery information. This change makes the managed Windows shell contract explicit, upgradeable, and diagnosable.

## Managed Windows shell contract

- Provision MSYS2 coreutils, grep, and sed with `m2-bash` in the managed starter environment.
- Add `Library\\usr\\bin` to the Windows activation path so the managed utilities resolve without relying on an incidental Git Bash installation.
- Probe the managed Bash executable and guaranteed utility set, expose the platform and shell capability through Runner readiness, and refresh the probe after setup.
- Update `run_shell` and `check_runner` descriptions so the agent follows the target Runner capability rather than assuming host commands.

## Persisted environment upgrade and diagnostics

- Detect required starter packages missing from an existing environment, install only the missing specifications, and retain an audit revision.
- Avoid repeating migration for a newly created starter that already received the complete package contract.
- Attach a bounded `COMMAND_NOT_FOUND` diagnostic only when exit code 127 is accompanied by Bash's standard simple-command failure, preserving stderr as evidence and recommending an available utility or Python equivalent.

## Windows stack command shims

Route `.cmd` and `.bat` service entry points through `cmd.exe`, passing argument values through the child environment. Native executables keep their direct spawn path. This handles command shims while preserving spaces and literal argument metacharacters.

## Validation

Final tested commit: `82a8be4a0468008a1d49b4f5e14ba803c6313789`.

**The Windows product environment uses Node 22.** All operator-reported Windows product journeys below were performed with Node 22.


At the author's explicit request, final-head validation is limited to affected tests and relevant product journeys; full local gates were not repeated. Earlier full runs on `f028f2fb` remain non-green: UT 6,046/6,051 passed (5 failures), ST 50/51 passed (1 failure), and mocked browser E2E 124/133 passed (9 failures, 0 skipped). Their root causes were not all established by baseline comparison; these historical results are not claimed as passes or definitively unrelated failures.

Fixes #777

Owner: Dev2
Written-by: Dev-2
Tip SHA: 0bb3ee16884843a09d30278a63db007ba3f4da5d
Base: a429ba1d4eca17af8cfabb9f28abe9d651e38e6c (main at push; branch rebased onto it, no overlap)

`web_fetch`/`web_search` handed search-result titles and snippets to the model with named HTML references still encoded. Only `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot` and `nbsp` decoded, so a page title like `Café — a review` reached the prompt and the report verbatim, and the sources a science search cites most often (encyclopedias, European sites) are exactly the entity-heavy ones. This decodes every named reference a browser resolves, in the same single pass as before.

## What changed

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts`: the five-name map is replaced by the full WHATWG named character reference set — 2125 semicolon-terminated names — expanded into a `Map` once at module load. `nbsp` keeps its existing ordinary-space mapping; numeric references, the single-pass rule (`&lt;` → `<`) and unknown names (`&bogus;` stays literal) are unchanged. The decoding loop is the same one-scan replace it was; only the data changed shape and moved out of this module.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html-entities.ts` (new): the table itself — a `name;code point;…` constant, 246 folded lines — under a 37-line header that states the source (WHATWG named character references via CPython's `html.entities.html5`, 2231 keys of which the 2125 semicolon forms are what this pattern accepts), the retrieval date, the exact `python3` snippet that regenerates the body, and the licence position: the standard's table reproduced as factual data — names and code points any HTML parser needs — not copied from another project's source. `html.ts` keeps the decoder and goes from 79 lines to 90 (+11); 368 is only the shape this branch's previous commit had with the table inline, and this commit moves it out. The data is 246 of the new file's 284 lines.
- `tsconfig.base.json`: one line, `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`. The import in `html.ts` keeps a `.ts` extension so `node --experimental-strip-types` — the command the issue reproduces with — resolves the sibling source instead of failing with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; that option is what lets tsc accept the specifier and still emit `./html-entities.js` (verified: the built `dist/web/native/html.js` line is `import { NAMED_ENTITIES_PACKED } from "./html-entities.js";`). It belongs in the base config rather than the package one: the root tests config used by `pnpm typecheck` extends only `tsconfig.base.json`, and with the option in `packages/data-source/tsconfig.json` alone that check fails with `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts(73,39): error TS5097: An import path can only end with a '.ts' extension when 'allowImportingTsExtensions' is enabled.` From the base config both the package build and that check pass. It changes nothing else in the tree — the only `test/` file that `tsc` type-checks imports `.js` paths; the Playwright specs under `test/` are not in any tsconfig.
- `html-entities.ts` is force-added: `.gitignore`'s `data-*/` rule also matches the `packages/data-source/` directory (`git check-ignore -v` reports `.gitignore:91`). I left that rule alone to keep this PR single-purpose; say the word if you would rather have it anchored as `/data-*/` and I will open a separate issue.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts`: cases for the names in the issue (`eacute`, `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `apos`, `diams`, `rsquo`, `ldquo`/`rdquo`, Latin-1, symbols), case sensitivity, an unknown name, the single-pass rule after the table widened, and a guard that the exported table still has exactly 2125 entries plus one two-scalar value (`NotEqualTilde`), so a dropped or mis-chunked line cannot pass as a smaller table. The test file is unchanged by the move.

Size, whole PR: 4 files, 344 insertions, 8 deletions (`html-entities.ts` +284, `html.test.ts` +41/−1, `html.ts` +18/−7, `tsconfig.base.json` +1).

## Red first

Decoder tests. Command:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/web/native/html.test.ts
```

Before the fix:

```
# Subtest: decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
not ok 3 - decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
  expected: "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
  actual: 'café — 5–10 … O'Brien'
# Subtest: decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
not ok 4 - decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
  expected: 'Ää'
  actual: 'Ää'
# pass 5
# fail 2
```

Table guard. The guard lands in its own commit before the export exists, so it is red on the change that adds only the test:

```
# pass 0
# fail 1
SyntaxError: The requested module './html.js' does not provide an export named 'NAMED_ENTITIES'
```

and it fails the way it is meant to when one entry is dropped from the packed constant (mutation check, one `AElig;c6;` field removed, then restored):

```
not ok 8 - keeps every entry of the generated WHATWG table
  expected: 2125
  actual: 2124
# pass 7
# fail 1
```

Green after the implementation, same command as the decoder run: `# pass 8`, `# fail 0`. The package suite goes from 74 to 75 tests with the guard: `# tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0`.

## The issue's reproduction

Command from #777:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

On this tip:

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

The middle line is the single-pass guarantee: the decoded ampersand does not start a second scan.

## Gates

On this tip, in `packages/data-source` unless noted:

```
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json                                        # exit 0 (build)
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit                               # exit 0
$ node --experimental-strip-types -e 'import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(...)'
  café — 5–10 … O'Brien                                          # exit 0
$ npm test                                                        # # tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0
$ cd ../.. && node scripts/check-architecture.mjs                 # 333 source files, boundaries OK
$ cd ../.. && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json        # exit 0
$ cd ../.. && pnpm --recursive typecheck                          # 34 packages Done, exit 0
```

`pnpm architecture:check` is **98 passed / 1 failed** on this host: `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs` shells out to `.ci/run-research-python.sh race`, which needs a writable uv Python install and network (`Read-only file system` at `~/.local/share/uv/python`); it does not touch `packages/data-source`. `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` itself is green, as shown above.

## Not run

- Repo-level UT/ST/E2E, CodeCheck (GitCode) and the Docker/binary layers: CI. This PR changes one package's text extractor and its test, plus one compiler option; the package tests, both tsc configurations, the architecture check and the recursive typecheck were run locally.

pr:814.body:
## Problem

Evolve is the one capability that keeps running and producing results after the turn that started it ends, but the desktop app had no way to reach it: `/evolve-design` opened nothing, so a search could only be designed, confirmed and watched in the web client. A user working in the desktop app has to switch surfaces mid-task, and the run they left behind is unreachable from where they are.

## What this adds

- **Create dialog** — collects the two things a person actually knows (what should get better, which search algorithm fits) and hands that sentence to the conversation as the command the user would have typed. The agent still designs the scorecard, runs the probe and owns the checkpoints.
- **Checkpoint pace switch** — on by default. Turning it off sends `/evolve-design --no-confirm`: the agent still does the work of every step and still reports each checkpoint, labelled as automatic, but does not wait for a reply between them. Checkpoint 3's cost summary is kept, and a blocker that needs a decision (missing dataset, ambiguous goal, an approval the agent cannot give) still stops. The pace is recorded on the goal as `checkpointMode`; an absent field reads as `confirm`, which is what every existing run did.
- **Checkpoint cards** — each of the four checkpoints is drawn as a card in the transcript rather than as more prose: the step (`检查点 1/4`), the question, the few lines to read, and two answers — confirm and continue, or write the change in the card and send it from there. Once a later turn exists the card folds to its header, so a finished design reads as four lines instead of four screens; the card still waiting on you stays open. A run with the pace switch off still shows the card, marked automatic, with no buttons. The card is read from the answer's own `evolve-checkpoint` fence (a block tagged with the skill's name, `evolve-design`, is read the same way), so it survives a reload; a client that does not draw cards falls back to the block as readable code.
- **Session shelf** — a thin row under the session header. A running search stays reachable when the panel is closed, and a session that never used evolve renders exactly as before.
- **Result panel** — follows the run's SSE stream, falls back to polling the run list, and answers in order: best score and how it moved, the candidate table, a selected candidate's diff, and why it was rejected. The inspector becomes a drawer on a narrow window.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop`: `npm run typecheck`; `npm test` — 760 pass, including new command parsing, dialog, shelf, panel, pace-switch, checkpoint-fence and checkpoint-card cases.
- `services/api` evolution suites (proposal, pre-flight, call budget, thinking control) — 51/51.
- `packages/evolve` 11/11, `packages/schema` 29/29.
- The desktop e2e suite gains `apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts` with a mocked evolve runtime, including three checkpoint-card journeys: confirm sends the reply, an automatic card asks for nothing, and a change is written and sent from inside the card (the composer is never touched). Playwright is not installed in this worktree, so it runs in CI rather than locally.

## Acceptance

The end-to-end path is the tutorial sample in `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`), and the UI review tracked in #798 is the other acceptance item.

Related to #798 — this PR does not close it.

Fixes #812

Draft. Evolve can score a search from an NPU shell execution, and a scorecard can limit which fields a candidate is allowed to change.

## Summary
- An NPU search submits a signed `POST /shell-executions` to the Runner and waits. Success is `completed` with `device` equal to `npu`. A queued, running, failed, or non-NPU result has no numeric score, and it is not stored as 0. The local sandbox is not used as a fallback.
- The scorecard names `direction.editable`. A candidate that is not that JSON object, or that changes any other field, is refused before it is scored. A search with no direction is unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] `services/evolve/tests/test_npu_direction.py`: 4 passed. Covers a fixed-field rejection, refusal without a direction or a runner, a non-NPU result, and one signed submit that waits from running to an NPU score.
- [ ] A real Runner with an Ascend device.

pr:826.body:
Related to #812

Partial. Keep #812 open.

A directed search can now run on the conversation's selected runner. A JSON the search had already measured was still spending a round, and the NPU path handed the search library one task, which that library refuses to start on. A search that does not name editable fields stays the existing free program search.

## Directed edits

The chat agent starts the run and does not pick later steps. PUCT chooses which measured node to expand. The model then proposes one JSON object. Only the fields the user ticked may change. A change to any other field, or a value that is not JSON, is rejected before the runner and has no score. A proposal that matches an edit already measured is not sent to the card. The model is asked again, inside the same slot, for a different JSON.

There is no task-specific update rule. The model sees the measured values and their scores and proposes the next JSON itself.

## NPU scoring

Each candidate is one fresh shell execution on the conversation's selected runner, in a sandbox with no network. The fixed program computes the score. The candidate is JSON bound as input, not the program that runs. Success is a completed execution whose result says the device is `npu` and includes a number. A job that is still queued or running is waited on and does not take another slot. A failure, a cancellation, or a missing result has no score and is not stored as 0.

The search library requires at least four tasks and a hold-out fraction strictly between 0 and 1. An NPU search supplies four task ids and holds one out. The domain caches the measurement, so those ids do not each use the card.

## Field table

The run shows the ticked fields. Each candidate row shows which field changed, the old value, the new value, and the score.

## Validation

- `services/evolve/tests/test_npu_direction.py`: 16 passed.
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run on this Windows host. Those layers need the bubblewrap sandbox used by the CI scripts.
- Local stack, one selected NPU card: a directed search completed. The discrimination probe returned two different numeric scores for the starting JSON and a damaged field. A later search requested 10 rounds and stored 6 new measurements, then stopped because the round counter ended. Scores were read from the runner. No score was invented, and a missing result was not stored as 0.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED for the mocked browser suite: this host cannot run the bubblewrap CI layers.

Local stack: the directed NPU search above completed on one selected card and returned runner scores. The field table was not clicked through in a browser in this update.

## Release

Release category: release:feature

User impact: a search can score candidates on the conversation's selected NPU runner, and can limit edits to named JSON fields.

Compatibility and migration: none for a search that does not ask for a runner or a field list. That path stays the existing program search.

The GitHub label is pending a maintainer.

**更正上一版正文（我自己写错、reviewer 已据其回复，在此一并收回）**：上一版说这行是投影"因为构建机 C 盘只剩 2.4 GB，低于 `MIN_FREE_BYTES` 的 5 GB 门禁，`pnpm dist` 在这台机器上跑不起来"。这个理由是错的——`MIN_FREE_BYTES`（`win_desktop/src/wizard-data-dir.ts:8`）是**首启数据目录向导**的运行时门槛，`build.mjs` 与 `assemble-backend.mjs` 里**没有任何** free-space 检查，且构建产物全部落在 E 盘（实测 142 GB 可用），C 盘余量与能否出包无关。真实情况是：我此前把运行时门槛误当成构建门槛，并据此把唯一阻断项（真机证据）搁置了十几个小时。更正后实测了构建链，撞到的真阻断是**路径长度**而不是磁盘空间：`compileall` 把 `.pyc` 先写成 `<name>.pyc.<id(path)>` 再改名（后缀**长度** 14 字符是实测：本机 `compile_dir` 编 40 个文件，40/40 个临时名的后缀都是 13 位数字加前导点；那次运行的 pid 是 `23144`、只有 5 位，所以后缀不是 pid——早先正文写的 `<pid>` 是错的机制标签，数字本身没错），那 14 字符后缀配上 A5 实测的 `maxRel=192`，在长构建根下是 60+192+14=**266**，超过 Windows 的 259 可用字符，于是 JW venv 预编译以 `FileNotFoundError` 失败（正是本 PR 新加的"预编译硬失败"门禁把它拦下来了）。改走短构建根后是 12+192+14=218，余量 41；release5 当初也是这么构建的（`release5-assemble.log:3` 记 `out = X:\p5`）。同一算术在 electron-builder 那一层也成立且更紧：payload 会被拷进 `<output>\win-unpacked\resources\…`，仓库内默认的 `win_desktop\release`（62 字符）算下来是 62+14+192=**268**，同样超限，短输出目录 240 才装得下——A5 门禁只管 payload 根、没覆盖这层拷贝。代码里的 `COMPILEALL_TEMP_MARGIN = 19`（`assemble-backend.mjs:957`）与这里的实测 14 是同一个量，差 5 是**故意的**：19 是保守上界，`id()` 的十进制位数不是契约，取宽只会让 A5 更严不会更松；反过来按「14 是实测」去把常量改成 14，会朝不安全的那一侧收紧余量，请勿这么做。出包与实测数字随后回填。唯一与 C 盘余量真实相关的，是壳单测里 `probeDataDir: real writable dir with disk space passes` 这一项（它量的就是那个 5 GB 运行时门槛）。

硬约束全程保持：**离线双击即用、首启零网络、首启不变慢**（W15 全量 pyc 预编译不触碰，且 assemble 现对预编译失败硬失败）。

## 评审改了什么（这些在评审前都已作为回归或 no-op 发布过，现各有测试或构建门禁钉住）

- **babel 曾被当作死重清扫，静默降级了成品的 HTML 压缩器。** 那条规则的理由写的是"jinja2 硬依赖"，但 JW venv 里**根本没装 jinja2**，规则引用了一个不存在的包。真实链路是 `openjiuwen/html_compressor.py:55`（惰性、无保护的 `import_module("trafilatura")`）→ trafilatura → courlan → **模块作用域**导入 babel（`courlan/filters.py:11`）。`compress()` 吞掉 `ModuleNotFoundError` 并回退 beautifulsoup，所以它**无报错、无日志、exit 0**地发布了，只是每次 HTML 压缩的 title/author/date 全为 None。规则已删除，探针断言 4 改跑产品自己的压缩器，extractor 不是 `"trafilatura"` 就让构建失败。另外"删 `babel/locale-data` 省字节"也实测证伪：`Locale.parse` 会对**每个**合法 locale 抛 `FileNotFoundError`，而 courlan `filters.py:185` 的 `except (TypeError, UnknownLocaleError)` 接不住——把静默降级变成崩溃。
- **两个安装目录守卫用 `Abort` 取消，实际不取消。** `Abort` 在 custom page **creator** 里只是"跳过本页"，向导照旧推进到 InstFiles 并装进用户刚拒绝的目录，而 MessageBox 文案说会返回目录页。改为 `Quit`；又因为 custom page creator 里的裸 `Quit` 退出码是 **0**（实测矩阵：`.onInit` 裸 Quit = 2，page creator 裸 Quit = 0，页面位置不影响），两处各加 `SetErrorLevel 1`，使无人值守场景下"被拒绝的安装"不再报告成功。
- **codex vendor 清扫曾指向扁平化产不出来的路径，437 MB 的收益是 no-op。** 现枚举全部可达形态，且**下探不受名字门控**——平台包赢得 primaryOf 时会把 wrapper 嵌到 `@openai/codex-sdk` 下，受门控的遍历永远进不去。重放 `primaryOf` 实测：wrapper-primary 顺序 7 个 location 条目 → 2 个 distinct 目录，旧的门控遍历找到 2/2（这正是缺口在那次构建里存活的原因）；platform-primary 顺序 → 3 个 distinct，门控遍历只找到 1/3。
- **A1b 探针曾只证明"留下的还能用"，规则静默失配时门禁照样全绿。** 现增加断言 5 强制包表（`onnxruntime`/`kubernetes` 必须 ABSENT，`babel`/`courlan`/`trafilatura`/`chromadb`/`openjiuwen` 必须 PRESENT）；默认 EF 的 `works` 在 payload 模式下不再是合法结果；codex vendor 清扫另有一道**按内容**（`codex-package.json`）而非按名字的独立复查——复查若复用清扫自己的名字正则就会在正则失配时一起失明。
- `nsh-syntax-check` 的第三档 PATH 发现曾是死代码：裸 `catch {}` 连 `execFileSync` 未导入的 `ReferenceError` 一起吞掉，把编程错误报成"makensis not found"。现只白名单两种实测的 not-on-PATH 形态。
- 安装根与数据目录分离（两者曾默认同一字面量，卸载会删掉 `envs/`、`secrets/` 和全部会话），路径检查改为平台无关（`win32.isAbsolute` + `win32.parse`）。

pr:838.body:
## Summary

Part of #835.

This is the first KE core slice proposed in #835. It introduces only the pure text, extraction, and entity-resolution domain of the Knowledge Engine; it does not register API routes, agent tools, UI, background jobs, or runtime settings.

### Included

- Text parsing and retrieval primitives, including JATS, LaTeX, document levels, trigram/search, and citation helpers.
- LLM extraction schemas/prompts and the provenance gate requiring document anchors for extracted knowledge.
- Entity normalization, matching, merge policy, offline resolution, and sample evaluation data.
- Independent-review hardening for single-line display math, relevance-ordered FTS over-fetch, repeated citation anchors on one line, JATS formula alternatives, optional LaTeX macro defaults, and token-safe entity endpoint matching.
- Additional bot-review hardening: bounded worker-based regex execution, Unicode entity screening, LaTeX preamble removal, multiword/CJK entity and novelty matching, and grouped JATS citation IDs.
- CodeCheck cleanup for loop style and redundant non-null assertions, without changing test expectations.
- Follow-up review hardening: grep input is capped before worker cloning, worker startup and regex execution have separate deadlines, and large-corpus hits survive with honest scan truncation. The provenance fallback now requires ordered token evidence (including single-character entity tokens), rejecting word-permuted or semantically inverted quotes.
- Package-local unit tests and the package/lockfile wiring needed to build `@sciencediscovery/knowledge-engine`.

### Explicitly excluded

- Graph, growth, and evaluation orchestration modules.
- SQLite/API services, connectors, PDF workers, agent integration, and Web UI.
- `pairs.realworld.json` and other large/local fixtures.
- qa/, .tmp/, credentials, and local development artifacts.

The package index exports only modules present in this stage. Four graph-dependent resolution tests from the full reference implementation remain for the graph stage; no production module was stubbed to hide that dependency.

## Validation

- Windows package build: passed.
- Windows package typecheck: passed.
- Fresh native WSL clone of this branch:

- Windows package build/typecheck: passed.
- Root test-source typecheck (`tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`): passed.
- Windows architecture script checks: **38/38 passed**.
- Final independent review of the grep and provenance rework: **all-clear**, including race/timeout probes and 25 repeated search-suite runs without a flake.

- The full WSL architecture script run was **98/99**: the unrelated RACE case failed while cloning its external evaluator (`fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect` / `fatal: early EOF`); no B1 file participates in that path.

pr:843.body: The in-app feedback path only existed as a proposal: nothing collected what a user saw when something broke, so every report started from "it does not work". This wires the whole chain for the web and desktop front ends: a dialog that captures kind, description, frequency and impact (both required, since a report without them cannot be triaged), a draft/history store, and a receipt code the user can quote. The report is relayed by a Cloudflare Worker into a private GitHub issue, with KV-backed dedupe, per-IP and per-install rate limits and a daily quota so the endpoint cannot be used as a spam funnel. Payload building, redaction, PII detection and the receipt format live in operational-logging so both apps and the tests share one contract, and the offline screen seeds the dialog with the failure's diagnostics so a "cannot reach the local service" report arrives with boot state, origin and user agent already attached. /kind feature **What does this PR do / why do we need it**: - `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts`: the shared contract — payload building, field validation, redaction, PII detection, contact classification and receipt generation, imported by both clients and the Worker so the wire format cannot drift. - `packages/feedback-worker`: a Cloudflare Worker that relays a submission into a private GitHub issue (labels `source:in-app`, `kind:`, `needs-triage`, `contact:`), with KV-backed dedupe keyed by reporter and content, a per-IP hourly limit, a per-install daily limit, a daily issue quota, a CORS allowlist, and a 422 fallback that retries without labels so a repository missing a label does not lose the report. - `apps/web` and `apps/desktop`: the same dialog (kind, description, frequency, impact — frequency and impact mandatory), a draft and a 50-entry history in `localStorage`, the receipt display, a 我要反馈 entry in the desktop sidebar footer, and an entry on the offline screen that pre-fills the failure's diagnostics. - i18n in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` and in both desktop dictionaries (`text/zh.ts`, `text/en.ts`). **Which issue(s) this PR fixes**: Closes #844 **What scenarios were tested, and what were the verification results（Function, performance, reliability, etc.）**： - Unit tests: `operational-logging` 12 cases, `feedback-worker` 12 cases (CORS, 16 KiB rejection, invalid JSON and wrong field types, success path, duplicate within the window, per-install 429, daily quota 503, GitHub 5xx surfacing 502 without leaking the token, reporter-scoped dedupe, 422 label fallback), plus 8 + 8 status-code mapping and 7 + 7 store cases in the two clients. - Suites: web 248 pass / desktop 86 pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean for the shared package, the Worker and both apps. - Manual end-to-end against the deployed Worker: desktop dialog → receipt `FB-775M-N8A8` shown and recorded in 我的反馈; local backend stopped → reload lands on the offline screen → 我要反馈 (description pre-filled, diagnostics expandable, `boot: offline (unreachable)`) → receipt `FB-XKXW-FGSZ`; backend restarted → 重试 recovers in one click. - Behaviour checks: 提交 stays disabled until frequency and impact are chosen, with the reason shown; the same content from the same install returns the original receipt instead of opening a second issue; a full-length description still carries the two mandatory triage lines. Known gap: the mandatory-field rule has no component-level test yet — it is covered by the manual verification above. The plan is to extract the form-state predicate into a shared pure function and assert it from both apps. **Self-checklist**: + - [x] **Design**: Has the solution corresponding to the PR been reviewed by the Maintainer, and have all review comments been replied to and revised + - [x] **Test**: Has the code in the PR been fully covered by UT/ST test cases, and have the newly added test cases been uploaded to the repository along with this PR or already uploaded. + - [x] **Verification**: Does the PR description contains a detailed description of the verification results regarding the achievement of the expected goals for the Feature, Refactor, and Bugfix to this PR. + - [x] **Interface**: Does it involve changes to external interfaces? The corresponding changes have been approved by the interface review organization, and the annotation information for the API has been correctly refreshed. + - [x] **Document**: Does it involve modifications to the official website documentation? If so, please submit the materials to the Doc repository in a timely manner. ## Visual evidence (desktop app) Drag each image from `feedback-ui/` onto the line marked for it (the uploader inserts the link in place). Order matches the list requested in review. 1. Sidebar footer — 我要反馈 to the right of the GitHub star 2. The dialog on open, nothing filled in 3. The gate — description typed, 出现频率 / 影响程度 still unselected: 提交 stays disabled and the reason is shown 4. After submitting — receipt `FB-4SET-7JJR` 5. 我的反馈 after one submission — the same receipt is stored 6. Offline screen — 我要反馈 pre-fills the failure, diagnostics collapsed and expanded 7. English UI — dialog and receipt state A 30–60 s recording of the end-to-end flow is not attached yet; it is being prepared and will follow on this PR.

pr:853.body:
The nightly research and BioMnibench runs need a consistent model configuration and more resilient handling of transient model failures. This change uses the `nightly-research` environment, preserves requested DeepSeek reasoning settings through session configuration, and retries interrupted model turns only before answer text or tool calls are emitted.

## Nightly model configuration

- Configure real-model generators and the BioMnibench judge for DeepSeek thinking enabled at low effort by default; environment variables can override the API variant and thinking settings.
- Preserve explicitly requested DeepSeek thinking effort in model and session settings; default to high when no effort is supplied.
- Read the configured API variant consistently in all six real-model journeys and validate Biomni's persisted thinking snapshot against the controls supported by that variant.

## Reliability

- Recover transient mutation errors within a shared deadline.
- Retry interrupted reasoning-only model streams within the shared request retry budget, buffering reasoning so discarded attempts are not sent to callers.
- Improve network permission tool guidance and cover the model, gateway, evolution and BioMnibench changes with focused tests.

## Validation

- Current head: `fa34928`.
- `pnpm --filter "@sciencediscovery/schema..." build` passed.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/model test` passed (7 test files).
- `pnpm typecheck` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Real-model E2E, including the previously reported L3-files journey and binary release x86_64 workflow, has not been rerun on this head; the previous run was not green and remains unresolved pending fresh CI evidence.

## E2E user journeys

The prior run's basic real-model journey did not settle the L3-files file-editing run within its 120-second wait. This PR does not claim that failure is resolved; a successful rerun is still required.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: explicitly configured DeepSeek thinking effort is retained, and some transient model stream failures can be retried before an answer or tool call is emitted.

Compatibility and migration: no migration required; nightly real-model jobs use `nightly-research`, which must contain their required model and data credentials.

pr:854.body:
Opening a subagent's detail panel froze the desktop app for three to four seconds on a long run. The whole record was parsed and laid out at once — a closed `<details>` still mounts its children — every tool output went through `react-markdown`, and opening a replayed child re-read the whole roster from the API, though the panel only ever shows one child.

## Render a fold's body on first open

A closed native fold still mounts its subtree, so the panel paid for parsing and laying out tool output, the brief and historical steps that nobody could see. The new `Disclosure` component renders its body when the fold is first opened and keeps it afterwards, so reopening is instant. `open` stays uncontrolled: the browser still owns the open state, which is what lets a running step collapse on its own when it finishes. Running thinking stays open, as before.

## Show tool output as text, not Markdown

Tool input, output and progress are terminal text, not prose. They now render in a `<pre>`; the child's replies and thinking still go through Markdown. This removes the largest Markdown parse in the panel, since tool output is most of a long record's bytes.

## Read one child instead of the roster

`GET /api/sessions/:id/subagents/:sid` returns one child with its steps. The panel uses it when a replayed child is opened; a running child keeps following its own stream. On the server the store clones only that child rather than every child in the session. The roster route remains for callers that list children; the contract table and a contract scenario cover the new route.

A running child is also re-read from that route until it settles, because a wake turn publishes its continuation under a run the panel does not tail. The read returns the whole record, so it pauses while the window is hidden and resumes with one read when the window comes back. If several reads in a row fail, the panel says the record is no longer refreshing instead of looking live while frozen.

## Compare repeated steps by field

`mergeSubagentSteps` used to `JSON.stringify` both copies of every step on every stream tick. `content` can be hundreds of kilobytes, so a step that had not changed was still serialized twice. The comparison is now field by field, with prose compared as the string it is and only the small structured fields going through JSON. The field list is a key set that satisfies `Record<keyof SubagentStep, true>`: a field added to the schema fails the build here instead of being silently ignored. A unit test pins that an unchanged step keeps its identity.

## Visual evidence

The panel after the record is opened, with both folds closed (zh, 1440x900, default 720 px panel):

![opened](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/evidence/pr-854/zh-wide-1-opened.png)

The timeline open, every step still folded, then one tool step open with a long line wrapping inside its box and a failed step whose stack trace keeps its line breaks:

![timeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/evidence/pr-854/zh-wide-3-timeline.png)
![tool step open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/evidence/pr-854/zh-wide-4-tool-open.png)
![stack trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/evidence/pr-854/zh-wide-5-stack-trace.png)

The same states at the panel's minimum width (480 px) and in English:

![narrow panel, English](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/evidence/pr-854/en-narrow-4-tool-open.png)

Every state — just opened, task open, timeline open with folded rows, one tool step open, failed step with a stack trace, running vs finished thinking — is captured in Chinese and English at 1440x900 with the default panel and at the 480 px minimum. Index: [README](https://github.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/blob/evidence/pr-854/README.md). Uncut recordings, about 39 s each, driving the same states: [Chinese](https://github.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/blob/evidence/pr-854/panel-walkthrough-zh.webm), [English](https://github.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/blob/evidence/pr-854/panel-walkthrough-en.webm).

## Validation

The measurement is committed as `apps/desktop/e2e/panel-performance.spec.ts`. It builds a 137-step record of 15 KB per step (about 2 MB), opens it in the browser, and prints click-to-visible and the longest main-thread task. Run one worker, alone:

```
PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=.e2e/browsers \
  apps/desktop/e2e/node_modules/.bin/playwright test \
  --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts \
  apps/desktop/e2e/panel-performance.spec.ts
```

| Tree | Click to visible | Longest main-thread task | Long tasks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `3fc77a3f0d` (reviewed base) | 3850 / 3902 / 3926 / 4120 ms | 2803 / 2835 / 2793 / 2882 ms | 2 |
| `5a80ef65` | 502 / 504 / 521 ms | 0 ms | 0 |
| `1677180f` (this head) | 520 ms | 0 ms | 0 |

On the base tree the same spec also fails its mount assertion: 137 step rows are in the DOM while every fold is closed. On this head it passes. Under parallel load (beside the whole panel suite) click-to-visible rises — 5010 ms in one such run — while the longest main-thread task stays at 0 ms; the long task is the felt freeze, and wall clock under shared CPU is not a stable number, which is why the E2E test asserts the mount state and only budgets 15 s for visibility.

Desktop unit tests: 720 passed, 0 failed. Desktop `tsc` and the workspace `pnpm typecheck` pass. The panel suite (`panel-interactions.spec.ts` + `panel-performance.spec.ts`) passes 13/13.

UT layer (`pnpm ci:ut`): planned 6168, executed 6139, passed 6125, failed 14, skipped 0.

The 29 planned-but-unexecuted tests carry `swarm:required`. They are not a gap in this change's coverage: the JiuwenSwarm toolchain could not install on this host, so the harness left those entries out of the worker plans. 20 are in `services/api/src/server.test.ts` (gateway/model naming, title refinement, queued runs, approval switching, timeouts, MCP literature flow) and 9 in `services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts` (usage, Reviewer stop, blocked-run queueing and cancellation, child-stream endpoint, stuck-run stop).

Fixes #847

Owner: Dev-1
Written-by: Dev-1

## What changed

`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:103` — the transfer row's total now counts the progress entries the API expanded the declared mappings into (`item.progress.length`) instead of the number of declared mappings (`item.files.length`). One line changed; the committed count is untouched.

`test/journey-execution-management.spec.ts` — the mocked partial transfer in the execution-management journey declared two files but carried a single `completed` progress entry, so the new denominator rendered `1/1` where the journey asserted `1/2`. The fixture now carries the file its own error text describes: `{ targetPath: "missing.txt", state: "failed", bytes: 0 }`. The assertion stays `1/2 files committed`; no web source and no existing assertion was relaxed.

## Why

`services/api/src/workspace-transfers.ts:107-117` expands every declared mapping with `job.files.flatMap(...)`, so a single directory mapping becomes N progress entries. The numerator already counted that expanded collection while the denominator counted mappings, so a directory with three files rendered `3/1 files committed`.

## Red-first evidence

Red commit `24ed67a4e0ee487c6bc64470c56de3a0425fca9c` (test only), on base `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`, `AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx`:

```

not ok 8 - a directory transfer counts the files it expands to, not the mappings
  actual rendered row: "3/1 files committed"
```

Same file after the fix (`7e143316816fadc54eb3813ec92853bddc45d0f9`): `# tests 8 / # pass 8 / # fail 0`.

## Verification (exit codes)

At `afe2df8ba325a8f8f51caba060f441e5b940a9c2`:

| gate | command | exit | reading |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck (recursive) | `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false typecheck` | 0 | — |
| tests typecheck | `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | 0 | — |
| L1 static | `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1 pnpm ci:l1` | 0 | `{"status":"PASS","planned":4,"executed":4,"passed":4,"failed":0}` |
| web UT | `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` | 0 | `# tests 1216 / # pass 1216 / # fail 0` |

ST: no case in the frozen 51-case plan covers `AgentActivityPanel` or the transfers API (`grep -E 'activity|transfer' .ci/test-catalog.mjs` returns nothing); L2 `standard-journeys` is the covering layer and the journey fixture above is the case it exercises. `pnpm ci:l1` on this host needs `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1` to skip its `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` prepare step, which fails with `EROFS` on the read-only store; the four L1 checks themselves pass.

pr:857.body:
Fixes #816

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What changed

`SessionStore.writeArray` wrote its temp file and then called a bare `rename`, so a transient Windows sharing violation (an antivirus scanner, a search indexer or a backup agent briefly holding the fresh file) rejected the write, and nothing above contained the rejection.

- `services/api/src/store.ts` — **every** replace in the store now goes through the platform facade's `renameReplace`: the state writer (`writeArray`), the deletion journal finalize (`operation.next.json` → `operation.json`), and both journal staging renames (`stageDeletion`, `rollbackStagedDeletion`). The sharing violation belongs to the target file, not to one writer, so leaving the deletion paths on a bare `rename` would have kept the same failure shape on delete/rollback.
- `services/api/src/platform/os/replace.ts` (new) — one replace policy for every platform: 20 attempts, `50 + 25·attempt` ms backoff. Patience is 19 waits, `19 × 50 ms + 25 ms × (0 + … + 18) = 5,225 ms` (about 5.2 s). A non-transient errno such as `ENOSPC` is thrown immediately.
- `services/api/src/platform/os/replace.ts` — the retried errno set is platform-aware (`transientReplaceCodes()`): Windows retries `EPERM`/`EACCES`/`EBUSY` because its redirector reports all three for a transient hold; POSIX retries only `EPERM`/`EBUSY`, because an `EACCES` there is a lasting mode/ownership problem and `writeArray` is on the chat run path — retrying it would add 5.2 s to every state write of an already-unwritable store instead of failing at once. `ReplaceFileOptions.transientCodes` allows an override.
- `services/api/src/platform/os/replace.ts` — when the attempts are exhausted the throw is a `FileReplaceError` that keeps the last errno in `code` and the original error in `cause`, names the destination and the attempt count, and now also **copies `errno`/`syscall`/`path`/`dest`** from the last failure. A consumer that classified state-write failures on those fields would otherwise have been silently downgraded; `code`, `cause` and the `FileReplaceError` identity are unchanged, so a caller (or a test) that reads them still works.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` — the run scheduler is started with `void`, so nothing observed its rejection. It now attaches a `catch` that logs `run_scheduler_failed` with the session id and the message.
- `services/api/src/platform/os/index.ts` / `win32.ts` / `types.ts` — the retry moves out of the Windows-only adaptation (which now performs the raw rename) up to the facade, so the durable write behaves the same on every platform.

## Where the exhausted write could kill the process

The caller is **`scheduleSessionRuns` (`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3380`)** — the per-session run drain started from every run-creating request. Its body is `void (async () => { … })()`, and the statement that escapes is the **terminal `await store.updateSessionRunStatus(sessionId, next.id, status, …)` inside the inner `finally` (`:3522`)** (plus the `listSessionRuns` in the outer `finally`): the inner `try/catch` does not cover its own `finally`, so a state write that exhausts the retries propagates out of the `while`, through the outer `finally`, and out of a promise nobody awaits. Node 22 treats that as an unhandled rejection and exits — the reported crash.

With the catch: the rejection is logged, `scheduledSessions` has already released the session, and the run keeps the last status it could persist (`running`), which `recoverSessionRuns` turns into `interrupted` at the next start. Nothing is silently lost and the process survives. The regression test below fails on the pre-fix code with exactly the unhandled rejection, so this is pinned rather than argued.

## Red-first evidence

Test commit `ce393efa` (test only) on base `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`, `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test …`:

- `src/store-deletion.test.ts` → `# tests 7 / # pass 6 / # fail 1`
  ```
  not ok 2 - a transient EPERM on the deletion journal finalize is retried
    error: "EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '…/.trash/<id>/operation.next.json' -> '…/.trash/<id>/operation.json'"
  ```
  (the bare rename on the journal path, found in review, fails exactly like the state writer did)
- `src/runs/index.test.ts` → `# tests 16 / # pass 15 / # fail 1`
  ```
  not ok 16 - a state write that fails after retries is contained instead of killing the API
    error: 'Could not replace …/session-runs/<id>.json after 20 attempts (EPERM)'
  ```
  (the rejection escapes the voided scheduler and node:test reports it — the crash shape)
- `src/platform/os/replace.test.ts` does not load at `ce393efa`: `transientReplaceCodes` is the new export the platform split (and its POSIX no-retry assertion) needs.

Green at `8cb37d8aa37dab30853d75dfe5462eb2341b29f5`: the same four files `node --import tsx --test src/platform/os/replace.test.ts src/store-deletion.test.ts src/runs/index.test.ts src/store-replace.test.ts` → `# tests 29 / # pass 29 / # fail 0`.

## Verification

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck (recursive) | `pnpm --recursive typecheck` | 0 | — |
| tests typecheck | `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | 0 | — |

Fixes #860

A compact token count rounds **before** it decides which unit to print, so `999_999` tokens become `${Math.round(999.999)}K` = `1000K` — a number that reads as a million while the exported field still says `999999`. The chart-axis formatter has the same shape (`999_999` → `1000.0K`). One threshold check is off by the unit boundary, not by one token.

## What changed

- `formatCompactTokenValue` crosses into `M` when the thousands rendering would round to `1000` (`Math.round(value / 1_000) >= 1_000`), so `999_500…999_999` print `1.0M` instead of `1000K`. Values that still round below that (`999_499` → `999K`) keep the existing behaviour, as do `10_000` → `10K` and `1_000_000` → `1.0M`.
- `formatChartNumber` applies the same boundary to its one-decimal thousands label (`999.9K` stays `999.9K`, `999_999` becomes `1.0M`, never `1000.0K`), so an axis tick cannot claim a unit the data has not reached.
- `formatTokenField` and every export path are untouched: the exported value is still the exact integer, which is what made the mismatch visible.

pr:868.body:
Fixes #866

## What this fixes

`sanitizeUploadFilename()` in `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts` guarded an empty name, a NUL byte, absolute paths, drive letters and traversal, but not Windows reserved device names. On a Windows workspace `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`, `LPT1`–`LPT9`, `CONIN$` and `CONOUT$` resolve in every directory and with any extension, so `con.csv`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log` passed the guard and failed later inside the workspace write with a raw `EPERM`/`ENOENT` that the upload response reports as an unclassified error (`CON` targets the console device instead of failing).

The fix rejects them with the same `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` code and error shape the other guard branches use, names the offending file in the message, and strips trailing dots/spaces first because Windows ignores them (`nul.`, `CON .csv`). Legal stems that only begin with a reserved word (`conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `auxiliary.csv`) and two-digit ports (`com10.csv`) keep working — the same test asserts both directions.

The guard is platform-independent on purpose, so Linux and macOS reject these names too: portability — an upload must be writable on every supported host, and a file accepted on Linux but unusable on a Windows workspace would only fail later there.

## Red → green

The test was written first and fails on `main` `8708320f`:

```
not ok 2 - sanitizeUploadFilename rejects Windows reserved device names
  error: 'Missing expected exception: CON must be rejected as a Windows reserved device name'
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
# tests 16
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

After the fix: `node --import tsx --test src/workspace-upload.test.ts` → `# tests 16 / # pass 16 / # fail 0`.

Commits keep the pairing: `96b34e1d` test (red), `a2cebfbc` fix.

## Must-fix from review: the refused name now answers 400, not 500

`agent-ci-infra-bot` found the gap: `sanitizeUploadFilename` rejects the new names with `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH`, but the request handler decides 400-vs-500 **by message** (`isKnownClientInputError`, `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:20-32`), and the new message names none of the seven classified patterns. So the exact scenario this PR exists for — uploading `CON.csv` — answered `500 Internal server error` instead of naming the file.

Fixed on the same branch, tip `1a7b1b997bfe5e23af38d3abab59893a33e32ddd`, in two commits:

- `c0173957` (test, red first): a **route-level** test in `services/api/src/server.test.ts` (`WSP-004`) that uploads `CON.csv` through the real HTTP surface and asserts the status, the file name in the body, and that the workspace stayed empty. Before the fix: `500 !== 400`.
- `1a7b1b99` (fix): `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` joins the handler's existing stable-code branches (`services/api/src/http/index.ts`, one line beside `SKILL_LIBRARY_VALIDATION`), so the 400 follows the **code** rather than the prose a later wording edit could change. Every branch of the guard is tagged with that code, so this covers the whole family, not just the reserved-name message — no regex added, and no message reworded to please a pattern.

One consideration on where it went: the reviewer's finding points at the message classifier, and adding a ninth prose pattern there would have worked for this message only. The code branch is the smaller and more durable of the two, and it does not loosen any other 400/500 decision.

`services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` is unchanged and still 16/16 — the function-level contract this PR added is untouched; what changed is the status a client sees.

## Second finding from the same review: the stream syntax (same guard, not a new rule)

The device-name guard took its stem up to the first `.` and never looked at `:`, so `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA` were accepted while `nul.txt` was refused. Windows resolves both to the device in every directory, so that was the same reservation under another spelling:

```
"CON.csv"      -> rejected
"nul.txt"      -> rejected
"NUL. "        -> rejected
"nul:stream"   -> accepted before this commit
"con:$DATA"    -> accepted before this commit
"report:2024.csv" -> accepted before and after
```

Fixed as the **sixth branch of the same predicate**, not as a character rule: `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` now takes its stem before the colon as well as before the dot, and refuses only when that part names a device. A colon in front of an ordinary stem is a legal file name on Linux and macOS, so `report:2024.csv` and `data:2024.tsv` keep passing unchanged — refusing every `:` would have traded this bug for a portability one.

Red first, `services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` on `1a7b1b99`:

```
not ok 1 - sanitizeUploadFilename rejects the stream syntax of a Windows reserved device name
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
    +   'accepted',
    +   'accepted'
    -   'rejected',
    -   'rejected'
      ]
```

The same test carries the over-rejection guard (`assert.equal(sanitizeUploadFilename("report:2024.csv"), "report:2024.csv")`), which was green before the fix and stays green after it. After: `# tests 18 / # pass 18 / # fail 0` across `workspace-upload.test.ts` and `error-classification.test.ts`.

Nothing outside `sanitizeUploadFilename` had to change for this — the handler branch from the first finding already answers 400 for the code — so this stays one pull request rather than becoming a second one against #866.

pr:870.body:
Fixes #862

## What this fixes

`SessionStore.writeArray()` published state through a `.state-<pid>-<uuid>.tmp` file and ran its cleanup in `finally` without a guard:

```ts
} finally {
  await rm(temporaryPath, { force: true });
}
```

When `rename` was refused (on Windows an antivirus scanner, search indexer or backup agent holds the freshly written file, so `MoveFileEx` returns `EPERM`) and the `rm` was refused for the same reason, the `finally` threw the bare cleanup `EPERM` and **replaced** the error that explains the loss. The caller then saw an unclassified `EPERM` on a `.tmp` path instead of the classified replace failure, so nothing could tell a locked file apart from a full disk.

The fix swallows the cleanup failure (`.catch(() => undefined)`); the replace error is the one that says what was lost.

## Red → green

| | |
|---|---|
| **Red** `88e6aa07` | `node --import tsx --test src/store-replace-cleanup.test.ts` → `2 tests / 1 pass / 1 fail`; failing assertion `the cleanup failure must not replace the replace error` (the surfaced error is the mocked `rm` EPERM, the `rename` EPERM is gone) |
| **Green** `0bae8739` | same command → `2 tests / 2 pass / 0 fail` |
| **Review round** `09b4ccb7` | adds the `attempts === 20` / `cause.code` assertions (inert before #857, live after) — same command → `2/2` |

The Security review's anti-forgery assertions are in `09b4ccb7`: when the surfaced error is a `FileReplaceError` (the classified shape #857 introduces on `main`), the test pins `attempts === 20` and `cause.code === "EPERM"`. On this base `writeArray` still calls plain `rename`, so that branch is inert here and becomes live the moment #857 lands — no follow-up tip is needed for it.

The two tests are split (per the Security review): **A** asserts the caller still sees the replace failure when both `rename` and the cleanup `rm` report `EPERM` (it accepts either the raw replace error before #857 or a `FileReplaceError` whose `cause` is it — the check reads `error.cause?.message` too); **B** asserts a failing replace still removes its temporary file, so no `.tmp` is left behind.

Both mocks use `syncBuiltinESMExports()` because `store.ts` imports `rename`/`rm` as named ESM bindings, and both only touch paths whose `basename` starts with `.state-` — the store's own temporary files — so no other write in the fixture is affected. The mock hands control back to the host after the test (`active` flag plus restore) so the next test is not affected by the still-bound ESM export.

pr:876.body:
Fixes #874

## What this fixes

The API treats `unknown` as a finished-but-unverified outcome for the live surface: `services/api/src/workspace-transfers.ts:17` and `shell-executions.ts` both define terminal as *not queued and not running*, and an unfinished record found after an API restart is stored as `state: "unknown"` with `finishedAt` set and the reason it stopped being tracked.

But the API deliberately keeps one branch open for it. `services/api/src/shell-executions.ts` `cancel()`:

```ts
// Unknown after restart may still be running remotely; cancellation is safe, resubmission is not.
if (!terminal(execution.state) || execution.state === "unknown") { … }
```

The panel had a single predicate doing both jobs — `const active = (state) => ["queued", "running", "unknown"].includes(state)` (`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:20`) — so an `unknown` record rendered as `process-live` forever (open body, hidden summary, never foldable history), the execution Cancel guard (`:94`) was enabled for it, while the transfer Cancel guard used a hand-written `["queued", "running"]` (`:106`) and disabled its button. The panel gave the same outcome two different answers, and neither the live surface nor the guards matched the API.

Two predicates now:

- `live = state === "queued" || state === "running"` — decides the live surface (`ProcessRecord`) and the **transfer** Cancel guard;
- `cancellable = live(state) || state === "unknown"` — used **only** by the **execution** Cancel guard, because that is exactly the branch the API keeps actionable.

So an unknown execution folds into the ordinary history record (summary row, recorded error shown) yet keeps a reachable "Cancel execution" button; an unknown transfer folds into history with Cancel disabled, because the API settles transfers itself and nothing is left running remotely.

Four routes in the same family read one artifact id. `content` (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3353`) asks `store.getArtifactVersion()` first and answers 404; `provenance` and `diff` called `artifactVersionProvenance()` / `artifactVersionDiff()`, which throw a bare `new Error("Artifact version not found")` (`services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:169` and `:349`). The top-level mapper only turns `Project|Session|Proxy server|Provider|Model not found`, `Execution|Transfer|Timer|Subagent not found: …` and a few codes into 404, so both fell through to the 500 branch — and wrote an `unclassified_request_error` log for what is simply a stale version id.

Now both routes check the version before calling the helper, exactly like `content`, and answer `404 {"error":"Artifact version not found"}`.

The same defect exists one level up, on both versions *list* routes: `/api/projects/:p/artifacts/:a/versions` and its Session-scoped sibling pass the id straight to `store.listProjectArtifactVersions()`, which throws a bare `Error("Artifact not found")` — again a 500 plus an `unclassified_request_error`. Both now check the project/Session and the artifact first and answer `404` naming what is missing (`Project not found: …` / `Artifact not found`); the success path is untouched.

`diff` keeps its two comparison-base cases apart, per the issue's expected shape:

- `?against=<id>` given but not found → **404** (a requested resource is missing);
- `?against` absent and the previous version does not exist → **400** `A previous artifact version is unavailable for comparison` (the request asks for a diff this artifact cannot have yet, which is a client-side input problem, not a missing `to` version).

The helpers are unchanged, so their defensive throws still hold for any caller that skips the route.

## Red → green

Red first (`6864420d`, test only), `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-missing.test.ts`:

```
content:    { status: 404, error: 'Artifact version not found' }
provenance: { status: 500, error: 'Internal server error' }
diff:       { status: 500, error: 'Internal server error' }
projects/:p/artifacts/:a/versions: { status: 500, error: 'Internal server error' }
# tests 1 / # pass 0 / # fail 1
```

Green after the fixes (`f67b91e9` for the version routes, `3c21ad91` for the list routes): same command → `1/1 pass`; `provenance.test.ts` + `dashboard.test.ts` → `86/86 pass`.

The test drives a real `createApiServer` (`offlineMcpTransport`, no runner) against a freshly created project/session, then asks all three version routes for the same random version id and compares status **and** error body, so a future 500 with a different message cannot pass quietly. It then asks the project-scoped list route for a random artifact id, the Session-scoped one, and a route with a random project id, each expecting 404.

## Ran / Not run

Ran (exit codes verbatim):

1. `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → **0**
2. `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → **0**
3. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-missing.test.ts` → **0** (`1/1`)
4. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/provenance.test.ts src/dashboard.test.ts` → **0** (`86/86`)
5. `pnpm architecture:check` (no lint script in this repo) → **1**, one failure `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`: sandbox `uv` cannot create a temp file (`Read-only file system (os error 30)`), unrelated to this diff.

Not run: the `?against=` 404 and the missing-previous 400 branches have no version fixture in this harness (creating an artifact version needs an execution), so the test pins the sibling-404 case the issue measured; the two `diff` branches are covered by the code path and stated above. The ST/E2E layer runs in CI.

## Diffstat

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…HEAD`:

```

```


## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: asking for the provenance, the diff, or the version list of an artifact or artifact version that does not exist (an expired link, a version removed by retention, a diff pointing at a deleted version) now answers `404` with the reason instead of `500 Internal server error`; the artifact dialog can say the version is gone instead of failing, and the server no longer logs a false `unclassified_request_error`.

pr:886.body:
Fixes #883

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What changed

`_NODE_LIMIT` is a hard cap of 500 nodes, and the contract at `query.py:319` says only results **beyond** it carry `truncated: True`. The flag was computed *after* a Cypher `LIMIT` bound to exactly the cap, so the Python side could never observe a 501st row: a complete 500-row answer and a cut one were indistinguishable and both reported `truncated: true`. The panel then drew `N of 500+ (truncated) match(es) in view` — the `+` asserting a further match that does not exist — and a session graph of exactly 500 nodes was badged as partial.

`query.py` now has one helper, `_cap_page(rows)`, returning the kept page and `len(rows) > _NODE_LIMIT` as the flag. Two shapes use it:

- **Cypher-driven reads** — `query_match` (`:431`), `by_node_type` (`:465`), `by_edge_type` (`:518`), `get_subgraph` (`:272`) and `_serialize_subgraph` (`:1298`): the Cypher limit is bound to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`, the page is cut to `_NODE_LIMIT` and the extra row alone decides the flag. `query_match`/`by_node_type` count the **raw rows** before `_to_hit`, the variant the issue prefers: a row dropped because its label has no id field is not a truncation. In `get_subgraph` the node-id set used to filter edges and synthesize the folded scope→product surrogates is built from the kept page, so no rendered edge points at a node the caller did not receive.
- **Assembled reads** — `get_scope_expansion` (`:898`) and `get_group_expansion` (`:1024`): these build their node set from several queries (children + produces subtree + edge endpoints; group members + one surrogate edge each) and have **no Cypher `LIMIT`** to raise, so `cap + 1` does not apply to them. The cap is applied to the assembled page instead, and an edge whose endpoint fell outside the page is dropped rather than rendered against an absent node. `get_group_expansion` and `_serialize_subgraph` were not in the issue's list of five: they carry the identical predicate (`len(...) >= _NODE_LIMIT` over a set that had not been cut at all — flagging a page they never truncated), so they are fixed in the same slice rather than left as the same defect on two more surfaces.

`total` keeps its previous meaning (the number of rows the response carries), so no client contract changes; `services/api` and the web panel forward the flag verbatim and need no edit.

## Red first

Test commit `9ce6d309` (test only), base `89cd2d30`:

```
$ cd services/memory-graph && uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q
14 failed in 0.50s
```

Three distinct failure shapes prove the tests reach the real paths:

- `assert True is False` — a complete 500-row answer reported as truncated (the reported defect, once per capped reader);
- `assert 500 == (500 + 1)` — the reader bound `$limit` to the cap itself, so the flag cannot be decided at all;
- `assert 501 == 500` — the two assembled readers returned all 501 nodes: the page had not been cut even though it was flagged.

Green at `e1957043`: the same command gives `14 passed in 0.15s`.

## Validation

The branch is rebased onto the current main tip `89cd2d30` (it was first based on a mirror that still served `8708320f`); `services/memory-graph` has no upstream drift between the two, and every reading below was taken again at the rebased commits.

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| new cap cases | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed` (7 readers × exactly-500 / 501) |
| memory-graph suite, tip | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ -q` | `123 passed, 15 warnings, 78 errors` |
| memory-graph suite, same tree without the new file (baseline) | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `109 passed, 14 warnings, 78 errors` |
| error set | `diff` of the `ERROR tests/...` lines of the two runs | identical (78 lines) |

The 78 errors are the pre-existing `@needs_neo4j` suite on this host — every one fails in setup with `Failed: needs a live Neo4j`, and the set is node-for-node the same with and without this diff (`187` collected before, `201` after the 14 new cases).

The cases assert more than the flag: for each reader a 501-row result must return exactly 500 rows; the assembled readers must drop the spine edge that points into the cut row; `_serialize_subgraph` and the four Cypher readers must bind `$limit` to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`.

Not run: anything needing a live Neo4j (the Cypher and the rendered panel text itself), because there is no graph on this host and `ci.yml` has no memory-graph job — the issue notes this, so the local pytest output above is the acceptance evidence. The TypeScript gates (`pnpm --recursive typecheck`, `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`) are not run: the diff touches no TypeScript.

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…e1dee252`: 3 files, `+656/−19` (`query.py` `+93/−19`, `tests/test_node_limit.py` `+320`, `tests/test_node_limit_rule.py` `+243`). No existing assertion is relaxed.

## Review fix (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` on `e1957043`, review `5773456818`)

`yuanzhou75` found that the new test file stopped the whole `UT` layer before a single case ran: the tagged audit (`test/support/tagged/python/science_tags.py:103-108`) accepts only `pytest.mark.parametrize` arguments that pass `ast.literal_eval`, and `CAP` / `CAP + 1` are a `Name` and a `BinOp`. Because the audit runs in `pytest_collect_file`, collection aborted with `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: .../test_node_limit.py:107` and `merge-gate` never evaluated. Fixed at `04ce9c89`, in the shape the review asked for:

- **All seven** parameter tables (lines 105/123/155/181/227/266/290) are now `[(500, False), (501, True)]` with their existing ids, and each case opens with `assert query._NODE_LIMIT == 500  # the table above is literal on purpose`. `CAP` stays and is still used by the body assertions, including the one requiring `$limit == CAP + 1`.
- One more registration defect the audit then exposed: the module carried **no** `science_tags` module mark, so once the audit passed the catalog step raised `ValueError: Missing tag group: category` — the same `PYTHON_COLLECTION_FAILED` for the layer, one step later. It now has the line every sibling in this suite has: `pytestmark = pytest.mark.science_tags(category='ut', os='linux', arch=('amd64', 'arm64'))`.

Verified at `04ce9c89` with the harness's own code, not a stand-in for it:

```
$ cd services/memory-graph && python3 -c "import sys; sys.path[:0]=['../../test/support/tagged/python']; import science_tags, pathlib; science_tags.audit_source(pathlib.Path('tests/test_node_limit.py'))"
(no output) exit 0        # before: ValueError: DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: tests/test_node_limit.py:107
```

```
$ PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 PYTHONPATH=<repo>/test/support/tagged/python \
  uv run --project services/memory-graph --extra test python -m pytest -p science_tags \
  --strict-markers --rootdir <repo> --collect-only -q \
  --science-root=<repo> --science-catalog=<file> $(ls services/memory-graph/tests/test_*.py)
201 tests collected in 0.99s     # exit 0
```

That is the command `coordinator.mjs`'s `collect()` runs — same `-p science_tags`, `--strict-markers`, `--rootdir`, `--science-catalog`, plugin autoload off — over every source `pythonSources('memory-graph')` globs. The catalog it wrote has 201 entries, 14 of them from this file, tagged `category:ut, os:linux, arch:amd64, arch:arm64, tier:l2, status:reviewed, ...`. Before the change the same command died at `:107`; with only the tables fixed it died again at the missing `category`.

| gate | command | reading at `04ce9c89` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tag audit | `science_tags.audit_source(tests/test_node_limit.py)` | exit 0 |
| tagged collection, whole project | `pytest -p science_tags --collect-only` over `services/memory-graph/tests/test_*.py` | `201 tests collected`, exit 0, 201 catalog entries |
| new cap cases | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed, 1 warning` |
| memory-graph suite | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ -q` | `129 passed, 16 warnings, 78 errors` |

The one warning the module adds is `PytestUnknownMarkWarning: Unknown pytest.mark.science_tags`, which every sibling module in this suite emits when pytest runs without the tagged plugin (`tests/test_logging_config.py` on its own gives `1 passed, 1 warning`); the plugin registers the marker and the collection above passes `--strict-markers`. The 78 errors are the unchanged `@needs_neo4j` setup failures.

No other file changed; the five commits stay separate: `9ce6d309` red test, `e1957043` fix, `04ce9c89` this registration fix, `86bbd1a5` the rule cases below, `e1dee252` the rule fix.

### Second review: one meaning for `truncated` (thread `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM6zusPi`)

The review found three counting conventions for one flag in the same PR. I took the first of its two options and made it the only one: **`truncated` means the backend returned more rows than `_NODE_LIMIT`, counted on the rows that were read and *before* a row is dropped for having no identity.**

Why this rule and not "count only renderable hits":

- **Only the returned-row count can be decided.** Each Cypher read binds `LIMIT` to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`, and that one extra row is the whole probe. Filtering first spends the probe on a row that cannot be rendered: 500 readable hits plus an unrenderable 501st would look *complete* although a renderable 502nd may exist, which is a completeness claim nothing checked. The returned-row count claims only what the extra row proves — the answer went past the cap.
- **It is the question the panel text asks.** `N of 500+ (truncated)` says the graph holds more matches than are shown. True when 501 rows came back even if one cannot be drawn; false when 501 came back and the response says "complete".
- **A short page stays complete.** 500 rows with one unrenderable row → 499 rendered, `truncated: false`: nothing was left unread, so there is nothing to disclose. Both directions are pinned below.

What changed:

- `get_subgraph` now caps the returned `(label, node)` rows and then runs `_node_identity`; `_serialize_subgraph` caps the returned rows and then runs `_to_hit`. Those are the two readers that capped the *filtered* list.
- `query_match`, `by_node_type`, `by_edge_type` already capped the returned rows; `query_match`'s comment argued the opposite and now states the rule, and the other two carry the same sentence.
- `get_scope_expansion` and `get_group_expansion` cap the assembled page, where every element already has an identity by construction, so "rows read" and "renderable rows" coincide there — no behaviour change, and the comment says so.
- `_cap_page`'s docstring states the rule once, and why the filter has to run after the cut. The review's nit (`nodes = list(hit_rows)` and a rebind on the next line) disappears with the restructure: `nodes` is built directly from the kept rows.

`tests/test_node_limit_rule.py` (new, 6 cases) pins the rule rather than the arithmetic: an unrenderable row as the 501st sets the flag on `query_match`, `by_edge_type`, `get_subgraph` and `_serialize_subgraph`, and a complete 500-row page that holds one unrenderable row stays complete on `query_match` and `get_subgraph`. Two of the six fail on `86bbd1a5` — `assert False is True` on the two readers that filtered first — and pass on `e1dee252`; the four that already held are there so a future reader cannot silently move one side into the other's shape again.

Deferred, deliberately not in this PR: `get_scope_expansion` / `get_group_expansion` still read every child/member and cut in Python, so the cap bounds the response and not the query work — same as before this PR, noted for follow-up.

Readings at `e1dee252`:

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rule cases | `pytest tests/test_node_limit_rule.py -q` | `6 passed` |
| cap cases | `pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed` |
| whole suite | `pytest tests/ -q` | `129 passed, 16 warnings, 78 errors` (the 78 unchanged) |
| tag audit, both files | `science_tags.audit_source(...)` | exit 0 each |
| tagged collection | `pytest -p science_tags --collect-only` over `services/memory-graph/tests/test_*.py` | `207 tests collected`, exit 0, 207 catalog entries |

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: a memory-graph search that matches exactly 500 nodes no longer says `500+ (truncated)` — it reports the count as complete — and a session graph of exactly 500 nodes is no longer badged as partial. A query that really has more than the cap still reports `truncated` and still returns 500 rows.
Compatibility and migration: none.

pr:888.body:
Fixes #885

## What this fixes

In an `zh-CN` session a tool card mixed two languages inside one frame: `输入` came from the message catalog, and the headings immediately below it — `Result`, `Error`, `Created files`, `Produced artifacts` — were English literals minted by the parser. The copy button inherited the English half, so its accessible label read `复制Result`.

The parser keeps its English labels on purpose: `parseToolResultSections` output is read by the existing parser test and is the value the per-section copy button copies, so translating there would change a contract to fix a rendering defect. The locale is applied where the card renders instead, in `apps/web/src/timeline/ToolIoSections.tsx`:
