pr:890.body:
Fixes #887

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What changed

`POST /api/sessions/:id/files` resolved `body.path` through `resolveWorkspaceFile` — which only refuses absolute paths and escapes — and wrote the result straight to disk. On a Windows workspace that makes `CON` target the console device and `nul.txt` fail with a raw `EPERM` the handler never classifies, so the client saw `500 Internal server error`. The reserved-device-name guard existed only in the upload path.

Chosen fix: **direction 2** — the predicate became a workspace invariant instead of an upload-only check.

- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` — new exported `isWindowsReservedDeviceName(name)`, sitting directly beside `assertWorkspacePath`. It matches the stems Windows resolves in every directory (`con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com1`–`com9`, `lpt1`–`lpt9`, `conin$`, `conout$`), strips trailing dots/spaces first (`nul.`, `CON `), and treats everything before the first dot as the stem, because the extension is irrelevant to a device. It is exported through the package index (`export * from "./workspace.js"`).
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts` — the write route walks **every segment** of `relative(workspaceRoot, target)` (the helper is a segment rule, so `CON/notes.txt` is refused before `mkdir("…/CON")`) and answers **400 naming the offending segment**. The route keeps accepting nested relative paths; the upload path's "plain basename only" rule is still not imposed here.

Why not direction 1 (call `sanitizeUploadFilename` in the handler): on this base that function has **no** reserved-name branch — it only rejects empty/NUL/absolute/traversal names, which `resolveWorkspaceFile` already enforces — so calling it today would be a no-op for the reported defect. Adding the rule inside it here would duplicate `#868`'s open hunk in the same function (and that PR exists to fix exactly that statement). Putting the predicate beside `assertWorkspacePath` gives both write paths one home once they meet.

### Relation to `#868` (open)

`#868` carries the identical rule inline in `sanitizeUploadFilename`. This diff deliberately does **not** touch `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts`, so the two do not overlap: when `#868` lands, its guard should call `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` and drop the inline copy (one hunk), leaving main with a single implementation. Whichever merges second does that; if `#868` lands first I will rebase this branch and make that change here.

## Review fix — P2, a device name in a directory segment (review `5773758545`, reviewed at `93af68c8`)

The first version applied the predicate to `basename(target)`, i.e. only the last segment. The route accepts nested relative paths, so `body.path = "CON/notes.txt"` had basename `notes.txt` and passed the guard; the write then reached `mkdir(dirname(target), { recursive: true })`. On a Windows host `CreateDirectory("…/CON")` fails (Node surfaces `EPERM`/`ENOENT`), which is the same unclassified 500 this PR removes; on Linux it creates an unportable `CON/` directory. The helper was already documented as a segment rule, so the call site was the narrow part.

Fixed as asked: the route now splits `relative(workspaceRoot, target)` on the host separator and refuses the first reserved segment. That subsumes the old last-segment case, and the message names the segment the client must change (`"CON"` for `CON/notes.txt`, `"nul.dir"` for `nul.dir/x.csv`) instead of a basename it never sent.

The predicate's doc comment no longer claims to be called from every writer. It states the per-segment rule, names where it is applied today (this route), and says that the agent-side workspace tools, which write through `assertWorkspacePath`, are not wired to it yet.

`WSP-005` (`services/api/src/server.test.ts`) now covers, in addition to the top-level names (`CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, `CON .csv`, and the named-stream forms added below) and the look-alikes from the first version:

- `CON/notes.txt` → 400, the message names `CON`
- `nul.dir/x.csv` → 400, the message names `nul.dir` (stem before the first dot is `nul`, and Windows refuses the directory too)
- `notes/CON.txt` → 400 (control: clean directory, device-name file — refused before this change too)
- `conifer/notes.txt` → 201 (control: the walk must not start refusing legitimate nested paths)

## Review fix — F1, a device's named stream (`nul:stream`, `CON:$DATA`)

The predicate cut the stem at the first dot only, so Windows' named-stream spellings slipped through: `nul:stream` kept its colon, `/^(?:con|prn|aux|nul|com[1-9]|lpt[1-9]|conin\$|conout\$)$/i` never matched, `CON:$DATA` likewise, and the write route answered 201 and created a file a Windows host resolves to the device's stream rather than to a file. Windows takes everything before the colon as the device, so the stem is now cut at the first dot and then at the first colon:

- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` — `name.split(".")[0]?.split(":")[0]?.replace(/[. ]+$/, "")`. `con:$DATA` → `con`, `nul:stream` → `nul`, `NUL:stream` → `NUL`; `conin$`/`conout$` keep the `$` because no colon splits them; the trailing-dot/space strip still runs last, so `nul.` and `CON ` match exactly as before.
- The route needed no change: it already walks every segment through the predicate, so `{"path":"nul:stream"}` now answers 400 naming `nul:stream`.
- `#903` is re-scoped: F1 (named streams) is fixed here, so the follow-up keeps only D2, the POSIX segment split (`CON\notes.txt` when the host separator is `/`).

## Red first

Original case at base `89cd2d30` (test commit `1c3259df`, now the first half of `WSP-005`):

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
not ok 1 - WSP-005 a reserved device name in a session file write answers 400 and names the file
  error: CON must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

The two new directory cases are red at the previous tip `93af68c8` (`0a1ca4fc` is test only). The loop stops at the first failure, so each was run as the only new case:

```
$ node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
  error: CON/notes.txt must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
$ (same command, `nul.dir/x.csv` as the only new case)
  error: nul.dir/x.csv must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
```

`notes/CON.txt` and `conifer/notes.txt` are green at `93af68c8` by design: they are the controls, so they carry no red reading.

Named-stream case at `c4fb33d4` (test commit `ddd14462`):

```
$ cd packages/workspace && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern isWindowsReservedDeviceName src/workspace.test.ts
not ok 1 - isWindowsReservedDeviceName treats a named stream as its device
  error: nul:stream names a device stream
  false !== true
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1

$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
not ok 1 - WSP-005 a reserved device name in a session file write answers 400 and names the file
  error: nul:stream must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

The API route test reads `@sciencediscovery/workspace` from `dist`, so the package was rebuilt from `c4fb33d4` before this red run; an older local `dist` otherwise masks the defect.

## Validation

The API tests load `@sciencediscovery/workspace` from its built `dist`, so the package is built first (CI does the same: the shared runner runs `pnpm build` before the heavy layers).

| tests typecheck | `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| predicate case | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern isWindowsReservedDeviceName src/workspace.test.ts` (`packages/workspace`) | `1/1` pass |
| route case | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts` (`services/api`) | `1/1` pass |
| workspace route group | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "WSP-00" src/server.test.ts` (`services/api`) | `3/3` pass |
| package UT | `npm test` (`packages/workspace`) | `101 tests / 101 pass / 0 fail` |
| api server suite | `node --import tsx --test src/server.test.ts` (`services/api`) | `109 tests / 108 pass / 1 fail`: `PDF upload extracts full text and tables into the session workspace` needs `reportlab` in `services/paper/.venv` (environment, not this diff) |
| api UT (full, earlier run at `c4fb33d4`) | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` | `1866 tests / 1860 pass / 6 fail`: 5 environment (`No module named uvicorn` in `services/evolve/.venv`; `No module named 'reportlab'` ×3; missing `@openai/codex-linux-x64`), 1 load flake in `evolution/orchestrator.test.ts` (`timed out waiting for the run to finish`) that passes on its own (`--test-name-pattern "settled"` → `3/3`). None touch this diff. |

Not run: a real Windows host — the guard is deliberately platform-independent, so the Linux route test exercises the same code path; there is no Windows-only branch in it.

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…HEAD`: 4 files, `+134/−6` (`workspace.test.ts` `+20/−1`, `workspace.ts` `+29`, `http/index.ts` `+17/−5`, `server.test.ts` `+68`). No existing assertion is relaxed; the two edits to existing test lines are the look-alike loop gaining `conifer/notes.txt` and the top-level refusal loop gaining `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA`.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: writing a session file whose name or directory component is a Windows device (`CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, `CON .csv`, `CON/notes.txt`, `nul.dir/x.csv`, and the named-stream forms `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA`) now answers 400 naming the offending segment, on every platform, instead of returning 201 and creating a file a Windows host cannot open (or a write that silently goes to the console or fails as a 500). Ordinary names such as `conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `com10.csv` and `conifer/notes.txt` are unaffected.
Compatibility and migration: none — only names Windows itself cannot create are refused.

pr:904.body:
Desktop's built-in source switches currently change connector permissions, while Web source selection changes the sources sessions use by default. This can make a source appear enabled in Desktop without selecting its tools for an ordinary session. This PR makes the Desktop system settings page edit the global default source selection through `enabledConnectorIds`.

## Data source selection

- Rename the page to **Data sources** and add **Use by default** checkboxes for built-in and custom sources.
- Save the global `enabledConnectorIds` list while preserving unrelated overrides, instead of writing `plugins["connector.<id>"].enabled` for built-in selections. Retain the existing `web`-only fallback when the effective list is absent.
- Replace bulk enable/disable actions with **Select all / Clear selection** for listed sources. These actions change selection without reconnecting or disabling custom services.
- Keep custom MCP connection configuration separate: **Enable service** remains in the edit modal, alongside the existing edit, test and delete actions.
- Display catalog/service readiness independently of selection. Selecting a source does not establish that its service is ready or that its tools can be called.
- Update English/Chinese text and settings-page rendering tests.

This is a global defaults editor. It does not introduce a Desktop per-session selector or change backend selection, inheritance, permissions, or tool execution contracts. No settings migration is included.

pr:905.body:
Desktop run failures expose raw provider diagnostics in the main conversation, including English error tokens in the Chinese UI. This PR presents localized recovery guidance first and keeps the original diagnostic information available under an expandable **Technical details** section.

## Failure presentation

- Map all seven `RunFailureCode` values to English/Chinese summaries: timeout, unauthorized, rate-limited, transport-error, server-error, invalid-tool-call and semantic-error.
- Use a generic fallback for missing or unrecognized codes. Resolve the active language when rendering.
- Keep the original error code and message in the expandable details block rather than replacing or discarding diagnostic information.
- Use neutral wording for `semantic-error`, since the backend uses it as a catch-all classification and it does not establish that a model service rejected the request.
- Apply the same localized summary and folded raw-message presentation to persisted `timeout_notice` messages.
- Add coverage for language switching, fallback codes, replayed failures, diagnostic preservation and a failed tool inside a successful run.

## Scope and remaining limitation

A timeout notice and a run-failed status can still both appear. The client cannot reliably associate a `timeout_notice` message with a specific run, so this PR keeps both visible. Reliable deduplication remains a follow-up requiring a suitable association contract. This partially addresses #846; it does not complete that issue's duplicate-alert criterion.

pr:906.body:
First batch of the first-message latency plan (#799): warm the MCP catalog while the user is still on the ready screen, and stop paying a second `skills.list` RPC on every run that imports nothing. Together they address the two largest measured chunks of the first message — the ~48s stdio catalog cold-start (field) and part of the ~4s `skills.list` x3 chain in the SD-side run preparation.

## Warm the MCP catalog right after agent-ready (S1)

On a fresh install the bundled stdio MCP servers spawn and enumerate their tools on the first chat run; field measurements put this chunk at ~48s of the 60-135s first-message latency. The shell's `watchAgentReady` already polls `/agent/info`, and the moment `jiuwenswarm.reachable` turns true it now issues `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload` in the background — the MCP settings page's refresh request, and the one endpoint that actually connects and enumerates. The spawns and tool enumeration then overlap the ready screen instead of the first message.

The endpoint choice was corrected during live verification (commit ef65229e): the first revision fired `GET /api/mcp/sources`, which only reads the cached manifest/status list — on a running stack it answered 200 in ~1s and spawned nothing, and the first chat run still paid the full catalog load. The reload endpoint spawned every bundled source in ~3.3s on the same stack, with the stdio processes visible on the host. Verified locally: catalog warmed at boot → a first message afterwards pays zero MCP chunk (E1.6 evidence pack).

Best-effort by contract: failures are logged to `shell.log` (`[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources/reload -> <status>` or a failure line) and never surface to the user. When the warmup loses the race, the run path re-runs the same steps — no behavioural fork, only a head start.

## One `skills.list` per sync when nothing imports (S3a)

`SkillSync.sync()` ran `skills.list` twice per run: `_sync()` listed to diff staged skills against JiuwenSwarm's, and the tail listed again to refresh the adapter's `directories` map. That map only carries ScienceDiscovery-marked skills, which can only appear through this adapter's own imports — a run that imports nothing changes no directory, so the second listing was the first one's answer. `_sync()` now reports whether it imported anything; `sync()` re-lists only then. The import path is byte-for-byte today's behaviour (pre-import listing + post-import refresh); the steady-state path saves one RPC round trip per run and still populates the map from the single listing, including right after an adapter restart.

This is step S3a of the run-preparation-chain plan; S3c (acceptance-path parallelisation) remains a follow-up.

## One `skills.list` per run, cached 30s with write-through invalidation (S3b)

After S3a a steady-state run still paid two `skills.list` RPCs: `_sync()` listed to diff staged skills, and the API's reconcile listed again through `GET /agent/skills`. Both read the same list, and the adapter performs every write to that list itself (`skills.import_local` in `_import`, `skills.toggle` in `set_enabled`) — so a short-TTL cache with write-through invalidation serves both reads from one fetch while keeping the cached answer at least as fresh as the last write. Back-to-back runs staging the same skills now send **one `skills.list` per run instead of two**; an import or a toggle invalidates immediately, and a zero TTL restores today's fetch-every-read behaviour as the kill switch.

A cache hit never changes what JiuwenSwarm receives: import decisions still run against the freshest answer the adapter itself has written, and a direct JW-side edit can only stay invisible for the 30s TTL — the trade the plan documents. Step S3b of the run-preparation plan.

## Validation

- `pnpm --dir win_desktop build` — clean (esbuild).
- `pnpm --dir win_desktop typecheck` — clean (tsc).
- `pnpm --dir win_desktop test` — 164 pass / 0 fail (5 first-chat-warmup tests: URL/header construction, POST method to the reload endpoint, happy path, failure propagation, timeout bounds; baseline was 159 before this change).
- Live stack check (dev stack, 2026-11-05): `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload` with the shell's auth header returned 200 in ~3.3s and spawned all 13 bundled stdio sources (`ready`); the prior `GET` on the same stack returned 200 in ~1s and spawned nothing — this is what motivated the endpoint fix.
- Adapter: `uv run pytest tests/` (services/adapter) — 292 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `test_diagnostics.py::test_private_rotating_file`, is pre-existing on this host: it fails identically on the unmodified base commit in the same worktree (verified with `git stash`), and the change does not touch diagnostics. All 15 skills tests pass, including 5 that count the RPCs: a no-import sync lists exactly once and still populates the directories map (S3a); an importing sync still lists twice (pre-import + post-import refresh, S3a unchanged); two `listed()` calls within the TTL share one RPC, a no-import sync and the next `listed()` share one RPC (S3b); an import and a toggle each invalidate so the next read re-fetches (S3b); a zero TTL restores fetch-every-read (S3b kill switch).
- Not covered here: packaged-install validation (GUI-interactive install, three boot profiles, cold-install first message). That needs an installer build and a quiet machine; it is scheduled and will be reported before this PR is marked ready.

## E2E user journeys

Local stack (dev tree, base 79d26dd6 + this branch), mock OpenAI endpoint on loopback answering SSE in ~30 ms, quiet load window, same-window pairs (D5 discipline: fresh session first message vs same-session second, median of 3):

1. **Warmup fires end-to-end (the S1 claim).** Desktop shell launched against the live stack; `shell.log` recorded `[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources/reload -> 200`, and the API log recorded `mcp_catalog_loaded durationMs=3846 failedServerCount=0 serverCount=3 toolCount=39` in the same second. The 6 bundled stdio MCP server processes were visible on the host before any message was sent. PASS.
2. **First/second message, web-only connectors (E1 anatomy口径).** First message 5.5s / 9.4s / (one round lost to a transient Windows file-lock EPERM, retried clean) — median ≈ 5.5-9.4s; second message 3.5s median. The 2026-11-03 baseline on the old base was 26.09s / 8.67s; the drop is mostly upstream work landed in the meantime (patch 0020 moved the 12.4s observability import off the hot-start path) plus the quiet load window — this pair is reported as no-regression evidence, not as S1/S3a attribution. PASS (no regression).
3. **First message with an MCP tool call, cold vs warm catalog (the S1 mechanism).** Session with `enabledConnectorIds: ["web","uniprot"]`, mock model answers the prompt with one `mcp__uniprot__search` call. Cold catalog (API boot refresh had failed: `mcp_connection_failed … MCP connection timeout` × 3 servers at startup, as it does on this host): run completed in ~7.7s with the catalog load inside the run. Warm catalog (after `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload`, the exact S1 request): run completed in 5.7s, tool call answered in 16ms, no connection events in the run window. Delta ≈ 2s on this warm-filesystem dev box; the field cold-install figure the plan cites is ~48s (E1.6 evidence). PASS — the warmup demonstrably moves the catalog load out of the first run.
4. **S3a mechanism.** Adapter unit tests count the RPCs directly (a no-import sync sends exactly one `skills.list`, an importing sync still sends two); the dev-stack venv still runs the pre-S3a adapter build, so the in-stack numbers above are the conservative (two-list) path. PASS by unit test; in-stack A/B lands when the venv is refreshed.

Failure attribution: the only run failures in the session were transient host file-lock EPERMs on skill-snapshot rename (Windows antivirus/indexer) — retried clean, not product failures. The pre-existing `test_private_rotating_file` failure is documented in Validation above.

Commands: `node .tmp/mock-openai.mjs` (mock, SSE instant), `node .tmp/fml-ab.mjs 3` and `node .tmp/fml-s1-ab.mjs cold|warm` (drivers; client-side SSE timing + event timeline). Counts: journey 1 = 1/1 PASS; journey 2 = 5/6 runs clean (1 env-retry); journey 3 = 1/1 cold + 1/1 warm PASS; journey 4 = 10/10 unit tests.

## Release

Release category: `release:performance` (GitHub label pending a maintainer — the author has read-only access to the upstream repository and cannot apply it).
User impact: faster first message on installed builds (the MCP catalog no longer cold-starts inside the first chat run) and slightly cheaper every run (one fewer `skills.list` round trip in the steady state). No UI change, no configuration change, no behaviour change on failure paths.
Compatibility and migration: none.

pr:908.body:
Fixes #884

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What is wrong

`GET /api/sessions/:session/artifact-versions/:version/diff` answered **500 `Internal server error`** when either version of the pair is not textual, and logged a false `unclassified_request_error`. `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:357` threw a plain `Error("Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions")`, whose prose matches no client-input pattern in `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` and no not-found mapper in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, so the top-level catch classified a client-input problem as a server fault.

Measured at `7057aaf6` with two `application/zip` versions of one artifact in one session (red commit `0be111de` only):

```
GET /api/sessions/<id>/artifact-versions/<version>/diff
500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
```

The same request, with logging configured the way `startPlatform` does (not by `createApiServer` alone), wrote:

```
ERROR [api] event=unclassified_request_error errorMessage="Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions" method=GET path=/api/sessions/<id>/artifact-versions/<version>/diff status=500
```

## The fix — option 2 from the issue, in the helper

`artifactVersionDiff` now throws `new ApiStatusError(400, "Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions")`. The rejection is classified by **class** (the top-level catch answers `ApiStatusError.statusCode` before any prose matching), and it sits where the rule lives, so every caller of the helper answers the same 400 instead of only this route. No new message pattern was added to `isKnownClientInputError`.

The versions both exist; this is not a missing resource, which is why it is a 400 and not the 404 family `#881` adds.

### Why the route was not touched (overlap with #881)

`#881` (ours, open) rewrites the `diff` route block in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` for the missing-`to` / missing-`against` cases. Hoisting the media-type check into that same block would (a) collide textually with `#881`, and (b) put the from-version resolution in two places: the route would have to repeat what the helper already computes, and the next caller of the helper would get the 500 again. This fix touches only `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts`; the two behaviours are complementary (`#881` = missing version, this = both present but not comparable), so whichever lands second keeps both without a conflict.

### Import note

`services/api/src/runs/index.ts` already imports `artifacts/index.ts`, so importing `ApiStatusError` from `runs` inside `artifacts` would have closed a cycle between two large modules. The class therefore lives in `services/api/src/http/api-status-error.ts`, which imports nothing; `runs/index.ts` imports it and re-exports it (its public API is unchanged, so the existing import in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` still works), and `artifacts/index.ts` imports the leaf directly. No reverse edge was added and no cycle exists.

The leaf move keeps the identity check honest: `services/api/src/http/index.ts` still matches `error instanceof ApiStatusError` against the class the helper throws, which the new test proves by driving that exact path — a divergent class object would answer 500, not the 400 asserted there.

## Red → green

`services/api/src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` (test-only commit `0be111de`) seeds versions through `SessionStore.createArtifactVersion` and asks the real route, so no execution is driven: an `application/zip` pair, a pair that switches from `text/markdown` to `application/zip`, and a `text/markdown` control pair that must keep diffing.

Red at `7057aaf6`:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts
not ok 1 - a non-textual artifact pair answers a client error instead of 500
  error: |-
    binary pair must answer 400 with the reason, not 500
      body: { error: 'Internal server error' }
      status: 500
# tests 1 / # pass 0 / # fail 1
```

Green at `207243a7` (same command): `1 test / 1 pass / 0 fail`, exit 0. That run was still green by luck — see the review fix below.

The false log is gone in the same manual repro: `STATUS 400 {"error":"Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions"}`, `grep -c unclassified_request_error` → `0`, and the request is logged as `http_request_failed … statusCode=400`.

## Review fix — the fixture seeded after the server's `ready` chain

`sciencediscovery-bot`'s thread on `artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts:130` is right and this is a test-only correction: `createApiServer` returns before `ready` (which ends in `store.load()`) has run, and the fixture seeded after `server.listen`, so the test passed only when the seeds landed before that load. Two commits, no product code changed:

- `b3eb58b8` makes the ordering explicit: a request settles `ready` before the seeds. It is red, deterministically, on a machine that starts the server quickly:
  ```
  not ok 1 - a non-textual artifact pair answers a client error instead of 500
      binary pair must answer 400 with the reason, not 500
      +     error: 'Internal server error'
      +   status: 500
  ```
  (the 500 is the pre-fix behaviour: the route's `store` has already loaded a catalog without these versions, `getArtifactVersion` returns `undefined`, and `artifacts/index.ts` throws the plain `Error("Artifact version not found")`.)
- `76e911b5` removes the race instead of winning it: `startHttpFixture` is split into `createFixture` + `startHttpServer(context, fixture)`, the test writes every version first and starts the server afterwards, so `ready` loads a catalog that already contains them. No wait, retry or timeout is involved.

Green five consecutive runs of the same command, one process each:

```
[run 1] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 2] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 3] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 4] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 5] # pass 1 # fail 0
```

`tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` exit 0; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` exit 0. This review fix alone is `1 file, +14/−7` (`git diff --stat 207243a7..76e911b5`).

## Validation

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| new test, red | `node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` | `1/0/1`, exit 1 (at `7057aaf6` + test commit) |
| new test, green | same | `1 test / 1 pass / 0 fail`, exit 0 (at `207243a7`) |
| UT slice for the touched module | `node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts src/artifact-lifecycle.test.ts src/provenance.test.ts src/dashboard.test.ts` | `88 tests / 88 pass / 0 fail`, exit 0 (at `207243a7`) |
| typecheck (api) | `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` | exit 0, 0 errors |
| typecheck (tests project) | `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | exit 0, 0 errors |

Environment note, so the numbers are reproducible: this worktree's `node_modules` predates the current lockfile and the sandbox cannot write to the pnpm store, so `@types/ssh2` (declared by `packages/executor`) and the `packages/feedback-worker/node_modules` workspace link were missing before the first typecheck run. Without them the api typecheck reported 18 errors, all in `packages/executor/src/ssh-connection.ts` / `ssh-keys.ts` (missing `ssh2` declarations) and the tests typecheck 4 in `packages/feedback-worker` — none in the touched files. Installing the declared `@types/ssh2` into the local `node_modules` and adding that workspace link brings both to exit 0; no repository file was changed for it.

Not run: the full `services/api` UT suite (only the module slice above), the L2/ST/E2E layers, and a real server with a real artifact-producing execution — the route test seeds the catalog directly because the media-type rule is checked before any CAS read, which is exactly the point the issue makes.

`git diff --stat 7057aaf6…HEAD`: 4 files, `+247/−13` (`artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` +199, `http/api-status-error.ts` +34, `runs/index.ts` +6/−12, `artifacts/index.ts` +8/−1), 5 commits (`0be111de` test, `b6de0d8e` fix, `207243a7` the class move that removes the import cycle, `b3eb58b8` red and `76e911b5` green for the review fix above).

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: comparing two binary artifact versions (two `.zip` uploads, a text version against a later binary one) now answers `400 {"error":"Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions"}` instead of `500 Internal server error`, and the server no longer logs a false `unclassified_request_error` for a request the client can avoid. Textual pairs still diff as before.

Compatibility and migration: none — the 400 body is the message the helper already carried; only its status and classification change.

pr:913.body:
`search_preprints` asked the provider for `/{days}d/0/json`. bioRxiv and medRxiv answer that request with HTTP 200, an empty `collection`, and a "Both dates must be in yyyy-mm-dd format" message, so the gateway read a rejected request as "no matches" and the assistant told users the window contained no preprints.

## Dated-range requests

`config/external-urls.json` now carries a `yyy-mm-dd` range template instead of the invalid `{days}d` form, and `_preprint_search` computes the window in UTC (`days=1` yields a single-day range). UTC avoids "today" landing in the provider's future.

## Provider failures are no longer silent

A `messages[0].status` that reports a rejected request now raises instead of returning a clean empty result. Invalid requests still return HTTP 200, so this status message is the only failure signal the provider gives.

An empty window is not a rejection: the provider answers one with its own status, `no posts found`, and no `total`. That status is accepted and mapped onto the existing empty-window warning — "The provider reports no preprints published between …" — so a `days=1` search on a quiet day, or a category with nothing in the window, returns an empty result rather than a tool error.

## Newest-first scanning within the tool deadline

The provider serves a window oldest-first, and its trailing path segment is a record offset, not a page number: measured on both servers, cursor 1 starts one record after cursor 0, so adjacent cursors share 29 of 30 records. The search starts at the newest offset and walks backwards, dedupes DOIs that shift between pages while the window moves, and reports how much of the window it actually scanned. Previously the warning implied the whole window had been filtered.

The walk has to fit the 30 s deadline that the Node MCP transport gives a search tool call, so it spends a wall-clock budget rather than counting pages:

- one HTTP client for the whole scan, so pages reuse the connection instead of paying a TLS handshake each;
- every request on this path, the first page included, is bounded by the same deadline;
- the newest page alone first, because it usually fills `limit`, then up to four pages in flight;
- a 20 s stop, leaving headroom for the answer to return, with the warning saying the scan stopped early;
- each page gets the budget that is left, so a slow page costs that page and not the
  pages of its batch that already answered;
- one reconnect when the provider closes an idle keep-alive connection between pages.

The page fetched to learn `total` (offset 0) is reused as the tail of the walk instead of being downloaded and discarded; coverage counts distinct offsets, so the reused tail is not reported twice.

## Validation

- Gateway suite: 43 tests, 43 passed, 0 failed.
  `PYTHONPATH=services/gateway/src python -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_*.py'`
  (run from the branch head with the service virtualenv because workspace dependency preparation could not complete in this environment — see below).
- L1 slice on this head: planned 4, executed 4, passed 4, failed 0, skipped 0.
- Live provider smoke, no mocks:
  - Empty window: bioRxiv `liver`, 1 day, `category=zoology` → 0 records, warning "The provider reports no preprints published between 2026-11-05 to 2026-11-05", answered in 2.5 s. Before this round the same call raised.
  - medRxiv `diabetes`, 30 days, limit 3 → 2 records from the newest page, "Scanned 30 of 1873 … stopped at its 20-second time budget". The host used for this smoke fetched 6–9 s per page at the time, so the budget, not the scan design, ended it.
  - bioRxiv `liver`, 30 days, limit 5 → "Scanned 30 of 7257", stopped at the time budget, 0 records from that page; the same query returned 5 records when the host's per-page latency was under 2 s.
  - `lookup_doi` for a returned bioRxiv DOI: still returns its versions (no regression).
- Not run locally: UT, ST and E2E. The shared runner's preparation (`uv sync`) stalls downloading dependency wheels from the PyPI CDN at roughly 20 KB/s in this environment; switching to a mirror conflicts with the committed lockfile. No assertion was weakened or skipped to work around it. The gateway suite above exercises the changed code, and CI runs the full layers on this head.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED: the mocked browser E2E layer was not run for the reason above. The affected path is an MCP tool invoked by the assistant rather than a browser journey; the live provider smoke in Validation is the substitute evidence for it. Tested SHA: ec7b75d6.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: bioRxiv and medRxiv searches return matching recent preprints instead of an always-empty list; a rejected provider request surfaces as an error rather than as "no results"; an empty date window stays an empty result. The tool warning now states how much of the date window was scanned and whether the scan stopped early.

Compatibility and migration: the configuration key `data_sources.preprints.details_by_days_template` is replaced by `data_sources.preprints.details_by_range_template`; a deployment that uses a customized copy of `config/external-urls.json` must apply the same rename. Running gateway processes must be restarted because the URL table is cached in-process.

Labels: `release:fix`, `bug` and `bot-reviewed` are applied.

pr:915.body:
Fixes #914

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## Problem

`UT` on PR #890 (tip `fdb835fb`, run `42015883088`, job `127206585414`) failed `services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py::ArchitectureBoundaryTests::test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` with a `FileNotFoundError` instead of an assertion:

```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
'.../services/api/.tmp/agent-skill-creator-1793877061398-12103/projects/.../skill-snapshots/.716ffbc5-....skill-snapshot/antibody-design/scripts/install_pipeline_deps.sh'
```

The UT layer read `planned 6366 / executed 6366 / passed 6365 / failed 1 / skipped 0`; the group holding it was `1 failed, 30 passed in 4.55s` (the other 30 gateway Python tests ran normally). The same test set was green on the previous tip of that branch (`c4fb33d4`, run `41890794011`), and the failing PR's diff touches neither `services/gateway` nor `services/api/.tmp`.

## Cause

`_files()` walks `services/api`, `packages`, `apps/web` and `test/api` and skips only `__pycache__`, `dist`, `node_modules`. `services/api/.tmp` is a live runtime workspace root, not source: `services/api/src/server.test.ts` and the skill-creator paths create session trees there while other workers run and delete them after. The walk lists a path, the owning test removes it, `read_text()` raises, and the boundary assertion is replaced by an error that has nothing to do with the pull request's diff. The cost is a full CI cycle plus a rerun that we cannot trigger ourselves.

## Red first

Two deterministic regression tests at `7057aaf6` (test commit `1c7817a2`). Both create their probe under `services/api/.tmp` and remove it in cleanup:

```
FAILED services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py::GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests::test_a_workspace_file_removed_after_listing_is_skipped
E   FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../services/api/.tmp/probe-boundary-3.ts'

FAILED services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py::GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests::test_a_generated_workspace_is_not_walked
E   AssertionError: 'content: services/api/.tmp/probe-boundary-3.ts' unexpectedly found in ['content: services/api/.tmp/probe-boundary-3.ts']

2 failed, 3 passed, 1 warning in 7.71s
```

The first reproduces the CI shape exactly without relying on timing: the listing yields a path that is already gone when the walk reads it. The second is the `.tmp` root itself being walked as source. Both fail on `main` and pass after the fix.

## After fix

Two changes, one file:

- `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` gains `.tmp`: like `dist`, it is generated runtime data, not source.
- The read side treats `FileNotFoundError` as "the file vanished after the listing" and skips that path: a source file removed mid-walk cannot be asserted on, and an assertion is not what we want to raise here.

```
$ python3 -m pytest services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py -q
5 passed, 1 warning in 3.93s
```

pr:921.body: Fixes #919 ## Problem PR #892 gives `cancelled` its own summary bucket in `apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx`, and `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` covers only that one case — a single `cancelled` record. Nothing pinned the other side of the same rule: `queued`, `running`, `unknown` and a record with **no `state`** must keep falling through to `unconfirmed`, and a mixed notice must summarise one entry per bucket. A future bucket, or a reordering of the filter chain, reclassifies those states with the suite still green. ## Cause The outcome line is built from four filters over `notice.records`: ``` completed = records.filter(state === "completed") failed = records.filter(state === "failed") cancelled = records.filter(state === "cancelled") unconfirmed = records.filter(state !== "completed" && state !== "failed" && state !== "cancelled") ``` `RuntimeNoticeRecord.state` is optional (`packages/schema/src/session.ts:138`), so the catch-all is the only thing that keeps every state without a bucket of its own visible — and after #892 shifted that boundary, no test asserted the fall-through side or the per-bucket join. ## Change One file, tests only — no product code: `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx`, **+36/−0** (1 file). 1. `a notice under way still summarises as unconfirmed, not as its own bucket` — `records` with `queued`, `running`, `unknown`, and one object with no `state` renders `4 unconfirmed` and no `cancelled` bucket. 2. `a mixed notice summarises each outcome bucket instead of collapsing them` — `1 completed + 1 failed + 1 cancelled` renders `1 completed · 1 failed · 1 cancelled` plus the three badges. Branch base: `2908e9e8` (`#892`'s merge commit), so the tree below is the tree CI sees. ## Red-first evidence Command, from `apps/web`: `node --import tsx --test tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` ### Case 1 — break the catch-all Temporarily adding `&& record.state !== "running"` to the `unconfirmed` filter (the regression the test exists to catch: a state silently losing the fall-through). Only the new case goes red, and the rendered summary drops from `4 unconfirmed` to `3`: ``` ok 2 - each record opens the matching activity record not ok 3 - a notice under way still summarises as unconfirmed, not as its own bucket ok 4 - a mixed notice summarises each outcome bucket instead of collapsing them # tests 6 # pass 5 # fail 1 ``` ``` The input did not match the regular expression /4 unconfirmed/. Input: '… 3 unconfirmed …' ``` Restored with `git checkout -- apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx`. ### Case 2 — remove the `cancelled` bucket #892 added Temporarily dropping the `cancelled` filter row and letting `cancelled` fall back into the catch-all (that is, reverting #892's product change in place). Both the new mixed case and #892's own case go red: ``` not ok 4 - a mixed notice summarises each outcome bucket instead of collapsing them not ok 6 - a cancelled execution is summarised as cancelled, not unconfirmed # tests 6 # pass 4 # fail 2 ``` ``` The input did not match the regular expression /1 completed · 1 failed · 1 cancelled/. Input: '… 1 completed · 1 failed · 1 unconfirmed …' ``` Restored again; `git status` shows only the test file. ### Green, and the reads ``` ok 1 - a runtime notice reads as what finished and how, never as the model prompt ok 2 - each record opens the matching activity record ok 3 - a notice under way still summarises as unconfirmed, not as its own bucket ok 4 - a mixed notice summarises each outcome bucket instead of collapsing them ok 5 - a notice persisted without records keeps its count summary and still hides the prompt ok 6 - a cancelled execution is summarised as cancelled, not unconfirmed # tests 6 # pass 6 # fail 0 ``` Ran: - `node --import tsx --test tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` (in `apps/web`) — `6 tests / 6 pass / 0 fail`; the two red-first runs above are `5 / 1` and `4 / 2`. - `../../node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` (in `apps/web`) — exit 0, no output. - `git diff --numstat upstream/main..HEAD` — `36 0 apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx`. Not run: - `pnpm ci:l1` locally — its prepare step runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which cannot write the local pnpm store here; CI runs L1 on this PR. - UT/ST as a layer locally — the numbers above are the same file run directly with the same runner (`tsx --test`).

pr:922.body:
Fixes #665

`web_fetch`'s public-URL guard still lets four IPv6 families through even though each one carries an IPv4 address the guard already knows how to judge. A model-supplied URL such as `http://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/` or `http://[2002:a9fe:a9fe::]/` reaches loopback or the link-local metadata endpoint, while the equivalent `::ffff:127.0.0.1` is rejected. This closes those four holes and pins both directions — blocked literals stay blocked, public embedded addresses stay routable.

## What was wrong

`ipv6Blocked()` only consults `ipv4Blocked()` for IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) and IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d`) forms, where the embedded IPv4 address sits in the last two hextets. Four other families carry the same address somewhere else:

| family | prefix | where the IPv4 address sits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NAT64 well-known | `64:ff9b::/96` | last 32 bits |
| NAT64 local-use | `64:ff9b:1::/48` | last 32 bits |
| 6to4 | `2002::/16` | hextets 2–3 |
| IPv4-translated | `::ffff:0:0:0/96` | last 32 bits, after `ffff` and 16 zero bits |
| Teredo | `2001:0::/32` | last 32 bits, bitwise inverted |
| site-local (deprecated) | `fec0::/10` | no IPv4 — the range itself is non-public |

No branch inspected those positions, so each form fell through to `return false`.

## What changed

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts` gains one helper, `dotted(high, low)`, and `ipv6Blocked()` learns to extract the embedded address for the six rows above and hand it to the existing `ipv4Blocked()` — the documented prefixes are matched, the address is decoded, and the verdict is the same predicate that already rejects `127.0.0.1` and `169.254.169.254`. There is no second copy of the IPv4 block list, no blanket range ban, and no refactor of the existing mapped/compatible branches: `ipv6Blocked()` keeps its shape and the new decoders delegate.

Teredo needs the inversion because the client address is stored XOR-ed with `0xffffffff`; `2001:0:808:808::80ff:fffe` therefore decodes to client `127.0.0.1`, not to the relay `128.255.255.254`.

The test computes nothing itself: it asserts the same 15 cases from both directions, plus the literal path (`assertPublicUrl("http://[...]/")`) and the resolver path (`assertPublicUrl(url, resolver)`), so a future change that fixes only literals fails.

## Red first

The new test, run against the unfixed `url-guard.ts` (`git checkout <test-commit> -- url-guard.ts`):

```
# Subtest: web_fetch judges NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local literals by their embedded IPv4
not ok 11 - web_fetch judges NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local literals by their embedded IPv4
  ---
  error: |-
    64:ff9b::7f00:1

    false !== true

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  name: 'AssertionError'
  expected: true
  actual: false
  operator: 'strictEqual'
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

The loop stops at the first failing literal, so the same nine blocked literals were also probed one by one against the unfixed predicate — each line below is one assertion that fails with `false !== true`:

```
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("64:ff9b::7f00:1"), true, "NAT64 /96 -> 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe"), true, "NAT64 /96 -> 169.254.169.254")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("64:ff9b:1::7f00:1"), true, "NAT64 /48 -> 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("2002:7f00:1::"), true, "6to4 -> 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("2002:a9fe:a9fe::"), true, "6to4 -> 169.254.169.254")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("::ffff:0:7f00:1"), true, "IPv4-translated -> 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("::ffff:0:a9fe:a9fe"), true, "IPv4-translated -> 169.254.169.254")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("fec0::1"), true, "site-local")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("2001:0:808:808::80ff:fffe"), true, "Teredo -> client 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
```

## After the fix

```
# tests 16
# pass 16
# fail 0
```

The reverse direction is asserted in the same test, so the fix cannot be "block the prefix": `64:ff9b::808:808`, `64:ff9b:1::808:808`, `2002:808:808::`, `::ffff:0:808:808`, `2001:0:808:808::f7f7:f7f7` (Teredo for `8.8.8.8`) and `2606:4700:4700::1111` all stay routable, both as literals and through `assertPublicUrl`.

Diffstat against `main` `f4dd1813`:

```
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts | 49 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts      | 29 +++++++++++--
 2 files changed, 75 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

Ran:
- `node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts` in `packages/data-source` — `# tests 16 # pass 16 # fail 0`; the same command on the unfixed source is the red above (`# pass 15 # fail 1`).
- `tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- Per-literal probe of the nine blocked addresses against the unfixed predicate — the nine `false !== true` lines above.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` (full layers) were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser/API/CLI journey was added: the change is a predicate inside the `web_fetch` URL guard, and the mocked E2E subset does not exercise NAT64/6to4 literals.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: a model-supplied `web_fetch` URL that encodes a private, loopback or link-local IPv4 address in NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated, Teredo or site-local form is now rejected with `PublicUrlError` instead of being fetched; public addresses in the same forms keep working.

Compatibility and migration: none. Public NAT64/6to4 egress is explicitly covered by the reverse assertions above.

pr:924.body:
Fixes #839

A delimited dataset preview told the reader the file had as many columns as its widest line. A two-column `.csv` with one 5,000-field row was announced as `The file has 5000 columns; the preview shows the first 1001.` — a statement about a schema the file does not have. The column count now comes from the header; the wide row is reported as the cells it loses (`clippedCells`), not as columns.

## What was wrong

`parseDelimitedTable` derived one number, `totalColumns = Math.max(header.length, widest)`, and used it for two different jobs:

- the grid width (`width = min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`), which is a presentation cap, and
- `clippedColumns.total`, which the payload documents as *the file's own column count* and which the viewer prints verbatim when it exceeds `shown`.

For the issue's fixture — `a,b` header, 100 two-cell rows, one 5,000-field line as line 101, i.e. outside the default row window — the wide line is not a returned row at all. It still set `totalColumns = 5000`, so the payload reported `clippedColumns {shown: 1001, total: 5000}` and warned about 5,000 columns, while `clippedCells` was `0`: no returned cell was lost.

## What changed

`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `parseDelimitedTable` only:

- `totalColumns` is now `header.length` — the header is the schema; a data line is a row, not a column definition.
- `width` keeps its previous value, `min(max(header.length, widest), MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`, so the rectangular payload, `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS`, `MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS` and the grid width are untouched. The width question in the issue title (a two-column file still renders 1,001 mostly-blank columns) is deliberately left to its own change; this one fixes the false number and the sentence built from it.
- The column warning still fires only when `total > shown`, which now means the header itself is wider than the preview — the case where "the file has N columns, the preview shows the first M" is true.

The payload contract is unchanged: `clippedColumns` keeps `{total, shown}` and `shown` keeps its width meaning; `clippedColumns.total` is the only value that changes, and `clippedCells` / `clippedColumns` are still reported separately.

Two existing assertions encoded the old meaning and are updated with it:

- `a delimited preview caps a pathological line and counts what it leaves out` — the wide line is inside the window there, so the payload now reports `{shown: 1001, total: 2}` and exactly one sentence, `199000 cells past the preview width are not shown.`
- `a long file does not cost a legitimate table its columns` — its fixture had a one-name header (`title`) over six-cell rows, so the header and the rows disagreed; the header now names all six columns (`title,a,b,c,d,e`) and the assertion `{shown: 6, total: 6}` still holds. The test's intent (file length must not cost a column) is unchanged.

## Red first

New test `a wide line past the row window does not become the file's column count`, run against the unfixed `parseDelimitedTable`:

```
not ok 63 - a wide line past the row window does not become the file's column count
  ---
  error: |-
    the file has as many columns as its header

    5000 !== 2

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  name: 'AssertionError'
  expected: 2
  actual: 5000
  operator: 'strictEqual'
# tests 67
# pass 66
# fail 1
```

## After the fix

```
# tests 67
# pass 67
# fail 0
```

The new test pins, for the fixture above: `clippedColumns.total === 2`; no warning matching `/has \d+ columns/`; `clippedCells === 0`; every returned row is as wide as the grid; and `columns.length` is *not* pinned, so the fix is provably scoped to the reported number, not to the grid width.

Diffstat against `main` `f4dd1813`:

```
 services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts | 17 ++++++++----
 services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts     | 50 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++---
 2 files changed, 57 insertions(+), 10 deletions(-)
```

Ran:
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` — `# tests 67 # pass 67 # fail 0`; the same file on the unfixed source is the red above (`# pass 66 # fail 1`).
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.

Not run:
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` (the whole api suite) and the `ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e` layers were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser journey: the rendered `DatasetTable` meta line is covered by the payload assertions here; the visual 1,001-column grid is the open width half of the issue, not this change.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: a delimited preview of a file with a wide data line no longer claims a column count the header does not have, and no longer warns about columns in the same breath as cells; a header genuinely wider than the preview still gets the column sentence.

Compatibility and migration: none. `clippedColumns` keeps its shape; only `total` changes for files whose widest line is wider than their header.

pr:927.body:
Fixes #925

## What happens

Under zh-CN — the product default — the Session activity panel prints the two values it takes from
server data as raw API tokens:

- the status badge on every execution, transfer and reminder record renders `item.state` verbatim,
  so a running execution reads `running`;
- the execution meta line renders `item.provenance` verbatim (`工作区 ws_a · 溯源 pending`), and the
  record's accessible label (fold summary, focus label) reads `local · main · running`.

## Cause

`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` rendered `item.state` / `item.provenance` straight into the
tree, and `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` carried the 25 `activity.*` chrome keys but no keys for
those two value domains. Every other surface already translates them (`WakeNotice.tsx` maps wake
states through `chat.wakeNoticeState.*`, `GovernedDownloadCards.tsx` does the same for downloads);
this was the one activity surface left in English.

## Change

Product: two files, +51/−8.

- `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` — `activity.state.{queued,running,completed,failed,cancelled,unknown}`
  and `activity.provenance.{pending,committed}` (en: `Queued … Unknown`, `Pending`/`Committed`; zh:
  `排队中/运行中/已完成/失败/已取消/未知`, `待提交`/`已提交`), added beside `activity.resumeAgentScope`
  in both catalogues without reordering anything else.
- `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` — two module-scope key maps plus `stateLabel(state)` /
  `provenanceLabel(provenance)`, which fall back to the raw value for anything the catalogues do not
  carry. Used in the three badge children (executions, transfers, reminders), the three
  `ProcessRecord` labels and the `executionMeta` call.

Untouched by design: the `activity-badge ${item.state}` class (styling keys on it), `live` /
`cancellable`, the `progress.length` accounting, and every other badge in the app. A transfer's
`partial`, a reminder's `fired` and provenance `unconfirmed` are out of scope and keep their raw
token — the fallback branch is asserted, not assumed.

Test: `apps/web/tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx`, +38 — one new case, no assertion migration in
the eight existing cases.

## Red-first

Command, from `apps/web`: `node --import tsx --test tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx`

Before the fix (test present, product untouched) — only the new case fails, and the tree shows the
raw token exactly as the issue reports it:

```
not ok 9 - a zh-CN badge names its state and provenance instead of printing the API token
  Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
  + actual - expected
    [
      'activity-badge running',
  +   'running'
  -   '运行中'
    ]
# tests 9
# pass 8
# fail 1
```

After the fix: `# tests 9 / # pass 9 / # fail 0`, and the same render no longer contains
`溯源 pending` (it reads `溯源 待提交`), while the class is still `activity-badge running`.

The new case also pins the two boundaries: an unknown state keeps its raw token
(`activity-badge paused` → `paused`) and `unconfirmed` provenance stays untranslated; and it renders
the panel under `initialLocale="en"` to confirm the English wording is `Running` / `provenance
Pending` — the eight existing cases (English chrome: `View logs`, `Cancel execution`, `Resume …`)
stay green, so no assertion migrated.

## Reads

Ran:

- `node --import tsx --test tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx` (in `apps/web`) — before `9 / 8 pass / 1 fail`,
  after `9 / 9 / 0`.
- `../../node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` (in `apps/web`) — exit 0, no output.
- `git diff --numstat upstream/main..HEAD` — `33	8` component, `18	0` messages, `38	0` test.

Not run:

- `pnpm ci:l1` locally — its prepare step runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which cannot write
  the local pnpm store here; CI runs L1 on this PR.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claim-Id: cfb62886f9854b6ab1a2f7e824417cdb Branch: dev1/fix/wake-notice-cancelled-outcome Base: 89cd2d30c93e At: 2026-11-04T18:15:54Z ### Checklist - [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help. - [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version. - [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed. ### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem **What the user sees.** When a background execution ends because it was cancelled, the runtime notice card in the transcript summarises it as **"1 unconfirmed"**, while the record printed one line below in the same card carries the badge **"cancelled"**. The card contradicts itself about the same execution, and the summary tells the researcher the outcome is unknown when they cancelled it themselves. - current: 1 cancelled execution → summary `Synced 1 background execution result(s)` + `1 unconfirmed`, record badge `cancelled`. - expected: 1 cancelled execution → summary `Synced 1 background execution result(s)` + `1 cancelled`, record badge `cancelled`. **Where.** `apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx:53-58` is the summary bucketing. It has three entries — `completed` (`:54`), `failed` (`:55`) and a catch-all (`:56`, `record.state !== "completed" && record.state !== "failed"`). `cancelled` is not a bucket of its own, so it falls into `chat.wakeNoticeUnconfirmed` (`:56`), even though the same file already maps it to its own badge label at `:26` (`cancelled: "chat.wakeNoticeState.cancelled"`). The catalog reflects that split: the summary keys are enumerated at `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:2631-2633` and the badge at `:2641` (zh: summary `:5591-5593`, badge `:5601`), and no `chat.wakeNoticeCancelled` summary key exists. A notice persisted before `records` existed still renders from its counts (`WakeNotice.tsx:69-71`), so that path is unaffected. **Minimal reproduction (red first, no browser).** Add this case to `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` (the file already renders the component with `renderToStaticMarkup`): ```tsx const notice: RuntimeNotice = { executions: 1, timers: 0, prompt: "[Execution notifications]", records: [ { agentId: "main", kind: "execution", runnerId: "local", sourceId: "exec-1", state: "cancelled" }, ], }; const html = renderToStaticMarkup(createElement(WakeNotice, { notice })); assert.match(html, /1 cancelled/); ``` Run on the base commit: ``` cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/zz-wake-notice-cancelled-probe.test.tsx ``` Observed (the probe file is temporary and prints the two competing readings): ``` # \# SUMMARY "1 unconfirmed" # \# BADGE cancelled not ok 1 - probe: a cancelled execution is summarised as cancelled, not unconfirmed error: |- The input did not match the regular expression /1 cancelled/. Input: '

Synced 1 background execution result(s)1 unconfirmed

  • cancelled…' # tests 1 # pass 0 # fail 1 ``` **Fix direction (smallest slice).** Add one bucket to `outcomes` (`WakeNotice.tsx:53-58`) for `record.state === "cancelled"` and one message pair, `chat.wakeNoticeCancelled` — `"{count} cancelled"` next to `messages.ts:2633`, `"{count} 项已取消"` next to `:5593`. Keep the catch-all at `:56` for `unknown`, `queued`, `running` and for records with no catalog entry (`state` undefined), which is what "unconfirmed" actually means today. The per-record badge and the persisted-without-records path (`WakeNotice.tsx:69-71`) stay unchanged. **Acceptance.** - a notice with 1 completed + 1 failed + 1 cancelled execution summarises as `1 completed · 1 failed · 1 cancelled` with no `unconfirmed` — this is the assertion that fails on the base commit; - a record whose catalog entry is gone (no `state`) still summarises as `1 unconfirmed`; - `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` keeps its existing cases green, and the new case fails on `89cd2d30` for the reported reason, not for a missing import. ### Detailed Environment Information Description - Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (2026-11-04). - `apps/web` (React + Vite). ## What happens

`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py::ArchitectureBoundaryTests::test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` can fail with `FileNotFoundError` instead of an assertion, because it walks `services/api` while other tests are writing and deleting their temp workspaces under `services/api/.tmp`.

Observed once on a pull request whose diff does not touch this test, `services/gateway`, or anything that writes `agent-skill-creator-*`:

```
FAILED tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py::ArchitectureBoundaryTests::test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names
  FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
  '.../services/api/.tmp/agent-skill-creator-1793877061398-12103/projects/15036584-.../sessions/f6ab2480-.../skill-snapshots/.716ffbc5-....skill-snapshot/antibody-design/scripts/install_pipeline_deps.sh'
```

- run `42015883088`, `UT` job `127206585414`: `planned 6366 / executed 6366 / passed 6365 / failed 1 / skipped 0`
- the group holding it: `1 failed, 30 passed in 4.55s`; the other 30 are gateway Python tests that ran normally
- the same test set passed on the previous tip of the same branch (run `41890794011`)

## Why

```python
NODE_ROOTS = (REPOSITORY_ROOT / "services" / "api", REPOSITORY_ROOT / "packages", REPOSITORY_ROOT / "apps" / "web", REPOSITORY_ROOT / "test" / "api")
IGNORED_DIRECTORIES = {"__pycache__", "dist", "node_modules"}

def _files(root):
    for path in root.rglob("*"):
        if path.is_file() and not any(part in IGNORED_DIRECTORIES for part in path.parts):
            yield path
```

`services/api/.tmp` is a live runtime workspace root: `services/api/src/server.test.ts` and the skill-creator paths create and remove session trees under it while other workers run. `_files()` lists a path and the test then reads it; when the owning test deletes it in between, the read raises and the whole boundary assertion is lost.

## Impact

Any pull request whose `UT` layer overlaps that window fails a test that has nothing to do with its diff. The cost is a full CI cycle plus a rerun we cannot perform ourselves (`POST /actions/runs/<id>/rerun-failed-jobs` → `403 Must have admin rights to Repository`), so it turns into a maintainer round-trip per hit.

## Proposed fix

1. Add `.tmp` to `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES`: like `dist`, it is generated runtime data, not source.
2. Treat a file that disappears between the listing and the read as gone rather than as a boundary violation (`FileNotFoundError` → skip that path); a source file removed mid-run cannot be asserted anyway.
3. Deterministic regression test: create `services/api/.tmp/probe.ts` containing a forbidden vendor token, run the boundary walk, and assert the walk reports nothing for it (this fails on `main` today, because `.tmp` is not ignored).

Related but distinct: `#872`, `#878` (a different `packages/data-source` timing flake) and `#909` (ST runtime download) — this one is a shared-root walk race, not a timeout.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Dev-Lead

## What happened

A long real research run can end with only this text on the page:

```text
The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration and input, then retry. · interaction round execution failed
```

The sentence before the dot is `runFailure.semantic-error` in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`. The detail after the dot is the fixed string `interaction round execution failed`. In the DeepAgent interaction-round handler that string replaces the caught exception: the handler logs the exception and returns `error_code=round_execution_error` with that fixed message. The original exception does not reach the page or the E2E log.

Observed runs, both with an empty final answer and `delivery.status` `"failed"`:

- main Nightly [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`), **DRB-62**, 23.7 minutes. One subagent completed. The session had `literature_sources.json` and showed 271K usage and 20 executions. The required `deepresearchbench-62.md` was not delivered. Run status was `failed`.
- release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020) (`6d3c49a8`), **DRB-58**, 21.0 minutes. Run status was `failed`. The session had `literature_sources.json`, `hgt_animals_sources.md`, and `hgt_plants_sources.md`. One child was `completed` and another was still `running`. A PubMed call had returned HTTP 429 from `eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov`. Literature-connector 429s are already tracked in #208.

The same DRB-62 passed on the beta run (36.1 minutes), and the same DRB-58 passed on the main run (51.0 minutes). The model and gateway had already served those sessions for about 20 minutes, so this is not a wrong API key or a missing model id.

## Expected

The failed round keeps the underlying exception message (gateway status, tool error, or runtime exception) in the run error that the page and the test can read. A round that ran for many minutes is not described only as a model-configuration rejection.

## Evidence limits

The server log for these two runs was not retrieved, so the exception that was swallowed is not known. The page text and the run status are known.

## Problem
PR #460 delivered default local namespace isolation for embedded JiuwenSwarm. The product decision on #257 requires a **complete config/runtime boundary**, not only a renamed default directory: SD must not silently adopt standalone Swarm configuration via inherited env vars, home/registry lookup, or runtime service discovery, and must not let port collision silently attach SD to another Swarm service.

## Expected
- Embedded Swarm config and state are owned by ScienceDiscovery; discovering a user’s standalone Swarm (including same instance name) must not replace or merge SD’s model/skill/agent/tool behavior.
- Outer-process Swarm-specific environment variables, default SDK paths, and service discovery must not bypass the SD-owned boundary unless the user explicitly configured an SD-supported override with clear ownership.
- setup/start/status/env/stop, logs, and connection endpoints resolve to the same SD-owned instance; port conflicts are handled without silently connecting to a sibling Swarm.

## Verification cases

1. **Standalone config does not drive SD**
   - **Preconditions:** Disposable home/namespace; standalone Swarm instance (including same name `sciencediscovery`) with deliberately different identifiable config.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Start ScienceDiscovery with default embedded settings.
     2. Change standalone model/skill/agent settings and start/stop the standalone instance.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** SD behavior and backend ownership remain SD’s; standalone changes do not alter SD settings or which instance SD uses.

2. **Env / discovery bypass**
   - **Preconditions:** Outer environment carries standalone Swarm-specific variables and/or occupied ports that could point at a non-SD instance.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Launch SD without an explicit user opt-in to that standalone endpoint.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** SD does not silently read standalone registry/config or connect to the foreign service; conflicts surface safely rather than mis-binding.

3. **SD lifecycle leaves standalone intact**
   - **Preconditions:** Both SD embedded and standalone instances live in the disposable namespace.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Run SD setup/start/stop and change SD settings.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Standalone registry/config/sessions remain unmodified and the standalone process is not stopped by SD lifecycle.

## Context
- Env: Evidence from #257 product decision comment (`embedded-swarm-isolation-decision`) and #460 partial scope (local isolation done; broader boundary still called out).
- Refs: Parent #257; fixing PR #460 (merged). Default path isolation landed in #460; this Issue tracks remaining boundary / env / discovery acceptance from that decision.
- Notes: Do not auto-migrate or delete ambiguous standalone data. Explicit SD-supported overrides remain allowed when ownership is clear.

closed_recent.author: JinhZhao
closed_recent.body:
# [Bug] Agent run stalls after todo_create tool.started without completion event and hits 240s idle timeout

## Summary

During a real end-to-end run on the SD stack, the agent's event stream stopped emitting progress for roughly **4 minutes 13 seconds** immediately after a `tool.started` event for the `todo_create` tool. No matching `tool.output` or `tool.completed` event was ever emitted for that invocation. The run was then terminated by the gateway's idle-timeout watchdog with the error:

```
Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms
```

This issue records the **observed fault symptom** and the associated evidence. The **internal root cause is not determined**: we do not know whether the stall happened inside the `todo_create` tool implementation, the gateway's tool-dispatch layer, the model gateway, or an underlying runtime component. Attribution to any specific component (SiliconFlow, SQLite, network, single gateway module, etc.) is intentionally **not** made here.

## Run identifiers

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Run ID | `a990cea3-bbf3-4e02-a0da-a4bd95237e79` |
| Session ID | `b52f69ac-eb99-4777-91ca-9aee2eb9063c` |
| Agent Run ID (evidence) | `9b87d4ab-0798-470b-bbb6-ed2c32167a65` |
| User Message ID | `ce4e1c3e-4f3b-495a-91f5-6285317c8664` |
| Model ID | `e1c88640-84b2-447c-ab9a-ef1e4604126b` |
| Skill selection mode | `all` (17 skills enabled) |
| Created at | `2026-11-03T11:14:19.514Z` |
| Started at | `2026-11-03T11:14:38.558Z` |
| Finished at | `2026-11-03T11:21:05.622Z` |
| Final status | `failed` |
| Terminal error | `Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms` |

## Observed event sequence (stall window)

The SSE stream against `/api/sessions/{sid}/messages` (with `Accept: text/event-stream`) delivered the following frames around the stall window. All timestamps are UTC on 2026-11-03. `id` is the SSE sequence id; `receivedAt` is the client-side receive timestamp.

| SSE id | receivedAt | type | detail | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 149 | 11:16:27.313 | `agent.record` | `model.completed` (turn 1) | last model-completed record before tool call |
| 150 | 11:16:27.394 | `assistant.response.settled` | turn 2 | LLM response stream closed |
| **151** | **11:16:27.402** | **`tool.started`** | **`todo_create` (status `running`)** | **last normal progress event** |
| — | *11:16:27.402 – 11:20:40.144* | — | **no SSE frames received** | **~4 min 13 s stall window** |
| **152** | **11:20:40.144** | **`agent.record`** | **`state.committed`** | first event after stall window |
| **153** | **11:21:05.507** | **`run.failed`** | `error: "Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms"`, `errorCode: timeout` | terminal failure |
| 154 | 11:21:05.712 | `run.status` | `status: failed` | final state notification |

### What is missing

For every observed `tool.started` earlier in the same run, the stream delivered a matching `tool.output` (sometimes with a `null` SSE id) and a `tool.completed` within seconds:

| Tool | tool.started id | tool.output | tool.completed id |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rename_session` | 98 | line 99 (null id) | 99 |
| `list_files` | 100 | line 102 (null id) | 101 |
| **`todo_create`** | **151** | **— missing —** | **— missing —** |

The `todo_create` invocation is the only tool call in this run whose lifecycle is not closed.

## Evidence

- **Raw SSE capture**: `raw_sse.jsonl` (156 lines, covering SSE ids 1–154 plus two `tool.output` frames with null ids). The stall-window excerpt above is taken verbatim from this file.
- **Run final status**: `run_final_status.json` reports `status: failed`, `error: "Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms"`, `finishedAt: 2026-11-03T11:21:05.622Z`.
- **Idle-timeout source**: `services/api/src/agent-run/run-deadlines.ts` implements a dual deadline (turn + idle). The idle deadline is rearmed by `progress()` on every gateway event; if no progress is reported for `idleMs` (240 000 ms in this run), `expire("idle")` fires and the run is failed with the message observed above.
- **Progress trigger sites**: `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` calls `markProgress()` from the SSE `emit()` path, the model-gateway progress path, the `run_started` path, and adapter events. During the stall window, none of these sites fired, consistent with the SSE stream going silent.

## Expected behavior

- A `tool.started` event should be followed by a `tool.output` and a `tool.completed` (or a `tool.failed`) within a bounded, reasonable interval.
- If a tool invocation cannot complete, the gateway should either time it out at a tool-level budget or surface a `tool.failed` event, so the run can terminate cleanly with an attributable cause.
- The idle watchdog should fire only when the gateway as a whole has truly stopped making progress, not as the primary symptom of a single tool hanging.

## Actual behavior

- After `tool.started(todo_create)` at 11:16:27.402Z, no further progress event was emitted for 4 min 13 s.
- No `tool.output` or `tool.completed` for `todo_create` was ever emitted.
- The idle watchdog fired at the 240 s budget and terminated the run with a generic stall error.
- The first post-stall event (`agent.record state.committed`) arrived 13 s after the inferred watchdog expiry; the terminal `run.failed` arrived 25 s after that.

## Impact

- The run's scientific work in progress (turn 1 of a multi-turn research plan) was lost.
- The user-visible error message (`no gateway progress for 240000 ms`) does not identify which component stalled, which makes self-diagnosis difficult.
- The missing tool lifecycle events make post-mortem attribution impossible from the SSE stream alone.

## Reproduction

1. Start the SD stack (`scripts/start-stack.sh` or `docker compose up`) on any host.
2. Create a project and a session.
3. Enable the default skill set (17 skills, including the one that exposes `todo_create`).
4. Send the following prompt (the same prompt used in the affected run):

   > 我正在研究 Pd 催化 1,3-二烯的选择性发散反应，希望理解不同配体、溶剂和 CO 条件如何影响羰基化与分子内环化路径。请识别关键科学问题、已知信息和未知信息，制定可执行的研究计划，并说明哪些步骤需要文献、计算或实验支持。不要直接给出未经验证的机理结论。

5. Open an SSE connection to `/api/sessions/{sid}/messages` with `Accept: text/event-stream`.
6. Observe whether a `tool.started` for `todo_create` is followed by matching `tool.output` / `tool.completed` events, or whether the stream stalls for minutes and ends with `run.failed` / `Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms`.

The fault is **intermittent** in our experience: the same stack and prompt do not reproduce the stall on every run. That is part of what makes the issue worth tracking upstream — the manifestation is real, the trigger is not yet isolated.

## Environment where this was observed

- OS: Windows 11 (22631)
- Runtime: Docker Desktop with bind-mounted data directory (9P filesystem)
- SD build: `sd-catalystpi-probe` worktree, M4 milestone
- Model gateway: SiliconFlow (external LLM provider, via the SD model-gateway layer)
- Memory Graph backend: Neo4j sidecar

## What this issue is NOT claiming

- It does **not** attribute the stall to SiliconFlow, the model gateway, SQLite, the memory-graph sidecar, the network, or any single gateway component.
- It does **not** claim that the idle watchdog is wrong to fire; the watchdog behaved as designed. The question is why no progress was reported for 240 s.
- It does **not** claim that the stall is deterministically reproducible from the prompt alone.

## Suggested investigations (for upstream, not prescriptive)

- Add tool-lifecycle logging on the gateway: for every `tool.started`, record the matching `tool.output` / `tool.completed` / `tool.failed` and the elapsed time, even when the run is later terminated by the idle watchdog.
- Add a per-tool execution budget, independent of the run-level idle timeout, so a single hanging tool fails the tool rather than the whole run.
- Surface the stalled tool's name in the terminal `run.failed` error message, so users and operators can attribute the fault without replaying the SSE stream.
- Correlate this run's gateway-side logs (model-gateway requests, tool dispatch, adapter events) with the SSE capture to identify where the `todo_create` invocation stopped making progress.

## Relates to

- Issue A (same submission batch) — `/health` serial-composition design. Orthogonal; the two issues share the same local test environment but do not share a causal link.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] Agent run stalls after todo_create tool.started without completion event and hits 240s idle timeout
