## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The reproduction below is minimal, self-contained, and includes the observed result.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Current:** when a workspace transfer copies a directory, the Activity panel's transfer row reports the *number of declared mappings* as the file total while the committed count comes from the *expanded* files, so a directory of three files reads `3/1 files committed`.

**Expected:** `3/3 files committed` — the total is the number of files the transfer is actually copying.

### Where

`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:103` (read on `main` `c4f5ecb36ca0439d8e45cc30f1e8d0210413ea70`):

```tsx
<small>{t("activity.filesCommitted", { committed: item.progress.filter((file) => file.state === "completed").length, total: item.files.length })}</small>
```

`item.files` is the transfer *request* — 1-50 explicit mappings, where one mapping may be a directory (`packages/schema/src/workspace-transfer.ts:6`). `item.progress` is the expanded per-file work list (`workspace-transfer.ts:14`), and the API builds it by expanding every mapping into one entry per file (`services/api/src/workspace-transfers.ts:107-115`):

```ts
job.progress = job.files.flatMap((file) => {
  const selected = entries.filter((item) => item.path === file.sourcePath || item.path.startsWith(`${file.sourcePath}/`));
  ...
  return selected.map((entry) => ({ ... }));
});
```

So `progress.length` is the file count and `files.length` is the mapping count; the numerator and the denominator count different things. The same panel already renders `item.progress` as the file list (`AgentActivityPanel.tsx:105`), so the denominator contradicts the list right below it.

### Red-first reproduction (fails on `main` `c4f5ecb`)

Minimal self-contained test, rendered with `react-test-renderer` and a stubbed `ApiClient` — one declared directory mapping, three expanded completed files:

```tsx
const activity = { executions: [], timers: [], agents: [], transfers: [{
  id: "t1", sessionId: "session", agentId: "main", state: "completed",
  sourceWorkspaceId: "ws_a", targetWorkspaceId: "ws_b",
  files: [{ sourcePath: "data", targetPath: "data" }],
  createdAt: "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  progress: [
    { sourcePath: "data/a.csv", targetPath: "data/a.csv", size: 1, sha256: "a".repeat(64), bytes: 1, state: "completed" },
    { sourcePath: "data/b.csv", targetPath: "data/b.csv", size: 1, sha256: "b".repeat(64), bytes: 1, state: "completed" },
    { sourcePath: "data/c.csv", targetPath: "data/c.csv", size: 1, sha256: "c".repeat(64), bytes: 1, state: "completed" },
  ],
}] };
const client = { getAgentActivity: async () => activity } as unknown as ApiClient;
await act(async () => { view = create(createElement(AgentActivityPanel, { client, sessionId: "session" })); });
assert.match(JSON.stringify(view.toJSON()), /3\/3 files committed/);
```

Observed on `main` `c4f5ecb` (probe run against the same sources):

```
not ok 1 - a directory transfer reports its expanded files as the total
  error: The input did not match the regular expression /3\/3 files committed/.
  Actual rendered row: "3/1 files committed"
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

### Suggested fix (red first)

1. Add the assertion above to `apps/web/tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx` and watch it fail with `3/1`.
2. Change the denominator to the expanded file list: `total: item.progress.length` (a one-line change at `AgentActivityPanel.tsx:103`). `committed` already counts `progress` entries, so both sides then describe the same collection.
3. The test passes with `3/3`; a transfer of a single file stays `1/1`, and a partial transfer reads `2/3`.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- Commit: `main` `c4f5ecb36ca0439d8e45cc30f1e8d0210413ea70` (bug lines re-read there; probe executed on the same sources)
- OS: Linux x86_64 (container)
- Node.js: `v22.23.2`
- pnpm: `11.1.2`
- Command: `node --import tsx --test apps/web/tests/<probe>.test.tsx` from the repository root, after the workspace packages are built
- Relevant packages: `react@19.2.7`, `react-test-renderer@19.2.7`, `tsx@4.23.1`
- No network, no credentials, no real workspace needed: the panel is rendered with a stubbed `ApiClient`.

## Additional Information

- Search before filing: `"files committed"` (5 hits: none is this defect), `"fileProgress"` (0), `"AgentActivityPanel"` (2: #238/#394, a different Session-not-found bug), `"progress.length"` + transfer (0). No open issue or PR covers the transfer row's total.
- The bug is only visible when a mapping expands to more than one file (a directory mapping); single-file transfers read `1/1` and look correct, which is why it survived.
- Related but distinct: #840/#841/#842 are about the artifact preview payload, not the Activity panel.

## Version Information

- `main` at `c4f5ecb36ca0439d8e45cc30f1e8d0210413ea70`
- Web client: `@sciencediscovery/web` workspace package at that commit
- API: `@sciencediscovery/api` workspace package at that commit
- The affected file `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` is identical at `8708320f80af8a72ea96653e2a71bd89d83a6850` and at `c4f5ecb`

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: dae5b8d1b8af4de3885faca176d3c50a
Branch: dev2/fix/cas-has-corrupt-object
Base: ad34dd7847f6
At: 2026-10-29T05:08:29Z

## What is wrong

`CasStore.has()` in `packages/cas/src/index.ts:74-82` answers the boolean existence question by calling `read()`. `read()` re-hashes the bytes and throws `CAS integrity failure` when a stored object no longer matches its digest, and `has()` only maps `ENOENT` to `false` (`:79`), so a corrupt object makes `has()` throw. Its sibling `verify()` (`:84-92`) deliberately maps the same condition to `false`. Two predicates over the same store therefore disagree: `verify()` says "not valid", `has()` raises.

## Reproduction (live main `ad34dd7847`, file blob `584cf1eaefc7ec9b5c4c2125de7bf13c39039ba0`)

```
$ node --import tsx -e '<put "hello world" via CasStore, then overwrite the blob with "HELLO WORLD">'
put -> b94d27b9934d 11
has before -> true
verify after corruption -> false
has after corruption -> THREW CAS integrity failure
```

The overwrite keeps the byte length, so this is exactly the "same size, different bytes" corruption case the store already detects elsewhere.

## Expected

`has(hash)` is a total boolean predicate: `true` only when the object is present and valid, `false` when it is missing **or corrupt** - the same answer `verify()` gives. A caller deciding "is this object still usable, or must I republish?" must not have to catch an untyped integrity error to find out.

## Why it matters

The store is used as a cache in front of publication paths (`put` / `retain` / republish decisions): those call `has()` to choose between "reuse" and "write it again". With a corrupt blob they crash with `CAS integrity failure` instead of taking the republish branch, and the error is thrown from a method whose contract is a boolean. PR `#657` made vanished refs republish; corrupt bytes are the neighbouring case and still have this shape.

## Fix scope

Extend the `has()` catch to map the integrity failure to `false` the way `verify()` already does (about two lines), plus one test next to the existing `index.test.ts` cases. No new dependency, no behaviour change for a valid or a missing object.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product

Claim-Id: e14724d388ec405da6ff5ddb06ae8a4f
Branch: dev/662-bug-web-fetch-public-url-guard-accepts-i
Base: a074172f60e5
At: 2026-10-29T03:58:14Z

## Reproduction

Node v22.23.2, live main `a074172f` (04:35Z).

Pure guard + reachability, one script:
```
node --import tsx --test .local/ipv4-mapped-ssrf-repro.test.ts
```
3/3 fail; and an end-to-end check of the same URL:
```
guard: accepted | fetch status: 200 body: LOCAL-LOOPBACK-RESPONSE
```
(run against a local server bound to 127.0.0.1 — `assertPublicUrl("http://[::ffff:7f00:1]:<port>/")` returns instead of throwing, and `fetch` then reaches loopback.)

## Current vs expected

Current: `isBlockedAddress("::ffff:7f00:1")` and `("::ffff:a9fe:a9fe")` return `false`, so `assertPublicUrl` accepts the hex IPv4-mapped/compatible forms and `web_fetch` can reach loopback and the link-local metadata endpoint.
Expected: every IPv4-mapped/compatible IPv6 literal is judged by its embedded IPv4, so both are rejected with `PublicUrlError("local and private network URLs are not allowed")`.

## Code evidence (live main a074172f)

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts:58-69`:
```ts
function ipv6Blocked(address: string): boolean {
  const value = normalizeIpv6(address);
  ...
  // IPv4-mapped/compatible forms must be judged by their embedded IPv4.
  const embedded = value.match(/(\d{1,3}(?:\.\d{1,3}){3})$/);
  if (embedded?.[1]) return ipv4Blocked(embedded[1]);
  return false;
}
```
The regex only matches the dotted form; `::ffff:7f00:1` / `::ffff:a9fe:a9fe` (and `0:0:0:0:0:ffff:7f00:1`) fall through to `return false`. `:72-77` dispatches every IPv6 literal here. Gate: `packages/data-source/src/web/native/index.ts:167` `: await assertPublicUrl(input.request);`.

## Suggested red test

Extend `packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts` → `web_fetch refuses private and loopback targets`:
```
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("::ffff:7f00:1"), true);
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("0:0:0:0:0:ffff:a9fe:a9fe"), true);
await assert.rejects(assertPublicUrl("http://[::ffff:7f00:1]:8080/"), PublicUrlError);
await assert.rejects(assertPublicUrl("http://[::ffff:a9fe:a9fe]/latest/meta-data/"), PublicUrlError);
```
Command: `cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts`. Verified red on current main (3/3, `false !== true` and `Missing expected rejection.`).

Fix: expand the IPv6 literal to 8 hextets; when the first six are 0 and hextet 7 is `0xffff` (mapped) or all seven are 0 (compatible), build the dotted quad from the last two hextets and reuse `ipv4Blocked`. `services/runner/src/egress-gateway.ts:123` repeats the dotted-only regex, but its input comes from a resolver, so this path is the one reachable from a model-supplied URL.

## Duplicate check (open + closed, REST search)

`ipv4-mapped`, `isBlockedAddress`, `url-guard`, `SSRF`, `assertPublicUrl`, `web_fetch private network`, `"::ffff"`, `mapped address` → 0 hits. Nearest: #326/#329 (closed; the opposite — public URLs falsely rejected). No open PR touches `url-guard.ts`.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] web_fetch public-URL guard accepts IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals, reaching loopback and link-local metadata endpoints

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #91](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/91) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Start the server and confirm "I can actually run analyses now".

## What I saw instead

- On Linux, when sandbox (bwrap) probing fails (e.g. the host disables unprivileged user namespaces), `services/launcher/src/preflight.ts` only prints a `WARNING` line; `services/launcher/src/serve.ts` ignores the result, keeps starting, and finally prints `ScienceDiscovery is ready at ...`.
- The green connection dot in the top bar only means the frontend can talk to the local API (`Connection OK`). It says nothing about sandbox availability, the scientific Python environment, or model quota.
- Users believe everything is ready, then the run fails mid-analysis — often with raw low-level errors.

## Why this is confusing

"Ready" and the green light create false confidence; the failure happens only after the user has invested time writing a prompt and uploading data.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- When startup preflight finds the sandbox unusable, surface a prominent in-app notice ("analyses cannot run in this environment", with the reason) instead of a single terminal warning.
- Separate "frontend connected" from "compute ready" in the status indicator.
- Open question (needs a product decision): when compute is unavailable, should the app block new analyses entirely, or allow read-only browsing of past sessions and artifacts? The two strategies differ a lot in UX; decide before implementing.

Design note: the preflight result already exists in the startup chain (`runPreflight`); what is missing is exposing it to the web UI and layering the status display.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] Sandbox unavailability only warns in the terminal while serve still reports ready; surface real compute readiness

## Summary

Biomni real E2E shows large endpoint-dependent variation in model-request latency and total generation time. Earlier runs through an OpenAI-compatible relay also ended after a terminal model turn with no text or tool call. We need enough safe wire-level diagnostics to tell an upstream empty completion from an SSE/parser defect, and to separate model/API latency from agent work.

This is distinct from #232, which records explicit HTTP 500/503 gateway errors.

## Local measurements

The two Biomni cases were run in parallel on the same Windows/WSL machine, with evaluation disabled, the `task` tool removed (no subagents), and no Jina key. `generation` is the benchmark's generation duration; request timing is the elapsed time of completed `[model-stream]` requests in `stack.log`. All rows below passed delivery. The relay run used `https://yibuapi.com/v1` with model alias `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; the direct runs used `https://api.deepseek.com` with model alias `deepseek-flash`.

| Case | Endpoint / runs | Generation | Completed model requests | Median request | Reported total tokens |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DA-13-3 | relay, r5 | 37.46 min | 71 | 25.16 s | 504,634 |
| DA-13-3 | direct, r6/r7/r9/r10 | 5.71–20.67 min | 26–44 | 6.10–13.93 s | 118,066–140,022 |
| DA-14-1 | relay, r5 | 31.31 min | 63 | 20.18 s | 177,043 |
| DA-14-1 | direct, r6/r9/r10 | 20.75–35.79 min | 54–72 | 11.59–19.01 s | 191,883–284,635 |

The seven direct samples all passed delivery, with zero reported SSE parse errors or SSE error records. Earlier local relay samples had a normalized final model turn with empty text, no tool call, and `finish_reason=stop`, after which the run was marked completed without the expected deliverable. Those older samples did **not** retain raw SSE records, so they cannot establish whether the upstream service sent an empty completion or the local stream adapter lost content. The direct samples also used a local empty-turn guard and SSE parsing fixes, so the passing rate is **not** an isolated endpoint A/B result.

## Why the current evidence is insufficient

- The relay and direct runs used different model aliases. The model's chosen steps, request counts, and token totals varied substantially, so total-duration differences are not an estimate of API latency alone.
- Even with the same direct endpoint, DA-13-3 varied from 5.71 to 20.67 minutes, and DA-14-1 from 20.75 to 35.79 minutes. Agent behavior and task content remain major contributors.
- A normalized empty final turn does not reveal whether the wire response was empty, malformed, or incorrectly mapped locally.

## Requested investigation / acceptance criteria

1. Save privacy-safe per-request diagnostics in real E2E artifacts: endpoint identity and model alias, request ID, HTTP status, dispatch/headers/first byte/first SSE record/completion timestamps, SSE record and parse-error counts, final content/tool-call presence, `finish_reason`, and retry/error classification. Do not save credentials or prompt/response bodies in the default diagnostic log.
2. Treat an empty terminal assistant turn with no tool call as an error rather than a successful final answer. Preserve the upstream request ID and framing summary when this occurs.
3. Compare relay and direct endpoints with the same model, request body, workload, and concurrency. Report per-request latency distributions separately from total agent duration and token use.
4. In CI summaries, identify explicit provider failures, empty completions, and local parse/mapping failures separately from research-quality failures.

I can provide the local benchmark metrics and sanitized `[model-stream]`/`[model-sse-summary]` excerpts if useful. No API keys or prompt contents are included here.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] perf(model): investigate endpoint-dependent Biomni latency and empty terminal turns

# [Bug] Idea Tree initial ideation can fail due to inconsistent exploration-type instructions and proposal validation

## Summary

The Idea Tree research workflow can fail during its initial ideation round, leaving only the ROOT node and no generated candidate hypotheses.

The initial IDEATE prompt encourages `exploit` proposals except when deliberately exploring novel directions. However, an initial research tree has no existing candidates or insights that an `exploit` proposal can reference.

The validator correctly enforces references for exploit proposals, but the prompt does not adequately address this initial-state constraint.

## Observed behavior

**Original baseline run**

- Research created successfully.
- ROOT node persisted.
- LLM ideation invoked.
- Validation failed after one correction.
- Error: `Proposal references an unknown candidate or insight`
- Final research state: `interrupted`
- Candidate count: 0

**Diagnostic run with a temporary prompt modification**

- The IDEATE prompt was modified to explicitly require `explore` during the initial round.
- A mock-based direct engine test generated two candidates and completed evaluation.
- A real Agent E2E run using SiliconFlow DeepSeek V4.1 Flash still failed during ideation.
- Error: `Exploit proposals must name their evidence and targeted insight`
- Final research state: `interrupted`
- Candidate count: 0

The diagnostic modification was not accepted as a product fix. The original source file has been restored on disk, while the running process baseline remains unverified.

## Relevant code

- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/prompts.py`, initial IDEATE instructions (lines 11-14)
- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py`, proposal reference validation (lines 448-458)
- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py`, exploit proposal requirements (lines 459-467)
- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py`, correction and retry handling (lines 260-263)

## Expected behavior

When a research tree contains no prior candidate or insight, initial ideation should produce valid new candidate proposals without referencing nonexistent objects.

Invalid references must continue to be rejected. Subsequent exploit proposals should reference existing candidates and insights.

## Actual behavior

The initial ideation workflow terminates after proposal validation fails and one correction attempt does not resolve the invalid proposal.

No candidate hypotheses are persisted, preventing subsequent evaluation and tree evolution in the observed runs.

## Diagnostic findings

The evidence supports an inconsistency between initial-state prompt instructions and proposal validation requirements.

A mock-based test succeeded after clarifying the prompt, but a real-model diagnostic run still failed. The exact raw model responses and full effective prompts were not captured, so model noncompliance and correction-specific causes remain unverified.

## Suggested investigation

1. Inspect the effective IDEATE prompt and initial research state.
2. Verify how `explorationType` is generated and parsed.
3. Check that first-round proposals cannot reference nonexistent candidates or insights.
4. Examine correction behavior when exploit proposals lack valid references.
5. Add real-model integration tests alongside deterministic schema tests.
6. Preserve strict referential integrity; do not silently convert invalid exploit proposals into explore proposals without an explicit, validated design decision.

## Impact

Blocks candidate generation and downstream evaluation in the reproduced Idea Tree research runs.

## Reproduction context

- **Test environment**: ScienceDiscovery container deployment
- **Model**: SiliconFlow DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
- **Template**: `scientific-hypothesis-general/v1`
- **Trigger**: Create idea research with empty initial tree, invoke ideation stage

## Evidence availability

Research state JSON, SSE event records, test reports, and code version audit are available upon request. Internal identifiers will be sanitized before sharing.

## Suggested fix approaches

1. **Validator relaxation**: Allow empty references for exploit proposals in round 1 (auto-convert to explore)
2. **Prompt enhancement**: Add JSON schema examples and explicit round-1 markers
3. **Code-level enforcement**: Force `explorationType=explore` in round 1 before validation
4. **Model evaluation**: Assess instruction-following capability across different LLM providers
closed_recent.title: [Bug] Idea Tree initial ideation can fail due to inconsistent exploration-type instructions and proposal validation

closed_recent.author: nanzhaogang
closed_recent.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Both clients (`apps/web` and `apps/desktop`) can fail in ways a user cannot describe from memory: a stuck run, a wrong artifact, an offline shell. Today the only way to report one is to leave the app, open GitHub, and write an issue from scratch — which loses the version, OS, locale and the failure state the app itself already knows. Error surfaces (including the "cannot reach the local service" screen) end in a dead end with no way to say anything.

This issue tracks the full delivery: a shared submission contract, a Cloudflare Worker that relays reports into a private GitHub issue, a feedback dialog in both front ends, an entry point on the offline screen that seeds the dialog with the failure's diagnostics, and a receipt code the user can quote when following up.

Related: the desktop shell must not be left out of a feature that only lands in `apps/web`; the offline screen is the surface that has no report path at all today.

Related pull request: branch `feat/user-feedback` — feature implementation, tests and deployment notes.

## Design Ideas

- **One contract, three consumers.** Payload building, redaction, PII detection, field validation and receipt generation live in `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts` and are imported by `apps/web`, `apps/desktop` and the Worker. The wire format cannot drift between the two clients and the server.
- **Triage fields are required.** Frequency (always / sometimes / once) and impact (blocks me / slows my work / affects the experience) are mandatory: a report without them cannot be routed or prioritized, so the dialog keeps 提交 disabled and states why, rather than accepting an untriaged issue.
- **A receipt instead of an account.** A submission returns `FB-XXXX-XXXX`, drawn from a 32-symbol alphabet (no `I/O/0/1`) to stay readable over the phone. It is shown once, kept in local history, and is what support asks for.
- **Diagnostics on by default, redacted on the way out.** Key names are forced to `[REDACTED:key]`, Windows profile paths are normalized, and the user can uncheck the block. The offline screen pre-fills diagnostics with boot state, origin and user agent so a "cannot connect" report arrives with evidence attached.
- **PII is advisory, not a wall.** Phone numbers, ID cards and emails in the description raise a confirmation step instead of silently rewriting the text, because the user may be quoting exactly what broke.
- **Draft and history stay local.** The draft is written to `localStorage` on every change and restored on reopen; the last 50 submissions live beside it. Nothing is stored server-side except the issue itself.
- **Abuse control belongs to the relay, not the client.** Keyed dedupe for seven days, a per-IP hourly limit, a per-install daily limit and a daily issue quota keep a public endpoint from becoming a spam funnel — and a duplicate returns the original receipt instead of creating a second issue.
- **The token never ships.** The GitHub PAT lives as a Cloudflare secret; the bundle only knows the Worker URL.

## Involved Public APIs

One new endpoint, on the Worker (not on the product's REST service): `POST /api/feedback`.

- Request: `{ v: 1, clientTs, kind, title, body, contact?, meta, diagnostics? }`; `v` is the contract version and `clientTs` an ISO timestamp. `kind ∈ {bug, idea, other}`; `contact` is `{ type: "email" | "github", value }`; body 10–2000 characters (its UTF-8 size is checked before sending); title capped at 120; diagnostics capped at 4000; the whole request capped at 16 KiB.
- Response `201 { receipt, createdAt }`. Failures are `{ error }` objects: `400 invalid` (with a `fields` map) or `400 invalid_json`, `403 forbidden`, `409 duplicate` (carries the original receipt), `413 too_large`, `429 rate_limited`, `502 upstream_failed`, `503 unavailable`. No issue URL is returned — the tracker issue lives in a private repository.
- CORS: an explicit origin allowlist, configurable through `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, covering the local dev ports of both clients.
- Endpoint constant: `FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT` / `FEEDBACK_API_PATH` in `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts`.

No route of `services/api` changes; the clients do not proxy feedback through the local backend, so reporting still works when the backend is down.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `packages/operational-logging`: new `feedback` entry point (contract, validation, redaction, receipts, PII) and its reuse of the existing `redaction` and `diagnostics` helpers.
- `packages/feedback-worker`: new workspace package — Worker entry, GitHub issue creation, KV-backed limits, mock-GitHub tests.
- `apps/web`: dialog, API client mapping status codes to user-facing failures, draft/history store, entries in the header and in `ErrorDiagnosticActions`.
- `apps/desktop`: the same dialog and store, a 我要反馈 entry in the sidebar footer to the right of the GitHub star, and an entry on the offline screen that pre-fills diagnostics; the dialog is mounted in the offline branch so that entry works.
- Internationalization: every string lands in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` and in both `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts` and `en.ts`; the two dictionaries must stay structurally identical.
- Infrastructure: a `FEEDBACK_KV` namespace and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` secret on Cloudflare; labels `source:in-app`, `kind:<kind>`, `needs-triage` on created issues.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Unit tests (47 cases across 6 files):**
  - `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.test.ts` (8): receipt format and 100k uniqueness, redaction of keyed values and profile paths, advisory PII detection, contact classification, title derivation, payload building, field validation.
  - `packages/feedback-worker/src/index.test.ts` (9): CORS preflight and disallowed origin, 16 KiB rejection before parsing, 400 on bad JSON/fields, success path creating an issue, 409 duplicate within the window, per-install daily 429, daily quota 503, GitHub 5xx surfacing 502 without leaking the token.
  - `apps/web/tests/FeedbackApi.test.ts` (8) and `apps/desktop/tests/feedback-submit.test.ts` (8): status-code to failure mapping in each client.
  - `apps/web/tests/FeedbackStore.test.ts` (7) and `apps/desktop/tests/feedback-store.test.ts` (7): install id persistence, draft default and round-trip, corrupt-data fallback, history capped at 50, removal by receipt.
- **Component tests:** not yet written. The required-field rule (`frequency` and `impact` both chosen before submit) is currently covered by manual verification only; the plan is to extract the form-state predicate out of the dialog into a shared pure function and assert it from both apps.
- **End-to-end (manual, against the deployed Worker):** submit from the desktop dialog → receipt shown and recorded in 我的反馈; stop the local backend, reload, land on the offline screen → 我要反馈 → description pre-filled and diagnostics expandable → submit → receipt; restart the backend → 重试 recovers in one click. Verified receipts: `FB-775M-N8A8` (normal), `FB-XKXW-FGSZ` (from the offline screen).
- **Regression:** the offline screen still renders exactly as before when no feedback is submitted; ordinary sessions are untouched; the web feedback dialog behaves identically to the desktop one.

Commands that must pass: `pnpm check` (architecture check, typecheck, unit tests); `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test`; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report can be submitted from `apps/web` and from `apps/desktop`, and a GitHub issue is created with `source:in-app`, `kind:<kind>` and `needs-triage`.
- [ ] Frequency and impact are mandatory in both clients: an untouched form keeps 提交 disabled and shows 出现频率和影响程度为必填项.
- [ ] The receipt shown after submission matches the one in 我的反馈 and the issue body.
- [ ] The offline screen's 我要反馈 opens the dialog with the failure text pre-filled and diagnostics available (not "本条反馈没有可用诊断信息").
- [ ] A submission from the offline screen still succeeds while the local backend is down.

## Additional Information

Deployed endpoint: `https://sciencediscovery-feedback.sciencediscovery.workers.dev` (Cloudflare requires the `<worker>.<subdomain>.workers.dev` form). KV namespace `FEEDBACK_KV`; secrets `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `REPO_OWNER`, `REPO_NAME`; deployment via `npx wrangler deploy` from `packages/feedback-worker`. Deployment and verification steps are in `packages/feedback-worker/README.md`.

---

## 🚀 背景描述

两端客户端（`apps/web` 与 `apps/desktop`）都会出现用户无法靠记忆描述清楚的故障：运行卡住、产物不对、本地服务连不上。今天要反馈这类问题，用户必须先离开应用、打开 GitHub、从零写一个 issue——版本、系统、语言、当时的故障状态全部丢失，而这些信息应用本身就有。报错界面（包括「连不上本地服务」那一页）是个死胡同，用户没有地方说一句话。

本 issue 跟踪完整交付：共享的提交契约、把反馈转成私有 GitHub issue 的 Cloudflare Worker、两端一致的反馈对话框、在离线页把故障诊断预填进对话框的入口，以及用户可以引用的回执码。

相关：一个只落在 `apps/web` 的功能，不应把桌面端漏掉；而离线页正是目前完全没有反馈入口的地方。

相关 PR：分支 `feat/user-feedback`——功能实现、测试与部署说明。

## 设计思路

- **一份契约、三个使用方。** payload 构造、脱敏、PII 检测、字段校验与回执生成集中在 `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts`，由 `apps/web`、`apps/desktop` 与 Worker 共同引用，两端与服务的线上格式不会漂移。
- **分诊字段必填。** 出现频率（总是 / 偶尔 / 仅一次）与影响程度（无法使用 / 影响工作效率 / 影响使用体验）为必填项：缺少这两项的报告无法定级与派发，因此对话框在未选时保持「提交」禁用并说明原因，而不是收下一条无法分诊的 issue。
- **用回执码，而不是账号。** 提交返回 `FB-XXXX-XXXX`，字符集剔除 `I/O/0/1` 以便口头转述；提交成功时展示一次，并保留在本地历史里，客服只需要这个码。
- **诊断信息默认附带、出口前脱敏。** 键名强制为 `[REDACTED:key]`，Windows 用户目录路径归一化，用户可以取消勾选。离线页会自动带上启动状态、origin 与 user agent，让「连不上」这类报告自带证据。
- **PII 只提示、不拦截。** 描述里的手机号、身份证、邮箱触发一次确认，而不是偷偷改写文本——用户可能正是在引用出错的内容。
- **草稿与历史留在本地。** 草稿随输入写入 `localStorage`，下次打开恢复；最近 50 条提交记录与之并列。服务端除 issue 本身外不存任何内容。
- **限流属于中继，不属于客户端。** 七天内的去重、按 IP 的小时限流、按 installId 的日限流与每日 issue 配额，防止公开端点变成垃圾入口；重复内容返回原回执码，不再开第二个 issue。
- **Token 永不进包。** GitHub PAT 存在 Cloudflare secret 里，前端只知道 Worker 地址。

## 涉及的公共 API

新增一个端点，位于 Worker（不落在产品 REST 服务上）：`POST /api/feedback`。

- 请求：`{ v: 1, clientTs, kind, title, body, contact?, meta, diagnostics? }`；`v` 为契约版本，`clientTs` 为 ISO 时间戳。`kind ∈ {bug, idea, other}`；`contact` 为 `{ type: "email" | "github", value }`；正文 10–2000 字（发送前按 UTF-8 字节校验）；标题上限 120；诊断上限 4000；整个请求上限 16 KiB。
- 响应 `201 { receipt, createdAt }`。失败统一为 `{ error }` 对象：`400 invalid`（附 `fields` 明细）或 `400 invalid_json`、`403 forbidden`、`409 duplicate`（带原回执码）、`413 too_large`、`429 rate_limited`、`502 upstream_failed`、`503 unavailable`。不返回 issue 链接——追踪 issue 位于私有仓库。
- CORS：显式 origin 白名单，可通过 `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` 配置，默认覆盖两端本地开发端口。
- 端点常量：`packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts` 中的 `FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT` / `FEEDBACK_API_PATH`。

`services/api` 的路由不变；两端不经过本地后端转发反馈，因此本地服务挂掉时仍可提交。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `packages/operational-logging`：新增 `feedback` 入口（契约、校验、脱敏、回执、PII），复用既有的 `redaction` 与 `diagnostics`。
- `packages/feedback-worker`：新增 workspace 包——Worker 入口、GitHub issue 创建、KV 限流、基于 mock GitHub 的测试。
- `apps/web`：对话框、把状态码映射为用户可读失败原因的 API 客户端、草稿/历史存储、头部入口与 `ErrorDiagnosticActions` 中的入口。
- `apps/desktop`：同一套对话框与存储、侧栏底部 GitHub 星标右侧的「我要反馈」入口，以及离线页上预填诊断的入口；对话框在离线分支同样挂载，保证该入口可用。
- 国际化：新增文案同时进入 `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` 与 `apps/desktop` 的 `text/zh.ts`、`en.ts`，两份字典结构必须完全一致。
- 基础设施：Cloudflare 上的 `FEEDBACK_KV` namespace 与 `GITHUB_TOKEN` secret；新建 issue 打上 `source:in-app`、`kind:<kind>`、`needs-triage` 标签。

## 测试设计与测试计划

- **单元测试（6 个文件、47 个用例）：**
  - `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.test.ts`（8）：回执码格式与 10 万次唯一性、键值脱敏与路径归一化、PII 提示不改原文、联系方式分类、标题推导、payload 构造、字段校验。
  - `packages/feedback-worker/src/index.test.ts`（9）：CORS 预检与非法来源、解析前拒绝 16 KiB、非法 JSON/字段 400、成功建 issue、窗口内重复 409、installId 日限 429、每日配额 503、GitHub 5xx 返回 502 且不泄露 token。
  - `apps/web/tests/FeedbackApi.test.ts`（8）与 `apps/desktop/tests/feedback-submit.test.ts`（8）：两端各自的状态码到失败类型映射。
  - `apps/web/tests/FeedbackStore.test.ts`（7）与 `apps/desktop/tests/feedback-store.test.ts`（7）：installId 持久化、草稿默认值与往返、脏数据回退、历史上限 50、按回执码删除。
- **组件测试：** 尚未编写。必填项规则（未选出现频率与影响程度时不可提交）目前只有人工验证覆盖；计划把对话框里的表单状态判断抽成共享纯函数，两端各写断言。
- **端到端（人工，对已部署 Worker）：** 桌面端对话框提交 → 展示回执码且「我的反馈」有记录；停掉本地后端并刷新 → 进入离线页 →「我要反馈」→ 描述已预填、诊断可展开 → 提交 → 得到回执码；恢复后端 → 点「重试」一次即恢复。已验证回执码：`FB-775M-N8A8`（正常）、`FB-XKXW-FGSZ`（离线页）。
- **回归：** 不提交反馈时离线页与改动前完全一致；普通会话不受影响；Web 与桌面端对话框行为一致。

必须通过的命令：`pnpm check`（架构检查、类型检查、单元测试）；`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test`；`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`。

## 验收标准

- [ ] `apps/web` 与 `apps/desktop` 均可提交反馈，并创建带 `source:in-app`、`kind:<kind>`、`needs-triage` 的 GitHub issue。
- [ ] 两端的出现频率与影响程度均为必填：未选择时「提交」保持禁用，并显示「出现频率和影响程度为必填项」。
- [ ] 提交后展示的回执码与「我的反馈」记录、issue 正文中的一致。
- [ ] 离线页的「我要反馈」打开对话框时描述已预填，诊断信息可用（不是「本条反馈没有可用诊断信息」）。
- [ ] 本地后端停止时，从离线页提交仍然成功。

## 补充信息

已部署端点：`https://sciencediscovery-feedback.sciencediscovery.workers.dev`（Cloudflare 固定为 `<worker>.<子域名>.workers.dev` 形式）。KV namespace `FEEDBACK_KV`；secrets `GITHUB_TOKEN`、`REPO_OWNER`、`REPO_NAME`；在 `packages/feedback-worker` 下执行 `npx wrangler deploy` 部署。部署与验证步骤见 `packages/feedback-worker/README.md`。

closed_recent.author: qingkwl
closed_recent.body:
> 本 issue 是 [#799](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/799)（英文版）的**中文跟踪版**，供中文读者讨论；技术细节以英文版为准，两者同步更新。关联：英文版 #799 ｜ 上游相邻 issue：#582（输入 token 分析）、jiuwenswarm#6683 / #7101 / #9938。

## 🚀 背景描述

**起点——用户今天实际要等多久**。装机器上，会话首条消息耗时 **~60–135s**（我方 Windows 桌面端跟踪实测：典型 ~85s，全新安装冷启 ~135s），而同会话第二条仅 **~6s**。无论哪种启动口径（全新首启 / 热启动 / 运行中开新会话），首条税都在。

**税的构成**（日志逐行对时分解，开发栈 + 现场取证）：

| 段 | 大小 | 归属 | 机制 |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCP catalog 冷启动 | **~48s**（热后归零） | **SD 侧** | 内置 stdio MCP 进程在 catalog 首次刷新时才拉起并枚举工具；全新安装把这次刷新推迟到首条消息。本机实证：启动时预热 → 首条此段为 0 |
| SD 侧 run 准备链 | **~14s** | SD API | 每轮 run 前的串行 RPC 链（`skills.list` ×3 + 权限更新 + MCP 重注册）+ API 受理（~4s） |
| 会话装配 | 热态 **~5.3s**（0015 补丁前 ~17s） | JiuwenSwarm | 每会话 `create_instance`；0015–0017 已把 ~5.2s import 税挪出该路径 |
| 工具 schema 处理 | **每轮 ~7–8s** | 上游默认 | 每次模型调用全量携带 ~72 个工具定义 ≈ 2.8 万 token（`progressive_tool_enabled=false`；#582 同口径实测） |
| 模型网络/TTFT + 机器税 | 其余 | — | 真实模型耗时、冷机文件读取、杀软扫描 |

**"26.09s"该放在哪**（本 issue 初版错误地拿它当起点）：它是**解剖锚点、不是用户-facing 起点**——开发栈上"目录已热 + mock 模型"条件下的首条耗时（对照第二条 8.67s）。它唯一的用途是给各段定归属：证明 48s 在 SD catalog（JW `reconcile` 只连 1 个本地回环服务器，毫秒级）、量出 SD 侧准备链大小。若拿它当基线，会把真实问题少算一个目录段和模型时间。

**终点（预期值，待装机 A/B 替换）**。全部方案落地后：热启动口径首条 **6–10s**（现状 ~60–135s），第二条 ~5s（现状 ~6s），冷装机首条不再带 ~48s 目录税。**总优化空间：首条省 ~50–120s + 每条再省 ~3.5s**。

## 设计思路

按实测价值排序。已被测量证伪的选项一并记录，避免重复讨论。

1. **S1 —— agent-ready 后立即预热 MCP catalog**（壳层已实现，PR 随附）。
   壳的 `watchAgentReady` 已在探测 `/agent/info`；`jiuwenswarm.reachable` 一变真即在后台发起 `GET /api/mcp/sources`——与 MCP 设置页的 refresh 是同一个请求。stdio 进程拉起与工具枚举由此与用户看"就绪界面"的时间重叠。尽力而为：失败只写 `shell.log`；若预热输了竞速，run 路径会重跑同样的步骤，行为不分叉。
   直接证据：catalog 启动时预热 → 3 分钟后首条该段为 **0**。

2. **S3 —— 精简控制面 API 的每轮准备链**（计划，目录已热场景下剩余价值最大）。
   `executeAgentRun` 头部在 `chat.send` 前对 JiuwenSwarm 跑串行 RPC 链：`skills.list` ×3（解剖锚点合计 ~4s）、权限更新、每轮 MCP 重注册（~1–2s）。候选：skills 列表缓存（技能集变化时失效）、三次 list 合并、API 证明"工具表未变化"使 adapter 跳过注册往返。准备链幂等后，会话创建时预热也在考虑范围。

3. **J2 —— 渐进式工具暴露**（需上游讨论；JiuwenSwarm 原生）。
   `DEFAULT_PROGRESSIVE_TOOL_ENABLED=False` 使每次调用全量携带 ~72 个工具 schema（~2.8 万 token；mock 端点下占每轮 ~7s——即非模型耗时）。启用现成的 `ProgressiveToolRail` 并配少量 direct 白名单，可把**每轮**输入 token 砍掉约 3 倍。上游切入点：该常量的注释/docstring 已写 "enabled by default" 而代码返回 `False`——低争议入口。翻默认值前必须做真实任务召回率验证。

4. **J3 —— 会话装配 warm pool**（第二批）。
   扩展现有 `AgentWarmPool`，会话创建时预建 adapter；实测剩余价值 ~5.3s → 命中 ~1–2s，必须无缝兜底回今天的全量路径。

**已被测量证伪（存档以免重议）：**
- *J1 —— JW 侧 MCP 并发连接+超时*：JW 侧 reconcile 只开 1 个本地回环服务器（毫秒级）；48s 在 SD catalog。仅留作小型上游卫生提案。
- *S2 —— adapter lifespan 预注册*：工具表由控制面 API 每轮组装后经 `/agent/runs` 交给 adapter；adapter 启动时刻无表可预热，空表预热反而迫使首跑换代重注册。

## 涉及的公开 API

- 现有：`GET /api/mcp/sources`（MCP 设置页 refresh 端点；壳层 agent-ready 后也调用）。
- S1 无新 HTTP API / IPC / 配置面。S3 可能为 skills 缓存增加内部失效信号，其 PR 会列明。

## 与其他模块的关系

- `win_desktop`：壳 `watchAgentReady` 预热挂点 + `first-chat-warmup.ts`（新增，有单测）。
- `services/api`：S3 目标——`executeAgentRun` 头部、`jiuwenswarm-skills.ts` reconcile 链。
- `services/adapter`：`ensure_shared_tools` 本就有工具表 diff；S3 可使其走上"未变化"快速通道。
- JiuwenSwarm 补丁：S1/S3 不需要新补丁；J3 落为 0020+（编号与并行打包工作流协调）。
- `apps/desktop`：无 UI 变化；就绪屏时序不变。
- #582：互补——J2 直接针对该输入。

## 测试设计

- **S1（已在分支）**：URL/头部构造与超时单测（`win_desktop/test/first-chat-warmup.test.ts`）；壳全量 116/116 绿；`win_desktop` 构建干净（esbuild + tsc）。
- **集成 A/B**（每改动，D5 测量纪律）：dev 栈 + 本地 mock OpenAI + `agent_server.log` 逐行分段；基线与改动须在**同一主机负载窗口**内测量（并行打包构建会使绝对值失效）；新会话首条 vs 同会话第二条，3 轮取中位。
- **冷场景验证**：catalog 强制为冷（全新数据目录）时，确认壳预热在人类可感的首条消息前完成，且首个 run 不再含 stdio 拉起段。
- **回归**：壳构建 + 全量壳测试；S3 后 `pnpm test`（api 包）；触及补丁时 JW 冒烟（gateway/agentserver/主对话/记忆）。
- **装机验证**：GUI 交互安装（项目纪律，不用 `/S`），三档启动（全新首启/热启动/attach）+ 首响计时，第二条不回退。

## 验收标准

- 壳预热：`jiuwenswarm.reachable` 变真后 `shell.log` 出现 `[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources -> 200`（或失败行）；就绪屏时序与用户可见行为无任何变化；预热失败永不透出到用户。
- 冷装机首条不再含 stdio 拉起/工具枚举段（现场口径 ~48s）。
- 热启动首条：现场基线 ~60–135s → **S1+S3 后 ≤20s**【预期，待装机 A/B 替换】 → **全部方案后 6–10s**【预期】；第二条 ~6s 不回退（超出噪声），随 J2 降至 ~5s。
- 每轮输入：J2（上游接受后）工具 schema token -50% 以上，固定真实任务集零回归（召回率保持）。
- 必须通过：`pnpm --dir win_desktop build`、`node --test win_desktop/test/*.test.ts`、触及包的 `pnpm test`、上述装机三档。

## 附加信息

- 测量注记：解剖锚点数字测量时本机有并行打包构建，绝对值或偏高 10–25%；现场数字（60–135s）为实测，不受影响。结构性发现（分段边界、目录热则 MCP 段归零、JW 回环毫秒级）与负载无关。A/B 对永远同窗口测量。
- 修订记录（2026-11-03）：正文经评审后重新对齐——初版误以 26.09s 解剖锚点作为起点，低估了用户-facing 问题；起点已改为现场实测（~60–135s），26.09s 仅保留为其本来的内部归因锚点角色。
- S1 实现仅针对桌面壳；Linux/macOS 源码栈路径经同一控制面端点间接受益。

closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Three low-severity findings from the review of #861 and #864, deliberately left out of those pull requests because none of them is a data error, a crash or a performance regression. They are recorded here so the review threads have a real follow-up instead of "later".

**1. The header's new empty sentence blames the date range when a model or project filter caused the empty view.**

`apps/web/src/UsagePage.tsx` (line numbers from `main` `89cd2d30`):

```ts
980: const filteredEmpty = analytics.dailyByModel.length === 0 && analytics.overview.totalTokens === 0;
992: t(filteredEmpty ? "usage.subtitleFilteredEmpty" : "usage.subtitle", { models, tokens: … })
```

`usage.subtitleFilteredEmpty` reads "No usage in the selected range", but `analytics.overview` is narrowed by `from`/`to` **and** `modelProfileId`/`projectId` on the server (`services/api/src/model-usage.ts:302-313`), so selecting a model with no usage in the current range produces a header that names the range, directly above a body whose `usage.filteredEmptyHelp` says "No model usage matches the current date range or model filter." Two near-identical empty sentences stack, and the header's stated cause is wrong in the filter-only case.

Minimal reproduction: render `UsagePage` with a `summary` that has usage for `model-a` only, `filters={ modelProfileId: "model-b" }`, and an `analytics.overview` of `totalTokens: 0` with `dailyByModel: []` — the header prints "No usage in the selected range" although the range contains model-a's usage.

**2. The singular-sentence assertion also matches the plural, so it pins nothing.**

`apps/web/tests/UsagePage.test.tsx:395` asserts `match(/30 tokens across 1 model/)`. `1 model` is a prefix of `1 models`, so replacing `t(models === 1 ? "usage.subtitleOne" : "usage.subtitle", …)` with the plain `usage.subtitle` keeps the file green (`# pass 4 / # fail 0`), i.e. the test cannot catch the regression the PR was written to prevent.

**3. The chart-axis comment claims "the same rule", and the difference is unpinned.**

`apps/web/tests/UsagePage.test.tsx:74` says the chart axis uses the same rule as `formatCompactTokenValue`, but the thresholds differ by construction — the compact formatter switches at `Math.round(value / 1_000) >= 1_000` (`999_500`) while `formatChartNumber` switches at `thousands >= 999.95` (`999_950`) because it prints one decimal of thousands:

```text
bytes  compact   chart
999499 999K      999.5K
999500 1.0M      999.5K
999949 1.0M      999.9K
999950 1.0M      1.0M
```

Both outputs are right for their precision, but nothing states it, so a later "one formatter for both" refactor can move the axis label across `999_500…999_949` with every test still green.

**Expected.** (1) The header's empty state names its actual cause, or reuses the filter-agnostic `usage.filteredEmptyTitle` wording; (2) the singular assertion cannot match the plural (`\b` or `doesNotMatch(/across 1 models/)`); (3) the axis threshold difference is either documented and pinned (`assert.equal(formatChartNumber(999_500), "999.5K")`) or removed.

**Where.** `apps/web/src/UsagePage.tsx:980,992`; `apps/web/tests/UsagePage.test.tsx:74,395`.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`.
- `apps/web` (React + Vite), unit tests via `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` (`tsx --test`, Node `v22.23.2`, pnpm `11.1.2`, Linux x86_64).
- No browser or server needed for any of the three: the strings come from `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` and the formatters are pure functions.

### Additional Information

Found while reviewing #861 (`UsagePage.tsx` header model count) and #864 (`formatCompactTokenValue` unit crossing). Neither PR changes these; they are follow-ups, not blockers.

### Version Information

- `main` `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (2026-11-04).
- `apps/web` package version as of that commit.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Usage header blames the date range for a model filter, and its tests do not pin the singular or the axis threshold

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues for this symptom and found none (terms below).
- [x] I reproduced this on the latest `main` (`89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`).
- [x] This report includes the environment and a minimal reproduction.

### Detailed Description

**What the user sees.** A Session (or a per-message usage line) whose reported token count is just under one million is rendered as `1000K`: the usage chip in the Session header prints `1000K`, the usage page prints `1000.0K` on the chart axis for the same quantity, while the CSV export prints the exact `999999`. The display claims a count (1,000,000) that is not the stored one (999,999), and the unit jumps from `K` to `M` only once the value already crossed the boundary.

**Minimal reproduction** (pure formatter, no DOM):

```ts
import { formatCompactTokenValue } from "./apps/web/src/usageFormat.js";
console.log(formatCompactTokenValue(999_999));   // 1000K
console.log(formatCompactTokenValue(1_000_000)); // 1.0M
```

Observed on `89cd2d30`:

```text
# 999999 -> 1000K
# 1000000 -> 1.0M
```

**Expected.** `999999` renders as `1.0M` (or as an exact `999,999`), never as `1000K`; the compact value must not claim a count the backend did not report.

**Where.** `apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts:19-21` on `89cd2d30`:

- `apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts:19` — `if (value >= 1_000_000) return ...M`
- `apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts:20` — `if (value >= 10_000) return \`${Math.round(value / 1_000)}K\``; for `999_500..999_999` this rounds to `1000`, producing `1000K`.
- `apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts:21` — `if (value >= 1_000) return \`${(value / 1_000).toFixed(1)}K\``; same overflow at `999_950..999_999` would produce `1000.0K` if reached.

The same boundary exists in the chart-axis formatter `apps/web/src/UsagePage.tsx:151-152` (`formatChartNumber`), which prints `1000.0K` for the same values.

Consumers: the Session usage chip (`apps/web/src/App.tsx:922` and `:4831`, from `sessionUsage.totals.totalTokens`), per-message usage (`usageInlineLabel`/`usageBreakdownLabel`), and the usage chart axis.

**Red-first fix proposal.** First add a test that fails on `89cd2d30`:

```ts
assert.equal(formatCompactTokenValue(999_999), "1.0M");
```

then cap the `K` branch: if rounding would reach `1_000`, promote to the `M` branch (or floor instead of round), so `999_999` prints `1.0M` and `1_000_000` stays `1.0M`. `formatTokenField` (exact) and the CSV export are untouched. The internal `formatChartNumber` in `UsagePage.tsx` can be fixed the same way; if it is not exported for a direct test, assert it through the rendered chart tick text of a single-day usage page. A second assertion can cover the 1,000-token boundary (`999_999` vs `1_000_000`) as the regression guard.

**Duplicate check (open and closed).** GitHub search: `"1000K"` → 0; `formatCompactTokenValue` → 1 (issue #858, the Usage-page model count, a different bug); `"compact" token` and `token formatting` → only unrelated CI/settings issues. No open or closed issue reports the unit-boundary rounding, and no open PR touches `apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts` except `#811`, which adds `reasoningTokens` to the aggregation (`+4-2`) and does not change `formatCompactTokenValue` (`:17-22` on live main).

### Environment

- Commit: `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (live `main`, read 2026-11-04).
- Node `v22.23.2`, pnpm `11.1.2`, Linux x86_64.
- Command: `cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/zz-token-format-probe.test.ts` (temporary probe file, not committed).

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`
- Affected package: `apps/web` (`@sciencediscovery/web`)

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
## What happens A `.csv` dataset artifact whose version content is **0 bytes** never leaves the loading state in the artifact panel: the launch card is disabled, the raw fold says "Loading CSV Artifact…", and the CSV workspace cannot be opened. The version read has completed successfully — the gate only mistakes an empty document for "not loaded yet". Measured on live `main` `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (Node v22.23.2, `react-test-renderer`), rendering the real `ArtifactModal` with one `.csv` dataset artifact whose version is a 0-byte `text/csv` blob: ```text has-loading: true launch-disabled: true ``` and directly: ```text isCsvWorkspaceReady({ detected: true, loadedVersionId: "v", source: "", versionId: "v" }) === false // expected true ``` The same panel with a one-newline document (`source === "\n"`) is ready, so the zero-byte case is the only one stuck. Zero-byte uploads are an explicitly supported path (`services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts:87` "readMultipartUploads keeps zero-byte file parts"), and a 0-byte `.csv` that is later declared as an artifact reaches this code. ## Where - `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:236` — `return detected && Boolean(source) && Boolean(versionId) && loadedVersionId === versionId;` (`Boolean(source)` is the defect; `loadedVersionId === versionId` already proves the version has loaded). - `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:217` and `:222` — `disabled={!ready}` on the launch button and `ready ? :

{t("csv.loadingArtifact")}

`. - `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:570` / `:878` — the panel passes `csvWorkspaceReady` into `CsvArtifactPreview`. - `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:907` — `csvWindowOpen && artifact && version && csvWorkspaceReady` also keeps the window unmountable. Contrast measured on the same sources: `parseCsvText("\n", …)` throws `CSV must contain a header and at least one data row`, which the workspace shows as an actionable error. The empty document deserves the same treatment, not a permanent spinner. ## Red-first reproduction Add to `apps/web/tests/ScientificArtifacts.test.tsx` (same imports as the existing CSV tests): ```ts test("an empty CSV version is ready once its version has loaded", () => { assert.equal(isCsvWorkspaceReady({ detected: true, loadedVersionId: "version-1", source: "", versionId: "version-1", }), true); }); ``` Run: ```bash cd apps/web node --import tsx --test tests/ScientificArtifacts.test.tsx ``` Observed on `main` `89cd2d30`: ```text not ok 1 - an empty CSV version is ready once its version has loaded error: Expected values to be strictly equal: false !== true # tests 1 # pass 0 # fail 1 ``` The rendering half is the same failing state: after the version read resolves, the panel text still matches `/Loading CSV Artifact/` and `findAllByType("button").find(csv-artifact-launch).props.disabled === true`. ## Expected result and acceptance - `isCsvWorkspaceReady` must be true once `detected`, `versionId`, and `loadedVersionId === versionId` hold, even when `source === ""`. - The panel must then show a reachable, non-loading state for an empty CSV — either the CSV workspace (whose existing `CSV must contain a header and at least one data row` error is actionable) or an explicit empty-file message. It must not keep saying "Loading CSV Artifact…" after the read completed. - A non-empty CSV keeps today's behaviour: launch enabled, workspace opens, no loading copy. - Keep the not-loaded guards: a mismatched `loadedVersionId`, `detected === false`, or a missing `versionId` must stay `false`. Suggested fix: drop `Boolean(source)` from the gate and rely on `loadedVersionId === versionId` (the source is assigned in the same effect that sets `loadedVersionId`). Dedupe: searched open and closed issues and PRs for `isCsvWorkspaceReady` (0 hits), `"empty.csv"` / `"zero-byte CSV"` (no matching issue; zero-byte appears only in the upload test), and `"Loading CSV Artifact"` (0 hits). Related but distinct: `#842` / `#839` are the clipped-preview notice and width rule; `#446` is the large-CSV row limit. No open or closed item covers this gate.

closed_recent.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The reproduction below is minimal, self-contained, and includes the observed result.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Current:** a Shell execution or workspace transfer whose outcome the backend could not confirm is reported as `state: "unknown"` and is **finished** — the API marks it terminal, stamps `finishedAt`, and writes the reason ("API restarted; inspect completed files and target state before explicitly retrying. No files were replayed."). The Activity panel instead treats `unknown` as *in flight*: `active()` counts it, so the record renders through `ProcessRecord` as `process-live` — its summary row is hidden, its body is permanently open, and it never becomes a foldable history entry. The panel also contradicts itself on what can be done with it:

- an unknown **execution** gets an enabled `Cancel execution` button (`disabled={busy || !active(item.state)}`), even though the API already considers the run terminal;
- an unknown **transfer** is drawn as live but its `Cancel transfer` button is disabled (`disabled={busy || !["queued", "running"].includes(item.state)}`), so the row looks like work in progress that can never be stopped and never completes.

**Expected:** `unknown` is a finished, unverified outcome — not running work. It reads like every other terminal record (a foldable disclosure with its error), and the panel uses one predicate for both the rendering and the action guards, so a record that is shown as live is always a record that can be acted on.

### Where

`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:20` (read on `main` `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`, blob `7c6c81a8cac4`):

```ts
const active = (state: string) => ["queued", "running", "unknown"].includes(state);
```

used for both panels and for the execution action guard — `:87` (`active={active(item.state)}` on executions), `:101` (the same on transfers), `:94` (execution cancel), while the transfer cancel at `:106` uses its own list `["queued", "running"]`.

`apps/web/src/ProcessRecord.tsx:41` turns that flag into the live surface:

```tsx
return <details className={active ? "process-live" : `process-record ${className}${failed ? " failed" : ""}`} open={active || expanded} ref={element}
```

The backend already answers the question `active()` gets wrong; both stores define "terminal" as *not queued and not running*, which includes `unknown`:

- `services/api/src/workspace-transfers.ts:17` — `const terminal = (state) => !["queued", "running"].includes(state);`
- `services/api/src/workspace-transfers.ts:31-34` — an unfinished transfer after an API restart becomes `state: "unknown"`, `finishedAt` set, error recorded;
- `services/api/src/workspace-transfers.ts:155` — a `PUBLICATION_UNCONFIRMED` file makes the whole job `unknown`;
- `services/api/src/shell-executions.ts:72` — `const terminal = (state) => state !== "queued" && state !== "running";`
- `services/api/src/shell-executions.ts:228` and `:444` — executions left unverified are stored as `state: "unknown"`.

### Red-first reproduction (fails on `main` `89cd2d30`)

```tsx
// apps/web/tests/activityUnknown.test.tsx
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { createElement } from "react";
import { act, create, type ReactTestRenderer } from "react-test-renderer";
import { AgentActivityPanel } from "../src/AgentActivityPanel.js";
import type { ApiClient } from "../src/api/client.js";

const activity = {
  executions: [{ id: "lost", agentId: "main", runnerId: "local", workspaceId: "ws_a",
    state: "unknown", provenance: "unconfirmed", error: "Runner restarted before completion was recorded" }],
  transfers: [{ id: "t1", sessionId: "session", agentId: "main", state: "unknown",
    finishedAt: "2026-01-01T00:00:05.000Z", sourceWorkspaceId: "ws_a", targetWorkspaceId: "ws_b",
    files: [{ sourcePath: "a.csv", targetPath: "a.csv" }], createdAt: "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    progress: [{ sourcePath: "a.csv", targetPath: "a.csv", size: 1, sha256: "a".repeat(64), bytes: 0, state: "unknown" }] }],
  timers: [], agents: [],
};
const client = { getAgentActivity: async () => activity } as unknown as ApiClient;
let view: ReactTestRenderer;
await act(async () => { view = create(createElement(AgentActivityPanel, { client, sessionId: "session" })); });
const live = view!.root.findAll((node) => node.type === "details" && String(node.props.className).includes("process-live"));
assert.equal(live.length, 0, "a record whose outcome is unknown is finished, so it must not be shown as live");
```

Observed on `main` `89cd2d30` with `cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/activityUnknown.test.tsx`:

```
# PROCESS_LIVE_RECORDS 2 ["process-live","process-live"]
# CANCEL_TRANSFER_DISABLED [true]
# AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: a record whose outcome is unknown is finished, so it must not be shown as live
# pass 0 # fail 1
```

**Suggested fix (one PR):** make the panel's predicate match the backend's — `const active = (state) => state === "queued" || state === "running"` — and use it for the execution cancel guard too (`:94`), replacing the hand-written list at `:106`. An unknown record then renders as a `process-record` disclosure with the error the API already stores (`:90`, `:104`), and no record is drawn as live while its action is disabled.

## Environment

- `main` `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`
- `node v22.23.2`, `pnpm 11.1.2`, Linux x64
- Trigger in a real session: start a Shell execution or workspace transfer, restart the API (or have a Runner restart mid-run); the Activity panel then lists the record as in flight
- Reproduce: `cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/activityUnknown.test.tsx`

## Version Information

- ScienceDiscovery `main` @ `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (2026-11-04)
- Affected surfaces: Session → Activity panel (`executions`, `transfers` folds); the same `active()` helper is exported for nothing else, so the blast radius is this panel

## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The reproduction below is minimal, self-contained, and includes the observed result.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Current:** in the Chinese UI every tool-result card in the run timeline shows its section headings in English — `Result`, `Error`, `Created files`, `Produced artifacts` — while the section directly above them (`Input`) is already rendered as `输入` from the message catalog. The screen mixes languages inside one card, and the copy button's accessible label becomes `复制Result`.

**Expected:** the section headings follow the reader's locale just like `Input` does: `结果` / `错误` / `创建的文件` / `生成的文件` (wording up to the author) in `zh-CN`, unchanged English in `en`. `stdout` / `stderr` stay verbatim: they are protocol stream names, not prose.

### Where

Read on `main` `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`.

The labels are produced as English literals in `apps/web/src/timeline/tool-result-sections.ts:34-37`

```ts
{ id: "stdout", label: "stdout", pattern: /^stdout:[ \t]?(.*)$/ },
{ id: "stderr", label: "stderr", pattern: /^stderr:[ \t]?(.*)$/ },
{ id: "created-files", label: "Created files", pattern: /^created files:[ \t]?(.*)$/ },
{ id: "produced-artifacts", label: "Produced artifacts", pattern: /^produced artifacts:[ \t]?(.*)$/ },
```

and `apps/web/src/timeline/tool-result-sections.ts:86-87`

```ts
function resultLabel(status: ToolTrace["status"]): string {
  return status === "failed" ? "Error" : "Result";
}
```

The renderer then prints that raw string without consulting the catalog: `apps/web/src/timeline/ToolIoSections.tsx:82` passes `section.label` into `renderSection`, and `ToolIoSections.tsx:45` renders it as `{label}` inside `<span className="tool-io-label">`. The same component already calls `useLocale()` (`ToolIoSections.tsx:9-10`) and localizes everything around it — `t("timeline.input")` at `:75`, the copy label `t("copy.section", { label })` at `:46` — so only these five headings bypass the catalog.

The catalog already has the two generic headings and nothing uses them: `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:1018-1019` (`"timeline.result": "Result"`, `"timeline.error": "Error"`) and `:3986-3987` (`"结果"`, `"错误"`) are dead keys — grep for `timeline.result` / `timeline.error` outside `messages.ts` returns no hit on `89cd2d30`.

### Why it is a bug, not a feature request

`Input` and the copy label are localized from the same component and the same catalog, so the untranslated headings are an unfinished wire-up rather than an unrequested feature. The dead `timeline.result` / `timeline.error` keys are the missing wire-up made visible. Precedent: #871 (queued-cancel toast answered in English) and closed #45 (Chinese UI shows hardcoded English).

### Red-first reproduction (fails on `main` `89cd2d30`)

Add `apps/web/tests/tool-result-labels.test.tsx` and run `cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/tool-result-labels.test.tsx`. It renders the real `ToolIoSections` under `LocaleProvider initialLocale="zh-CN"` and reads back the rendered headings:

```tsx
const trace = { id: "t1", name: "run_python", status: "completed" as const, args: { code: "print(1)" } };
const labels = (html: string) => [...html.matchAll(/class="tool-io-label">([^<]*)</g)].map((m) => m[1]);
const render = (outputText: string, t = trace) => renderToStaticMarkup(
  createElement(LocaleProvider, { initialLocale: "zh-CN" }, createElement(ToolIoSections, { outputText, trace: t })),
);
assert.deepEqual(labels(render("some raw output")), ["输入", "结果"]);
assert.deepEqual(labels(render("stdout:\nok\ncreated files: out.csv")), ["输入", "stdout", "创建的文件"]);
assert.deepEqual(labels(render("boom", { ...trace, status: "failed" as const })), ["输入", "错误"]);
```

Observed on `89cd2d30` — 3 failed / 0 passed:

```
actual:   [ '输入', 'Result' ]                  expected: [ '输入', '结果' ]
actual:   [ '输入', 'stdout', 'Created files' ] expected: [ '输入', 'stdout', '创建的文件' ]
actual:   [ '输入', 'Error' ]                   expected: [ '输入', '错误' ]
# pass 0
# fail 3
```

Note the first element is already `输入`: the failure is entirely the untranslated headings, not the harness.

### Acceptance

- The three assertions above pass with the headings localized in `zh-CN` and still `Result` / `Error` / `Created files` / `Produced artifacts` in `en`.
- `stdout` / `stderr` remain verbatim in both locales.
- The existing parser contract is untouched: `apps/web/tests/tool-result-sections.test.tsx` asserts `section.label === "Created files"` and must stay green — localize at render time (`ToolIoSections.tsx`), not by changing `parseToolResultSections` output.
- The copy button reads `复制结果` / `复制错误`, not `复制Result`.

## Environment

- `main` `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`, Node v22, `apps/web` unit tests (`node --import tsx --test`).
- No backend, network or browser needed: the defect is a static render of one component.

## Version Information

- Repository version: `0.3.0` line on `main` `89cd2d30`.
- Scope: `apps/web/src/timeline/tool-result-sections.ts` (labels), `apps/web/src/timeline/ToolIoSections.tsx` (render), `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` (two new `zh-CN`/`en` keys for `created-files` / `produced-artifacts`; `timeline.result` / `timeline.error` already exist).

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 964fdbe623a640019c6b9325759c2d3f
Branch: dev1/fix/723-escape-nested-window-guard
Base: 8bcc2237e4b5e4aa992267bedbb7e9cc591cc79f
At: 2026-11-02T08:43:15Z

## ScienceDiscovery evidence-backed issue

**Live main:** `8bcc2237e4b5e4aa992267bedbb7e9cc591cc79f` (`test(launcher): cover unavailable Runner startup warning`)
**Area:** `apps/web` — memory-graph explorer vs. nested artifact viewer (CSV workspace / Mol*)
**Filed by:** ScienceDiscovery Product

### Summary

Pressing **Escape** while a CSV workspace or Mol* viewer is open on top of the memory-graph explorer tears down **both**: the nested window and the whole explorer layer. The same interaction is already guarded in the standalone artifact viewer — the explorer is the only layer without the guard, and its embedded artifact modal is the exact place where the guard is skipped.

### Current behavior (file:line)

1. **`apps/web/src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:1051-1055`** — unconditional global close:

   ```tsx
   useEffect(() => {
     const onKey = (event: KeyboardEvent) => { if (event.key === "Escape") onClose(); };
     window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
     return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey);
   }, [onClose]);
   ```

2. **`apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:719-726`** — the same interaction with the opposite semantics, plus the embedded bypass at `:720`:

   ```tsx
   useEffect(() => {
     if (embedded) return;                                   // :720 — bypassed inside the explorer
     function onKey(event: KeyboardEvent): void {
       if (event.key === "Escape" && !csvWindowOpen && !molstarOpen) onClose();   // :722
     }
     window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
     return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey);
   }, [csvWindowOpen, embedded, molstarOpen, onClose]);
   ```

3. The two nested windows each bind their own window-level Escape and neither stops propagation, so one keypress runs both handlers:
   - `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/CsvArtifactWindow.tsx:156-168` — `if (event.key === "Escape") onClose();`, no `stopPropagation`.
   - `apps/web/src/MolstarWindow.tsx:129-133` — `if (event.key === "Escape") onClose();`, no `stopPropagation`.

4. **Reachability:** `ScientificArtifacts.tsx:872`/`:829` keep the CSV workspace and Mol* viewer mounted while `ScientificArtifacts.tsx:932` renders the explorer above the artifact section; the explorer in turn embeds the artifact modal at `MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:1700-1715` (`embedded` on `:1702`). So "explorer open + nested CSV/Mol* open" is a normal state, not a corner case: open a dataset preview, open the CSV workspace, click "view in memory" (`:928`), then press Escape. In embedded mode the artifact layer's own guard is gone (`:720`), and the explorer's unconditional handler is the only one left.

5. **Same file already knows the pattern:** `apps/web/src/MemoryGraphTour.tsx:74-86` binds Escape in the capture phase and calls `stopPropagation()`, with the comment "it must NOT collide with the explorer's global Escape → onClose (which closes the whole explorer)". That guard exists for the tour only; the embedded artifact windows were never given one.

### Expected semantics

Escape closes the **topmost** layer only: with the CSV workspace or the Mol* viewer open inside the explorer, Escape closes that window and leaves the explorer mounted (selected node, filters, unfolded set and viewport preserved); a second Escape, with neither nested window open, closes the explorer. The standalone artifact viewer keeps its current double-Escape behavior (CSV/Mol* first, modal second).

### Impact

One keypress destroys the exploration state the user built: the selected node and its detail/artifact panel, the unfolded/scope-expanded node set, the active chain highlight, the search query and filter chips, and the canvas pan/zoom. The user has to re-open the explorer and re-drill to the same node, and the CSV/Mol* window they were reading is gone at the same instant. This reads as "Escape closed everything" rather than "Escape closed the window I was in".

### Verification plan (no DOM harness in this repo)

`apps/web/package.json` has no jsdom, happy-dom or @testing-library; tests use `react-dom/server` `renderToStaticMarkup` (383 call sites), and `tests/MemoryGraphEntryFocus.test.tsx:25-27` states the canvas is "a WebGL island the SSR test harness cannot run". Two jsdom-free precedents apply:

- pure predicate extraction from this very file — `shouldFocusEntryNode` (`MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:736`) tested in `tests/MemoryGraphEntryFocus.test.tsx`;
- source-text assertions for wiring, e.g. `tests/SidebarDrawer.test.tsx:75-80`, `tests/ProxySettingsEditor.test.tsx:154`.

Acceptance:

1. Export `shouldCloseOnEscape(csvWindowOpen: boolean, molstarOpen: boolean): boolean` from `apps/web/src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx`, returning `!csvWindowOpen && !molstarOpen`.
2. New `apps/web/tests/MemoryGraphEscapeGuard.test.tsx` covering all three combinations: `(true,false)→false`, `(false,true)→false`, `(false,false)→true`.
3. Wire the explorer's global Escape effect to that predicate with the live nested-overlay state of the embedded artifact modal (the embedded modal already tracks `csvWindowOpen`/`molstarOpen` at `ScientificArtifacts.tsx:494-495`); any wiring that satisfies the observable below is acceptable.
4. Observable acceptance: with a CSV workspace or Mol* viewer open inside the explorer, one Escape closes only that window and the explorer stays mounted with its selected node, filters and unfolded set; the next Escape closes the explorer. Standalone artifact viewer behavior unchanged.

Red evidence on live main today — the module imports headlessly, and the guard does not exist:

```
$ cd apps/web && node --import tsx -e "import('./src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx').then(m=>{console.log('exports:', Object.keys(m).join(','));console.log('shouldCloseOnEscape =', typeof m.shouldCloseOnEscape)})"
exports: CHAIN_BUTTONS,MemoryGraphExplorer,NODE_LABELS,buildScopeChildCounts,countScopeChildren,countVisibleAndTotal,findArtifactNodeInGraph,findCodeNodeInGraph,findSourceFileNodeInGraph,mergeChainScopeExpansions,mergeExpansions,shouldFocusEntryNode
shouldCloseOnEscape = undefined
```

```
$ grep -rn "Escape\|shouldCloseOnEscape" apps/web/tests/
tests/ProxySettingsEditor.test.tsx:154:  assert.match(source, /event\.key === "Escape"/);
tests/SidebarDrawer.test.tsx:75:  // Escape closes the drawer, ...
```

No test covers Escape in the explorer today; `node --import tsx --test tests/MemoryGraphEntryFocus.test.tsx` passes 6/6, so the harness and the predicate precedent are proven.

### Not a duplicate

Open-issue search (`Escape in:title`, `escape explorer`, `memory graph close`, `MemoryGraphExplorer`) finds no report: the only Escape-titled issue is closed #672 (HTML entity decoding). Our open PRs `#311/#648/#658/#663/#664/#676/#678/#680/#709/#722` touch none of these files or handlers (#648 is the web test build, #658/#663 text truncation, #664 fetch guard, #676 desktop, #678/#680/#709 CAS, #722 evolve evidence, #311 evolve trigger).

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: ebfd6b084d6c47d39c50227fadbd2150
Branch: dev1/fix/run-stream-turn-placement
Base: 0e7075c475fe
At: 2026-11-01T17:46:50Z

## Environment

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- live `main` sha: `0e7075c475fe657a7e772d7efdaa55cab1bcd9ba` (2026-11-01T17:05:39Z)
- Node v22.23.2; the desktop reducer is plain TypeScript and needs no Electron runtime.

## Reproduction (headless, no UI)

The desktop transcript folds a run's events with `reduceRunStream` in `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts`. The existing test file already has the helpers `fold`, `responseStarted(responseId, turn)` and `delta(text, responseId)`.

1. Add this test to `apps/desktop/tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts`:

```ts
test("a later turn's text is not folded into turn 1 when its response.started arrives late", () => {
  const state = fold([
    responseStarted("r1"),
    delta("first turn", "r1"),
    { responseId: "r1", type: "assistant.response.settled" } as RunStreamEvent,
    delta("HELLO", "r2"),
    responseStarted("r2", 2),
    delta(" WORLD", "r2"),
  ]);
  const second = state.turns.find((turn) => turn.turn === 2);
  assert.deepEqual(state.turns[0]!.responses.map((response) => response.content), ["first turn"]);
  assert.equal(second?.responses[0]?.content, "HELLO WORLD");
});
```

2. Run it:

```
cd apps/desktop && node --import tsx --test tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts
```

3. Observed on live main: `# tests 39`, `# pass 38`, `# fail 1`.

```
not ok 9 - a later turn's text is not folded into turn 1 when its response.started arrives late
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
        'first turn',
    +   'HELLO WORLD'
      ]
```

## Current vs expected

Current state after folding the script above:

```json
[
  { "turn": 1, "responses": [{ "id": "r1", "text": "first turn" }, { "id": "r2", "text": "HELLO WORLD" }] },
  { "turn": 2, "responses": [{ "id": "r2", "text": "" }] }
]
```

Expected:

```json
[
  { "turn": 1, "responses": [{ "id": "r1", "text": "first turn" }] },
  { "turn": 2, "responses": [{ "id": "r2", "text": "HELLO WORLD" }] }
]
```

The second turn's whole answer is drawn inside the first turn, and the second turn is left with an empty answer block.

## Code evidence

- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:366-382` — `withResponse` handles a `responseId` it has never seen by creating a turn with the hard-coded `turn: 1` (`const created: AssistantTurn = { ..., turn: 1 }`), for every event type, including one whose start frame will later announce another turn.
- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:107-111` — `assistant.response.started` adds a blank block to *its own* turn and does not adopt the block already created for the same `responseId`, so the same response exists twice.
- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:404-411` — `locateTurn` returns the first turn that owns the `responseId`, so after the start frame arrives every later delta keeps landing in the wrongly-anchored turn-1 block; turn 2's block stays empty forever.
- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:357-365` — the comment at `withResponse` documents this ordering as supported ("A frame that arrives before its `assistant.response.started`, or with no open response at all, opens a block rather than dropping the text").
- `apps/desktop/tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts:139-142` — the existing coverage is a single-turn orphan (`fold([delta("orphan text")])`, no `responseId`, no second turn), which is why this gap is green today.

## Why it happens in practice

- A frame that cannot be read is folded as `null` while its cursor still advances (`reducer.ts:88-96`, and PR #616 made that path explicit). If the unreadable frame is an `assistant.response.started`, its deltas are then anchored to turn 1 by the branch above.
- The same comment block says older records omit `responseId` on text frames (`reducer.ts:357-365`). Such a delta is routed by `locateTurn(state, undefined)` to the newest turn's newest block; when that text belongs to turn 2 before turn 2 exists, `withResponse` again creates `turn: 1`, and the subsequent `assistant.response.started(turn 2)` leaves an empty second block.
- Replay (`foldRunRecords`) reuses the same reducer, so a finished run opened from the desktop transcript reproduces the same wrong attribution, not just the live stream.

## Suggested fix (one file, ~10-20 lines)

In `withResponse`, remember a block created for an unknown `responseId` (for example a `pending` map on the state, or a block placed at `turn: 1` that is moved when its start frame arrives): on `assistant.response.started`, adopt/move the existing block for that `responseId` instead of appending a blank one. Keep the current single-turn fallback when no start frame ever arrives, so `apps/desktop/tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts:139-142` stays green.

## Acceptance

- The test above is added and passes; the file reports `# tests 39` / `# pass 39` / `# fail 0`, i.e. the 38 existing tests stay green.
- `node --import tsx --test tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts` in `apps/desktop`.

## Impact

The desktop transcript misattributes a turn's answer text to the previous turn and renders an empty answer block, and because tools and subagents are placed on the newest turn (`reducer.ts:146-196`), the transcript's step order no longer matches what happened. The same reconstruction feeds replayed finished runs, so the error persists after reload instead of being a live-only glitch.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed issues and pull requests: `reduceRunStream`, `run-stream reducer`, `"response.started" turn`, `"turn 1" transcript`. Results are the feature PR that introduced the reducer (#500) and the frame-error PRs (#505, #616); none of them reports or fixes the turn placement above.

closed_recent.body:
## Summary

The desktop source viewer closes a triple-quoted string on the first `"""` that follows an odd *or even* number of backslashes. An even count does not escape the delimiter, so a legal, terminated string swallows the rest of the file: every following line is tokenised as `string`.

## Repro (live main `1e886583`)

Node v22.23.2, from the repository root:

```bash
cat > /tmp/t1.ts <<'TS'
import { highlightPython } from "./apps/desktop/src/app/python-source.ts";
const src = 'x = """a\\\\"""\ny = 2\n';
highlightPython(src).forEach((l, i) => console.log(i + 1, JSON.stringify(l)));
TS
node --import tsx /tmp/t1.ts
```

Observed:

```
1 [{"text":"x = "},{"kind":"string","text":"\"\"\"a\\\\\"\"\""}]
2 [{"kind":"string","text":"y = 2"}]
```

Expected: line 2 carries no `string` token, because `"""a\\"""` is a complete Python string (`\\` is one escaped backslash, so the delimiter is unescaped) and `y = 2` is code.

## Cause

`apps/desktop/src/app/python-source.ts:130-132`:

```ts
// An escaped delimiter is part of the string, not its end.
while (end > 0 && source[end - 1] === "\\") end = source.indexOf(delimiter, end + 1);
```

The test is "a backslash precedes the delimiter", not "an odd number of backslashes precedes it". `"""a\\"""` has two, so the real terminator is skipped and scanning resumes at the next `"""` — or at end of file, which is the failure above.

## Expected fix

Count the run of `\\` before the candidate and only skip when the count is odd (~5 lines, same function).

## Suggested red test

`apps/desktop/tests/python-source.test.ts` (exists; 8 tests, none covers an escaped backslash before a delimiter) — `a triple-quoted string ending in an escaped backslash does not swallow the code after it`:

```ts
const lines = highlightPython('x = """a\\\\"""\ny = 2\n');
assert.equal(lines[1]?.some((token) => token.kind === "string"), false);
```

```bash
node --import tsx --test apps/desktop/tests/python-source.test.ts
```

## Dedupe

Searched open+closed for `highlightPython`, `triple-quoted string view`, `"source view" python`: 0 hits. `#537` (closed) added highlighting to the web artifact preview, a different module.

Filed by ScienceDiscovery Product.
