closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## What happened

Nightly real-model E2E fails the whole Daily gate when a single request to the configured OpenAI-compatible model gateway returns a provider error. Other cases in the same job still pass, and the same case can pass on another run the same night.

On 2026-10-06, main Nightly run [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`) executed 10 real cases: 5 passed, 5 failed, 0 skipped, in 3.0 hours. The job uses `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash` and `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL=https://yibuapi.com/v1`. Playwright is configured with `retries: 0` and one worker.

Three of those failures were gateway responses, and the product already showed them:

- **DRB-75** failed in 9.3 seconds. No subagent and no tool call ran. The page showed error 181001: HTTP 500 from the gateway, body `Database error, please contact the administrator`, type `new_api_error`.
- **PUCT-COMPRESS** failed in 11.5 seconds with the same HTTP 500 text in `run.error`. No search started.
- **workspace plan and run-anchored subagent** failed after 7.0 minutes. The page already showed HTTP 503: `No available channel for model deepseek-v4-flash under group default (distributor)`, code `model_not_found`, wrapped as the same 181001 gateway error. The test then waited out a 420 second timeout for a plan section that never appeared.

The other five cases in that job passed, including DRB-58 after 51.0 minutes and TC-E2E-01 after 43.0 minutes. The same three cases passed on the release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020) (`releases/v0.3.0.beta` at `6d3c49a8`) the same night. The previous night, that same beta commit passed all 10 real cases in [37382672011](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37382672011).

## Why this is a product/CI problem

The gateway is failing one request at a time, not the whole job. A 500 or 503 still fails the real-E2E job, which fails Nightly. There is no retry, and the suite does not record these as an external provider fault separate from a product regression.

## Expected

A transient gateway 500 or 503 is visible as that provider error. One such request does not have the same meaning as a product run that finished and failed to deliver. Cases that passed in the same job stay visible as passes.

## Evidence limits

This does not say the gateway was down for the whole job. It also does not cover the research cases that ran for about 20 minutes and then ended without a report; those are separate failures.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] ci: Nightly real E2E fails the gate on one transient model-gateway 500 or 503

closed_recent.author: qingkwl
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

`services/api` has Windows-specific OS behavior requirements with no platform seam (#491):

- Owner-only (0600/0700) file semantics rely on `chmod`, which only toggles the read-only bit on Windows; the most sensitive files in the service (encrypted model/MCP credential master key, generated SSH private keys) are left unprotected.
- Atomic replace via rename transiently fails on Windows with EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY while antivirus scanners or search indexers hold the destination; callers currently see raw errors.
- At-rest secret protection has no Windows story at all (POSIX file permissions carry the protection; Windows needs per-user encryption).

PR #492 carried an earlier version and was closed; this re-lands the API platform facade with a clean scope (platform layer only, no consumers rewired yet), a green typecheck, no unresolvable references, and Windows real-machine evidence.

## Expected

1. `services/api/src/platform/os/` provides the facade: `types.ts` (adaptation surface), `index.ts` (single dispatch point), `posix.ts` (transparent passthrough), `win32.ts` (Windows implementation).
2. Adaptations: `restrictToOwner` (icacls owner-only ACL, SID-based grantee for locale-safety), `renameReplace` (retry with backoff on transient locks), `wrapSecret`/`unwrapSecret`/`isWrappedSecret` (DPAPI per-user encryption, identity on posix).
3. POSIX behavior unchanged (chmod, plain rename, identity wrapping).
4. `node:test` suites cover both adaptations, including a real DPAPI round-trip on Windows.
5. Consumer rewiring (secrets store, ssh-config) lands in follow-up PRs stacked on this one.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows facade behaviors

Preconditions: Windows host.
Steps: Run `node --import tsx --test services/api/src/platform/os/win32.test.ts`.
Expected / pass: 9/9 green, including a real DPAPI wrap/unwrap round-trip of a master-key-sized blob and icacls-based restrictToOwner assertions. **Verified on Windows 11 23H2, Node v24.21.0.**

### Case 2 — POSIX unchanged

Steps: Run the posix suite; on Linux CI the posix file is a passthrough by construction.
Expected / pass: posix suite green; no behavior change vs main.

### Case 3 — Facade only, no consumers yet

Steps: Inspect the diff.
Expected / pass: New files only; no existing api file is modified in this PR (consumers arrive as separate stacked PRs).

## Related

- Implements #491 (API OS platform abstraction)
- Parent: #400
- Re-lands the api-platform portion of the closed #478/#492 per their review feedback (typecheck green, platform-only scope, no internal references, Windows evidence)
closed_recent.title: [Feature] API OS adaptation facade (owner-only permissions, replace-with-retry, at-rest secret wrapping)

closed_recent.author: qingkwl
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

`services/runner` has Windows-specific behavior requirements with no platform seam:

- Killing a child with POSIX signals does not tear down the process tree on Windows (#482): the runner needs `terminateTree` semantics (`taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F`), while POSIX must keep the current signal-based behavior unchanged.
- Owner-only (0600) permission semantics rely on `chmod`, which only toggles the read-only bit on Windows (#477 covers the general platform work; the runner side needs `restrictToOwner` through the facade).
- Conda environment specifics (delay-load DLL directories, the bundled m2-bash shell location, win-64 package substitution guidance) are spread over platform branches today.

PR #478 carried an earlier version of this work but was closed; this re-lands the runner-platform portion with a clean scope (runner only), a green typecheck, no unresolvable references, and real-machine Windows evidence.

## Expected

1. `services/runner/src/platform/` provides the facade: `types.ts` (adaptation surface), `index.ts` (single dispatch point), `posix.ts` (transparent passthrough), `win32.ts` (Windows implementation: `terminateTree` via taskkill, `restrictToOwner` via icacls, conda path/shell helpers).
2. Runner call sites use the facade only: `killSandboxProcess` goes through `terminateTree`; server-side 0600 semantics go through `restrictToOwner`. No direct `process.platform` branches for these concerns in consumer code.
3. POSIX behavior unchanged (signals, chmod).
4. `node:test` suites cover both adaptations.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows tree kill (matches #482 Case 1)

Preconditions: Windows host; a Node child that spawns a grandchild that stays alive.
Steps: Call `terminateTree(child)`; inspect the process list for both PIDs.
Expected / pass: Both PIDs are gone; helper returns true. **Verified on a real Windows 11 machine** with the packaged runner build: child + grandchild gone within 1s (evidence script `verify-482-case1.mjs` run recorded 2026-10-28).

### Case 2 — POSIX unchanged

Steps: Run the runner suite (`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/runner test`).
Expected / pass: 37/37 green on Windows with the posix passthrough; on Linux the behavior is identical to main (posix file is a passthrough only).

### Case 3 — Facade only

Steps: Inspect runner call sites for tree-kill/permission paths.
Expected / pass: All go through `platform/index.ts`; no raw taskkill / chmod outside `platform/`.

## Related

- Implements the runner half of #482 (tree-kill) and part of #477 (owner-only permissions)
- Parent: #400
- Re-lands the runner-platform portion of the closed #478 with review feedback addressed (typecheck green, runner-only scope, no internal references, Windows evidence)
closed_recent.title: [Feature] Runner OS adaptation facade (terminateTree / restrictToOwner / conda paths)

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

`SseFrameDecoder` in `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts` keeps a partial frame in memory until it sees the `\n\n` terminator. On `main` at `ca98c195`:

- `push` appends the chunk to the retained buffer — `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:41-44` (append at line 42);
- `drain` re-normalizes the whole buffer with `this.buffer.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")` and only then looks for a blank line — `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:51-70` (lines 55 and 56);
- `flush` is only reached when the stream ends — `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:46-49`, called from `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:111`.

If a stream keeps sending bytes for a frame that never receives its terminating blank line, the buffer grows for as long as that stream stays open. Memory grows with bytes received, and because the whole buffer is re-scanned on every chunk, total work grows quadratically. While the stream is open nothing bounds it and nothing reports it; if the stream ends, the tail reaches `flush()` and is counted as a skipped frame (#616). The gap this issue closes is the **live window**. Growth needs continuing bytes after an unterminated frame — a server that merely stalls sends nothing and so grows nothing.

**This is pre-existing on `main` and is not introduced by PR #616.** #616 handled a payload that does not parse (`stream.ts:129-140`); this is a framing failure, where no complete frame is ever handed to `JSON.parse`. #616 does cover the end-of-stream case (an over-long tail reaches `flush()` and is then counted as a skipped frame), so the remaining gap is only while the stream is still open — which is the case for a live run. The decoder region is byte-identical at `ca98c195` and at #616's head.

`pump` (`apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:105`) is the only production consumer. The API's own writer always terminates a frame with `data: <json>\n\n` (`services/api/src/runs/index.ts`, `writeSse`), so a normal server does not trigger this; it needs a stream whose writer omits the terminator while continuing to send data.

## Expected

> Contract note: #616 merged into `main` at `5b25c260` on 2026-10-28. The skipped-frame path exists now, so this issue specifies skip-once-and-continue, not a stream-ending failure.

- The decoder's retained buffer is bounded by a constant, so an unterminated frame cannot grow memory without bound.
- On exceeding the ceiling, the decoder discards bytes up to and including the next `\n\n` — that terminator closes the oversized frame, it does not start a new one — and never hands the dropped tail to `JSON.parse`, so a crafted tail cannot be re-interpreted as a new event.
- #616 is merged into `main` (`5b25c260`, 2026-10-28), so the skipped-frame path is available: the drop is reported **once** through it (the existing "Skipped N updates that could not be read." wording), the frame is counted once, and the stream continues instead of ending. No second notice and no new error mode.
- No bytes after the drop are parsed, and no event or cursor id is taken from the dropped tail. On reconnect the client's cursor is whatever the last fully received frame set it to.
- Clean streams and frames below the bound behave exactly as today.
- An earlier revision of this issue said the drop should end the stream as a bounded framing failure, because `main` had no skipped-frame path at the time. That is no longer the contract: #616 landed, and skip-once-and-continue is what this change does.

## Repro shape (unit level)

```ts
const decoder = new SseFrameDecoder();
for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i += 1) decoder.push('id: 1\ndata: {"type":"run.started"}');
// no frame is emitted, no error is raised, and decoder.buffer keeps growing
```

Then append `'\n\n'` plus a valid frame: at `main` the retained buffer has no upper bound, and only the later terminator releases it.

## Suggested guard (sketch, not prescriptive)

- Add a `MAX_FRAME_CHARS` constant to the decoder; pick it with headroom over the largest event the API emits (live tool results are the biggest frames).
- When no boundary is found and the buffer exceeds it, discard bytes up to and including the next `\n\n` — that terminator closes the oversized frame, it does not begin a new one — never hand the dropped tail to `JSON.parse`, count the frame once, and resume parsing after it so later well-formed frames still arrive. Report it through #616's existing one-notice path; do not add a second notice or a new error mode. Advance no cursor from bytes that were not fully received.
- Optional, same change: normalize only the newly appended part of the buffer instead of re-scanning all of it on every chunk (`stream.ts:55`) — this removes the quadratic term.
- Reuse the existing wording ("Skipped N updates that could not be read.") rather than adding a second notice.

## Verification cases

1. **Endless unterminated frame** — the retained buffer stays at or below the bound; the frame is given up on, its terminator is consumed, and the stream continues, so one bad frame does not end a live run.
2. **One failure, not many** — the oversized frame is counted once and reported once through the existing notice; a stream without such a frame reports nothing; the dropped tail is never parsed (a crafted tail that would parse as JSON still yields no event and no cursor advance).
3. **Clean stream unchanged** — every frame delivered, no error (existing `apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts` cases stay green).
4. **Large but legal frame** — a frame below the bound still parses fully.
5. **No cursor from unread bytes** — the drop produces no event and no cursor advance; the replay cursor stays at the last fully received frame's id, and a cap drop never hands over an id from bytes that were never fully read.
6. **No new setting** — the ceiling is a module constant, not user configuration, preserving #505's "no new setting" constraint.

## Context

Found while reviewing PR #616 at `c7d49f79` (static review, no tests run). Adjacent to #505 but a different failure class (framing vs `JSON.parse`), so it is tracked separately. Client-only; no server change and no protocol change is needed.

Out of scope, stated so it is not mistaken for covered: with bounded memory, a peer that simply stops writing still keeps the stream open forever — `running` stays true and the follow path never settles. That is a stall/liveness question, not a memory one, and it exists on `main`. This issue does not address idle or stalled streams, and it does not change the pre-existing fact that a clean close with no parsed terminal is silent on the follow path (`use-workspace.ts:892-910`: `closeRunStream` marks `terminal: true`, a run still executing server-side can look finished). That is a separate liveness/wording item, unchanged by this fix.

Owner: ScienceDiscovery Dev-1 (desktop). Labels and milestone deliberately left to the maintainer: #505 sits on `v0.3.0`, and this repo-side label write is not available to us.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] desktop: cap the SSE frame decoder buffer so an unterminated frame cannot grow without bound

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

After a remote Shell Execution is accepted, a lost status observation is recorded in two places that disagree.

The shell execution record becomes `unknown` / `unconfirmed`. That means the remote result has not been confirmed. It does not mean the command failed. Inspecting that execution reconciles the record with the Runner by the same Execution ID and does not resubmit the command (see #185).

The provenance execution run written when that observation throws is different. The dispatch error path appends an execution run with `status: "failed"`, `exitCode: null`, and stderr set to the observation error. `ExecutionRun.status` only allows `succeeded`, `failed`, and `cancelled`. Runs are append-only, so a later reconciliation that adopts the Runner's committed result updates the shell execution record and leaves this run unchanged.

Skill distillation and the memory graph read execution runs. They can treat an unconfirmed observation as a job failure, and they still see that failure after the shell execution record has been reconciled to the Runner's real outcome.

## Expected

- An observation that stays unconfirmed is not reported as a successful job or as a failed job by the execution-run record, by skill distillation, or by the memory graph.
- If reconciliation later adopts a committed Runner result for that same Execution ID, those readers see that result.
- A Runner outcome that really failed or was cancelled, including a non-zero exit or a recorded failure with a committed version, is still stored as failed or cancelled.
- The command is not replayed.

## Note

#185 does not choose how to represent an unconfirmed run. `ExecutionRun.status` has no value for "not confirmed", and the run list is append-only. This issue tracks that choice. It is separate from the shell-execution reconciliation fix.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] An unconfirmed shell observation is stored as a failed execution run

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## 范围与证据

汇总 [2026-10-24 Nightly run 40121906605](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605) 的三项剩余问题。运行版本：`9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be`。

#514 / #515 修复的 Ubuntu 26.04 / Python 3.14 依赖准备已通过，本次不再作为阻塞项。以下区分实际运行结果与源码诊断，不据此认定所有 main CI 都失败。

## 1. real research-8 的会话标题断言未跟随显示规则更新

[失败 job 120955308760](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120955308760) 已实际执行该用例，在点击 Add session 后失败：

- [`issue-67-34-inline-cards.spec.ts:221`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be/test/issue-67-34-inline-cards.spec.ts#L219-L228) 期望 `Untitled session`，实际为 `Untitled session 2`。
- #510 已合入同一 Project 多个未命名会话显示序号的行为，实际标题与该规则一致。当前证据支持“测试期望过时”，不能据此认定产品的计划/子任务功能损坏。
- 此前的计划、follow-up、reload 断言已通过；失败后的切回原会话及位置保持断言尚未执行，不能算通过。
- #511 仍讨论编号集合与排序的 UX 口径，本 issue 不替它决定方案，只修复测试对已实现显示规则的错误假设。

## 2. 已执行失败的分片被汇总成 NOT_RUN

[research-8 结果 artifact 12574909042](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/artifacts/12574909042) 的 `e2e-real/tagged/summary.json` 明确记录：

- planned=1、executed=1、passed=0、failed=1；
- 该身份的 `outcome=FAIL`。

但 [汇总 job 120992446082](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120992446082) 输出 executed=18/19、passed=18，并将该用例标为 `NOT_RUN`。

源码诊断：[`.ci/real-report.mjs:19-24`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be/.ci/real-report.mjs#L19-L24) 在失败分片的 `results.push(...summary.results)` 之前抛出 `SHARD_FAILED`，丢掉了其已执行结果。需要保留身份、版本、digest 等校验通过的失败证据，同时继续让 gate 失败。该运行应准确呈现 19 executed、18 passed、1 failed，而不是将执行失败混同为未运行。

## 3. 两项 UT 等待完成超时，原因待查

[UT job 120955273894](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120955273894)：4754 planned / 4754 executed / 4752 passed / 2 failed / 0 skipped。

[UT artifact 12572160563](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/artifacts/12572160563) 中的实际失败：

- `ut/tagged/group-279/worker-1-events.jsonl`：`services/api/src/evolution/orchestrator.test.ts` 的 `a measured run is staged before the sidecar is asked to start`，报 `timed out waiting for the run to settle`。
- `ut/tagged/group-343/worker-1-events.jsonl`：`services/api/src/server.test.ts` 的 `running sessions accept queued runs and start them after the active run completes`，报等待 run 进入 `completed` 超时。

[同一 SHA 较早的 UT job 120785725594](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40064771478/job/120785725594) 在 Ubuntu 26.04 上 4754/4754 通过。现有证据不能区分测试时序、环境或产品状态推进问题，不认定为负载抖动或确定性回归。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 会话切换测试按当前显示规则及明确的 Session 身份校验，补齐“新增会话 → 切回原会话 → 原计划/时间线位置保持”的验证；不删除原行为断言。
- [ ] 为汇总器补充“分片实际执行但失败”的无模型回归测试，保留 executed/failed 计数和失败身份；身份不匹配、缺失、重复、跳过等情况仍不得放行。
- [ ] 使用上述已有结果验证汇总应为 19 executed / 18 passed / 1 failed，退出码仍非零；不通过跳过失败分片把 gate 改绿。
- [ ] 分别定位两项 UT 超时，保留最后运行状态及相关事件等诊断证据，补充针对性回归验证；仅延长超时或重跑成功不能作为已定位的证据。

本 issue 基于已有日志、artifact 与源码核对，未触发新的付费模型调用或 CI 重跑。
closed_recent.title: [Bug] ci: 修复 Nightly 会话标题断言与失败分片统计，排查两项 UT 超时

closed_recent.body:
## Problem
Desktop workspace upload sends `File.name` into FormData without client-side basename sanitization. Path escape remains a server responsibility (`readWorkspaceFile` notes this), but a crafted name such as `../outside.txt` or a name containing `/` should be rejected or renamed on the client as defense in depth.

## Expected
Before upload, the client strips path segments / rejects unsafe names so only a basename reaches FormData; server still remains the authority and continues to rename/reject escapes.

## Verification cases

1. **Crafted relative name**
   - **Preconditions:** Open session with workspace panel; upload enabled (session not archived).
   - **Steps:**
     1. Upload (or simulate) a `File` whose `name` is `../outside.txt`.
     2. Inspect the FormData filename and the resulting workspace listing.
   - **Expected / pass:** Client does not send `../outside.txt` as-is (sanitize/reject); server listing shows no escape outside the session workspace.

2. **Name with slash**
   - **Preconditions:** Same as (1).
   - **Steps:** Upload a `File` whose `name` contains `/` (e.g. `a/b.txt`).
   - **Expected / pass:** Client basename-only or reject; no nested path created via the client name alone.

3. **Normal basename unchanged**
   - **Preconditions:** Same as (1).
   - **Steps:** Upload `notes.md`.
   - **Expected / pass:** File appears under the session workspace with the expected name (rename-on-conflict still applies).

## Context
Follow-up from review of https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/501. Non-blocking; server-side path authority noted in-PR.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] desktop: sanitize upload File.name basename before FormData (defense in depth)

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

The workspace **Artifacts** list appears **project-scoped**: while working in session B, files from session A in the same project still show up (sometimes grouped under the other session’s name). Not a data-loss bug — the model still read the correct uploads — but the list is noisy and easy to mis-click.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 demos:

- Scenario 1: session B’s file count included session A artifacts.
- Scenario 2: during Specialist session, Case A reports still listed under “Skill csv-quality-check” while new files appeared under “Specialist CSV质检”.

## Why this may be intentional

Project-level sharing can be desirable (reuse a CSV across sessions, compare outputs). This issue is filed **low priority** to force an explicit product decision, not to demand an immediate change.

## Design questions (need a call)

1. Should Artifacts default to **current session only**, with an opt-in “Show project files”?
2. Or keep project scope but visually separate **This session** vs **Other sessions** with clearer hierarchy?
3. Should uploads be session-private by default and only promoted to project library on pin/share?

## Expected after a design pass

Whatever the choice, the panel should make scope obvious so users do not think another session’s outputs belong to the active run.

## Priority

**Low** — polish / information architecture; confirm against intended project-workspace model before changing.

## Related

Not a substitute for timeline density (#330).
closed_recent.title: [Usability] workspace Artifacts panel is project-scoped and mixes other sessions’ files

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
## Problem
A Windows durability fix for CAS directory `fsync` (`O_RDWR` on `win32` because `FlushFileBuffers` needs a writable handle) and `toNamespacedPath` for SQLite paths landed inside the conversational-configuration protocol PR (#553), mixed with unrelated schema/protocol work. On Linux the `win32` branch is never taken, so CI here cannot exercise the failure mode (silently weaker directory sync if the open/handle is wrong).

## Expected
- CAS Windows durable-directory sync ships in its own small PR (or clearly scoped commit series) with Windows verification attached.
- Configuration/protocol PRs do not carry unrelated CAS durability changes.

## Verification cases
1. **Writable-directory sync on Windows**
   - Preconditions: Windows host; CAS `VersionStore` / `RefStore` initialized on a normal NTFS directory.
   - Steps: Create/update a live ref that triggers `syncDirectory`; confirm no throw from `open(..., O_RDWR|O_DIRECTORY)` + `handle.sync()`.
   - Expected / pass: Operation succeeds; refs.sqlite and object dirs remain consistent after process kill mid-write (WAL + FULL sync still hold).
2. **Long / namespaced path**
   - Preconditions: Windows; store path that needs `\\?\` / namespaced form (deep or near-MAX_PATH tree).
   - Steps: Open `RefStore` / lease DBs via the same helpers.
   - Expected / pass: `DatabaseSync(toNamespacedPath(...))` opens; no path-not-found solely from missing namespace prefix.
3. **Negative — read-only directory**
   - Preconditions: Directory without write ACL for the process.
   - Steps: Trigger `syncDirectory`.
   - Expected / pass: Failure is loud (thrown/propagated), not a silent no-op sync; caller sees the error.
4. **Linux unchanged**
   - Preconditions: Linux CI/dev.
   - Steps: Same CAS unit/integration paths as today.
   - Expected / pass: Still uses `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY`; no behavioral change.

## Context
Refs #553 (CAS hunks in `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts`, `workspace-lease.ts`, `workspace-lifecycle.ts`). Spotted during review of the four-PR configuration stack; out of scope for the shared configuration protocol.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] CAS: isolate Windows durable-directory sync (O_RDWR + toNamespacedPath) from feature stacks

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claim-Id: 7f14c14bab4842d79ca977e50342115e Branch: dev/926-bug-run-timeline-prints-raw-english-stat Base: 2908e9e8bb4f At: 2026-11-05T13:41:38Z ## What happens In the Session run timeline every tool and every reasoning record carries a status badge that renders the raw API token. With the UI in Chinese (the product default) a finished tool call shows: ```html
… completed ``` while the same render's own chrome is Chinese (`aria-label="Agent 活动"`, `已调用 run_shell`, `复制Result`). So the locale is applied and the badge is the piece that never went through the catalogue: `running`, `completed`, `failed` are printed in English on every record of the main run view. ## What is expected The badge keeps the state as its CSS class and names the state in the UI language: `运行中`, `已完成`, `失败` (`Running`, `Completed`, `Failed` in English — the same words the timeline already uses elsewhere, e.g. `timeline.toolRunning` "工具正在运行…", `record.toolCompleted` "已调用 {name}"). ## Where it comes from - `apps/web/src/timeline/RunTimeline.tsx:1045` — thinking record: `{entry.status}`. - `apps/web/src/timeline/RunTimeline.tsx:1102` — tool record: `{entry.trace.status}`. - `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` has no keys for these values; the nearest existing key is `timeline.runStatusFallback` (en `1018`, zh `4045`), which is a sentence, not a badge label. - `apps/web/src/styles/timeline.css:42` styles the badge and already applies `text-transform: capitalize`, which is why the English token looks like a word; CSS needs no change. Value domains — `apps/web/src/timeline/RunTimeline.tsx:68`, `:79` (thinking: `completed | running`), `packages/schema/src/session.ts:362` (tool trace: `completed | failed | running`). ## Failing test (reproduce before the fix) Server-side render is enough — no browser and no async fixture: ```tsx // apps/web/tests/zz-timeline-badge-probe.test.tsx (temporary, not committed) const html = renderToStaticMarkup(createElement(LocaleProvider, { initialLocale: "zh-CN" }, createElement(RunTimeline, { entries: [{ id: "entry", type: "tool", expanded: false, trace: { id: "tool-1", name: "run_shell", status: "completed", summary: "Done" } }], isRunning: false, onToggle() {}, }))); assert.match(html, /已完成|完成/); assert.doesNotMatch(html, /timeline-status completed">completedcompleted已调用 run_shell… completed… # tests 1 # pass 0 # fail 1 ``` ## Environment - `main` @ `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673` - node `v22`; from `apps/web`: `node --import tsx --test tests/` - locale forced with `LocaleProvider initialLocale="zh-CN"`; the probe is a throwaway file and must not be committed. ## Smallest mergeable slice Two files, about 10 lines, no logic change: 1. `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` — add `timeline.status.{running,completed,failed}`, one entry per key in the en block beside `timeline.runStatusFallback` and one in the zh block beside its counterpart. 2. `apps/web/src/timeline/RunTimeline.tsx` — a `timelineStatusLabel(status)` helper that calls `t()` with the key and falls back to the raw token for a value the catalogues do not carry, used in the two badge sites above. Boundaries: the `timeline-status ${status}` class and the `entry.status === "running"` / `"failed"` comparisons keep using the raw value; `timeline.css` is untouched; only the two badge texts change. ## Acceptance - The probe passes: a completed tool renders `已完成`, a running thinking record renders `运行中`, a failed tool `失败`. - Under `initialLocale="en"` the badges read `Running` / `Completed` / `Failed`, and `apps/web/tests/RunTimeline.test.tsx` keeps passing. - A status the catalogues do not know renders its raw token rather than an empty string or a missing-key placeholder. ## Not the same as `#925` `#925` covers `AgentActivityPanel` (executions/transfers/reminders) and its own eight `activity.state` / `activity.provenance` keys; this issue is a different component and file with its own three keys, so the two do not overlap in code or in acceptance. Open pull requests touching `apps/web/src/timeline/RunTimeline.tsx`: none (checked with `is:pr is:open` plus a per-PR file list over the current open set); open issues mentioning a timeline status translation: none.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claim-Id: 8c2885cfabeb4ba4ba2f1b4c6db60f65 Branch: dev/925-bug-activity-panel-prints-raw-english-st Base: 2908e9e8bb4f At: 2026-11-05T13:37:29Z ## What happens The Session activity panel (`Executions & reminders`) is fully translated except for the two values it takes from server data, which are printed as the raw API token even when the UI language is Chinese: - the status badge on every execution, transfer and reminder record renders `item.state` verbatim, so a running execution shows `running`; - the execution meta line renders `provenance` verbatim, so it reads `工作区 ws_a · 溯源 pending`, and the record's accessible label (fold summary, focus label) reads `local · main · running`. Chinese is the product default, so this is what a default-locale user sees. ## What is expected The badge keeps the state as its CSS class (styling must not change) but names the state in the UI language: `排队中`, `运行中`, `已完成`, `失败`, `已取消`, `未知`. The provenance reads `待提交` / `已提交`. Under English the labels stay the words the rest of the UI already uses: `Queued`, `Running`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Cancelled`, `Unknown`, and `Pending` / `Committed`. ## Where it comes from - `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:97`, `:111`, `:122` — `{item.state}`; the class must keep `item.state`, only the child text needs a label. - `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:98` — `t("activity.executionMeta", { provenance: item.provenance, workspace: item.workspaceId })` passes the raw token into the sentence. - `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:96`, `:110`, `:121` — the `label` prop of `ProcessRecord` interpolates `item.state`. - `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` carries 25 `activity.*` keys in both catalogues (en `2738-2759`, zh `5757-5778`) but none for these values, which is why this is the one activity surface that still shows English. Value domains, for whoever writes the keys: `packages/schema/src/execution.ts:45` (`queued|running|completed|failed|cancelled|unknown`), `apps/web/src/api/runs.ts:40` (timers: `pending|fired|cancelled`), `packages/schema/src/execution.ts:101` (provenance: `pending|committed|unconfirmed`). The other surfaces already do exactly this, so the pattern is in-tree: `apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx:72` maps wake states through `chat.wakeNoticeState.*`, `apps/web/src/GovernedDownloadCards.tsx:50` does the same for download states. ## Failing test (reproduce before the fix) Render the panel under the Chinese locale with one running execution and assert the tree does not carry the English token. The probe below is a temporary file — it is not part of the branch, it exists to prove the failure: ```tsx // apps/web/tests/zz-activity-badge-probe.test.tsx (temporary, not committed) const activity = { executions: [{ id: "job", agentId: "main", runnerId: "local", workspaceId: "ws_a", state: "running", provenance: "pending" }], transfers: [], timers: [], agents: [], }; const client = { getAgentActivity: async () => activity } as unknown as ApiClient; let view: ReactTestRenderer; await act(async () => { view = create(createElement(LocaleProvider, { initialLocale: "zh-CN" }, createElement(AgentActivityPanel, { client, sessionId: "session" }))); }); const tree = JSON.stringify(view!.toJSON()); assert.match(tree, /执行/); assert.doesNotMatch(tree, /running/); ``` Command and observed output: ``` $ cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/zz-activity-badge-probe.test.tsx not ok 1 - zh-CN badge names the state in Chinese error: |- The input was expected to not match the regular expression /running/. rendered fragment: {"type":"span","props":{"className":"activity-badge running"},"children":["running"]} # tests 1 # pass 0 # fail 1 ``` The same render shows the second half of this issue: `"工作区 ws_a · 溯源 pending"` — `provenance` is untranslated in the sentence produced by `activity.executionMeta`, and the process record's label is `local · main · running`. ## Environment - `main` @ `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673` - node `v22`; from `apps/web`: `node --import tsx --test tests/` - default locale zh-CN; the probe forces it with `LocaleProvider initialLocale="zh-CN"`, and the panel's own chrome in the same render is Chinese (`执行与提醒`, `查看日志`, `取消执行`), so the locale is applied and the English tokens are not a locale-detection artifact. ## Smallest mergeable slice Two files, about 30 lines, no logic change: 1. `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` — add `activity.state.{queued,running,completed,failed,cancelled,unknown}` and `activity.provenance.{pending,committed}`, one entry per key in the en block beside `activity.resumeAgentScope` and one in the zh block beside its counterpart. 2. `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` — a `stateLabel(state)` / `provenanceLabel(provenance)` helper that calls `t()` and falls back to the raw value for any value the catalogues do not carry (a newer API can add a state), used in the three badge children, the `executionMeta` call and the three `label` props. Boundaries: the `activity-badge ${item.state}` class, the `live`/`cancellable` predicates and the `progress.length` accounting stay exactly as they are; no assertion migration in existing tests; no change to any other badge or badge format in the app. ## Coverage note `#876` (merged today, `dev2/fix/874-activity-unknown-terminal`) is the only recent change to this file and it touched neither the badge text nor the `executionMeta` call — it moved `unknown` out of `live()` and switched `filesCommitted` to `progress.length`. There is no open pull request against `AgentActivityPanel.tsx`. ## Acceptance - The probe passes: under zh-CN the badge text is `运行中` while `className` is still `activity-badge running`, and the execution meta line no longer contains `pending`. - Under `initialLocale="en"` the visible text is unchanged from `main` apart from the badge/provenance wording, so `apps/web/tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx` keeps passing. - A state or provenance value the catalogues do not know renders its raw token rather than an empty string or a missing-key placeholder. - Scope stays at the eight keys above; a transfer's `partial`, a reminder's `fired` and provenance `unconfirmed` are deliberately out of scope and keep rendering their raw token.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
## What happens

A delimited dataset preview (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `parseDelimitedTable`) takes its width from the **widest line of the whole file**, so one outlier line decides how many columns every returned row shows. A two-column file that contains a single line with 200,001 fields renders as 1,001 columns, 999 of them carrying an empty header and an empty cell in every row.

## Where

- `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` (at `0477d328`): `const widest = lines.reduce(...)`, `const totalColumns = Math.max(header.length, widest)`, `const width = Math.min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)` (`MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS = 1001`), and the blank header names built at `columns: header.length >= width ? header.slice(0, width) : [...header, ...Array.from({length: width - header.length}, () => "")]`.

## Measured at `0477d328` (default `maxRows`)

- two-column header plus one line of 200,001 fields: `columns 1001`, `clippedColumns {total: 200001, shown: 1001}`, rows padded to 1001 cells each, so 999 columns and ~99,900 cells in the payload are blank.
- the same file without the outlier line: `columns 2`.

## Why it matters

The preview is widened by a line that is not part of the returned rows, and the extra columns carry no header - the grid shows a two-column table as a 1,001-column one. `clippedColumns` does report `{total, shown}`, so the cut is signalled, but the blank columns themselves are still rendered.

## Suggested fix

Cap the *unnamed surplus* columns the way the CSV importer already does (`apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts`, `surplusColumnLimit`: `min(16, max(2, header.length))`) while never capping header columns, and keep reporting the dropped cells in `clippedCells` / `clippedColumns`.
items.title: [Bug] One outlier line sets a delimited preview's width, so a two-column file renders 1,001 mostly-blank columns

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 53d81f15168944ff829f0c202b92560e
Branch: dev2/fix/web-settings-client-error
Base: f4dd18137e93
At: 2026-11-05T13:26:12Z

## What happens

`PUT /api/web/settings` answers **500 `{"error":"Internal server error"}`** when a caller sends a value `normalizeWebSettings` rejects, instead of a 400 that names the field. Two of the three user-facing rejections in that function are not recognised as client-input errors, so they fall through to the catch-all.

Reproduced against live `main` `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673` with a route-level probe (deleted afterwards, tree clean):

```
# status 500
# body {"error":"Internal server error"}
not ok 1 - PUT /api/web/settings answers a client error for an unsupported fetch provider
  error: an unsupported provider is a client error, got 500
  500 !== 400
# tests 1 / # pass 0 / # fail 1
```

Command: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/zz-web-settings-probe.test.ts`, where the probe starts `createApiServer` (offline MCP transport) and sends

```ts
fetch(`${origin}/api/web/settings`, {
  body: JSON.stringify({ fetchProvider: "definitely-not-a-provider" }),
  headers: { authorization: "Bearer test-token", "content-type": "application/json" },
  method: "PUT",
});
```

The same request with a valid provider answers 200, so the route itself and its auth are fine; only the rejection is misclassified.

## Expected

A 400 whose body names the offending field, e.g. `Unsupported web fetch provider` (and `Unknown web setting: <key>` for an unrecognised field), the way `deepseekEnabled must be a boolean` already answers 400 today.

## Root cause

- `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:377-379` (throw at `:378`) throws a plain `Error("Unsupported web fetch provider")`, and `:372` throws `Error("Unknown web setting: <key>")`.
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1255-1259` calls `store.updateWebSettings(await readJson(...))` with no local mapping, so both reach the shared chain at `:3894-3940`.
- That chain classifies plain errors by prose only: `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:24-31` (`is required`, `must`, `contains an unknown value`, `cannot`, `does not match`, `invalid`, `unsafe … path`, `plain basename`). Measured at this commit by importing the predicate:

```
"Unsupported web fetch provider" false
"Unknown web setting: nope" false
"deepseekEnabled must be a boolean" true
```

so the first two land in `unclassified_request_error` (`http/index.ts:3934-3940`) and become a 500 that is logged as a server fault.

## Smallest fix (one function + one dispatch line)

Give the two rejections a stable code and map it where the other codes are mapped — the same shape `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`/`SKILL_LIBRARY_VALIDATION` already use:

1. `services/api/src/store/settings.ts`: throw `Object.assign(new Error("Unsupported web fetch provider"), { code: "INVALID_WEB_SETTINGS" })` at `:377-379`, and the same code for the unknown-key throw at `:372`.
2. `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3932`, next to `SKILL_LIBRARY_VALIDATION`: `else if (code === "INVALID_WEB_SETTINGS") sendError(response, 400, message);`.

Do **not** import `SessionStoreHttpError` into `store/settings.ts` to get the 400: `services/api/src/store.ts:277-283` already imports `normalizeWebSettings` from that module, so the reverse import creates a cycle (the same reason #884's review rejected `ApiStatusError` there). Do not add another prose pattern either — `error-classification.ts:15-19` says new code should use a stable code.

## Acceptance

- `PUT /api/web/settings` with `{"fetchProvider":"definitely-not-a-provider"}` answers **400**, body names the field, and no `unclassified_request_error` is logged.
- `PUT /api/web/settings` with an unrecognised key (e.g. `{"nope":1}`) answers **400** naming it.
- A valid update (e.g. `{"searchCacheTtlSeconds":17}`) still answers **200** and reads back through `GET /api/web/settings`.

## Environment

`main` `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673`, Node `v22.23.2`, Linux, `services/api` test harness (`node --import tsx --test`). Route declared public surface in `test/contract/routes.json`.

items.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

The CI today is a cumulative gate model: PRs run L1/L2, the merge group runs L3, the nightly runs L4 and a release runs L5 (see the header comment of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). As the suite grows, three engineering capabilities have to be built in step:

1. **Test coverage**: the Coverage job merges only the UT and ST layers, the mocked browser E2E is not measured, and no gate reads the published coverage as an admission threshold.
2. **CI stability**: real-model E2E (L3/L4/L5) depends on external services and credentials, and occasional failures have no systematic mechanism for flake identification, isolation and tracking.
3. **Release CI efficiency**: the L5 release pipeline has no end-to-end budget of <5 hours, and the bulk data downloads (the ~1.5 GB JiuwenSwarm install, dependencies, datasets) happen again on every run.

Related files:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the L1–L5 pipeline: policy / ut / st / coverage / e2e-plan / real-e2e jobs)
- `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml` (real E2E; `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` inputs)
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (the L5 release)
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` (the case catalog and profile selection)
- `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`, `.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`, `.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs` (policy and result summaries)
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs` (coverage merge and summary)

## Design Ideas

### 1. Test coverage

**Baseline** — the `releases/v0.3.0.beta` line, authoritative run at `6d3c49a`:

| metric | whole repo | Node | Python |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| lines | 73.11% (105840/144777) | 73.19% | 72.08% |
| branches | 63.59% (39639/62335) | 63.85% | 59.63% |
| functions | 81.43% (7208/8852) | 81.43% | — |

- Weakest modules by line coverage: `idea-tree` 45.61%, `schema` 51.84%, `web` 56.14%, `scripts` 63.49%, `artifact-json` 63.16%, `specialist` 68.51%, `gateway` 68.40%.
- Cases: 3934 tagged — UT 3694/3806, ST 2/4, E2E 69/124; real-model 0/16, LLM judge 0/8, external 0/89, legacy 0/42.

**Gaps**

- Coverage is display-only: no gate reads it, and the `external` / `real` / `llm` classes are permanently 0.

**Plan**

1. Gate on industry health lines rather than the current 73%:

| metric | healthy | excellent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lines | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| branches | ≥70% | ≥85% |
| functions (Node) | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| statements | ≥80% | — |
| new / changed code (diff on a PR) | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| core paths (auth, sandbox execution, gateway, API routes) | ≥90% | ≥95% |
| per-package floor | ≥60% | — |

2. Land it in that order: diff coverage is enforced immediately (new code meets the line, existing code is not blocked), and the whole-repo figure ratchets upward and may never fall.

3. Starting gap: lines 73.11% (−6.89pt), branches 63.59% (−6.41pt), functions 81.43% (already passing). Four packages sit below the 60% floor — `idea-tree` 45.61%, `schema` 51.84%, `web` 56.14%, `services/runner` 0% — and each gets its own raise target.

4. Case-level coverage, not just a case count: a profile is the gate tier a run resolves to (`pr` / `merge` / `daily` / `release`), and `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` states which tag combinations each one selects. Today the 16 real-model, 8 LLM-judge and 89 external cases are selected by no profile at all, so they never run and read 0 forever; every case must either be selected by a profile or explicitly marked out of scope in the tag catalog, so the omission surfaces at review time.

5. Tie cases to modules: the tagged catalog carries the case-to-module mapping, so a new module without an executing case fails the gate, and `planned / executed / passed` remains the execution view beside it.

**Cases no profile can ever select.** `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` defines every profile as one of five rules (L1/L2 hermetic, L3/L4/L5 real), so a tag combination outside those rules never runs. On the `main` catalog (359 cases), 45 are permanently dead:

| tag shape | why no rule matches | cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status:legacy` | hermetic accepts only `reviewed`; real only `reviewed` / `external` | 42 |
| `status:quarantined` | same, with no path back in | 1 |
| `category:st` + `model:real` | the real rule is pinned to `category:e2e` | 1 |
| `npu:required` | all five rules require `npu:none` | 1 |

Four more shapes are structurally dead and simply have no case yet: `os:macos` / `os:windows`, `arch:arm64` outside real e2e, `judge:llm` combined with `model:none` / `mock`, and any case missing a `tier` tag — the old release-line catalog has no tier dimension, so under today's policy it would match nothing at all.

A further 131 cases read 0 without being dead: 61 UT and 70 real e2e do run, but the `ut` and `e2e-real` slice catalogs are never uploaded (`slices` registers only `e2e` and `st`), so their execution cannot be attributed.

- Fix the 45: delete or migrate the 42 `legacy` cases, give `quarantined` an exit, retag `st` + `real` as `e2e` or mark it out of scope, and open a separate NPU tier or declare it unsupported.
- Reachability check in the catalog check (`ci:catalog:check`, reusing the rule union exported by `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs`): a case whose tags match no profile fails catalog generation, so a dead case is caught at review time instead of reading 0 for months.

### 2. CI stability

- Automatic failure classification: product defect / environment / external dependency / test flake.
- Flake governance: when a case's failure rate over its last N runs crosses a threshold, mark it quarantined automatically — it keeps running and recording results, but its failure no longer blocks merges, and a tracking issue is opened for the owner. It leaves quarantine once it passes N consecutive runs, so a flaky case neither freezes the queue nor silently disappears.
- No blanket retry. A case is rerun only when its failure is attributable to network jitter or an unstable gateway / upstream — connect and read timeouts, connection resets, DNS failures, HTTP 429/5xx, interrupted streams. Every other failure, including a flaky real-model case, is reported as it happened and handled by the classification and quarantine above. A retry is labelled as an infrastructure retry, its count is visible per case, and sustained gateway failures beyond the retry budget are reported as an infrastructure incident rather than a test failure.
- Explore disabling the model's thinking mode, or setting the reasoning effort to its lowest level: much of the flakiness of the real-model cases comes from the randomness of the reasoning path; disabling or minimizing thinking narrows the output variance, makes the results more reproducible, and shortens per-case inference time (an efficiency win as well). The conclusion has to be backed by an A/B experiment — run both configurations N times each, compare pass rates and failure variance; if the pass rate does not regress beyond the accepted bound, fix it as a CI-only inference configuration applied to the L3/L4/L5 journeys only, leaving the product default untouched.

### 3. Release CI efficiency (<5h)

- Give the L5 pipeline a 5-hour end-to-end budget, add a timing view of actual per-job duration against that budget, and alert automatically when it is exceeded.
- Compress duration through caching (pnpm / uv / JiuwenSwarm are cached already), parallel test sharding (the mocked E2E matrix exists; extend it to UT/ST), and trimming redundant layers from the release profile.
- Run the real-model journeys at the lowest thinking effort: thinking off, or reasoning effort at its minimum, for L3/L4/L5 — reasoning tokens are the dominant cost of a case, so this shortens per-case latency directly. It is the same A/B switch as the stability item; here it is measured as p50/p95 duration per case against the 5-hour budget and fixed once the pass rate shows no regression.
- Data-download optimization: inventory the bulk downloads in the pipeline (the ~1.5 GB JiuwenSwarm install with its virtualenv, pnpm / uv dependencies, test datasets and fixtures, model and sidecar data, Docker images, and the base images of the release binaries) and eliminate the repeated ones item by item — pre-download into `actions/cache`, use an internal mirror / CDN, prefetch in parallel with the build steps, and key the cache on lockfiles / content hashes. Track download time separately in the budget view; a rerun with a cache hit must not download the bulk again.
- Produce an L5 duration baseline report marking the top-N slowest jobs and the optimization suggestions (including the share of download time).

## Involved Public APIs

No new or changed product public APIs; all of this is CI-internal capability.

- Reuse the existing CI-internal interfaces: `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list --profile ... --slice ...` (case selection), the `.ci-results` directory layout, and the `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` inputs of `real-e2e.yml`.
- The new outputs (coverage report and duration baseline report) are uploaded as artifacts, following the existing artifact naming convention (e.g. `node-coverage-summary-${scope}-${sha}`).

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `.ci/` scripts: the policy, matrix and summary scripts are extended to emit coverage and timing data.
- `test/support/tagged`: the case catalog gains coverage-ownership and flake-marker fields.
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`: a wider merge scope and a new output format.
- `release.yml`: the L5 budget check hooks into the existing `workflow_call` chain.
- No product code changes (apps/*, services/*); the model thinking-mode configuration is injected through the CI / E2E harness only and does not touch product defaults.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Coverage**: with a change of a known coverage delta, verify that the PR comment and the threshold block trigger correctly; verify the numbers are sound once the E2E layer is included.
- **Stability**: on a test branch, produce deterministic failures and random failures, and verify the classification, the quarantine isolation and the auto-issue flow; inject network jitter and gateway failures (timeout, connection reset, 429/5xx, interrupted stream) and verify the case is retried and, when it then passes, recorded as a pass with a visible retry count, while a product-defect failure is not retried; run the thinking-mode A/B experiment N times per arm, and verify that the failure variance narrows with no unacceptable pass-rate regression.
- **Efficiency**: take the last 3 release runs as the baseline, verify that the budget view times correctly and that the L5 end-to-end is <5 hours after the optimization; verify that the bulk data downloads take near-zero time on a cache hit; and record the per-case p50/p95 duration with thinking off or at its lowest, before and after.
- All of the above is CI behavior and automatable within L2; no new real-model cases are added (the existing L4/L5 journeys are reused).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Coverage is gated on the industry health lines: whole-repo lines ≥80%, branches ≥70%, functions ≥80% and statements ≥80%; new code ≥80% diff coverage; each package ≥60% and core paths ≥90%.
- [ ] Case-level coverage is closed: no case sits outside every profile, and every module maps to at least one case the gating profile actually executes.
- [ ] Flaky cases are identified and quarantined automatically; only failures caused by network jitter or an unstable gateway are retried, labelled as infrastructure retries and never applied to product defects; the thinking-mode (off / lowest) A/B experiment is concluded and, if viable, fixed as a CI-only inference configuration.
- [ ] The L5 release CI finishes end-to-end in <5 hours with in-pipeline over-budget alerts, every bulk download is cache/prefetch managed with no re-download on a cache hit, and the real-model journeys run at the lowest thinking effort with the latency gain recorded.

## Additional Information

- This is an engineering-effectiveness request; maintainers are invited to schedule it as the three sub-items above.

---

## 🚀 背景描述

当前 CI 采用累积门禁模型：PR 跑 L1/L2，merge_group 跑 L3，nightly 跑 L4，发布跑 L5（见 `.github/workflows/ci.yml` 头部注释）。随着用例规模增长，三个方面的工程能力需要同步建设：

1. **用例覆盖度**：Coverage 任务只合并 UT、ST 两层，mocked browser E2E 未被度量，且没有任何门禁把已发布的覆盖度作为准入阈值。
2. **CI 稳定性**：真实模型 E2E（L3/L4/L5）依赖外部服务与凭据，偶发失败缺乏系统性的抖动识别、隔离与跟踪机制。
3. **版本 CI 效率**：L5 发布流水线尚无 <5 小时的端到端时长预算约束，大额数据下载（JiuwenSwarm 安装约 1.5 GB、依赖、数据集）在每次运行中反复发生。

相关文件：

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`（L1–L5 主流水线：policy / ut / st / coverage / e2e-plan / real-e2e 等 job）
- `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`（真实 E2E；`profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` 输入）
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`（L5 发布）
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`（用例目录与 profile 选择）
- `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`、`.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`、`.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs`（策略与结果汇总）
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`、`scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`（覆盖度合并与摘要）

## 设计思路

### 1. 用例覆盖度

**基线**——取 `releases/v0.3.0.beta` 线（authoritative，SHA `6d3c49a`）：

| 指标 | 整仓 | Node | Python |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 行 | 73.11%（105840/144777） | 73.19% | 72.08% |
| 分支 | 63.59%（39639/62335） | 63.85% | 59.63% |
| 函数 | 81.43%（7208/8852） | 81.43% | — |

- 行覆盖率最弱的模块：`idea-tree` 45.61%、`schema` 51.84%、`web` 56.14%、`scripts` 63.49%、`artifact-json` 63.16%、`specialist` 68.51%、`gateway` 68.40%。
- 用例：3934 个，UT 覆盖 3694/3806、ST 2/4、E2E 69/124；真实模型 0/16、LLM judge 0/8、external 0/89、legacy 0/42。

**问题**

- 覆盖度只用于展示，没有任何门禁读取；`external` / `real` / `llm` 三类用例恒为 0。

**方案**

1. 门禁取业界健康线，而不是当前的 73%：

| 指标 | 健康线 | 优秀线 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 行覆盖 | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 分支覆盖 | ≥70% | ≥85% |
| 函数覆盖（Node） | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 语句覆盖 | ≥80% | — |
| 新增/变更代码（PR diff） | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 核心链路（认证、沙箱执行、网关、API 路由） | ≥90% | ≥95% |
| 单包下限 | ≥60% | — |

2. 按上述顺序落地：diff 覆盖立即生效（新代码按健康线走，不阻塞存量），整仓数值以棘轮方式只升不降。

3. 当前差距：行 73.11%（差 6.89pt）、分支 63.59%（差 6.41pt）、函数 81.43%（已达标）。4 个包低于 60% 下限——`idea-tree` 45.61%、`schema` 51.84%、`web` 56.14%、`services/runner` 0%——各自设定提升目标。

4. 用例维度覆盖，而不只是用例数量：profile 是一次运行解析出的门禁档位（`pr` / `merge` / `daily` / `release`），具体选中哪些 tag 组合由 `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` 定义。目前 16 个真实模型、8 个 LLM judge、89 个 external 用例不被任何 profile 选中，等于永远不跑、永远显示 0；要求每条用例要么被某个 profile 选中，要么在 tag 目录中显式标注「不在范围」，让遗漏在评审阶段就暴露。

5. 用例与模块绑定：tag 目录维护「用例 → 模块」映射，新增模块若没有可执行用例则门禁失败；`planned / executed / passed` 作为与之并列的执行视图。

**永远不会被任何 profile 选中的用例。** `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` 把每个 profile 定义为五条规则之一（L1/L2 hermetic、L3/L4/L5 real），不符合这些规则的 tag 组合永远不会被执行。以 `main` 目录（359 条）为例，45 条是彻底死用例：

| tag 形态 | 为何无规则命中 | 条数 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status:legacy` | hermetic 只收 `reviewed`，real 只收 `reviewed` / `external` | 42 |
| `status:quarantined` | 同上，且没有回到门禁的路径 | 1 |
| `category:st` + `model:real` | real 规则硬编码 `category:e2e` | 1 |
| `npu:required` | 五条规则全部要求 `npu:none` | 1 |

另有四类结构性死角，目前恰好没有对应用例：`os:macos` / `os:windows`、非 real e2e 的 `arch:arm64`、`judge:llm` 搭配 `model:none` / `mock`，以及任何缺少 `tier` 标签的用例——release 线那份旧目录没有 tier 维度，按当前策略会全部失配。

还有 131 条显示为 0 但并不属于死用例：61 条 UT 与 70 条 real e2e 实际在跑，只是 `ut` 与 `e2e-real` 两个切片的 catalog 从未上传（`slices` 只登记了 `e2e` 和 `st`），导致执行结果无法归因。

- 处置 45 条：删除或迁移 42 条 `legacy`；为 `quarantined` 补上出口；`st` + `real` 改 tag 为 `e2e` 或标注不在范围；`npu` 单独开档位或声明不支持。
- 在 catalog 校验（`ci:catalog:check`，复用 `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` 导出的规则并集）中增加可达性检查：用例 tag 若不属于任何 profile，catalog 生成即失败，让死用例在评审阶段暴露，而不是显示 0 数月。

### 2. CI 稳定性提升

- 失败自动归类：产品缺陷 / 环境 / 外部依赖 / 用例抖动（flake）。
- 抖动治理（quarantine）：同一用例近 N 次运行失败率超阈值时自动标记为隔离——它继续运行并记录结果，但失败不再阻断合并，同时自动创建跟踪 issue 派给 owner；连续 N 次通过后自动解除隔离，既不冻结合并队列，也不会让用例悄悄消失。
- 不做统一重试。仅当失败可归因于网络抖动或网关、上游不稳定（连接与读取超时、连接重置、DNS 失败、HTTP 429/5xx、流中断）时才自动重跑；其他失败——包括真实模型用例本身的抖动——如实上报，交由上面的失败归类与 quarantine 处理。重试会标注为基础设施重试，用例维度可看到次数，超出重试预算的持续性网关失败按基础设施故障上报，而不是记为用例失败。
- 探索关闭或调低模型思考模式（thinking / reasoning effort 设为最低档）：真实模型用例的抖动很大程度来自推理路径的随机性，关闭/调低思考模式可收窄输出方差、提升可复现性，同时缩短单用例推理耗时（兼具效率收益）。结论需以 A/B 实验数据支撑：对比开启 vs 关闭（或最低档）两组各 N 次运行的通过率与失败方差，若通过率无可接受退化，则固化为 CI 专用推理配置，仅作用于 L3/L4/L5 journey，不影响产品默认行为。

### 3. 版本 CI 效率提升（<5hr）

- 为 L5 流水线定义端到端时长预算 5 小时，pipeline 内增加各 job 实际耗时 vs 预算的计时看板，超预算自动告警。
- 通过缓存（pnpm / uv / JiuwenSwarm 已有）、用例分片并行（mocked E2E matrix 已具备，推广到 UT/ST）、release profile 裁剪冗余层级来压缩时长。
- 真实模型用例以最低思考强度运行：L3/L4/L5 关闭思考或把 reasoning effort 调到最低——推理 token 是单个用例的主要开销，这一步直接缩短单用例耗时。与稳定性项共用同一组 A/B 开关，这里以每条用例的 p50/p95 耗时对照 5 小时预算衡量，确认通过率无退化后固化。
- 数据下载优化：盘点流水线中的大额数据下载（JiuwenSwarm 安装约 1.5 GB 及其 virtualenv、pnpm / uv 依赖、测试数据集与 fixture、模型与 sidecar 数据、Docker 镜像、二进制基础镜像），逐项消除重复下载——预下载进 `actions/cache`、走内部镜像源 / CDN、与构建步骤并行预取、按 lockfile / 内容寻址命中缓存；下载耗时单独计时并纳入预算看板，缓存命中后的重复运行不应再产生大额下载。
- 输出 L5 耗时基线报告，标注 top-N 耗时 job 与优化建议（含下载耗时占比）。

## 涉及的公共 API

不新增、不修改产品公共 API；全部为 CI 内部能力。

- 复用现有 CI 内部接口：`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list --profile ... --slice ...`（用例选择）、`.ci-results` 结果目录格式、`real-e2e.yml` 的 `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` 输入。
- 新增产物（覆盖度报告、耗时基线报告）统一作为 artifacts 上传，遵循现有 artifact 命名约定（如 `node-coverage-summary-${scope}-${sha}`）。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `.ci/` 脚本：策略、矩阵、汇总脚本需扩展以输出覆盖度与耗时数据。
- `test/support/tagged`：用例目录需补充覆盖度归属与抖动标记字段。
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`、`scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`：扩展合并范围与输出格式。
- `release.yml`：L5 预算检查嵌入现有 `workflow_call` 链。
- 不改动产品代码（apps/*、services/*）；模型思考模式配置仅通过 CI / E2E harness 注入，不影响产品默认行为。

## 测试设计与测试计划

- **覆盖度**：构造已知覆盖变化的变更，验证 PR 评论与阈值拦截正确触发；验证 E2E 层纳入后报告数值合理。
- **稳定性**：在测试分支制造确定性失败与随机失败，验证分类、quarantine 隔离与自动建单流程；注入网络抖动与网关失败（超时、连接重置、429/5xx、流中断），验证用例被自动重试、重试后通过则记为通过且重试次数可见，而产品缺陷类失败不触发重试；思考模式 A/B 实验两组各跑 N 次，验证关闭/最低档下失败方差收窄且通过率无可接受退化。
- **效率**：以最近 3 次 release 运行作为基线，验证预算看板计时准确，优化后 L5 端到端 <5 小时；验证缓存命中后大额数据下载耗时趋近于零；记录关闭/最低思考强度前后每条用例的 p50/p95 耗时对比。
- 上述验证均为 CI 自身行为，属于 L2 可自动化校验范围；不新增真实模型用例（复用现有 L4/L5 journey）。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 覆盖度按业界健康线设门禁：整仓行 ≥80%、分支 ≥70%、函数 ≥80%、语句 ≥80%；新代码 diff 覆盖 ≥80%；单包 ≥60%、核心链路 ≥90%。
- [ ] 用例维度覆盖闭环：没有用例落在所有 profile 之外，每个模块都至少映射到一个门禁 profile 实际执行的用例。
- [ ] CI 具备抖动用例自动识别与 quarantine 机制；仅网络抖动 / 网关不稳定导致的失败自动重试，标注为基础设施重试且不适用于产品缺陷；完成模型思考模式（关闭/最低档）A/B 实验并形成结论，可行则固化为 CI 专用推理配置。
- [ ] L5 版本 CI 端到端时长 <5 小时，流水线内有超预算告警；大额数据下载全部纳入缓存/预下载管理，缓存命中后无冗余下载；真实模型用例以最低思考强度运行并记录耗时收益。

## 补充信息

- 本 issue 为工程效能类需求，建议 maintainer 按三个子项拆分任务排期。

items.body:
**Gap left by PR #892.** PR #892 adds the `cancelled` summary bucket in `apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx:53-58` and one test for it (`apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx:73-86`). Nothing in the tree asserts the other side of that rule any more: that `queued`, `running`, `unknown`, and a record with **no `state`** still render as `unconfirmed`, and that a mixed set of records summarises per bucket.

### Where

- `apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx:53-58` — the summary bucketing (`completed`, `failed`, and the catch-all `record.state !== "completed" && record.state !== "failed"`).
- `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx:73-86` — the only case covering this rule, and it feeds a single `cancelled` record.

### Why this matters

The catch-all is what keeps every other state honest. Adding the `cancelled` branch shifted the boundary between "has its own bucket" and "falls through to unconfirmed", and no test pins the fall-through side:

- a future bucket (or a reordering of the `if` chain) can reclassify `queued`/`running`/`unknown` silently, with all tests still green;
- `RuntimeNoticeRecord.state` is optional (`packages/schema/src/session.ts`), so a record with no `state` at all must still land in `unconfirmed` — nothing asserts it;
- the mixed case is the one a researcher actually sees: `1 completed + 1 failed + 1 cancelled` must summarise as `1 completed · 1 failed · 1 cancelled`, not collapse into one bucket.

### Acceptance

One added test in `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx`, red before the fix it claims to pin and green after, no product-code change:

1. a notice whose `records` are `queued`, `running`, `unknown`, and one object with no `state` renders `4 unconfirmed` and no `cancelled` bucket;
2. a notice with `1 completed + 1 failed + 1 cancelled` renders `1 completed · 1 failed · 1 cancelled` (the `·` join inside `.wake-notice-outcome`) and three badges.

Red-first evidence required in the PR body: the command `node --import tsx --test tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` before (failing assertion, quoted) and after (pass counts).

### Context

Raised as F1 in review thread `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM6zwwXP` / `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM6z-Dd6` on PR #892; deliberately not fixed in that tip, because adding it there would replace the approved head and restart the review for a test-only gap. Bug #889 and PR #892 are unaffected: the `cancelled` behaviour itself is covered by `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx:73-86`.

## Summary

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts` gives its fault injection a wall-clock budget of about `200 ms` (`200` iterations at `1 ms`). On a busy runner that budget is exhausted before the injected fault lands, the case fails with `Timed out waiting for local fault injection`, and because `UT` is one of the jobs `merge-gate` aggregates, an unrelated pull request turns red on the only required status check in this repository.

Two pull requests were hit by the same identity in two different time windows today, and the same file passes in a normal run.

## Failing identity

```text
packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts::parallel 429 callers share cooldown, drain their queue and do not retry inside one slot@linux/amd64
message: "Timed out waiting for local fault injection"
```

## Evidence

**Hit 1 — `#872`**, `UT` job `126735548839`, run [`41875320473`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41875320473), read from the job's uploaded `ut-results` artifact (`group-227/worker-1-events.jsonl`; the job log itself only carries `Run`/`Done` lines). Group summary `planned 16 / executed 16 / passed 15 / failed 1`; whole layer `planned 6279 / executed 6279 / passed 6278 / failed 1`.

**Hit 2 — `#878`**, `UT` job `126741018427`, same identity, another window.

**Control — the same file passing**, `UT` job `126822084143` (`2026-11-04T19:54:21Z`): `Run 229/555: packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts (16)` → `Done (6210ms)`, layer `{"status":"PASS","planned":6281,"passed":6281,"failed":0}`.

Neither pull request touches `packages/data-source`: `#872` changes four files under `apps/web`, `#878` changes `apps/web` only. So the failing identity is unreachable from either diff.

## Cause

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts:98-101` polls for the first of 12 concurrent callers to observe the injected fault:

```ts
// ~200 iterations × 1 ms ≈ 200 ms total
```

When the event loop is loaded (parallel `UT` workers, coverage instrumentation), `200 ms` is not enough for the fault to be observed, and the wait falls through to `assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection")`. The product behaviour is correct; the budget is what fails.

## Effect

Any pull request can be blocked by this, and a re-run only helps if the runner happens to be less loaded. Contributors cannot re-run: `POST /actions/jobs/{id}/rerun` and `POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` answer `403 Must have admin rights to Repository` to a non-member token. So the only currently available recovery is asking a maintainer.

## Options

1. **Replace the fixed budget with a deadline** (for example `waitFor` with a `10 s` timeout and a short poll interval), so a loaded runner still passes and a genuinely missing fault still fails quickly enough.
2. **Wait on the event rather than polling** — if the injection can expose a promise or an emitter, awaiting it removes the timing assumption entirely.
3. If the current budget is deliberate, document the expected runner load and treat the red as a known flake; then it should not be able to block `merge-gate` for unrelated changes.

We can prepare option 1 as a pull request if that is the preferred shape; tell us which option you want and we will follow that instead of choosing for you.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
## Summary

Three review findings from #870, #878 and #888 are real but cannot ride those pull requests without invalidating approvals they already hold, so they are recorded here instead of being lost when the threads close. Each item names the file and line on `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`.

## 1. `#870` — the leftovers test matches the sentinel on the error message only

`services/api/src/store-replace-cleanup.test.ts:107`

`await assert.rejects(writeRun(store, sessionId), /sentinel-rename/)` matches only the thrown error's own `message`. Test A in the same file (`:88`) deliberately concatenates `error.cause?.message`, test B does not. Today `writeArray` still calls plain `rename` (`services/api/src/store.ts:2159`), so the mock's `EPERM` carries the sentinel in its own message and the assertion passes.

Once #857 replaces that call with `renameReplace`, the thrown error is a `FileReplaceError` whose message is `Could not replace <dest> after 20 attempts (EPERM)` and whose sentinel lives only in `cause`, so this test fails for the wrong reason. The fix is to assert `cause.message`, or `error.name === "FileReplaceError"` plus the sentinel, the same way test A does.

## 2. `#878` — the "unexpected status" toast test never reaches the fallback branch

`apps/web/tests/QueuedCancelToast.test.ts:50`

`interrupted` is terminal (`isTerminalRunStatus`, `apps/web/src/run-stream/model.ts:127`), so `queuedCancelToast("interrupted", t)` returns `app.queuedCancelOutcome.finished` and the assertion `assert.match(toast.title, /更新|结束/)` passes on the terminal branch. Of the seven statuses only `queued` reaches `app.queuedCancelOutcome.statusDetail`, and that branch has no `detail`, so `/undefined/` can never appear either. A regression that drops `{ status }` from `statusDetail` stays green.

Coverage only — no user-visible defect.

## 3. `#878` — the fallback detail interpolates a raw enum token

`apps/web/src/run-stream/model.ts:145`

`t("app.queuedCancelOutcome.statusDetail", { status })` prints the raw value, so an unexpected status renders `当前状态：queued` in the Chinese UI — the same mixed-language outcome #871 was filed about, one layer deeper. The catalog has one status label today (`app.queued` = "Queued" / "排队中", `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:2516` and `:5482`). The sentence also hard-codes the Stop button's name (`messages.ts:2520`, `:5486`) instead of interpolating `composer.stop` (`messages.ts:406`).

## 4. `#888` — the desktop tool card keeps the English headings

`apps/desktop/src/app/tool-io.ts:60-63`, `apps/desktop/src/views/ToolCard.tsx:128`, `apps/desktop/src/text.ts`

The web card localises `Result` / `Error` / `Created files` / `Produced artifacts` in #888, but the desktop shell renders the same card from its own parser markers and its own catalog, so a zh-CN user in the desktop app keeps the English headings next to `输入`-style ones. #885 as filed only names the web card; localising the desktop twin is a separate change with its own catalog.

## Expected behaviour

1. `store-replace-cleanup.test.ts` asserts the sentinel through `cause` (or on `error.name`), so it fails for the right reason after #857.
2. `QueuedCancelToast.test.ts` drives a status that actually reaches `app.queuedCancelOutcome.statusDetail` and asserts the rendered detail.
3. The fallback detail maps the status through the existing run-status labels and interpolates the Stop label from `composer.stop`.
4. The desktop tool card localises the four headings from its own catalog, with the same zh-CN strings the web card now uses.

## 5. `#868` and `#887` each carry a copy of the reserved-name predicate — fold them into one when the second lands

`#866` (PR `#868`) added `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` inside `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts`; `#887` (PR `#890`) added the same predicate in
`packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts`, exported through the package index, because on the base the sanitizer had no reserved-name branch at all.

Both PR bodies say "whichever merges second folds the copy into `sanitizeUploadFilename`". That sentence is not a work item, so it is recorded here:
after both land, `workspace-upload.ts` should call the exported helper and drop its inline copy, and the superscript-digit class
(`com[1-9¹²³]` / `lpt[1-9¹²³]`) must be the same in both spellings while the copy still exists.

Expected: one predicate in `packages/workspace`, one call site in the sanitizer, no second regex in `services/api`, and the reject lists in
`workspace-upload.test.ts` and the workspace package tests agreeing.

## 6. The setup wizard's GB tier is the top of the ladder, so a free disk at or above ~1024 GiB prints `1024.0GB`

`apps/desktop/src/views/SetupWizard.tsx:127-128`

`scaledSize(size, printed, 4)` stops at unit 3 and the terminal branch prints `value.toFixed(1) + "GB"` with no further level, so the rule the
#879 rewrite enforces ("the unit follows the number that is printed") has no answer at the top: `formatWizardFreeSpace(1024 ** 4)` → `"1024.0GB"`,
`formatWizardFreeSpace(2 * 1024 ** 4)` → `"2048.0GB"`, switching at `1_099_457_940_685` bytes (1023.95 GiB, the first value whose one-decimal GB
rounds to 1024.0).

This is **pre-existing**, not introduced by #879/#880 — the base printed the same above 1 GiB — so it does not block that fix; it is a product call:

- add a TB tier so the ladder ends at `1.0TB`, or
- accept `1024.0GB` above 1 TiB and say so in the doc comment.

Expected: one of the two, decided explicitly, with the reading at and just below `1_099_457_940_685` pinned in `apps/desktop/tests/size-boundary.test.ts`.

## What

`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:156` (`GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, added by #915) pins only one direction of the walk: both new cases assert that something is **not** reported. Nothing asserts that a violation still **is** reported after the ignore list changed.

## Trigger

`IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` is widened again, or `_files()` is narrowed, so that a real source root (`services/api`, `packages`, `apps/web`, `test/api`) stops being walked. Every current case still passes:

- `test_a_generated_workspace_is_not_walked` and `test_a_workspace_file_removed_after_listing_is_skipped` assert absence only;
- `test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` asserts `failures == []`, which a walk that sees nothing also satisfies.

The boundary test then silently stops policing the Gateway boundary with no red test anywhere.

## Fix

Add the mirror case in `GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, reusing the `mock.patch.object(sys.modules[__name__], "_files", ...)` plumbing already present at `:162`:

- have the patched walk yield a path under `services/api/src` (for example `services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts`) whose content contains a vendor token;
- assert `_node_boundary_failures()` returns that path, as `path: <relative>` or `content: <relative>`.

Three lines in the test file. No production code changes.

## Why it is worth a line

Measured at `f99cc8a24495544988045699b9e5c2429553e332` (review comment on #915): a fabricated `services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts` does produce `['path: services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts']`, and with the pre-change ignore set a probe in `services/api/.tmp` produces `['content: services/api/.tmp/probe-manual-537457.ts']`. The guard works today; only its regression direction is untested.

Found while reviewing #915 and tracked here so the review thread can be closed without losing the gap.

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
## Summary

When a research agent writes files to its workspace during a run (e.g. `analysis.py`, `cleaned-data.csv`, SVG figures, `results.json`, helper scripts), those files are **not registered as artifacts** in the project's artifact list (`GET /api/projects/:id/artifacts`). Only files that were explicitly uploaded by the user before the run (e.g. `clinical_trial.csv`) appear as artifacts.

This means the user cannot download, preview, or manage the agent's output files through the artifact panel — they are stranded in the session workspace.

## Observed

During RR-02 (clinical trial re-analysis) on master `9e9d83d5` + WSL2:

- The agent wrote **8 files** to its session workspace:
  - `analysis.py` (41 KB)
  - `cleaned-data.csv` (4.6 KB)
  - `figures/fig1_endpoint_by_group.svg` (14.6 KB)
  - `figures/fig2_baseline_vs_endpoint.svg` (12.8 KB)
  - `figures/fig3_forest_plot.svg` (5.9 KB)
  - `figures/fig4_qq_residuals.svg` (12.9 KB)
  - `results/results.json` (6.1 KB)
  - `scripts/clinical_stats.py` (10.8 KB)

- `GET /api/projects/:id/artifacts` returned only **1 artifact**: `clinical_trial.csv` (the user's pre-run upload).

- The agent's output files were verifiably present in the session workspace (confirmed by direct filesystem access and by re-running `analysis.py` to reproduce identical results).

## Run identifiers

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Run ID | `9e7a4a73-680` (cancelled after 30 min driver timeout, but workspace files were written) |
| Session ID | `3aece6df-fbca-410b-9eca-9f80b4c48da3` |
| Project ID | `56900995-89be-4290-a24b-b89f76ccbd82` |
| Created at | 2026-11-05T09:34:07Z |
| Model | glm-5.3-flash via yibuapi.com |
| SD commit | `9e9d83d5` (master) |

## Reproduction

1. Start the local stack: `scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local`.
2. Create a project/session, set `approvalMode: always_allow`.
3. Upload a CSV (`POST /api/sessions/:sid/workspace/upload`).
4. Send a data-analysis prompt that instructs the agent to write output files (e.g. `analysis.py`, `cleaned-data.csv`, figures, `results.json`).
5. Wait for the agent to write files to the workspace (observable via the session workspace filesystem).
6. Call `GET /api/projects/:pid/artifacts`.
7. Observe: only the uploaded CSV appears; the agent-written files are absent.

## Expected behaviour

Files written by the agent to the session workspace should be registered as project artifacts (or at minimum, surfaceable through the artifact panel) so the user can download, preview, and manage them without needing direct filesystem access.

The test guidance (§8.1) explicitly calls out "报告已写入工作区但未登记为产物" (report written to workspace but not registered as artifact) as a defect to look for.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu)
- SD commit: `9e9d83d5` (master, clean tree)
- JiuwenSwarm: `workswarm0.2.6`
- Model: `glm-5.3-flash` via yibuapi.com (OpenAI-compatible)
- API: `http://127.0.0.1:4310`, Runner: `4311`, Adapter: `4410`

## Reproducibility of the agent's analysis (verified)

As a side note, the agent's `analysis.py` was re-run in a clean directory and produced **identical** results (exact match on all primary and sensitivity analysis numbers), confirming the agent's work was scientifically sound — the only defect is that its outputs are not surfaced as artifacts.

items.author: moShangLouTou
items.body:
## 问题背景

Agent 工具调用结果直接进入模型上下文时，Shell 执行、环境、文件传输、Skill、MCP 等工具可能返回冗长原始数据、敏感字段或与当前推理无关的内容，导致上下文浪费并增加信息泄露风险。

仅对返回内容做简单截断也不够：MCP 的 `structuredData`、`crossReferences` 等结构化业务数据可能被意外遗漏；真正发生截断后，如果没有可读取的引用，Agent 就无法恢复所需证据，影响后续分析。

## 预期行为

- 模型看到的是有边界、与任务相关的结果摘要，而不是无约束的原始工具输出。
- 敏感凭据、下载源 URL 等不必要信息不进入模型视图或长期保存的审计元数据；合法的下载候选 ID、许可证、归属信息及文件大小等业务字段仍被保留。
- MCP 输出保留 `structuredData`、`crossReferences` 和分析摘要中的有效业务数据，并在限制大小时优先维持可解释性。
- 真实业务数据因截断丢失时，若持久化成功，应返回可通过 `read_tool_output` 获取完整证据的引用；若不可恢复，要明确告知，不能静默假装完整。
- 小结果无需不必要的持久化；深层嵌套、循环引用及存储失败等边界情况应可控。
- arXiv 工具结果提供可用的分页和论文获取路径。

## 建议修复范围

1. 针对 Shell、执行管理、环境、NPU、传输与 Skill 工具定义适用的模型可见结果字段。
2. 对审计元数据中的敏感数据与原始大载荷做防御性清理，并限制递归深度。
3. 为 MCP 结果构造大小受限的投影，覆盖 JSON 文本、结构化记录、交叉引用与分析摘要。
4. 对发生信息损失的结果建立可恢复的 `read_tool_output` 引用与明确的失败回退提示。
5. 在下载、文献检索及 PDF 读取等真实链路中核对关键字段和结果语义。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 工具输出遵守模型上下文大小约束，不包含不必要的敏感字段
- [ ] MCP 结构化结果及交叉引用不被静默丢弃
- [ ] 截断导致业务信息损失时有可读取引用，或明确标识恢复不可用
- [ ] 小结果不产生不必要的证据持久化
- [ ] 深层嵌套、循环引用、存储失败等场景可预测且不泄露原始载荷
- [ ] 下载候选、许可证/来源信息、arXiv 分页及论文获取链路不回归
- [ ] 覆盖相关单元测试与端到端执行 / MCP 场景

## 实现 PR

- #717 — `fix(tools): bound model-facing execution and MCP results`

关联版本计划：#718（工具输出与结果投影优化）。
