items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Fixes #665

`web_fetch`'s public-URL guard still lets four IPv6 families through even though each one carries an IPv4 address the guard already knows how to judge. A model-supplied URL such as `http://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/` or `http://[2002:a9fe:a9fe::]/` reaches loopback or the link-local metadata endpoint, while the equivalent `::ffff:127.0.0.1` is rejected. This closes those four holes and pins both directions — blocked literals stay blocked, public embedded addresses stay routable.

## What was wrong

`ipv6Blocked()` only consults `ipv4Blocked()` for IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) and IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d`) forms, where the embedded IPv4 address sits in the last two hextets. Four other families carry the same address somewhere else:

| family | prefix | where the IPv4 address sits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NAT64 well-known | `64:ff9b::/96` | last 32 bits |
| NAT64 local-use | `64:ff9b:1::/48` | last 32 bits |
| 6to4 | `2002::/16` | hextets 2–3 |
| IPv4-translated | `::ffff:0:0:0/96` | last 32 bits, after `ffff` and 16 zero bits |
| Teredo | `2001:0::/32` | last 32 bits, bitwise inverted |
| site-local (deprecated) | `fec0::/10` | no IPv4 — the range itself is non-public |

No branch inspected those positions, so each form fell through to `return false`.

## What changed

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts` gains one helper, `dotted(high, low)`, and `ipv6Blocked()` learns to extract the embedded address for the six rows above and hand it to the existing `ipv4Blocked()` — the documented prefixes are matched, the address is decoded, and the verdict is the same predicate that already rejects `127.0.0.1` and `169.254.169.254`. There is no second copy of the IPv4 block list, no blanket range ban, and no refactor of the existing mapped/compatible branches: `ipv6Blocked()` keeps its shape and the new decoders delegate.

Teredo needs the inversion because the client address is stored XOR-ed with `0xffffffff`; `2001:0:808:808::80ff:fffe` therefore decodes to client `127.0.0.1`, not to the relay `128.255.255.254`.

The test computes nothing itself: it asserts the same 15 cases from both directions, plus the literal path (`assertPublicUrl("http://[...]/")`) and the resolver path (`assertPublicUrl(url, resolver)`), so a future change that fixes only literals fails.

## Red first

The new test, run against the unfixed `url-guard.ts` (`git checkout <test-commit> -- url-guard.ts`):

```
# Subtest: web_fetch judges NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local literals by their embedded IPv4
not ok 11 - web_fetch judges NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local literals by their embedded IPv4
  ---
  error: |-
    64:ff9b::7f00:1

    false !== true

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  name: 'AssertionError'
  expected: true
  actual: false
  operator: 'strictEqual'
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

The loop stops at the first failing literal, so the same nine blocked literals were also probed one by one against the unfixed predicate — each line below is one assertion that fails with `false !== true`:

```
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("64:ff9b::7f00:1"), true, "NAT64 /96 -> 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe"), true, "NAT64 /96 -> 169.254.169.254")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("64:ff9b:1::7f00:1"), true, "NAT64 /48 -> 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("2002:7f00:1::"), true, "6to4 -> 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("2002:a9fe:a9fe::"), true, "6to4 -> 169.254.169.254")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("::ffff:0:7f00:1"), true, "IPv4-translated -> 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("::ffff:0:a9fe:a9fe"), true, "IPv4-translated -> 169.254.169.254")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("fec0::1"), true, "site-local")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("2001:0:808:808::80ff:fffe"), true, "Teredo -> client 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
```

## After the fix

```
# tests 16
# pass 16
# fail 0
```

The reverse direction is asserted in the same test, so the fix cannot be "block the prefix": `64:ff9b::808:808`, `64:ff9b:1::808:808`, `2002:808:808::`, `::ffff:0:808:808`, `2001:0:808:808::f7f7:f7f7` (Teredo for `8.8.8.8`) and `2606:4700:4700::1111` all stay routable, both as literals and through `assertPublicUrl`.

Diffstat against `main` `f4dd1813`:

```
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts | 49 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts      | 29 +++++++++++--
 2 files changed, 75 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

Ran:
- `node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts` in `packages/data-source` — `# tests 16 # pass 16 # fail 0`; the same command on the unfixed source is the red above (`# pass 15 # fail 1`).
- `tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- Per-literal probe of the nine blocked addresses against the unfixed predicate — the nine `false !== true` lines above.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` (full layers) were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser/API/CLI journey was added: the change is a predicate inside the `web_fetch` URL guard, and the mocked E2E subset does not exercise NAT64/6to4 literals.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: a model-supplied `web_fetch` URL that encodes a private, loopback or link-local IPv4 address in NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated, Teredo or site-local form is now rejected with `PublicUrlError` instead of being fetched; public addresses in the same forms keep working.

Compatibility and migration: none. Public NAT64/6to4 egress is explicitly covered by the reverse assertions above.

Consolidates the existing MCP settings work into one module PR: metadata, call timeout, enable/disable, removal of saved HTTP/SSE header groups and STDIO environment overrides, custom-server deletion, and replacement of existing credential header values. It also includes the connection-cache and credential-redirect fixes.

## Consolidation
Supersedes #764, #765, #766, #767, #768, #769, #771 and #772. Their original commits and tests are preserved by normal merges; no history was rewritten. This reuses #773 and creates no additional PR.
Shared UI prerequisites from #738, #746 and #757 are included. The exact encrypted-draft policy depends on the Memory credential groundwork now consolidated in #770; that prerequisite appears in the main-relative diff until it lands.

## Behavior
All existing manual-confirmation, separate recipient consent, finite-field, CAS, durable external-receipt and resolve-only recovery contracts remain. Saving does not probe a server, start a process or grant execution permission. Deletion uses the recoverable v3 encrypted envelope; older binaries cannot read that envelope. Existing connections may retain old settings until their ordinary reconnection. New MCP URLs, creation, OAuth and arbitrary header/environment editing are outside this PR.

## Validation
Candidate: 01170f3247d544923d0caa3c8f8097f4fa960b56, based on official main 7942ad1fd495cc623df67234d8a01201430da204.
- Related Windows integration and component tests: 222 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, via explicit changed test files and node --import tsx --test. On this tip, services/api configuration+mcp tests: 423 passed.
- Full workspace build and package/root test typechecks passed on the preceding combined ba806d13. The final scope-default/test-finalizer correction was then rebuilt for the API and all 222 tests were rerun on the candidate.
- Initial combined failures are retained; they were scope-default and test-finalizer merge errors, corrected before publication.
- Previous individual API/browser journeys remain historical evidence on their original SHAs, not passes for this combined candidate.

## E2E user journeys
Combined browser/public-API journeys, complete Linux/WSL, real services/models and the final eight-module combination remain unverified. Draft publication with these gaps was explicitly authorized. Do not infer passes from skipped draft CI jobs.

## Release
Release category: release:feature (GitHub label pending a maintainer).
User impact: one reviewable MCP settings module with existing secure user confirmation.
Compatibility and migration: ordinary journaled MCP settings edits can write the encrypted v2 envelope. Recoverable deletions can write v3. Older releases that expect a plain custom-server map cannot load either envelope. Settings and the operation journal are persisted atomically. No automatic downgrade is provided. Maintainer acceptance of this downgrade boundary is pending.

<!-- review-follow-up-20261103 -->
### Integration notes

- This branch overlaps shared UI and configuration changes in #756, #758 and #770. Reconcile the shared files against the target branch as those PRs land and rerun the HTTP capability-catalog test and MCP integration tests on the resulting tree.
- MCP HTTP/SSE requests reject redirects, including redirects to the same origin. Use the final server URL in its settings.
- The v3 MCP store envelope requires a reader that understands v3. Maintainer confirmation of that compatibility boundary and the combined real-model browser journey remains pending.

Refs #820

Sandbox network policy, new-session approval defaults, current Session approval mode and low-risk configuration automation remain separate explicit human decisions within one security module. Ordinary Agent proposals and tool Always allow cannot approve these changes. items.author: qingkwl
items.body:
First batch of the first-message latency plan (#799): warm the MCP catalog while the user is still on the ready screen, and stop paying a second `skills.list` RPC on every run that imports nothing. Together they address the two largest measured chunks of the first message — the ~48s stdio catalog cold-start (field) and part of the ~4s `skills.list` x3 chain in the SD-side run preparation.

## Warm the MCP catalog right after agent-ready (S1)

On a fresh install the bundled stdio MCP servers spawn and enumerate their tools on the first chat run; field measurements put this chunk at ~48s of the 60-135s first-message latency. The shell's `watchAgentReady` already polls `/agent/info`, and the moment `jiuwenswarm.reachable` turns true it now issues `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload` in the background — the MCP settings page's refresh request, and the one endpoint that actually connects and enumerates. The spawns and tool enumeration then overlap the ready screen instead of the first message.

The endpoint choice was corrected during live verification (commit ef65229e): the first revision fired `GET /api/mcp/sources`, which only reads the cached manifest/status list — on a running stack it answered 200 in ~1s and spawned nothing, and the first chat run still paid the full catalog load. The reload endpoint spawned every bundled source in ~3.3s on the same stack, with the stdio processes visible on the host. Verified locally: catalog warmed at boot → a first message afterwards pays zero MCP chunk (E1.6 evidence pack).

Best-effort by contract: failures are logged to `shell.log` (`[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources/reload -> <status>` or a failure line) and never surface to the user. When the warmup loses the race, the run path re-runs the same steps — no behavioural fork, only a head start.

## One `skills.list` per sync when nothing imports (S3a)

`SkillSync.sync()` ran `skills.list` twice per run: `_sync()` listed to diff staged skills against JiuwenSwarm's, and the tail listed again to refresh the adapter's `directories` map. That map only carries ScienceDiscovery-marked skills, which can only appear through this adapter's own imports — a run that imports nothing changes no directory, so the second listing was the first one's answer. `_sync()` now reports whether it imported anything; `sync()` re-lists only then. The import path is byte-for-byte today's behaviour (pre-import listing + post-import refresh); the steady-state path saves one RPC round trip per run and still populates the map from the single listing, including right after an adapter restart.

This is step S3a of the run-preparation-chain plan; S3c (acceptance-path parallelisation) remains a follow-up.

## One `skills.list` per run, cached 30s with write-through invalidation (S3b)

After S3a a steady-state run still paid two `skills.list` RPCs: `_sync()` listed to diff staged skills, and the API's reconcile listed again through `GET /agent/skills`. Both read the same list, and the adapter performs every write to that list itself (`skills.import_local` in `_import`, `skills.toggle` in `set_enabled`) — so a short-TTL cache with write-through invalidation serves both reads from one fetch while keeping the cached answer at least as fresh as the last write. Back-to-back runs staging the same skills now send **one `skills.list` per run instead of two**; an import or a toggle invalidates immediately, and a zero TTL restores today's fetch-every-read behaviour as the kill switch.

A cache hit never changes what JiuwenSwarm receives: import decisions still run against the freshest answer the adapter itself has written, and a direct JW-side edit can only stay invisible for the 30s TTL — the trade the plan documents. Step S3b of the run-preparation plan.

## Validation

- `pnpm --dir win_desktop build` — clean (esbuild).
- `pnpm --dir win_desktop typecheck` — clean (tsc).
- `pnpm --dir win_desktop test` — 164 pass / 0 fail (5 first-chat-warmup tests: URL/header construction, POST method to the reload endpoint, happy path, failure propagation, timeout bounds; baseline was 159 before this change).
- Live stack check (dev stack, 2026-11-05): `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload` with the shell's auth header returned 200 in ~3.3s and spawned all 13 bundled stdio sources (`ready`); the prior `GET` on the same stack returned 200 in ~1s and spawned nothing — this is what motivated the endpoint fix.
- Adapter: `uv run pytest tests/` (services/adapter) — 292 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `test_diagnostics.py::test_private_rotating_file`, is pre-existing on this host: it fails identically on the unmodified base commit in the same worktree (verified with `git stash`), and the change does not touch diagnostics. All 15 skills tests pass, including 5 that count the RPCs: a no-import sync lists exactly once and still populates the directories map (S3a); an importing sync still lists twice (pre-import + post-import refresh, S3a unchanged); two `listed()` calls within the TTL share one RPC, a no-import sync and the next `listed()` share one RPC (S3b); an import and a toggle each invalidate so the next read re-fetches (S3b); a zero TTL restores fetch-every-read (S3b kill switch).
- Not covered here: packaged-install validation (GUI-interactive install, three boot profiles, cold-install first message). That needs an installer build and a quiet machine; it is scheduled and will be reported before this PR is marked ready.

## E2E user journeys

Local stack (dev tree, base 79d26dd6 + this branch), mock OpenAI endpoint on loopback answering SSE in ~30 ms, quiet load window, same-window pairs (D5 discipline: fresh session first message vs same-session second, median of 3):

1. **Warmup fires end-to-end (the S1 claim).** Desktop shell launched against the live stack; `shell.log` recorded `[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources/reload -> 200`, and the API log recorded `mcp_catalog_loaded durationMs=3846 failedServerCount=0 serverCount=3 toolCount=39` in the same second. The 6 bundled stdio MCP server processes were visible on the host before any message was sent. PASS.
2. **First/second message, web-only connectors (E1 anatomy口径).** First message 5.5s / 9.4s / (one round lost to a transient Windows file-lock EPERM, retried clean) — median ≈ 5.5-9.4s; second message 3.5s median. The 2026-11-03 baseline on the old base was 26.09s / 8.67s; the drop is mostly upstream work landed in the meantime (patch 0020 moved the 12.4s observability import off the hot-start path) plus the quiet load window — this pair is reported as no-regression evidence, not as S1/S3a attribution. PASS (no regression).
3. **First message with an MCP tool call, cold vs warm catalog (the S1 mechanism).** Session with `enabledConnectorIds: ["web","uniprot"]`, mock model answers the prompt with one `mcp__uniprot__search` call. Cold catalog (API boot refresh had failed: `mcp_connection_failed … MCP connection timeout` × 3 servers at startup, as it does on this host): run completed in ~7.7s with the catalog load inside the run. Warm catalog (after `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload`, the exact S1 request): run completed in 5.7s, tool call answered in 16ms, no connection events in the run window. Delta ≈ 2s on this warm-filesystem dev box; the field cold-install figure the plan cites is ~48s (E1.6 evidence). PASS — the warmup demonstrably moves the catalog load out of the first run.
4. **S3a mechanism.** Adapter unit tests count the RPCs directly (a no-import sync sends exactly one `skills.list`, an importing sync still sends two); the dev-stack venv still runs the pre-S3a adapter build, so the in-stack numbers above are the conservative (two-list) path. PASS by unit test; in-stack A/B lands when the venv is refreshed.

Failure attribution: the only run failures in the session were transient host file-lock EPERMs on skill-snapshot rename (Windows antivirus/indexer) — retried clean, not product failures. The pre-existing `test_private_rotating_file` failure is documented in Validation above.

Commands: `node .tmp/mock-openai.mjs` (mock, SSE instant), `node .tmp/fml-ab.mjs 3` and `node .tmp/fml-s1-ab.mjs cold|warm` (drivers; client-side SSE timing + event timeline). Counts: journey 1 = 1/1 PASS; journey 2 = 5/6 runs clean (1 env-retry); journey 3 = 1/1 cold + 1/1 warm PASS; journey 4 = 10/10 unit tests.

## Release

Release category: `release:performance` (GitHub label pending a maintainer — the author has read-only access to the upstream repository and cannot apply it).
User impact: faster first message on installed builds (the MCP catalog no longer cold-starts inside the first chat run) and slightly cheaper every run (one fewer `skills.list` round trip in the steady state). No UI change, no configuration change, no behaviour change on failure paths.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Importing a research evidence package restores the conversation and the evidence needed to inspect and continue the original work. The `.sdresearch` plugin exports and imports workspace file versions, artifacts and provenance, execution history, trajectory details, and scientific memory.

## Behavior

- Imported sessions are read-only snapshots. **Create a new session to continue research** creates an independent, writable copy of the imported conversation and evidence. The copy runs as a background task that remains tracked after switching sessions; new research preserves the original snapshot.
- Workspace files open in a preview dialog. Text previews are limited to 256 KiB, supported images including PNG use the original bytes, and downloads preserve the original filename and complete contents.
- Trajectory export preserves model inputs, reasoning fragments, and tool-detail payloads. Import, restart, and continuation retain access to verified detail objects. Older packages cannot recover evidence they never contained.
- Necessary exports omit optional history and diagnostics while retaining required evidence dependencies. Complete exports offer independent checkboxes for full trajectory details and the full scientific-memory graph; deselecting the graph retains its summary. Export selections and source limitations survive import and repeat export.
- Export-size previews are keyed to the session revision and selection. Relevant changes invalidate previous results and trigger background preparation; unchanged sessions reuse their results without a fixed one-minute expiry. Pending results are shown as calculating rather than as a stale final size.
- Exports can run as persistent background jobs with status tracking, completion feedback, and original-name downloads. An export checks the source session revision before and after background creation; if the revision changes while it runs, the job fails instead of publishing stale evidence. A completed job remains downloadable during its retention window. Gzip compression is asynchronous; archive assembly still uses an in-memory tar buffer and is not a streaming implementation.
- User messages have a copy action; assistant reply copy actions remain available. Completed assistant replies offer **Branch to a new chat**, creating a writable conversation prefix through that reply. A persistent **Continue from chat** link returns to the immediate source reply. Imported read-only snapshots cannot be branched directly.
- Branching preserves attributable historical evidence, execution results, and reviewer-audit records, and discloses unavailable history. Busy sessions are rejected and request retries are idempotent. Import and continuation integrity checks compare the supported restored representation without inventing missing evidence.
- Importing a legacy package without scientific memory no longer fails snapshot capture solely because the graph service is unavailable. Packages containing scientific memory still require successful graph restoration. The scientific-memory summary is included in the snapshot payload type.

## Validation

Current head: `b6beeee333aa3e171503fe14a68d9b1c31f3bcc8`. The branch contains exactly one feature commit relative to `official/main`; author and committer are `zhaochen39 <zhaojichenjc@126.com>`.

CI run [41995297102](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41995297102) is running from this head. UT, ST and Research E2E have no final result yet, so this PR makes no passing full-suite claim.

Local targeted results on the current checkout:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Research package, export-preview and export regression tests | PASS |
| Research package HTTP test | BLOCKED by a missing local `@sciencediscovery/execution-router` link |

Targeted command:

```bash
node --import tsx --test packages/research-package/src/index.test.ts apps/web/tests/ResearchPackageActions.test.tsx apps/web/tests/research-background-tasks.test.ts services/api/src/research-export-previews.test.ts services/api/src/research-package-exports.test.ts services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts services/api/src/conversation-branches.test.ts
```

## E2E user journeys

Changed goals: import and inspect evidence; continue a snapshot in an independent writable session; preview/download workspace files; inspect trajectory and export scopes; copy messages; branch from a reply and navigate to its source; choose trajectory/graph export options; run an export in the background.

Expected outcomes: persistent inspectable evidence, original-name downloads, complete selected detail payloads, independent writable sessions, source navigation, revision-correct size previews, and background export completion/download feedback.

The research restore/export journey has been updated to select the full graph, inspect manifest/node contents, and exercise the immediate/background export controls. Browser execution uses the normal `pnpm ci:e2e` entry point with its pinned Playwright and Chromium preparation, the shipping JiuwenSwarm backend, mocked models, and isolated services/data. **Current status: queued in CI run [41995297102](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41995297102), not a passing journey certification.** No real/paid model journey was run. Targeted component/API regressions do not replace browser or external-client journey coverage.

## Scope and release

Local startup changes in `scripts/start-stack.sh`, `scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh`, `services/launcher/src/source-evolve.test.ts`, and `.env` are excluded. Their local contents and the pre-existing stashes are preserved. Deletion-staging data and running user services are not modified.

Compatibility: legacy evidence packages remain importable; absent historical evidence is disclosed rather than invented. Keep this PR open pending complete runtime validation, the requested bilingual screenshots, and review.

items.author: ink999107
items.body:
## Problem

Evolve is the one capability that keeps running and producing results after the turn that started it ends, but the desktop app had no way to reach it: `/evolve-design` opened nothing, so a search could only be designed, confirmed and watched in the web client. A user working in the desktop app has to switch surfaces mid-task, and the run they left behind is unreachable from where they are.

## What this adds

- **Create dialog** — collects the two things a person actually knows (what should get better, which search algorithm fits) and hands that sentence to the conversation as the command the user would have typed. The agent still designs the scorecard, runs the probe and owns the checkpoints.
- **Checkpoint pace switch** — on by default. Turning it off sends `/evolve-design --no-confirm`: the agent still does the work of every step and still reports each checkpoint, labelled as automatic, but does not wait for a reply between them. Checkpoint 3's cost summary is kept, and a blocker that needs a decision (missing dataset, ambiguous goal, an approval the agent cannot give) still stops. The pace is recorded on the goal as `checkpointMode`; an absent field reads as `confirm`, which is what every existing run did.
- **Checkpoint cards** — each of the four checkpoints is drawn as a card in the transcript rather than as more prose: the step (`检查点 1/4`), the question, the few lines to read, and two answers — confirm and continue, or write the change in the card and send it from there. Once a later turn exists the card folds to its header, so a finished design reads as four lines instead of four screens; the card still waiting on you stays open. A run with the pace switch off still shows the card, marked automatic, with no buttons. The card is read from the answer's own `evolve-checkpoint` fence (a block tagged with the skill's name, `evolve-design`, is read the same way), so it survives a reload; a client that does not draw cards falls back to the block as readable code.
- **Session shelf** — a thin row under the session header. A running search stays reachable when the panel is closed, and a session that never used evolve renders exactly as before.
- **Result panel** — follows the run's SSE stream, falls back to polling the run list, and answers in order: best score and how it moved, the candidate table, a selected candidate's diff, and why it was rejected. The inspector becomes a drawer on a narrow window.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop`: `npm run typecheck`; `npm test` — 760 pass, including new command parsing, dialog, shelf, panel, pace-switch, checkpoint-fence and checkpoint-card cases.
- `services/api` evolution suites (proposal, pre-flight, call budget, thinking control) — 51/51.
- `packages/evolve` 11/11, `packages/schema` 29/29.
- The desktop e2e suite gains `apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts` with a mocked evolve runtime, including three checkpoint-card journeys: confirm sends the reply, an automatic card asks for nothing, and a change is written and sent from inside the card (the composer is never touched). Playwright is not installed in this worktree, so it runs in CI rather than locally.

## Acceptance

The end-to-end path is the tutorial sample in `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`), and the UI review tracked in #798 is the other acceptance item.

Related to #798 — this PR does not close it.

items.body:
Desktop run failures expose raw provider diagnostics in the main conversation, including English error tokens in the Chinese UI. This PR presents localized recovery guidance first and keeps the original diagnostic information available under an expandable **Technical details** section.

## Failure presentation

- Map all seven `RunFailureCode` values to English/Chinese summaries: timeout, unauthorized, rate-limited, transport-error, server-error, invalid-tool-call and semantic-error.
- Use a generic fallback for missing or unrecognized codes. Resolve the active language when rendering.
- Keep the original error code and message in the expandable details block rather than replacing or discarding diagnostic information.
- Use neutral wording for `semantic-error`, since the backend uses it as a catch-all classification and it does not establish that a model service rejected the request.
- Apply the same localized summary and folded raw-message presentation to persisted `timeout_notice` messages.
- Add coverage for language switching, fallback codes, replayed failures, diagnostic preservation and a failed tool inside a successful run.

## Scope and remaining limitation

A timeout notice and a run-failed status can still both appear. The client cannot reliably associate a `timeout_notice` message with a specific run, so this PR keeps both visible. Reliable deduplication remains a follow-up requiring a suitable association contract. This partially addresses #846; it does not complete that issue's duplicate-alert criterion.

Windows direct execution provides managed Bash, but persisted environments can lack the Unix utilities that the tool contract implies, causing commands such as `head` to fail without actionable capability or recovery information. This change makes the managed Windows shell contract explicit, upgradeable, and diagnosable.

## Managed Windows shell contract

- Provision MSYS2 coreutils, grep, and sed with `m2-bash` in the managed starter environment.
- Add `Library\\usr\\bin` to the Windows activation path so the managed utilities resolve without relying on an incidental Git Bash installation.
- Probe the managed Bash executable and guaranteed utility set, expose the platform and shell capability through Runner readiness, and refresh the probe after setup.
- Update `run_shell` and `check_runner` descriptions so the agent follows the target Runner capability rather than assuming host commands.

## Persisted environment upgrade and diagnostics

- Detect required starter packages missing from an existing environment, install only the missing specifications, and retain an audit revision.
- Avoid repeating migration for a newly created starter that already received the complete package contract.
- Attach a bounded `COMMAND_NOT_FOUND` diagnostic only when exit code 127 is accompanied by Bash's standard simple-command failure, preserving stderr as evidence and recommending an available utility or Python equivalent.

## Windows stack command shims

Route `.cmd` and `.bat` service entry points through `cmd.exe`, passing argument values through the child environment. Native executables keep their direct spawn path. This handles command shims while preserving spaces and literal argument metacharacters.

## Validation

Final tested commit: `82a8be4a0468008a1d49b4f5e14ba803c6313789`.

**The Windows product environment uses Node 22.** All operator-reported Windows product journeys below were performed with Node 22.

- PASS: affected Runner/workspace packages and their workspace dependency builds.
- PASS: schema, Runner and workspace typechecks.
- PASS: targeted environment-store, readiness, shell-diagnostics and workspace-tool suites on WSL2 Linux amd64 / Node 22.19.0 — 89 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- PASS: `git diff --check`; worktree clean.

```text

```

At the author's explicit request, final-head validation is limited to affected tests and relevant product journeys; full local gates were not repeated. Earlier full runs on `f028f2fb` remain non-green: UT 6,046/6,051 passed (5 failures), ST 50/51 passed (1 failure), and mocked browser E2E 124/133 passed (9 failures, 0 skipped). Their root causes were not all established by baseline comparison; these historical results are not claimed as passes or definitively unrelated failures.

## E2E user journeys

PASS, operator-reported on final head `82a8be4` using native Windows Node 22 and local caches, through the real product setup API and chat/run_shell entry points:

1. Fresh installation: the product setup API created the starter environment offline and it reached `ready`.

Raw command transcripts/logs were not supplied for independent review, and no additional automated-test counts are inferred. The agent's native Windows Runner TypeScript-suite attempt from the WSL checkout could not load `tsx`; no test body ran in that attempt, and it is not counted as Windows suite coverage. macOS and arm64 were not exercised in this follow-up.

This checked command-shim argument handling, including a path with spaces and the literal `shim & %PATH% ready` argument. It is supplemental script evidence only; it does not describe the operator's Windows runtime or establish Node 22 coverage for that helper suite.

items.body:
Fixes #887

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What changed

`POST /api/sessions/:id/files` resolved `body.path` through `resolveWorkspaceFile` — which only refuses absolute paths and escapes — and wrote the result straight to disk. On a Windows workspace that makes `CON` target the console device and `nul.txt` fail with a raw `EPERM` the handler never classifies, so the client saw `500 Internal server error`. The reserved-device-name guard existed only in the upload path.

Chosen fix: **direction 2** — the predicate became a workspace invariant instead of an upload-only check.

- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` — new exported `isWindowsReservedDeviceName(name)`, sitting directly beside `assertWorkspacePath`. It matches the stems Windows resolves in every directory (`con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com1`–`com9`, `lpt1`–`lpt9`, `conin$`, `conout$`), strips trailing dots/spaces first (`nul.`, `CON `), and treats everything before the first dot as the stem, because the extension is irrelevant to a device. It is exported through the package index (`export * from "./workspace.js"`).
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts` — the write route walks **every segment** of `relative(workspaceRoot, target)` (the helper is a segment rule, so `CON/notes.txt` is refused before `mkdir("…/CON")`) and answers **400 naming the offending segment**. The route keeps accepting nested relative paths; the upload path's "plain basename only" rule is still not imposed here.

Why not direction 1 (call `sanitizeUploadFilename` in the handler): on this base that function has **no** reserved-name branch — it only rejects empty/NUL/absolute/traversal names, which `resolveWorkspaceFile` already enforces — so calling it today would be a no-op for the reported defect. Adding the rule inside it here would duplicate `#868`'s open hunk in the same function (and that PR exists to fix exactly that statement). Putting the predicate beside `assertWorkspacePath` gives both write paths one home once they meet.

### Relation to `#868` (open)

`#868` carries the identical rule inline in `sanitizeUploadFilename`. This diff deliberately does **not** touch `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts`, so the two do not overlap: when `#868` lands, its guard should call `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` and drop the inline copy (one hunk), leaving main with a single implementation. Whichever merges second does that; if `#868` lands first I will rebase this branch and make that change here.

## Review fix — P2, a device name in a directory segment (review `5773758545`, reviewed at `93af68c8`)

The first version applied the predicate to `basename(target)`, i.e. only the last segment. The route accepts nested relative paths, so `body.path = "CON/notes.txt"` had basename `notes.txt` and passed the guard; the write then reached `mkdir(dirname(target), { recursive: true })`. On a Windows host `CreateDirectory("…/CON")` fails (Node surfaces `EPERM`/`ENOENT`), which is the same unclassified 500 this PR removes; on Linux it creates an unportable `CON/` directory. The helper was already documented as a segment rule, so the call site was the narrow part.

Fixed as asked: the route now splits `relative(workspaceRoot, target)` on the host separator and refuses the first reserved segment. That subsumes the old last-segment case, and the message names the segment the client must change (`"CON"` for `CON/notes.txt`, `"nul.dir"` for `nul.dir/x.csv`) instead of a basename it never sent.

The predicate's doc comment no longer claims to be called from every writer. It states the per-segment rule, names where it is applied today (this route), and says that the agent-side workspace tools, which write through `assertWorkspacePath`, are not wired to it yet.

`WSP-005` (`services/api/src/server.test.ts`) now covers, in addition to the top-level names (`CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, `CON .csv`, and the named-stream forms added below) and the look-alikes from the first version:

- `CON/notes.txt` → 400, the message names `CON`
- `nul.dir/x.csv` → 400, the message names `nul.dir` (stem before the first dot is `nul`, and Windows refuses the directory too)
- `notes/CON.txt` → 400 (control: clean directory, device-name file — refused before this change too)
- `conifer/notes.txt` → 201 (control: the walk must not start refusing legitimate nested paths)

## Review fix — F1, a device's named stream (`nul:stream`, `CON:$DATA`)

The predicate cut the stem at the first dot only, so Windows' named-stream spellings slipped through: `nul:stream` kept its colon, `/^(?:con|prn|aux|nul|com[1-9]|lpt[1-9]|conin\$|conout\$)$/i` never matched, `CON:$DATA` likewise, and the write route answered 201 and created a file a Windows host resolves to the device's stream rather than to a file. Windows takes everything before the colon as the device, so the stem is now cut at the first dot and then at the first colon:

- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` — `name.split(".")[0]?.split(":")[0]?.replace(/[. ]+$/, "")`. `con:$DATA` → `con`, `nul:stream` → `nul`, `NUL:stream` → `NUL`; `conin$`/`conout$` keep the `$` because no colon splits them; the trailing-dot/space strip still runs last, so `nul.` and `CON ` match exactly as before.
- The route needed no change: it already walks every segment through the predicate, so `{"path":"nul:stream"}` now answers 400 naming `nul:stream`.
- `#903` is re-scoped: F1 (named streams) is fixed here, so the follow-up keeps only D2, the POSIX segment split (`CON\notes.txt` when the host separator is `/`).

## Red first

Original case at base `89cd2d30` (test commit `1c3259df`, now the first half of `WSP-005`):

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
not ok 1 - WSP-005 a reserved device name in a session file write answers 400 and names the file
  error: CON must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

The two new directory cases are red at the previous tip `93af68c8` (`0a1ca4fc` is test only). The loop stops at the first failure, so each was run as the only new case:

```
$ node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
  error: CON/notes.txt must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
$ (same command, `nul.dir/x.csv` as the only new case)
  error: nul.dir/x.csv must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
```

`notes/CON.txt` and `conifer/notes.txt` are green at `93af68c8` by design: they are the controls, so they carry no red reading.

Named-stream case at `c4fb33d4` (test commit `ddd14462`):

```
$ cd packages/workspace && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern isWindowsReservedDeviceName src/workspace.test.ts
not ok 1 - isWindowsReservedDeviceName treats a named stream as its device
  error: nul:stream names a device stream
  false !== true
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1

$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
not ok 1 - WSP-005 a reserved device name in a session file write answers 400 and names the file
  error: nul:stream must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

The API route test reads `@sciencediscovery/workspace` from `dist`, so the package was rebuilt from `c4fb33d4` before this red run; an older local `dist` otherwise masks the defect.

## Validation

The API tests load `@sciencediscovery/workspace` from its built `dist`, so the package is built first (CI does the same: the shared runner runs `pnpm build` before the heavy layers).

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| workspace build | `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/workspace/tsconfig.json` | exit 0 |
| typecheck (api) | `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| typecheck (workspace) | `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/workspace/tsconfig.json --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| tests typecheck | `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| predicate case | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern isWindowsReservedDeviceName src/workspace.test.ts` (`packages/workspace`) | `1/1` pass |
| route case | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts` (`services/api`) | `1/1` pass |
| workspace route group | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "WSP-00" src/server.test.ts` (`services/api`) | `3/3` pass |
| package UT | `npm test` (`packages/workspace`) | `101 tests / 101 pass / 0 fail` |
| api server suite | `node --import tsx --test src/server.test.ts` (`services/api`) | `109 tests / 108 pass / 1 fail`: `PDF upload extracts full text and tables into the session workspace` needs `reportlab` in `services/paper/.venv` (environment, not this diff) |
| api UT (full, earlier run at `c4fb33d4`) | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` | `1866 tests / 1860 pass / 6 fail`: 5 environment (`No module named uvicorn` in `services/evolve/.venv`; `No module named 'reportlab'` ×3; missing `@openai/codex-linux-x64`), 1 load flake in `evolution/orchestrator.test.ts` (`timed out waiting for the run to finish`) that passes on its own (`--test-name-pattern "settled"` → `3/3`). None touch this diff. |

Not run: a real Windows host — the guard is deliberately platform-independent, so the Linux route test exercises the same code path; there is no Windows-only branch in it.

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…HEAD`: 4 files, `+134/−6` (`workspace.test.ts` `+20/−1`, `workspace.ts` `+29`, `http/index.ts` `+17/−5`, `server.test.ts` `+68`). No existing assertion is relaxed; the two edits to existing test lines are the look-alike loop gaining `conifer/notes.txt` and the top-level refusal loop gaining `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA`.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: writing a session file whose name or directory component is a Windows device (`CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, `CON .csv`, `CON/notes.txt`, `nul.dir/x.csv`, and the named-stream forms `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA`) now answers 400 naming the offending segment, on every platform, instead of returning 201 and creating a file a Windows host cannot open (or a write that silently goes to the console or fails as a 500). Ordinary names such as `conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `com10.csv` and `conifer/notes.txt` are unaffected.
Compatibility and migration: none — only names Windows itself cannot create are refused.

Related to #812

Partial. Keep #812 open.

A directed search can now run on the conversation's selected runner. A JSON the search had already measured was still spending a round, and the NPU path handed the search library one task, which that library refuses to start on. A search that does not name editable fields stays the existing free program search.

## Directed edits

The chat agent starts the run and does not pick later steps. PUCT chooses which measured node to expand. The model then proposes one JSON object. Only the fields the user ticked may change. A change to any other field, or a value that is not JSON, is rejected before the runner and has no score. A proposal that matches an edit already measured is not sent to the card. The model is asked again, inside the same slot, for a different JSON.

There is no task-specific update rule. The model sees the measured values and their scores and proposes the next JSON itself.

## NPU scoring

Each candidate is one fresh shell execution on the conversation's selected runner, in a sandbox with no network. The fixed program computes the score. The candidate is JSON bound as input, not the program that runs. Success is a completed execution whose result says the device is `npu` and includes a number. A job that is still queued or running is waited on and does not take another slot. A failure, a cancellation, or a missing result has no score and is not stored as 0.

The search library requires at least four tasks and a hold-out fraction strictly between 0 and 1. An NPU search supplies four task ids and holds one out. The domain caches the measurement, so those ids do not each use the card.

## Field table

The run shows the ticked fields. Each candidate row shows which field changed, the old value, the new value, and the score.

## Validation

- `services/evolve/tests/test_npu_direction.py`: 16 passed.
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run on this Windows host. Those layers need the bubblewrap sandbox used by the CI scripts.
- Local stack, one selected NPU card: a directed search completed. The discrimination probe returned two different numeric scores for the starting JSON and a damaged field. A later search requested 10 rounds and stored 6 new measurements, then stopped because the round counter ended. Scores were read from the runner. No score was invented, and a missing result was not stored as 0.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED for the mocked browser suite: this host cannot run the bubblewrap CI layers.

Local stack: the directed NPU search above completed on one selected card and returned runner scores. The field table was not clicked through in a browser in this update.

## Release

Release category: release:feature

User impact: a search can score candidates on the conversation's selected NPU runner, and can limit edits to named JSON fields.

Compatibility and migration: none for a search that does not ask for a runner or a field list. That path stays the existing program search.

The GitHub label is pending a maintainer.

items.body:
Fixes #883

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What changed

`_NODE_LIMIT` is a hard cap of 500 nodes, and the contract at `query.py:319` says only results **beyond** it carry `truncated: True`. The flag was computed *after* a Cypher `LIMIT` bound to exactly the cap, so the Python side could never observe a 501st row: a complete 500-row answer and a cut one were indistinguishable and both reported `truncated: true`. The panel then drew `N of 500+ (truncated) match(es) in view` — the `+` asserting a further match that does not exist — and a session graph of exactly 500 nodes was badged as partial.

`query.py` now has one helper, `_cap_page(rows)`, returning the kept page and `len(rows) > _NODE_LIMIT` as the flag. Two shapes use it:

- **Cypher-driven reads** — `query_match` (`:431`), `by_node_type` (`:465`), `by_edge_type` (`:518`), `get_subgraph` (`:272`) and `_serialize_subgraph` (`:1298`): the Cypher limit is bound to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`, the page is cut to `_NODE_LIMIT` and the extra row alone decides the flag. `query_match`/`by_node_type` count the **raw rows** before `_to_hit`, the variant the issue prefers: a row dropped because its label has no id field is not a truncation. In `get_subgraph` the node-id set used to filter edges and synthesize the folded scope→product surrogates is built from the kept page, so no rendered edge points at a node the caller did not receive.
- **Assembled reads** — `get_scope_expansion` (`:898`) and `get_group_expansion` (`:1024`): these build their node set from several queries (children + produces subtree + edge endpoints; group members + one surrogate edge each) and have **no Cypher `LIMIT`** to raise, so `cap + 1` does not apply to them. The cap is applied to the assembled page instead, and an edge whose endpoint fell outside the page is dropped rather than rendered against an absent node. `get_group_expansion` and `_serialize_subgraph` were not in the issue's list of five: they carry the identical predicate (`len(...) >= _NODE_LIMIT` over a set that had not been cut at all — flagging a page they never truncated), so they are fixed in the same slice rather than left as the same defect on two more surfaces.

`total` keeps its previous meaning (the number of rows the response carries), so no client contract changes; `services/api` and the web panel forward the flag verbatim and need no edit.

## Red first

Test commit `9ce6d309` (test only), base `89cd2d30`:

```
$ cd services/memory-graph && uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q
14 failed in 0.50s
```

Three distinct failure shapes prove the tests reach the real paths:

- `assert True is False` — a complete 500-row answer reported as truncated (the reported defect, once per capped reader);
- `assert 500 == (500 + 1)` — the reader bound `$limit` to the cap itself, so the flag cannot be decided at all;
- `assert 501 == 500` — the two assembled readers returned all 501 nodes: the page had not been cut even though it was flagged.

Green at `e1957043`: the same command gives `14 passed in 0.15s`.

## Validation

The branch is rebased onto the current main tip `89cd2d30` (it was first based on a mirror that still served `8708320f`); `services/memory-graph` has no upstream drift between the two, and every reading below was taken again at the rebased commits.

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| new cap cases | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed` (7 readers × exactly-500 / 501) |
| memory-graph suite, tip | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ -q` | `123 passed, 15 warnings, 78 errors` |
| memory-graph suite, same tree without the new file (baseline) | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `109 passed, 14 warnings, 78 errors` |
| error set | `diff` of the `ERROR tests/...` lines of the two runs | identical (78 lines) |

The 78 errors are the pre-existing `@needs_neo4j` suite on this host — every one fails in setup with `Failed: needs a live Neo4j`, and the set is node-for-node the same with and without this diff (`187` collected before, `201` after the 14 new cases).

The cases assert more than the flag: for each reader a 501-row result must return exactly 500 rows; the assembled readers must drop the spine edge that points into the cut row; `_serialize_subgraph` and the four Cypher readers must bind `$limit` to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`.

Not run: anything needing a live Neo4j (the Cypher and the rendered panel text itself), because there is no graph on this host and `ci.yml` has no memory-graph job — the issue notes this, so the local pytest output above is the acceptance evidence. The TypeScript gates (`pnpm --recursive typecheck`, `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`) are not run: the diff touches no TypeScript.

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…e1dee252`: 3 files, `+656/−19` (`query.py` `+93/−19`, `tests/test_node_limit.py` `+320`, `tests/test_node_limit_rule.py` `+243`). No existing assertion is relaxed.

## Review fix (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` on `e1957043`, review `5773456818`)

`yuanzhou75` found that the new test file stopped the whole `UT` layer before a single case ran: the tagged audit (`test/support/tagged/python/science_tags.py:103-108`) accepts only `pytest.mark.parametrize` arguments that pass `ast.literal_eval`, and `CAP` / `CAP + 1` are a `Name` and a `BinOp`. Because the audit runs in `pytest_collect_file`, collection aborted with `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: .../test_node_limit.py:107` and `merge-gate` never evaluated. Fixed at `04ce9c89`, in the shape the review asked for:

- **All seven** parameter tables (lines 105/123/155/181/227/266/290) are now `[(500, False), (501, True)]` with their existing ids, and each case opens with `assert query._NODE_LIMIT == 500  # the table above is literal on purpose`. `CAP` stays and is still used by the body assertions, including the one requiring `$limit == CAP + 1`.
- One more registration defect the audit then exposed: the module carried **no** `science_tags` module mark, so once the audit passed the catalog step raised `ValueError: Missing tag group: category` — the same `PYTHON_COLLECTION_FAILED` for the layer, one step later. It now has the line every sibling in this suite has: `pytestmark = pytest.mark.science_tags(category='ut', os='linux', arch=('amd64', 'arm64'))`.

Verified at `04ce9c89` with the harness's own code, not a stand-in for it:

```
$ cd services/memory-graph && python3 -c "import sys; sys.path[:0]=['../../test/support/tagged/python']; import science_tags, pathlib; science_tags.audit_source(pathlib.Path('tests/test_node_limit.py'))"
(no output) exit 0        # before: ValueError: DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: tests/test_node_limit.py:107
```

```
$ PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 PYTHONPATH=<repo>/test/support/tagged/python \
  uv run --project services/memory-graph --extra test python -m pytest -p science_tags \
  --strict-markers --rootdir <repo> --collect-only -q \
  --science-root=<repo> --science-catalog=<file> $(ls services/memory-graph/tests/test_*.py)
201 tests collected in 0.99s     # exit 0
```

That is the command `coordinator.mjs`'s `collect()` runs — same `-p science_tags`, `--strict-markers`, `--rootdir`, `--science-catalog`, plugin autoload off — over every source `pythonSources('memory-graph')` globs. The catalog it wrote has 201 entries, 14 of them from this file, tagged `category:ut, os:linux, arch:amd64, arch:arm64, tier:l2, status:reviewed, ...`. Before the change the same command died at `:107`; with only the tables fixed it died again at the missing `category`.

| gate | command | reading at `04ce9c89` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tag audit | `science_tags.audit_source(tests/test_node_limit.py)` | exit 0 |
| tagged collection, whole project | `pytest -p science_tags --collect-only` over `services/memory-graph/tests/test_*.py` | `201 tests collected`, exit 0, 201 catalog entries |
| new cap cases | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed, 1 warning` |
| memory-graph suite | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ -q` | `129 passed, 16 warnings, 78 errors` |

The one warning the module adds is `PytestUnknownMarkWarning: Unknown pytest.mark.science_tags`, which every sibling module in this suite emits when pytest runs without the tagged plugin (`tests/test_logging_config.py` on its own gives `1 passed, 1 warning`); the plugin registers the marker and the collection above passes `--strict-markers`. The 78 errors are the unchanged `@needs_neo4j` setup failures.

No other file changed; the five commits stay separate: `9ce6d309` red test, `e1957043` fix, `04ce9c89` this registration fix, `86bbd1a5` the rule cases below, `e1dee252` the rule fix.

### Second review: one meaning for `truncated` (thread `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM6zusPi`)

The review found three counting conventions for one flag in the same PR. I took the first of its two options and made it the only one: **`truncated` means the backend returned more rows than `_NODE_LIMIT`, counted on the rows that were read and *before* a row is dropped for having no identity.**

Why this rule and not "count only renderable hits":

- **Only the returned-row count can be decided.** Each Cypher read binds `LIMIT` to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`, and that one extra row is the whole probe. Filtering first spends the probe on a row that cannot be rendered: 500 readable hits plus an unrenderable 501st would look *complete* although a renderable 502nd may exist, which is a completeness claim nothing checked. The returned-row count claims only what the extra row proves — the answer went past the cap.
- **It is the question the panel text asks.** `N of 500+ (truncated)` says the graph holds more matches than are shown. True when 501 rows came back even if one cannot be drawn; false when 501 came back and the response says "complete".
- **A short page stays complete.** 500 rows with one unrenderable row → 499 rendered, `truncated: false`: nothing was left unread, so there is nothing to disclose. Both directions are pinned below.

What changed:

- `get_subgraph` now caps the returned `(label, node)` rows and then runs `_node_identity`; `_serialize_subgraph` caps the returned rows and then runs `_to_hit`. Those are the two readers that capped the *filtered* list.
- `query_match`, `by_node_type`, `by_edge_type` already capped the returned rows; `query_match`'s comment argued the opposite and now states the rule, and the other two carry the same sentence.
- `get_scope_expansion` and `get_group_expansion` cap the assembled page, where every element already has an identity by construction, so "rows read" and "renderable rows" coincide there — no behaviour change, and the comment says so.
- `_cap_page`'s docstring states the rule once, and why the filter has to run after the cut. The review's nit (`nodes = list(hit_rows)` and a rebind on the next line) disappears with the restructure: `nodes` is built directly from the kept rows.

`tests/test_node_limit_rule.py` (new, 6 cases) pins the rule rather than the arithmetic: an unrenderable row as the 501st sets the flag on `query_match`, `by_edge_type`, `get_subgraph` and `_serialize_subgraph`, and a complete 500-row page that holds one unrenderable row stays complete on `query_match` and `get_subgraph`. Two of the six fail on `86bbd1a5` — `assert False is True` on the two readers that filtered first — and pass on `e1dee252`; the four that already held are there so a future reader cannot silently move one side into the other's shape again.

Deferred, deliberately not in this PR: `get_scope_expansion` / `get_group_expansion` still read every child/member and cut in Python, so the cap bounds the response and not the query work — same as before this PR, noted for follow-up.

Readings at `e1dee252`:

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rule cases | `pytest tests/test_node_limit_rule.py -q` | `6 passed` |
| cap cases | `pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed` |
| whole suite | `pytest tests/ -q` | `129 passed, 16 warnings, 78 errors` (the 78 unchanged) |
| tag audit, both files | `science_tags.audit_source(...)` | exit 0 each |
| tagged collection | `pytest -p science_tags --collect-only` over `services/memory-graph/tests/test_*.py` | `207 tests collected`, exit 0, 207 catalog entries |

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: a memory-graph search that matches exactly 500 nodes no longer says `500+ (truncated)` — it reports the count as complete — and a session graph of exactly 500 nodes is no longer badged as partial. A query that really has more than the cap still reports `truncated` and still returns 500 rows.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Fixes #673

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts` capped an extracted page with a bare `text.slice(0, MAX_DOCUMENT_CHARS)` (4096 UTF-16 units), so a character that straddles the cut left a lone high surrogate at the end of the body handed to the model.

Reproduction (`main` before the fix, logic copied verbatim):

```
$ node -e 'const MAX=4096; const text="x".repeat(MAX-1)+"😀"; console.log(JSON.stringify(text.slice(0,MAX).slice(-2)))'
"\ud83d"
```

  ---
  failureType: 'testCodeFailure'

## What changed

- `document()` in `fetch.ts` now drops a dangling high surrogate after the cut, so the result ends on a code point, never exceeds the 4096-unit budget, and creates no new lone surrogate. The same rule the artifact preview uses.
- New test `document truncation never ends in half a surrogate pair` covers both `renderTavilyExtract` and `renderExaContents` with an emoji straddling the boundary, plus a lone-surrogate check on the rendered document.
- Nothing else changes: same cap, same `# title\n\n` prefix, same vendor normalizers.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Fixes #867

## What the user sees

A workspace file of `1_048_575` bytes (1 MiB − 1) prints **`1024.0 KiB`** in the file-provenance modal, and `1_073_741_823` bytes print **`1024.0 MiB`**. The unit was picked from the *unrounded* value (`1023.999… KiB`, so the loop stopped at KiB) while the printed value came from `toFixed`, which rounded up to `1024.0` — a number no KiB value can hold. The CSV artifact inspector had the same boundary and additionally never left MiB, so `1_073_741_823` bytes always read `1024.0 MiB` there.

The size is the only quantitative evidence in a provenance record, so a value labelled with the wrong unit is the record itself being wrong.

## Change

- New `apps/web/src/formatBytes.ts` with one ladder (`KiB → MiB → GiB → TiB`) shared by both call sites. The unit is chosen from the **same rounded value that is printed**, so a size never prints at or above its unit's own base.
- The decimal policy is not changed: `"adaptive"` keeps `>= 10 ? 1 : 2` decimals (`1.50 KiB`, `12.3 MiB`), and the CSV inspector keeps its fixed one decimal.
- `WorkspaceFileProvenanceModal.tsx` drops its local `formatBytes` and uses the shared ladder.
- `csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts`'s exported `formatBytes` keeps its name and signature but delegates to the ladder with one decimal, and gains `GiB`/`TiB`.
- Bytes stay bytes (`1023 B`), an exact MiB stays `1.00 MiB` / `1.0 MiB`.

Readings after the fix: provenance `1_048_575 → 1.00 MiB`, `1_073_741_823 → 1.00 GiB`; CSV `1_048_575 → 1.0 MiB`, `1_073_741_823 → 1.0 GiB`, `1_099_511_627_775 → 1.0 TiB`.

## Red first (`#867` on `89cd2d30`)

```
not ok 1 - a provenance size one byte under 1 MiB never prints 1024.0 KiB
  error: '1024.0 KiB must not be printed: ...<dd>1024.0 KiB</dd>...'
not ok 2 - a provenance size one byte under 1 GiB never prints 1024.0 MiB
  error: '1024.0 MiB must not be printed: ...<dd>1024.0 MiB</dd>...'
not ok 4 - the CSV inspector size crosses the unit boundary it prints
  expected: '1.0 MiB'
  actual:   '1024.0 KiB'
# tests 5
# pass 2
# fail 3
```

The two passing tests are the "keeps the readings it already had" ones (`1023 B`, `1.00 MiB`, `1.50 KiB`, `5.50 MiB`, `1.5 KiB`, `5.5 MiB`), which pin the unchanged behaviour.

## After the fix

```
# tests 5
# pass 5
# fail 0
```

## Gates (at tip, exact commands)

```
pnpm --recursive typecheck                      -> exit 0
tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json                      -> exit 0
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test        -> exit 0  (# tests 1220 / # pass 1220 / # fail 0)
CI_E2E_PREPARED=1 pnpm ci:l1                    -> exit 0  (PASS 4/4)
```

## Diff (vs `89cd2d30`)

```
 apps/web/src/WorkspaceFileProvenanceModal.tsx |  13 +---
 apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts     |   8 +-
 apps/web/src/formatBytes.ts                   |  43 +++++++++++
 apps/web/tests/sizeBoundary.test.tsx          | 104 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 153 insertions(+), 15 deletions(-)
```

Release category: `release:fix` (the account cannot add the label itself — no push rights on labels).

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
## Summary

Ready for maintainer review and merge. This PR extracts Idea Tree from the evolve process into an independently runnable Python service and exposes its research capabilities as session-scoped MCP tools.

Current candidate: `d81b7bf3ebc8d9b1ed09914a439768f43a5abd3a` (one squashed commit). Related to #101 and #84; partial delivery of the broader integration acceptance scope, so keep #101 open. This establishes the service boundary ahead of the evolve migration in #102.

## Changes

- Move the Idea Tree engine, service layer, models, prompts and templates out of evolve's vendored implementation into `services/idea-tree`. Preserve the existing research algorithm and remove the old evolve router registrations.
- Add a dedicated FastAPI process with a health endpoint, shutdown cleanup, internal-token authentication and loopback port `4314`. Require a single ASGI worker because active research tasks and short-lived capabilities are process-local.
- Persist research, trees and settings in a service-owned data directory. Copy legacy records once without deleting originals; conflicting destination records fail migration rather than overwrite data.
- Publish `create_idea_research`, `get_idea_research`, `control_idea_research` and `view_idea_tree` through scoped MCP endpoints. Project/session identity and model callback credentials come from the trusted control plane rather than model arguments. Capabilities expire after five minutes; revoking a transport capability does not stop autonomous research.
- Replace the old API Python client with `IdeaTreeServiceClient`. Discover tool schemas from the service, preserve historical graph reads, research-created messages and SSE forwarding, and keep the six existing frontend research/graph/settings routes and response shapes.
- Include the service in stack startup, Docker packaging, isolated browser-test configuration, test discovery and coverage. Update English and Chinese developer documentation.

## Review fixes included

- Restore complete `evolveAvailability` initialization and bootstrap wiring.
- Restore the actual `research_service.py` service layer instead of the accidentally duplicated engine module.
- Migrate remaining tests away from the removed Python client and evolve vendor modules; remove the unused compatibility adapter.
- Remove the Evolve-readiness guard from independent Idea Tree routes.
- Disable Uvicorn access logging in the application lifespan as well as the launcher, preventing MCP capability URLs from being logged with direct `uvicorn ...:app` startup. Include a direct-Uvicorn regression.
- Correct stale developer-document paths and replace the redundant listener-address type assertion identified by CodeCheck with a runtime guard.

## Validation

GitHub Actions for the current candidate: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40816521503

| Check | Current-head result |
| --- | --- |
| L1 static checks | PASS |
| UT | PASS |
| ST | PASS |
| Mocked browser L2: governed, literature, research, standard-config, standard-journeys | PASS, all five shards |
| Coverage | PASS |
| merge-gate | PASS |
| GitCode CodeCheck | PASS |
| GitCode SCA, anti-poison and blacklist checks | PASS |
| CLA | All contributors confirmed signed |

GitCode mirror report: https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/pull/412/check

Real L3/L4/L5, binary release and Docker execution were skipped by this PR's CI policy; they are not counted as passes. The statuses above are job outcomes, not invented test-case counts.

Local validation before squash included full TypeScript checking (including test types), 12/12 protocol compatibility cases, 7/7 public research/client regressions, 7/7 standalone service/security cases and L1 4/4. Full local UT/ST/browser-L2 attempts were interrupted by host/WSL issues and did not produce complete passing summaries; the complete passing UT/ST/browser-L2 results above are from GitHub Actions. The squashed candidate has the identical source tree as the preceding validated head (`6101e330b75bbf6edca2747d1a981a7fd994cf94`).

## Deployment and scope

- Stop the old stack before upgrading. The maintained stack script and Docker packaging start the new service; custom supervisors must provide its process and matching URL/token configuration.
- Session ownership, chat-message writes and model-secret provisioning remain in the API control plane. Research still uses the existing run-bound LLM callback pending #102; provider API keys are not passed to the service.
- Artifact/provenance/CAS ownership remains outside this PR (#98).
- Targeted public-route, SSE and create-time message regressions are included. A complete baseline/candidate differential of all six public routes and a complete chat/agent event-stream golden trace are not claimed. These remaining broader #101 acceptance items must stay tracked explicitly rather than be inferred from green CI.

## Maintainer review and merge request

Please review and merge this PR after confirming acceptance of the independent Idea Tree service boundary: its process/port, internal token, state and settings ownership, one-time migration, and API-to-service protocol. The `needs-human` decision still requires a maintainer; this request does not claim it has already been approved.

The current CI gates and CodeCheck are green, CLA is confirmed, and the previous Draft/do-not-merge wording has been removed. Please re-review the current squashed commit and grant approval if the service boundary and the explicitly documented scope are acceptable for merge. No automatic merge has been enabled.

Release category: `release:feature` (label applied).

items.body:
Desktop's built-in source switches currently change connector permissions, while Web source selection changes the sources sessions use by default. This can make a source appear enabled in Desktop without selecting its tools for an ordinary session. This PR makes the Desktop system settings page edit the global default source selection through `enabledConnectorIds`.

## Data source selection

- Rename the page to **Data sources** and add **Use by default** checkboxes for built-in and custom sources.
- Save the global `enabledConnectorIds` list while preserving unrelated overrides, instead of writing `plugins["connector.<id>"].enabled` for built-in selections. Retain the existing `web`-only fallback when the effective list is absent.
- Replace bulk enable/disable actions with **Select all / Clear selection** for listed sources. These actions change selection without reconnecting or disabling custom services.
- Keep custom MCP connection configuration separate: **Enable service** remains in the edit modal, alongside the existing edit, test and delete actions.
- Display catalog/service readiness independently of selection. Selecting a source does not establish that its service is ready or that its tools can be called.
- Update English/Chinese text and settings-page rendering tests.

This is a global defaults editor. It does not introduce a Desktop per-session selector or change backend selection, inheritance, permissions, or tool execution contracts. No settings migration is included.

## Validation

Tested commit: `7ed2300ff3735a71168d143815e6814790f6986f`.
Environment: Linux x86_64 / WSL2, Node.js v22.19.0; local shell executor, direct component/unit tests.

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`: **684 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`: **PASS**.
- `git diff --check`: **PASS**.
- The commit's code tree matches the original data-source commit exactly. The data-source and failure-notice changes were split without changing their combined code tree.

The settings tests exercise rendering; they do not prove persistence, cross-client reloads or effective session tool availability. Full local CI layers were not rerun as part of this branch split. Remote checks must be evaluated on this new head.

## Product journey coverage

**Not verified in this update:** Desktop/Web sharing a backend; selecting and clearing sources followed by a new inheriting session; explicit project/session overrides; specialist supplementation; disabled/unavailable custom services; native Windows/macOS Desktop. These remain acceptance evidence gaps for #852. Unit/component tests are not substitutes for these journeys.

Related: #852, #718.
The run-failure presentation changes are submitted separately and are no longer part of this PR.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`. Applying the GitHub label is pending a maintainer because the contributor account lacks upstream label permissions.
User impact: Desktop source selection edits the session defaults rather than routine built-in permission switches.
Compatibility and migration: no schema changes; no migration included.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Fixes #863

## What the user sees

Settings › Models shows each provider row's context window and max output as a compact badge (`1M / 131k`). `compactTokenCount` rounded to whole units, so a declared 1,500,000 window rendered `2M` (and 1,400,000 rendered `1M`), and `999,999` rendered `1000k` — a count that reads as a million but is not. The badge is the only place the row shows these numbers, so the row advertises capacity the profile does not have.

## Change

`apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.tsx`:

- `1M ≤ value < 10M` keeps one decimal (`1,500,000 → 1.5M`, `1,400,000 → 1.4M`) and drops a trailing `.0`, so whole millions still read `1M` / `2M` (unchanged).
- The `k` branch rounds first and, when the rounded value reaches 1000, crosses into `M` (`999,999 → 1M`) instead of printing `1000k`.
- `≥ 10M` stays integer (`10,500,000 → 11M`), and `131,072 → 131k` / `200,000 → 200k` keep their existing output.
- The docstring is updated with the new rule — the old one said "as integers", which would have made the rounding look intentional.

No API change; `formatTokenField` and the CSV export are untouched.

## Red first (`#863` on the base)

```
not ok 2 - a context window between 1M and 10M keeps the fraction it has
  expected: '1.5M'
  actual: '2M'
