items.body:
Fixes #875

## What changed

Both screens now read one decision from a new `apps/web/src/tokenCountFormat.ts`
(`compactTokenParts`): the tier, the rounding and the `".0"` trimming live
there, and each surface only spells the unit it already printed — the usage
page `K`, the model badge `k`. Before this, the badge rounded to whole millions
from 10M (`10_500_000 → "11M"`) while the usage page kept the fraction
(`"10.5M"`) for the same count.

Tiers, now shared:

- 1M and up: one decimal, dropped when it is `".0"` (`1_000_000 → "1M"`,
  `10_500_000 → "10.5M"`, `12_345_678 → "12.3M"`).
- 10K–1M: whole thousands (`200_000 → "200K"` / `"200k"`).
- 1K–10K: one decimal (`6_600 → "6.6K"` / `"6.6k"`).
- Below 1K: the plain count.
- The rounding decides the crossing: `999_999 → "1M"`, never `"1000K"`.

Measured before the change on base `89cd2d30` (badge / usage page):

```text
    999999  badge  1000k   usage 1000K
   1000000  badge     1M   usage 1.0M
   1500000  badge     2M   usage 1.5M
   9960000  badge    10M   usage 10.0M
  10500000  badge    11M   usage 10.5M
  12345678  badge    12M   usage 12.3M
```

Below one million the number is shared and only the unit glyph still differs,
as it already did on both screens; the test pins that difference (`"200k"` vs
`"200K"`) so a later "one spelling" refactor is a conscious change. Two readouts
move as a consequence of one rule: the badge prints one decimal in the 1K–10K
tier (`2_000 → "2.0k"`, no test pinned the old `"2k"`) and a whole million loses
`".0"` (`1_000_000 → "1M"` on the usage page, which is also the direction of
#864).

## Rebased onto `48848578`, after #864 merged

`#864` (`489dedd0`, "never round a token count into a unit it has not reached")
landed on `main` after this branch was last pushed, so the branch is rebased onto
`48848578` (two commits, no merge commit), and the one textual overlap,
`apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts`, keeps both rules:

- **#864's boundary rule is kept**: the `Math.round(value / 1_000) >= 1_000`
  crossing lives inside `compactTokenParts` now, so `999_999` still reads as a
  million (never `1000K`) and `999_499` still prints `999K`.
- **This pull request's rule is kept**: `formatCompactTokenValue` delegates to
  the shared ladder, so the usage page and the model badge cannot disagree.

One expectation moved with the rebase, and it is a spelling, not a boundary:
USG-031 pinned `1.0M` for a whole million, while the shared ladder drops a
trailing `.0` on both screens (the badge has always printed `1M`). Those three
constants now read `1M`; the crossing and the `999K` neighbour are unchanged.
Readings on the rebased tip:

```text
   999499  badge 999k  usage  999K   below the crossing
   999500  badge   1M  usage    1M   crossing (this is #864's boundary)
   999999  badge   1M  usage    1M   never "1000K"
  1000000  badge   1M  usage    1M
  9960000  badge  10M  usage   10M
 10500000  badge 10.5M usage 10.5M
```

## Red first

`apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts` on base `89cd2d30`:

```text
$ cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts
not ok 1 - USG-020 the usage page and the model badge agree from one million up
  error: |
    Expected values to be strictly equal:

    '11M' !== '10.5M'
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

The same test pins the neighbours that were red before the fix: `9_960_000`
(`"10M"` vs `"10.0M"`) and `1_500_000` (`"2M"` vs `"1.5M"`), plus
`1_000_000 → "1M"` on both screens.

## After

```text
# tests 1
# pass 1
# fail 0
```

## Gates, all on the pushed tip `824b604a5c44b0234f0330048959dc98b0100928` (rebased onto `48848578`)

Ran:

- `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → exit 0 (34 projects)
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → exit 0
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web typecheck` → exit 0
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` → `# tests 1222 / # pass 1222 / # fail 0`, exit 0 — both sides of the rebase run here: `UsagePage.test.tsx` USG-031 (the case #864 landed) and `tokenCountFormat.test.ts` USG-020
- `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1 pnpm ci:l1` → `{"status":"PASS","planned":4,"executed":4,"passed":4,"failed":0,"skipped":0}`, exit 0
- collector: `apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts` is byte-identical to `aca6fe7b` (blob `504ada22…`), so the collection evidence below still stands; re-ran it on the rebased tree → `{"status":"PASS","planned":1,"passed":1,"skipped":0}`
- app-test probe (`tsc` over `apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts`, extending `apps/web/tsconfig.json` with `types: ["vite/client","node"]`) → exit 0

Not run locally: the L2/ST profiles beyond L1 (CI runs them) and any browser/E2E
journey — this change is one formatter plus its two call sites.

## Review round: the new case was not in the shared plan

The case above was green locally but **not collected by the shared plan**, so a
green UT slice never ran it. `apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts` imported
`test` from `node:test`; the collector only takes files whose source contains
`category:<slice>`, and `audit-node.mjs` rejects a non-type `node:test` import
(`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs:228`, `audit-node.mjs:47`). Every other file in
`apps/web/tests` declares `createTest(import.meta.url, { tags: [...] })` — 125 of
127 — and this one did not.

Before, on `67cf5e01`:

```text
$ node test/support/tagged/cli.mjs list \
    --path apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts --os linux --arch amd64 --import tsx
NODE_COLLECTION_FAILED; inspect node-collect.log

$ cat node-collect.log
Error: DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts:16;
use static declarations and move runtime work into hooks
    at fail (test/support/tagged/audit-node.mjs:21:29)
```

After, the file declares the same tags as its peers and the plan carries it:

```text
$ node test/support/tagged/cli.mjs list \
    --path apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts --os linux --arch amd64 --import tsx
… "id": "apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts::USG-020%20the%20usage%20page%20and%20the%20model%20badge%20agree%20from%20one%20million%20up",
    "tags": ["arch:amd64","arch:arm64","category:ut","fixture:standard","isolation:none",
             "judge:none","model:none","npu:none","os:linux","sandbox:none",
             "status:reviewed","swarm:none","tier:l2"]

$ node test/support/tagged/cli.mjs run \
    --path apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts --os linux --arch amd64 --import tsx
{"status":"PASS","planned":1,"passed":1,"skipped":0}
```

The tag set is byte-for-byte the one a peer collected case gets
(`apps/web/tests/IdeaResearchLabels.test.ts`, compared with `cli.mjs list`). The
package-level `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` path still runs the
same file: `compat.mjs` returns the native `node:test` module when no shared run
has registered a plan.

## What happened to the earlier merge-order note

The merge-order note this body used to carry is settled by `main`: #864 is in
(`489dedd0`), and its reconciliation lives in this pull request instead of in a
later flip. The badge assertions already on `main`
(`apps/web/tests/ProviderModelList.test.tsx:44-46` pins `compactTokenCount(1_000_000) === "1M"`
and `1_048_576 → "1M"`) print exactly what the shared ladder prints, so no other
test file moves: the only expectations this pull request flips are the three
`1.0M` constants in `UsagePage.test.tsx` USG-031 described above.

## Badge readings that move because the tiers are shared

The badge no longer rounds to whole millions from 10M, which is the point of
this fix, and two visible readings follow from that one rule:

- `1_500` goes from `2k` to `1.5k`: the 1K–10K tier keeps one decimal, because
  that is the tier both screens now share. No test pinned the old `2k`.
- 10K–1M still prints the lowercase `k` on the badge (`200_000` → `200k`) while
  the usage page prints `K`; that glyph difference is pinned in the test, so a
  later "one spelling" refactor has to be a conscious change rather than a silent
  one.

## Diff, base `48848578`

```text
 apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.tsx    |  6 +− 4
 apps/web/src/tokenCountFormat.ts        | 46 +− 0
 apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts             |  8 +− 7
 apps/web/tests/UsagePage.test.tsx       |  6 +− 3
 apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts | 45 +− 0
 5 files changed, 111 insertions(+), 14 deletions(-)
```

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Fixes #816

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What changed

`SessionStore.writeArray` wrote its temp file and then called a bare `rename`, so a transient Windows sharing violation (an antivirus scanner, a search indexer or a backup agent briefly holding the fresh file) rejected the write, and nothing above contained the rejection.

- `services/api/src/store.ts` — **every** replace in the store now goes through the platform facade's `renameReplace`: the state writer (`writeArray`), the deletion journal finalize (`operation.next.json` → `operation.json`), and both journal staging renames (`stageDeletion`, `rollbackStagedDeletion`). The sharing violation belongs to the target file, not to one writer, so leaving the deletion paths on a bare `rename` would have kept the same failure shape on delete/rollback.
- `services/api/src/platform/os/replace.ts` (new) — one replace policy for every platform: 20 attempts, `50 + 25·attempt` ms backoff. Patience is 19 waits, `19 × 50 ms + 25 ms × (0 + … + 18) = 5,225 ms` (about 5.2 s). A non-transient errno such as `ENOSPC` is thrown immediately.
- `services/api/src/platform/os/replace.ts` — the retried errno set is platform-aware (`transientReplaceCodes()`): Windows retries `EPERM`/`EACCES`/`EBUSY` because its redirector reports all three for a transient hold; POSIX retries only `EPERM`/`EBUSY`, because an `EACCES` there is a lasting mode/ownership problem and `writeArray` is on the chat run path — retrying it would add 5.2 s to every state write of an already-unwritable store instead of failing at once. `ReplaceFileOptions.transientCodes` allows an override.
- `services/api/src/platform/os/replace.ts` — when the attempts are exhausted the throw is a `FileReplaceError` that keeps the last errno in `code` and the original error in `cause`, names the destination and the attempt count, and now also **copies `errno`/`syscall`/`path`/`dest`** from the last failure. A consumer that classified state-write failures on those fields would otherwise have been silently downgraded; `code`, `cause` and the `FileReplaceError` identity are unchanged, so a caller (or a test) that reads them still works.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` — the run scheduler is started with `void`, so nothing observed its rejection. It now attaches a `catch` that logs `run_scheduler_failed` with the session id and the message.
- `services/api/src/platform/os/index.ts` / `win32.ts` / `types.ts` — the retry moves out of the Windows-only adaptation (which now performs the raw rename) up to the facade, so the durable write behaves the same on every platform.

## Where the exhausted write could kill the process

The caller is **`scheduleSessionRuns` (`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3380`)** — the per-session run drain started from every run-creating request. Its body is `void (async () => { … })()`, and the statement that escapes is the **terminal `await store.updateSessionRunStatus(sessionId, next.id, status, …)` inside the inner `finally` (`:3522`)** (plus the `listSessionRuns` in the outer `finally`): the inner `try/catch` does not cover its own `finally`, so a state write that exhausts the retries propagates out of the `while`, through the outer `finally`, and out of a promise nobody awaits. Node 22 treats that as an unhandled rejection and exits — the reported crash.

With the catch: the rejection is logged, `scheduledSessions` has already released the session, and the run keeps the last status it could persist (`running`), which `recoverSessionRuns` turns into `interrupted` at the next start. Nothing is silently lost and the process survives. The regression test below fails on the pre-fix code with exactly the unhandled rejection, so this is pinned rather than argued.

## Red-first evidence

Test commit `ce393efa` (test only) on base `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`, `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test …`:

- `src/store-deletion.test.ts` → `# tests 7 / # pass 6 / # fail 1`
  ```
  not ok 2 - a transient EPERM on the deletion journal finalize is retried
    error: "EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '…/.trash/<id>/operation.next.json' -> '…/.trash/<id>/operation.json'"
  ```
  (the bare rename on the journal path, found in review, fails exactly like the state writer did)
- `src/runs/index.test.ts` → `# tests 16 / # pass 15 / # fail 1`
  ```
  not ok 16 - a state write that fails after retries is contained instead of killing the API
    error: 'Could not replace …/session-runs/<id>.json after 20 attempts (EPERM)'
  ```
  (the rejection escapes the voided scheduler and node:test reports it — the crash shape)
- `src/platform/os/replace.test.ts` does not load at `ce393efa`: `transientReplaceCodes` is the new export the platform split (and its POSIX no-retry assertion) needs.

Green at `8cb37d8aa37dab30853d75dfe5462eb2341b29f5`: the same four files `node --import tsx --test src/platform/os/replace.test.ts src/store-deletion.test.ts src/runs/index.test.ts src/store-replace.test.ts` → `# tests 29 / # pass 29 / # fail 0`.

## Verification

| gate | command | exit | reading |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck (recursive) | `pnpm --recursive typecheck` | 0 | — |
| tests typecheck | `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | 0 | — |
| targeted UT | `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/platform/os/replace.test.ts src/store-deletion.test.ts src/runs/index.test.ts src/store-replace.test.ts` | 0 | `29/29` |
| package UT | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` | 1 | `1873 tests / 1868 pass / 5 fail`, all five environmental and untouched by this diff: `No module named uvicorn` in `services/evolve/.venv` (`idea-tree/research-entry.test.ts`), `No module named 'reportlab'` in `services/paper/.venv` (three PDF tests), and `Cannot find module '@openai/codex-linux-x64/package.json'` (`codex.st.test.ts`) |
| static/architecture | `pnpm architecture:check` | 1 | `98/99`; the single failure is `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs` calling `bash .ci/run-research-python.sh race`, which cannot create its temp dir (`/home/xuke/.cache/uv/...: Read-only file system (os error 30)`) on this host store |

The repository has no `lint` script or eslint configuration, so `pnpm architecture:check` is used as its static gate.

Not run: the ST/E2E layer locally (`st.agent-loop-mocked` stalls on `evolve-distribution.test.ts` on this host, untouched by the diff); ST is taken from CI on this pull request. No Windows host was available, so the Windows-only `EACCES` retry is asserted through `transientReplaceCodes("win32")` and injected errnos rather than observed on Windows.

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…HEAD`: 10 files, `+454/−26`. No existing assertion is relaxed.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: writing session run state no longer fails with a bare `EPERM` when another process briefly holds the target file (Windows AV scanners and indexers, SMB/NFS clients), and neither does the deletion journal; a persistent failure now surfaces as a classified `FileReplaceError` that names the destination, the errno and the attempt count instead of a raw `fs` error. A state write that still fails after the retries is logged as `run_scheduler_failed` instead of terminating the API process, and the affected run is recovered as `interrupted` on the next start.
Compatibility and migration: none.

items.body:
Fixes #879

## What the user sees

The desktop attachment tray prints a file of `1_048_575` bytes (1 MiB − 1) as **`1024KB`**, and `1_073_741_823` bytes (1 GiB − 1) as **`1024MB`**; the upload limit line prints the same boundary as **`1024 MiB`**. The unit was chosen from the *unrounded* value (`1023.999 KB` stops the ladder at KB) while the printed number was `Math.round(value)`, which rounds to `1024` — a number no KB value can hold.

## Change

- New `apps/desktop/src/app/size-units.ts` with one promotion ladder shared by both formatters. It promotes while the value the caller would **print** still reaches the base, so the unit choice and the printed number cannot disagree.
- `formatFileSize` (`attachments.ts`) and `formatByteLimit` (`upload.ts`) keep their own rounding policy — one decimal below a hundred units / whole numbers above it for the card, integer-or-one-decimal for a limit — and only the unit selection changes.
- Existing readings are unchanged: `0KB`, `512B`, `1KB`, `5.5KB`, `16.5KB`, `256KB`, `1MB`, `5MB`, `999 B`, `1 KiB`, `1 GiB`.

Readings after the fix: `1_048_575 → 1MB`, `1_073_741_823 → 1GB`, limit `1_073_741_823 → 1 GiB`.

## Red first (`#879` on `89cd2d30`)

```
not ok 1 - an attachment one byte under 1 MiB prints 1MB, not 1024KB
  expected: '1MB'
  actual:   '1024KB'
not ok 2 - an attachment one byte under 1 GiB prints 1GB, not 1024MB
  expected: '1GB'
  actual:   '1024MB'
not ok 3 - an upload limit one byte under 1 GiB prints 1 GiB, not 1024 MiB
  expected: '1 GiB'
  actual:   '1024 MiB'
# tests 4
# pass 1
# fail 3
```

The passing test is the "sizes that already read well" guard.

## After the fix

```
# tests 11
# pass 11
# fail 0
```

## Gates (at tip `2d40ed35`, exact commands)

```
pnpm --recursive typecheck                          -> exit 0
tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json                          -> exit 0
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck    -> exit 0
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test        -> exit 0  (# tests 729 / # pass 729 / # fail 0)
CI_E2E_PREPARED=1 pnpm ci:l1                        -> exit 0  (PASS 4/4)
app-test probe (tsc over apps/desktop/tests, `types: ["vite/client","node"]`) -> exit 0
```

## Diff (vs `89cd2d30`)

```
 apps/desktop/src/app/attachments.ts        |  6 +− 9
 apps/desktop/src/app/size-units.ts         | 36 +− 0
 apps/desktop/src/app/upload.ts             |  6 +− 8
 apps/desktop/src/views/SetupWizard.tsx     | 18 +− 7
 apps/desktop/src/views/WorkspacePanel.tsx  | 12 +− 5
 apps/desktop/tests/size-boundary.test.ts   | 98 +− 0
 6 files changed, 176 insertions(+), 29 deletions(-)
```

## Review round (`1ef302b9` → `67ab0fcb`)

Two points from the review, and the extra surfaces it asked about:

1. **The two ladders are deliberately separate.** `apps/web/src/formatBytes.ts` and `apps/desktop/src/app/size-units.ts` are independent products of the same rule living in two applications that share no code; the desktop app does not import from `apps/web`. They are not meant to be merged, and a future change to the rule has to touch both on purpose.
2. **Other desktop surfaces that print a byte size.** Searching the desktop app found two more, and both had the same boundary bug, so they now share `scaledSize` instead of their own ladder:
   - `views/SetupWizard.tsx` — the free-space line on the setup screen printed `1024MB` one byte under a GiB (`formatWizardFreeSpace`, now `scaledSize` with the shell's KB/MB/GB convention and whole megabytes);
   - `views/WorkspacePanel.tsx` — workspace file rows printed `1024.0 KiB` (`formatWorkspaceSize`, now `scaledSize` with binary units and one decimal).
   Their readings are pinned in the same test file.

## Second review round (`67ab0fcb` → `2d40ed35`): the promotion band

The review found one more spot of the same class, one level down from the exact
unit: `formatWizardFreeSpace` picked the unit from the value at **one decimal**
(`Number(value.toFixed(1))`) while KB and MB are **printed** as whole numbers.
So the band just under a unit — where one decimal still reads `1023.x` and the
printed number rounds to `1024` — stayed in its level:

```
1_073_600_000 -> "1024MB"   (1023.86 MB; 1_073_217_536 … 1_073_689_395)
1_048_064     -> "1024KB"   (1023.5 KB;  1_048_064 … 1_048_524)
```

The existing cases did not catch it because `1_048_575` and `1_073_741_823` are
`1024.0` at one decimal, so they promoted for the wrong reason.

Fix: `scaledSize` now asks the caller for the number **that level** prints
(`round(value, unit)`), and the wizard's `printed` helper is the same function
that formats the output — whole KB and MB, one decimal GB. The unit can then
never disagree with the printed number at any level. `attachments.ts`,
`upload.ts` and `WorkspacePanel.tsx` pass one-argument formatters and are
unchanged by this, because for them print and promotion were already the same
function.

Red first at `67ab0fcb` (two new cases, same file):

```
not ok 9 - the wizard's free-space line promotes KB inside the band, where one decimal still reads 1023.5
  expected: '1MB'
  actual:   '1024KB'
not ok 10 - the wizard's free-space line promotes MB inside the band, where one decimal still reads 1023.8
  expected: '1.0GB'
  actual:   '1024MB'
# tests 11
# pass 9
# fail 2
```

Green at `2d40ed35`: `1_073_600_000 → 1.0GB`, `1_048_064 → 1MB`, and the
neighbours that already read `1023` keep it (`1_073_217_535 → 1023MB`,
`1_048_063 → 1023KB`). `11/11`.

## Screenshot re-check on this tip

The four images in the evidence comment (`6637901377`) were taken before this
round. This round changed `scaledSize`'s promotion rule and the wizard's
free-space line, not `formatFileSize` or `formatByteLimit`, so the same desktop
harness was re-run on `2d40ed35` to read the tray again rather than assume it:

```text
$ SHOT_DIR=$PWD/.local/shots PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=$HOME/.cache/ms-playwright \\
    apps/desktop/e2e/node_modules/.bin/playwright test \\
    --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts zz-880-verify.spec.ts --reporter=list
[zh-CN] tray readings: ["BIN 1MB","BIN 1GB"]
[zh-CN] attach tooltip: 放进本次会话的工作区，智能体就能读到。单个文件最大 1 GiB。也可以直接把文件拖进界面。
[en] tray readings: ["BIN 1MB","BIN 1GB"]
[en] attach tooltip: Files go into this session's workspace, where the agent can read them. A single file may be up to 1 GiB. You can also drag files onto the window.
  2 passed (4.5s)
```

The two files were chosen through the composer's own button, as the real
`1_048_575`-byte and `1_073_741_823`-byte files: the cards read `1MB` and `1GB`
in both languages, and the attach button's tooltip states the `1 GiB` limit
(`单个文件最大 1 GiB` / `A single file may be up to 1 GiB`). The readings are the
tip's own, so the four images stay as they are — no re-shoot.

## Two polish items left in this tip (recorded, not changed)

The review at `67ab0fcb` raised no blocking finding and two small ones. Both are
kept out of the tip deliberately — a new commit would only re-open a review that
already says it has nothing to block — and they are written down here so they do
not live only in a thread:

1. **A third copy of the unit table** (`apps/desktop/src/views/WorkspacePanel.tsx`,
   `WORKSPACE_SIZE_UNITS`). It is the same `B/KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB` list as
   `attachments.ts` and `upload.ts`, all three consumed by `scaledSize`, so the
   *unit choice* cannot fork; only the print step's spacing and letter case are
   local. Moving the table into `apps/desktop/src/app/size-units.ts` (as
   `export const SIZE_UNITS`) is the right cleanup, and it is the one change that
   would have to touch all four call sites at once — a follow-up rather than a
   patch on a reviewed tip.
2. **Imports at the bottom of `apps/desktop/tests/size-boundary.test.ts`.** The
   two new view imports sit below the first tests; ESM hoists them so the file
   runs (9/9), but a reader meets the dependency after the assertions.

Neither changes a rendered string, a unit, or a test result. If a tracked ticket
is wanted for the pair, say so on the thread and I will open one; the code they
describe ships with this pull request, so they are recorded here in the meantime.

## Scope note

items.body:
Fixes #866

## What this fixes

`sanitizeUploadFilename()` in `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts` guarded an empty name, a NUL byte, absolute paths, drive letters and traversal, but not Windows reserved device names. On a Windows workspace `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`, `LPT1`–`LPT9`, `CONIN$` and `CONOUT$` resolve in every directory and with any extension, so `con.csv`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log` passed the guard and failed later inside the workspace write with a raw `EPERM`/`ENOENT` that the upload response reports as an unclassified error (`CON` targets the console device instead of failing).

The fix rejects them with the same `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` code and error shape the other guard branches use, names the offending file in the message, and strips trailing dots/spaces first because Windows ignores them (`nul.`, `CON .csv`). Legal stems that only begin with a reserved word (`conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `auxiliary.csv`) and two-digit ports (`com10.csv`) keep working — the same test asserts both directions.

The guard is platform-independent on purpose, so Linux and macOS reject these names too: portability — an upload must be writable on every supported host, and a file accepted on Linux but unusable on a Windows workspace would only fail later there.

## Red → green

The test was written first and fails on `main` `8708320f`:

```
not ok 2 - sanitizeUploadFilename rejects Windows reserved device names
  error: 'Missing expected exception: CON must be rejected as a Windows reserved device name'
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
# tests 16
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

After the fix: `node --import tsx --test src/workspace-upload.test.ts` → `# tests 16 / # pass 16 / # fail 0`.

Commits keep the pairing: `96b34e1d` test (red), `a2cebfbc` fix.

## Must-fix from review: the refused name now answers 400, not 500

`agent-ci-infra-bot` found the gap: `sanitizeUploadFilename` rejects the new names with `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH`, but the request handler decides 400-vs-500 **by message** (`isKnownClientInputError`, `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:20-32`), and the new message names none of the seven classified patterns. So the exact scenario this PR exists for — uploading `CON.csv` — answered `500 Internal server error` instead of naming the file.

Fixed on the same branch, tip `1a7b1b997bfe5e23af38d3abab59893a33e32ddd`, in two commits:

- `c0173957` (test, red first): a **route-level** test in `services/api/src/server.test.ts` (`WSP-004`) that uploads `CON.csv` through the real HTTP surface and asserts the status, the file name in the body, and that the workspace stayed empty. Before the fix: `500 !== 400`.
- `1a7b1b99` (fix): `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` joins the handler's existing stable-code branches (`services/api/src/http/index.ts`, one line beside `SKILL_LIBRARY_VALIDATION`), so the 400 follows the **code** rather than the prose a later wording edit could change. Every branch of the guard is tagged with that code, so this covers the whole family, not just the reserved-name message — no regex added, and no message reworded to please a pattern.

One consideration on where it went: the reviewer's finding points at the message classifier, and adding a ninth prose pattern there would have worked for this message only. The code branch is the smaller and more durable of the two, and it does not loosen any other 400/500 decision.

`services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` is unchanged and still 16/16 — the function-level contract this PR added is untouched; what changed is the status a client sees.

## Second finding from the same review: the stream syntax (same guard, not a new rule)

The device-name guard took its stem up to the first `.` and never looked at `:`, so `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA` were accepted while `nul.txt` was refused. Windows resolves both to the device in every directory, so that was the same reservation under another spelling:

```
"CON.csv"      -> rejected
"nul.txt"      -> rejected
"NUL. "        -> rejected
"nul:stream"   -> accepted before this commit
"con:$DATA"    -> accepted before this commit
"report:2024.csv" -> accepted before and after
```

Fixed as the **sixth branch of the same predicate**, not as a character rule: `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` now takes its stem before the colon as well as before the dot, and refuses only when that part names a device. A colon in front of an ordinary stem is a legal file name on Linux and macOS, so `report:2024.csv` and `data:2024.tsv` keep passing unchanged — refusing every `:` would have traded this bug for a portability one.

Red first, `services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` on `1a7b1b99`:

```
not ok 1 - sanitizeUploadFilename rejects the stream syntax of a Windows reserved device name
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
    +   'accepted',
    +   'accepted'
    -   'rejected',
    -   'rejected'
      ]
```

The same test carries the over-rejection guard (`assert.equal(sanitizeUploadFilename("report:2024.csv"), "report:2024.csv")`), which was green before the fix and stays green after it. After: `# tests 18 / # pass 18 / # fail 0` across `workspace-upload.test.ts` and `error-classification.test.ts`.

Nothing outside `sanitizeUploadFilename` had to change for this — the handler branch from the first finding already answers 400 for the code — so this stays one pull request rather than becoming a second one against #866.

## Ran / Not run

Ran (exit codes verbatim):

1. `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → **0**
2. `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → **0**
3. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/workspace-upload.test.ts` → **0** (`16/16` pass)
4. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/*.test.ts` → **1**, `680 tests / 677 pass / 3 fail`; the 3 failures are all `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'reportlab'` from `services/paper/.venv/bin/python` (`papers.test.ts` PDF fixtures) — environment, not this diff, and they fail the same way on `main` in this sandbox.
5. `pnpm architecture:check` (this repo has no lint script, so the architecture gate is the substitute) → **1**, one failure `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`, `error: Could not create temporary file / Read-only file system (os error 30) at path "/home/xuke/.cache/uv/.tmp…"` — the sandbox blocks `uv`, unrelated to this diff.

Not run: the ST layer (E2E/standard journeys) locally; CI runs it.

Gates on the final tip `fdf840a8f18e6ce7ec912ba30b20e3336e0bcdc9`:

6. `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → **0**
7. `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → **0**
8. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts src/workspace-upload.test.ts` → **0** (`18/18`, including the two stream-syntax refusals and the `report:2024.csv` accept)
9. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-004 src/server.test.ts` → **0** (`1/1`; on `a2cebfbc` the same test is `500 !== 400`)

Not run: the whole `services/api` suite (its three `reportlab`-missing failures are the sandbox baseline in point 4, unchanged), and the `services/runner` NPU test whose worker crash is a CI environment baseline — this diff does not touch either.

## The L2 red on this tip: `standard-journeys`, one journey, not the upload path

CI run `41885511550` (job `126770786423`, `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)`)
is red on this tip: `planned 60 / executed 60 / passed 59 / failed 1`. The one
failure is

```text
test/issue-85-foreground-exec-inbox.spec.ts:299 ›
  已完成的助手仍会被它没看过的后台结果唤醒，且不改道给主 Agent
step 2, at :355
Error: the wake should be delivered to the SubAgent
Expected pattern: /^subagent:/
Received string:  ""
Timeout 60000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate
```

What the job's own artifacts say (downloaded from that run, not inferred):

- `journey-report.md`: step 1 passed in 9.7 s. Step 2 is a 60 s `expect.poll`
  for a run with `automaticWake && status === "completed"` whose
  `notificationDelivery.agentId` starts with `subagent:`; it never saw one, so it
  reported `""`. The step's own log line is `无 console 错误/警告，无失败请求`
  ("no console errors/warnings, no failed requests"), and the failure snapshot
  shows the Session with its SubAgent card still present.
- The same shard, same stack, same run: the main-Agent wake journey
  `issue-77-wake-notice` passed in 11.2 s, and the two sibling
  `issue-85-foreground-exec-inbox` journeys passed (24.6 s, 14.7 s). So the mocked
  stack and the wake dispatch were working in that very run.
- The same spec on `#856` (run `41873712399`) and `#888` (run `41883672913`) is
  success on the same `standard-journeys` slice.

So the failure is **not** "the wake went to the main Agent" — nothing was
delivered to the main Agent, the wake did not start inside the test's 60 s
bound. This diff touches `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts`,
`services/api/src/http/index.ts` and two test files; it does not touch the wake
dispatcher, the SubAgent continuation or the frontend. Recorded as an
environmental flake of that journey, not repaired here: no code in this pull
request is changed for it and the tip is unchanged.

Local reproduction was attempted and is **not** claimed as run. The prepared
mocked slice falls back to a root `pnpm install` on this workstation, and the
sandbox refuses it — a modules purge it cannot confirm
(`ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY`), and with the store pinned back to
the populated one, `EROFS` when pnpm registers the project in a read-only store.
The stack itself came up (adapter, API, runner, JiuwenSwarm instance healthy)
before that step. So there are no local pass/fail readings for this journey from
this machine; the evidence above is the CI run's own artifacts and the same
slice's results on other tips.

## Third review round (`fdf840a8` → `40fabb65`): superscript port digits

The naming document lists superscript ¹ ² ³ as port digits, so `COM¹.txt` names the first
serial port in every directory exactly like `COM1.txt`. The class was ASCII-only, so those
spellings were accepted here and failed later at write time, like the bug this PR fixes.

Red on `fdf840a8` — the case added in `535fdc86` against the unchanged sanitizer:

```
not ok 2 - sanitizeUploadFilename rejects Windows reserved device names
  error: 'Missing expected exception: COM¹.txt must be rejected as a Windows reserved device name'
# tests 17 / # pass 16 / # fail 1
```

and the same three spellings through that sanitizer: `COM¹.txt accepted`, `com².csv
accepted`, `LPT³.log accepted`.

Green on `40fabb65` — `com[1-9¹²³]` / `lpt[1-9¹²³]`, and the same probe:

```
COM¹.txt rejected    com².csv rejected    LPT³.log rejected
COM10.csv accepted   nul:stream rejected  report:2024.csv accepted
# tests 17 / # pass 17 / # fail 0
```

The neighbours are unchanged: `com10.csv` stays accepted (a two-digit port is not
COM<n>), `report:2024.csv` stays accepted (a colon is legal on Linux and macOS),
`nul:stream` stays rejected.

Gates on `40fabb65`:

```
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck   -> clean
npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json                  -> exit 0
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test        -> 1864 pass / 4 fail
```

The four failures are `spawn …/services/paper/.venv/bin/python ENOENT` in
`papers.test.ts` and `idea-tree/research-entry.test.ts`: the paper service venv is absent
on this workstation, and neither file is touched by this diff. Not run: L1/L2/E2E — the
change is a two-character-class edit in the name check, and this branch's journeys do not
upload a device name.

## Diffstat

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…HEAD` (base `main` `89cd2d30`):

```
 services/api/src/http/index.ts            |  5 ++++
 services/api/src/server.test.ts           | 42 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts | 48 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts      | 34 +++++++++++++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 129 insertions(+)
```


## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: on Windows, uploading a file named after a reserved device (`CON.csv`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, `conin$.txt`, `nul.`) is rejected up front with `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` naming the file, instead of failing with a bare `EPERM` at write time (and, for `CON`, writing to the console device); ordinary names such as `conifer.csv` and `console.log` are still accepted.
Compatibility and migration: none — names that previously reached the filesystem unchanged are unaffected; only names Windows itself cannot write are now refused earlier.

Fixes #877

## What this fixes

Four routes in the same family read one artifact id. `content` (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3353`) asks `store.getArtifactVersion()` first and answers 404; `provenance` and `diff` called `artifactVersionProvenance()` / `artifactVersionDiff()`, which throw a bare `new Error("Artifact version not found")` (`services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:169` and `:349`). The top-level mapper only turns `Project|Session|Proxy server|Provider|Model not found`, `Execution|Transfer|Timer|Subagent not found: …` and a few codes into 404, so both fell through to the 500 branch — and wrote an `unclassified_request_error` log for what is simply a stale version id.

Now both routes check the version before calling the helper, exactly like `content`, and answer `404 {"error":"Artifact version not found"}`.

The same defect exists one level up, on both versions *list* routes: `/api/projects/:p/artifacts/:a/versions` and its Session-scoped sibling pass the id straight to `store.listProjectArtifactVersions()`, which throws a bare `Error("Artifact not found")` — again a 500 plus an `unclassified_request_error`. Both now check the project/Session and the artifact first and answer `404` naming what is missing (`Project not found: …` / `Artifact not found`); the success path is untouched.

`diff` keeps its two comparison-base cases apart, per the issue's expected shape:

- `?against=<id>` given but not found → **404** (a requested resource is missing);
- `?against` absent and the previous version does not exist → **400** `A previous artifact version is unavailable for comparison` (the request asks for a diff this artifact cannot have yet, which is a client-side input problem, not a missing `to` version).

The helpers are unchanged, so their defensive throws still hold for any caller that skips the route.

## Red → green

Red first (`6864420d`, test only), `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-missing.test.ts`:

```
content:    { status: 404, error: 'Artifact version not found' }
provenance: { status: 500, error: 'Internal server error' }
diff:       { status: 500, error: 'Internal server error' }
projects/:p/artifacts/:a/versions: { status: 500, error: 'Internal server error' }
# tests 1 / # pass 0 / # fail 1
```

Green after the fixes (`f67b91e9` for the version routes, `3c21ad91` for the list routes): same command → `1/1 pass`; `provenance.test.ts` + `dashboard.test.ts` → `86/86 pass`.

The test drives a real `createApiServer` (`offlineMcpTransport`, no runner) against a freshly created project/session, then asks all three version routes for the same random version id and compares status **and** error body, so a future 500 with a different message cannot pass quietly. It then asks the project-scoped list route for a random artifact id, the Session-scoped one, and a route with a random project id, each expecting 404.

## Ran / Not run

Ran (exit codes verbatim):

1. `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → **0**
2. `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → **0**
3. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-missing.test.ts` → **0** (`1/1`)
4. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/provenance.test.ts src/dashboard.test.ts` → **0** (`86/86`)
5. `pnpm architecture:check` (no lint script in this repo) → **1**, one failure `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`: sandbox `uv` cannot create a temp file (`Read-only file system (os error 30)`), unrelated to this diff.

Not run: the `?against=` 404 and the missing-previous 400 branches have no version fixture in this harness (creating an artifact version needs an execution), so the test pins the sibling-404 case the issue measured; the two `diff` branches are covered by the code path and stated above. The ST/E2E layer runs in CI.

## Diffstat

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…HEAD`:

```
 services/api/src/artifact-version-missing.test.ts | 78 +++++++++++++++++++++++
 services/api/src/http/index.ts                    | 41 +++++++++++--
 2 files changed, 112 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)
```


## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: asking for the provenance, the diff, or the version list of an artifact or artifact version that does not exist (an expired link, a version removed by retention, a diff pointing at a deleted version) now answers `404` with the reason instead of `500 Internal server error`; the artifact dialog can say the version is gone instead of failing, and the server no longer logs a false `unclassified_request_error`.
Compatibility and migration: none — existing `200` responses and the sibling `content` route's `404` are unchanged.

items.body:
Fixes #862

## What this fixes

`SessionStore.writeArray()` published state through a `.state-<pid>-<uuid>.tmp` file and ran its cleanup in `finally` without a guard:

```ts
} finally {
  await rm(temporaryPath, { force: true });
}
```

When `rename` was refused (on Windows an antivirus scanner, search indexer or backup agent holds the freshly written file, so `MoveFileEx` returns `EPERM`) and the `rm` was refused for the same reason, the `finally` threw the bare cleanup `EPERM` and **replaced** the error that explains the loss. The caller then saw an unclassified `EPERM` on a `.tmp` path instead of the classified replace failure, so nothing could tell a locked file apart from a full disk.

The fix swallows the cleanup failure (`.catch(() => undefined)`); the replace error is the one that says what was lost.

## Red → green

| | |
|---|---|
| **Red** `88e6aa07` | `node --import tsx --test src/store-replace-cleanup.test.ts` → `2 tests / 1 pass / 1 fail`; failing assertion `the cleanup failure must not replace the replace error` (the surfaced error is the mocked `rm` EPERM, the `rename` EPERM is gone) |
| **Green** `0bae8739` | same command → `2 tests / 2 pass / 0 fail` |
| **Review round** `09b4ccb7` | adds the `attempts === 20` / `cause.code` assertions (inert before #857, live after) — same command → `2/2` |

The Security review's anti-forgery assertions are in `09b4ccb7`: when the surfaced error is a `FileReplaceError` (the classified shape #857 introduces on `main`), the test pins `attempts === 20` and `cause.code === "EPERM"`. On this base `writeArray` still calls plain `rename`, so that branch is inert here and becomes live the moment #857 lands — no follow-up tip is needed for it.

The two tests are split (per the Security review): **A** asserts the caller still sees the replace failure when both `rename` and the cleanup `rm` report `EPERM` (it accepts either the raw replace error before #857 or a `FileReplaceError` whose `cause` is it — the check reads `error.cause?.message` too); **B** asserts a failing replace still removes its temporary file, so no `.tmp` is left behind.

Both mocks use `syncBuiltinESMExports()` because `store.ts` imports `rename`/`rm` as named ESM bindings, and both only touch paths whose `basename` starts with `.state-` — the store's own temporary files — so no other write in the fixture is affected. The mock hands control back to the host after the test (`active` flag plus restore) so the next test is not affected by the still-bound ESM export.

## Ran / Not run

Ran (exit codes verbatim):

1. `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → **0**
2. `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → **0**
3. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/store-replace-cleanup.test.ts` → **0** (`2/2`)
4. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/store.test.ts` → **0** (`121/121`, no regression in the existing store suite)

Not run: the full `services/api` suite and the ST layer locally for this revision; CI runs both.

## Diffstat

`git diff --stat main…HEAD`:

```
 services/api/src/store-replace-cleanup.test.ts | 111 +++++++++++++++++++++++++
 services/api/src/store.ts                      |   5 +-
 2 files changed, 115 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```


## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: when the temporary-file cleanup fails for the same reason the replace did (a Windows antivirus scanner or indexer holding the file), the caller now still receives the classified replace failure — with its errno and attempt count — instead of a bare `EPERM` from the cleanup.
Compatibility and migration: none — the cleanup still runs and still removes the temporary file; only its own failure stops overriding the error that caused it.

Fixes #858

The usage page header announced **every model ever recorded** while the token total beside it and the model list below it were narrowed by the selected dates. With `from=to=2026-08-04`, where all usage that day came from one model, the page read `30 tokens across 2 models` — a count that contradicts both the sentence's own token total and the single-row list underneath. A range that keeps no usage was worse: the header paired `0 tokens across N models` with a body that already says the view is empty.

## What changed

- The subtitle counts `filteredModelGroups.length` — the same date-scoped, model-filtered collection the list below renders — instead of falling back to `summary.byModel.length` (all time) whenever only dates are selected.
- One model reads `… across 1 model` through a new `usage.subtitleOne` key, so the singular sentence stays grammatical; existing keys keep their meaning.
- A range that keeps no usage returns a dedicated `usage.subtitleFilteredEmpty` (`No usage in the selected range`) instead of a zero-token sentence plus a model count, which matches the body's existing `usage.filteredEmpty*` state rather than restating it.

## Validation

Red first, on `89cd2d30`:
- `apps/web/tests/UsagePage.test.tsx` — `# tests 4 / # pass 3 / # fail 1`; `not ok 2 - USG-012 usage page renders model drilldown, chart and inline/table usage` because the header rendered `30 tokens across 2 models` while one model has usage on 2026-08-04; the empty-range case also rendered `0 tokens across …`.
- After the fix: `# tests 4 / # pass 4 / # fail 0`.

Gates at tip `dd33ea3490db70b16bf160c966b13ae775801639`:
- `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → exit 0
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → exit 0
- `pnpm ci:l1` → exit 0, `{"status":"PASS","planned":4,"executed":4,"passed":4,"failed":0,"skipped":0}`. Run with `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1`: the L1 runner's own prepare step shells out to `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which cannot run on this host because its pnpm store is read-only (`EROFS`); the four L1 checks themselves ran.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` → exit 0, `# tests 1215 / # pass 1215 / # fail 0`
- ST: not applicable — no case in the frozen ST plan covers the usage page (51 entries, none for usage rendering); this change has no server path.

Diffstat against `89cd2d30`: 3 files `+40/−3` (`UsagePage.tsx +11/−3`, `messages.ts +4`, `UsagePage.test.tsx +25`).

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED: no browser journey was run against a materialised stack for this change. The web UT reproduces the header/body mismatch through the real `UsagePage` component using the page's own fixtures (two models, dates 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-04, `overview.totalTokens` 30 for the filtered day).

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: the usage-page header now names the same date-scoped models as the token total and the model list it summarizes, and says the selected range holds no usage instead of showing `0 tokens across N models`.
Compatibility and migration: none.

items.body:
The nightly research and BioMnibench runs need a consistent model configuration and more resilient handling of transient model failures. This change uses the `nightly-research` environment, preserves requested DeepSeek reasoning settings through session configuration, and retries interrupted model turns only before answer text or tool calls are emitted.

## Nightly model configuration

- Configure real-model generators and the BioMnibench judge for DeepSeek thinking enabled at low effort by default; environment variables can override the API variant and thinking settings.
- Preserve explicitly requested DeepSeek thinking effort in model and session settings; default to high when no effort is supplied.
- Read the configured API variant consistently in all six real-model journeys and validate Biomni's persisted thinking snapshot against the controls supported by that variant.

## Reliability

- Recover transient mutation errors within a shared deadline.
- Retry interrupted reasoning-only model streams within the shared request retry budget, buffering reasoning so discarded attempts are not sent to callers.
- Improve network permission tool guidance and cover the model, gateway, evolution and BioMnibench changes with focused tests.

## Validation

- Current head: `fa34928`.
- `pnpm --filter "@sciencediscovery/schema..." build` passed.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/model test` passed (7 test files).
- `pnpm typecheck` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Real-model E2E, including the previously reported L3-files journey and binary release x86_64 workflow, has not been rerun on this head; the previous run was not green and remains unresolved pending fresh CI evidence.

## E2E user journeys

The prior run's basic real-model journey did not settle the L3-files file-editing run within its 120-second wait. This PR does not claim that failure is resolved; a successful rerun is still required.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: explicitly configured DeepSeek thinking effort is retained, and some transient model stream failures can be retried before an answer or tool call is emitted.

Compatibility and migration: no migration required; nightly real-model jobs use `nightly-research`, which must contain their required model and data credentials.

Fixes #647

Owner: Dev1
Written-by: Dev-1
Branch: `dev1/fix/647-web-test-module-resolution`

## Problem

A clean tree cannot run the web test suite. Every workspace package publishes its runtime entry from `dist/` (`packages/*/package.json` → `"default": "./dist/*.js"`) and no `dist/` is committed, so a package-level run that does not build first resolves those imports to files that do not exist:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx
# tests 448
# pass 385
# fail 63
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/operational-logging/dist/diagnostics.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/ErrorDiagnosticActions.tsx
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../@sciencediscovery/schema/dist/index.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/Markdown.tsx
```

The repo's own `pnpm test` hides this because it runs `pnpm build` first; the per-package script (`tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`) does not. The 63 victims are not defects — they fail at import time, before any assertion runs.

The failure is not specific to `operational-logging`: `schema`, `skill`, `plugin-sdk` and their transitive workspace dependencies fail the same way.

## Commits (red first)

1. `test(web): prove the suite dies when the workspace packages are unbuilt` — one test asserting that every `@sciencediscovery/*` entry the web app imports resolves to a file that exists. Red on the unbuilt tree:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts
not ok 1 - every workspace package the web app imports resolves from its built entry
  error: '@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/manifest resolves to
   .../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/dist/manifest.js,
   which does not exist; the workspace packages need building first'
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

Full suite on the same tree: **449 tests / 385 pass / 64 fail** (63 pre-existing + this one).

2. `fix(web): build the workspace packages the test suite imports` — `apps/web`'s `test` script now runs `scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs .` before `tsx --test`. The script walks `apps/web`'s workspace dependencies transitively and builds only the packages whose `dist/` is missing, using the repo's `typescript` and each package's own `tsconfig.json` — exactly what `pnpm build` would produce. It is a no-op once they are built, so the CI path that already ran `pnpm build` pays one directory listing and nothing else.

No test file is modified, and production resolution is untouched: the runtime entry stays `dist/`, which `node dist/server.js` and vite both need.

3. `test(scripts): pin the ensure-workspace-dist skip and build order` — the builder had no test of its own behaviour. Two cases run against a throwaway workspace (a copy of the script, fixture packages, and a stand-in `tsc` that records where it was pointed and writes the `dist/` the compiler would emit, so no TypeScript build is paid for):

- a package without `dist/` is built, a package that already has `dist/` is not rebuilt (its `dist/` is left untouched), and a second run of the script is silent;
- a package is built only after everything it depends on (`leaf` → `middle` → `top`, plus an unrelated sibling, built in that order).

Both cases are green as written. Their red side is a mutation, checked locally on the working tree and not committed: dropping the `dist/` skip fails the first case (`a second run must not rebuild a built package`), and moving `ordered.push(dep)` before the dependency visit fails the second.

## Verification

Red (clean tree, before the fix) → green:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # no dist/
# tests 449   # pass 385   # fail 64
$ node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web
built workspace packages without dist: @sciencediscovery/operational-logging,
@sciencediscovery/external-urls, @sciencediscovery/schema, @sciencediscovery/cas, …
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # deps built
# tests 1131   # pass 1131   # fail 0
```

The suite grows from 449 to 1131 because the files that could not load now run. Typechecks: `apps/web` `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0; repo `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` → 0. A second run of the builder prints nothing (idempotent).

## Labels and timing

`agent-ready` could not be applied to the issue by the team (the token gets 403 on label writes) and the owner's 60-minute deadline takes precedence over the usual 24-hour wait, so this is pushed ahead of the label being restored.

## Ran

- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts` → 0/1 before the fix, 1/1 after
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → 385/449 before, **1131/1131 after**
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (repo root) → 0
- `node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web` twice → 17 packages the first time, silent the second
- `node --test scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.test.mjs` → 2/2, and the same two cases fail under the two mutations above
- `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` → 70/71: the one failure is `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`, which shells out to `uv` and dies on the read-only `~/.cache/uv` on this host, unrelated to this change
- `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check` → `CI test catalog OK: 7 cases, 24 tags, 4 layers`

## Not run

- The shared tagged plan end to end (`node test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list`): on this tree it stops during collection with `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: apps/web/tests/markdown-math.test.ts:16`, a file this branch does not touch and which fails the same way alone at the base commit. The new file was collected on its own instead (`node-collect.mjs` → 2 cases, `category:ut`).
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` verbatim: on this host pnpm's dependency-status check aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` / `EROFS` on the pnpm store (outside the workspace, read-only), so the script's two commands were run directly, in order.

Release: fix

## Summary

Part of #835.

This is the first KE core slice proposed in #835. It introduces only the pure text, extraction, and entity-resolution domain of the Knowledge Engine; it does not register API routes, agent tools, UI, background jobs, or runtime settings.

### Included

- Text parsing and retrieval primitives, including JATS, LaTeX, document levels, trigram/search, and citation helpers.
- LLM extraction schemas/prompts and the provenance gate requiring document anchors for extracted knowledge.
- Entity normalization, matching, merge policy, offline resolution, and sample evaluation data.
- Independent-review hardening for single-line display math, relevance-ordered FTS over-fetch, repeated citation anchors on one line, JATS formula alternatives, optional LaTeX macro defaults, and token-safe entity endpoint matching.
- Additional bot-review hardening: bounded worker-based regex execution, Unicode entity screening, LaTeX preamble removal, multiword/CJK entity and novelty matching, and grouped JATS citation IDs.
- CodeCheck cleanup for loop style and redundant non-null assertions, without changing test expectations.
- Follow-up review hardening: grep input is capped before worker cloning, worker startup and regex execution have separate deadlines, and large-corpus hits survive with honest scan truncation. The provenance fallback now requires ordered token evidence (including single-character entity tokens), rejecting word-permuted or semantically inverted quotes.
- Package-local unit tests and the package/lockfile wiring needed to build `@sciencediscovery/knowledge-engine`.

### Explicitly excluded

- Graph, growth, and evaluation orchestration modules.
- SQLite/API services, connectors, PDF workers, agent integration, and Web UI.
- `pairs.realworld.json` and other large/local fixtures.
- qa/, .tmp/, credentials, and local development artifacts.

The package index exports only modules present in this stage. Four graph-dependent resolution tests from the full reference implementation remain for the graph stage; no production module was stubbed to hide that dependency.

## Validation

- Windows package build: passed.
- Windows package typecheck: passed.
- Fresh native WSL clone of this branch:
  - package build: passed;
  - package typecheck: passed;
  - **139 tests passed, 0 failed**, including all independent-review and bot-review regressions;
  - the catastrophic-backtracking regression completes in about 101 ms, bounded by the worker deadline;
  - architecture boundary check: passed across 364 package source files.
- Windows package build/typecheck: passed.
- Root test-source typecheck (`tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`): passed.
- Windows architecture script checks: **38/38 passed**.
- Final independent review of the grep and provenance rework: **all-clear**, including race/timeout probes and 25 repeated search-suite runs without a flake.
- GitCode CodeCheck on head `12d6b273`: **passed** (`success`, 0 annotations).
- The full WSL architecture script run was **98/99**: the unrelated RACE case failed while cloning its external evaluator (`fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect` / `fatal: early EOF`); no B1 file participates in that path.

# 学科知识引擎：摄取/生长/消解/消费全链 + 会话绑库与反幻觉运行时

> 与 GitCode MR [!125](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/125) 内容一致（对应 GitCode issue #86）。

把「学科知识」做成 SD 的一等资产：文献与结构化源摄取为带锚点溯源的知识图谱，图谱可离线生长、实体消解、社区聚类；对话内绑定知识库（kb scope）后，图谱成为受约束的知识来源，输出必须引用锚点，与证据账本 / 新颖性检查 / 引用核验构成多层反幻觉链路。

**283 文件，+50.8k，4 个按路径分组的 commit**（KE 核心 / agent 运行时 / Web / 技能与测试）。

---

## 新增功能

### 1. 知识引擎核心（`packages/knowledge-engine` + `services/api/src/knowledge-engine`）

- **存储域**：SQLite（知识库/文档/锚点/实体/边/社区/合并/作业/引用/公式），带迁移机制；算法核与存储分离，可独立评测
- **摄取**：LaTeX-first arXiv 通路（tar.gz 解包 + `\input` 递归内联）、JATS XML、视觉增强 PDF 解析；溯源门抽取——每个抽取结论挂文档锚点
- **生长**：离线 grow job，MMR + anchor-aware 多样本选择、收敛信号、结构化反思 directive 反哺下一轮
- **实体消解**：在线门 + 离线 job、物理合并与回滚（`ke_entity_merges`）、louvain 社区、根实体、社区报告
- **消费面**：`kb_search` / `kb_expand` / `doc_grep` 工具、entity_unified_search、三级文档阅读器（全文/结构/锚点）、引用 API（意图徽章 supporting / contrasting / mentioning + Similar / References / Cited-By）
- **REST**：`/api/ke/*` 全套 + 前端知识引擎页（cytoscape 图谱画布、生长控制面板、阅读器、引用面板）

### 2. 会话绑库（kb scope）

- session 设置新增 `kbScopeKbIds` / `kbScopeWebSearch` 运行时覆盖项；composer 底部选择器一键绑定/解绑，写路径为 fresh-GET 读改写，避免并发选择器互相回滚
- resident-summary 上下文贡献者持续注入**在库**图谱摘要（成熟度分级）；范围外知识库对工具面与摘要均不可见（防泄漏包装）
- 系统 prompt m8.3.1：上下文时钟、kb-scope 自管理指引、反编造纪律句——均在既有 5000 字符保护段预算内

### 3. 反幻觉与研究运行时

- 三级注入：证据账本（`evidence_ledger`）、新颖性检查（`novelty_check`）、引用核验（`verify_citation`）；KE 工具输出逐字文本打 nonce 不可信围栏
- finish-gate 收尾审计：技能声明 `metadata.pre-finish-audit` 即在收尾前注入审计 directive，有界续跑（≤2 次）
- 研究世界模型 `research_state`：目标钉住 / 计划生命周期 / 未决问题 / 已排除路径防复活 / 已试去重，JSON 文件锁崩溃可恢复
- 审批门计划生命周期（`packages/plan-mode`）：`propose_plan` / `revise_plan` 工具、约束级审批、版本绑定决策、决策日志；与上游 `update_plan` 快照机制共存（`AgentRunBindings` 同时携带 `planRepository` 与 `planStore`）
- stall-guard：模型调用无进展按空闲窗踢出重试（≤3 次），外层空闲看门狗兜底
- 记忆图谱镜像 `observeSessionPlan`；MCP 配置文件内容签名失效（保留上游按服务器签名比较，叠加文件级变更检测）

### 4. 技能包与评测

- 15 个方法论技能：knowledge-engine-explore/grow、evidence-notes、hypothesis-tournament、tree-search、robin-chain、virtual-lab、idea-debate、systematic-review、precise-qa、long-form-writing/audit、progressive-report、report-writer、table-analysis（多数声明 pre-finish-audit）
- 评测套件 `scripts/ke-*-eval.mjs`：growth delta-recall、discoverer 诚信维度、pairwise、citation（ALCE 三指标）、resolution、bench 539 题；`skill-test-runner` + ER 数据集构建器
- KE 旅程 E2E 9 条 + kb-scope / finish-gate 旅程，ke-stub 离线可跑

## 验证

Linux（Ubuntu WSL2），分支 `pr/knowledge-engine`（基于 upstream/main 最新 `ef65b6f`，4 个按路径分组的 commit）。

- 29 个 workspace 项目全量构建通过（含 web vite build）；`architecture:check` 通过（293 文件）
- 触及包测试全绿：workspace 119/119、context 50/50、tools 61/61、runtime-core 36/36、memory 35/35、schema 12/12、plan 5/5、plan-mode 2/2
- **services/api 全量套件 1020 tests / 1019 pass / 0 fail**（`node --test dist/*.test.js dist/**/*.test.js`，123s 干净退出）
- 与纯 upstream/main 对照树同环境跑 server.test.js 验证无回归：upstream 86/86，本分支 86/86；期间修复了三处合并引入的问题（MCP transport 双重 close、内置技能清单落位、保护段预算超限），并把 KE sqlite 连接补上服务器关闭回收（否则每个 boot 泄漏 db+wal+shm 句柄并在进程退出时挂起 drain）
- 双计划系统共存验证：propose_plan 审批门与 update_plan 快照在同 run 注册、互不干扰（context-assembly 集成测试覆盖）

Fixes #777

Owner: Dev2
Written-by: Dev-2
Tip SHA: 0bb3ee16884843a09d30278a63db007ba3f4da5d
Base: a429ba1d4eca17af8cfabb9f28abe9d651e38e6c (main at push; branch rebased onto it, no overlap)

`web_fetch`/`web_search` handed search-result titles and snippets to the model with named HTML references still encoded. Only `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot` and `nbsp` decoded, so a page title like `Café — a review` reached the prompt and the report verbatim, and the sources a science search cites most often (encyclopedias, European sites) are exactly the entity-heavy ones. This decodes every named reference a browser resolves, in the same single pass as before.

## What changed

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts`: the five-name map is replaced by the full WHATWG named character reference set — 2125 semicolon-terminated names — expanded into a `Map` once at module load. `nbsp` keeps its existing ordinary-space mapping; numeric references, the single-pass rule (`&lt;` → `<`) and unknown names (`&bogus;` stays literal) are unchanged. The decoding loop is the same one-scan replace it was; only the data changed shape and moved out of this module.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html-entities.ts` (new): the table itself — a `name;code point;…` constant, 246 folded lines — under a 37-line header that states the source (WHATWG named character references via CPython's `html.entities.html5`, 2231 keys of which the 2125 semicolon forms are what this pattern accepts), the retrieval date, the exact `python3` snippet that regenerates the body, and the licence position: the standard's table reproduced as factual data — names and code points any HTML parser needs — not copied from another project's source. `html.ts` keeps the decoder and goes from 79 lines to 90 (+11); 368 is only the shape this branch's previous commit had with the table inline, and this commit moves it out. The data is 246 of the new file's 284 lines.
- `tsconfig.base.json`: one line, `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`. The import in `html.ts` keeps a `.ts` extension so `node --experimental-strip-types` — the command the issue reproduces with — resolves the sibling source instead of failing with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; that option is what lets tsc accept the specifier and still emit `./html-entities.js` (verified: the built `dist/web/native/html.js` line is `import { NAMED_ENTITIES_PACKED } from "./html-entities.js";`). It belongs in the base config rather than the package one: the root tests config used by `pnpm typecheck` extends only `tsconfig.base.json`, and with the option in `packages/data-source/tsconfig.json` alone that check fails with `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts(73,39): error TS5097: An import path can only end with a '.ts' extension when 'allowImportingTsExtensions' is enabled.` From the base config both the package build and that check pass. It changes nothing else in the tree — the only `test/` file that `tsc` type-checks imports `.js` paths; the Playwright specs under `test/` are not in any tsconfig.
- `html-entities.ts` is force-added: `.gitignore`'s `data-*/` rule also matches the `packages/data-source/` directory (`git check-ignore -v` reports `.gitignore:91`). I left that rule alone to keep this PR single-purpose; say the word if you would rather have it anchored as `/data-*/` and I will open a separate issue.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts`: cases for the names in the issue (`eacute`, `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `apos`, `diams`, `rsquo`, `ldquo`/`rdquo`, Latin-1, symbols), case sensitivity, an unknown name, the single-pass rule after the table widened, and a guard that the exported table still has exactly 2125 entries plus one two-scalar value (`NotEqualTilde`), so a dropped or mis-chunked line cannot pass as a smaller table. The test file is unchanged by the move.

Size, whole PR: 4 files, 344 insertions, 8 deletions (`html-entities.ts` +284, `html.test.ts` +41/−1, `html.ts` +18/−7, `tsconfig.base.json` +1).

## Red first

Decoder tests. Command:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/web/native/html.test.ts
```

Before the fix:

```
# Subtest: decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
not ok 3 - decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
  expected: "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
  actual: 'café — 5–10 … O'Brien'
# Subtest: decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
not ok 4 - decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
  expected: 'Ää'
  actual: 'Ää'
# pass 5
# fail 2
```

Table guard. The guard lands in its own commit before the export exists, so it is red on the change that adds only the test:

```
# pass 0
# fail 1
SyntaxError: The requested module './html.js' does not provide an export named 'NAMED_ENTITIES'
```

and it fails the way it is meant to when one entry is dropped from the packed constant (mutation check, one `AElig;c6;` field removed, then restored):

```
not ok 8 - keeps every entry of the generated WHATWG table
  expected: 2125
  actual: 2124
# pass 7
# fail 1
```

Green after the implementation, same command as the decoder run: `# pass 8`, `# fail 0`. The package suite goes from 74 to 75 tests with the guard: `# tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0`.

## The issue's reproduction

Command from #777:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

On this tip:

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

The middle line is the single-pass guarantee: the decoded ampersand does not start a second scan.

## Gates

On this tip, in `packages/data-source` unless noted:

```
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json                                        # exit 0 (build)
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit                               # exit 0
$ node --experimental-strip-types -e 'import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(...)'
  café — 5–10 … O'Brien                                          # exit 0
$ npm test                                                        # # tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0
$ cd ../.. && node scripts/check-architecture.mjs                 # 333 source files, boundaries OK
$ cd ../.. && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json        # exit 0
$ cd ../.. && pnpm --recursive typecheck                          # 34 packages Done, exit 0
```

`pnpm architecture:check` is **98 passed / 1 failed** on this host: `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs` shells out to `.ci/run-research-python.sh race`, which needs a writable uv Python install and network (`Read-only file system` at `~/.local/share/uv/python`); it does not touch `packages/data-source`. `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` itself is green, as shown above.

## Not run

- Repo-level UT/ST/E2E, CodeCheck (GitCode) and the Docker/binary layers: CI. This PR changes one package's text extractor and its test, plus one compiler option; the package tests, both tsc configurations, the architecture check and the recursive typecheck were run locally.

items.body:
## What does this PR do / why do we need it

Implements the **full three-layer plan** for natural-language program evolution (GitHub issue #310): turn `/evolve-design` from a hidden slash command into something a natural-language sentence can trigger, with the framework actively recommending a tree-search evolution and the interaction staying natural-language end to end.

Today `/evolve-design` is a hidden slash command: a user must already know the prefix to start an evolution search, and the only visible entry is a button in the artifact detail modal that fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` (still requiring manual completion). The interaction is command-shaped, not natural-language.

### Layer 1 — Composer intent recognition (frontend)

- **`apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts`** (new): pure `detectEvolveIntent(message)` — true only when an improvement verb pairs with an evolvable target (`program` / `code` / `algorithm` / `function` / `model` / `script` / `artifact` …). Non-evolvable targets (`formatting` / `layout` / `description` / `explanation`) never match, and bare "better" with no target never matches. `isEvolveDesignCommand()` separates the explicit slash command from natural language.
- **`EvolveSuggestionBar`** (new): a low-intrusion confirmation bar. Detection only *offers*; the user must explicitly accept before the algorithm picker opens — an evolution search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations), so a false positive is worse than a missed suggestion.
- **`App.tsx`**: an explicit `/evolve-design` command opens the algorithm picker directly (existing behavior preserved); a natural-language intent shows the confirmation bar first, and only an accepted suggestion opens the picker. Both flags reset when the message leaves evolve intent.

### Layer 2 — Agent-driven recommendation (backend)

- **`packages/evolve/src/index.ts`**: the `create_evolve_run` tool description now tells the agent to **recommend** an evolution search when the user asks in natural language to improve a program / code / algorithm / model / result against a measurable target — not only when they type `/evolve-design`. The agent phrases it as a plain suggestion ("this looks like a search-shaped problem; want me to run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") and starts only after the user confirms. This builds on the evolve-design skill, whose description already lists natural-language triggers.

### Layer 3 — Visible entry points (frontend)

- **Composer**: a new sparkle "program evolution" button fills a natural-language prompt (`Improve the program: ` / `改进一下这个程序：`) instead of a slash command; `detectEvolveIntent` recognises it and offers the suggestion bar.
- **Artifact detail modal**: the evolve button now fills a natural-language seed prompt (`Make the artifact X better: ` / `让产物 X 变得更好：`) instead of the `/evolve-design ...` command text.
- **`intent.ts`**: adds `artifact` / `产物` as evolvable targets and `变得更好` as an improvement verb so both seed prompts are recognised.

### Why confirmation before the picker?

A search spends real budget. Detection is a guess, so it must only offer; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This is the core false-positive guard — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never routed into an expensive search.

### Why verb+target pairing?

Intent detection is deliberately narrow: `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `这个更好` / `make this better` all stay silent; only sentences pointing at an evolvable target (program / code / algorithm) match.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Closes #310.

## Review follow-up (2026-10-29)

- Closing keyword corrected to plain `Closes #310`; the earlier markdown-link form left GitHub's `closingIssuesReferences` empty, so the merge would not have auto-closed the issue.
- Blocking item "CI green on this tip" is already satisfied **on this tip**: run [40645827814](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40645827814) (attempt 2) is `success`, 17 checks success (L1, ST, UT, Coverage, merge-gate, 5x L2, Freeze mocked E2E, CodeCheck); L3/L4-L5/Docker/Binary are `skipped` by policy.
